In a pot with plenty of water about to boil, cook the tagliatelle and remove them when al dente. Drain the pasta, place it in a platter or a large bowl, and add the mushroom and asparagus preparation, stirring gently. Serve hot, seasoned with chopped parsley.
notes: The main ingredients of this recipe are the pasta and the vegetables (asparagus and mushrooms). If grated cheese is added or if it is accompanied by a second course based on meat, fish, eggs, or legumes, and with some seasonal fresh fruit desserts, we obtain a complete and balanced menu. In the preparation, there are no ingredients of animal origin, making it a suitable option for vegetarians. If desired, it can be seasoned with a little grated cheese (about 10 g per dish). Finally, remember that if you do not want to add salt, this is a tasty preparation seasoned with black pepper, garlic, and parsley.

title: The circus on a plate

ingredients.name: potatoes (for puree with a little milk and butter)

preparation: Peel and cook the potatoes. While still hot, mash them with a little milk and butter until you achieve a very fine paste. Steam the green beans and remove them when they are cooked al dente, meaning slightly crunchy. Cut them into pieces of approximately 2 cm. On a plate, place the mashed potatoes in the center forming a circle (this will be the base for the clown's face). Place the green beans on top as if they were spiky hair. Use the black olives to make the eyes. Cut the cherry tomatoes in half and place one half for the nose and one for each ear. Above each ear, place a strand of grated carrot previously dressed with oil and a few drops of vinegar or lemon juice. Reserve two slices from the center of the hard-boiled egg and grate or finely chop the rest and dress it with a few drops of oil.
notes: This is a first course that can be considered almost a main course because it incorporates egg. It is a dish with a carbohydrate base (the potatoes) and a good complement of vegetables with different textures (cooked, raw, and grated). It is considered easy to chew, suitable for children from two years old. The presentation and the variety of colors can facilitate the good acceptance of this preparation, which is ultimately a potato dish with vegetables.

title: White bean, pumpkin and rosemary cream
preparation: Peel and dice the pumpkin. Sauté the finely chopped onion and the peeled whole garlic cloves in a pot with hot oil until they begin to color. Add the pumpkin and pepper to the pot (and a bit of salt, if desired) and let cook for a few more minutes. Add the broth until everything is covered. Cover and let cook for about 10-15 minutes. Add the beans and the chopped rosemary, and let cook for a few more minutes. Blend, ensuring it becomes a very fine cream.
notes: This is a very complete recipe, thanks to the legumes (white or dried beans), which provide both carbohydrates and proteins. The pumpkin, rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals, completes the nutritional contribution of this very nutritious and flavorful dish. Toasted bread croutons can be added to the cream to provide a crunchy texture.

title: Leek and fennel cream with spices, sesame seeds and rosehips
preparation: Chop the ingredients and sauté them in olive oil until golden. Cover with water and boil for 15-20 minutes. Add the pepper, cumin, and ginger, then blend. If it is too runny, remove some liquid before blending. You can add it back if the cream turns out too thick. Once served, decorate the dish with sesame and rosehip seeds.
notes: This cream, made with vegetables from the cold season, is very simple, original, and very tasty. To the classic leek, the special flavor of fennel is added, the aromatic touch of spices, and the seeds give it an exotic touch. It is a good option as a starter, first course, or side dish, and enriches the menu with a significant amount of vegetables.

title: Cabbage and Potato Trinxat

ingredients.name: small pieces of ham or a handful of pine nuts (optional complements)

preparation: Bring plenty of water to a boil in a pot. Cut off the bottom of the cabbage and discard the dirtiest outer leaves. Then, clean the cabbage with water. Peel the potatoes and place them to boil whole, with a little salt if desired. 15 minutes later, add the cabbage and cover until cooking is finished. Slice the garlic into thin slivers and sauté them in a pan with oil, along with the small pieces of ham or the pine nuts, if choosing these complements. Once the potato is cooked, drain everything and mash it all together with a fork. Add half of the garlic and sauté the mixture well in the pan where the garlic was browned. It can be plated using a mold in each dish or shaped like an omelet. When serving the dish, decorate it with the remaining garlic (optionally with the ham or pine nuts).
notes: Cabbage is a vegetable very rich in water and fiber, providing few calories, and although it is associated with the cold season, it is available almost all year round. The presence of vitamins and minerals is also notable. By preparing it with potato, the dish becomes more substantial, and it would only lack a protein source for a second course. Some variations of trinxat also incorporate white beans or poached egg, and in these cases, the dish could be considered a one-pot meal. Among the optional garnishes, the one with pine nuts is milder and healthier. If you opt for ham, it is important to remember that it is a processed red meat high in fat, classified among the foods that are recommended not to consume habitually.

title: Rice with beans and turnips
preparation: Soak the beans overnight before. Boil them with the garlic and reserve the cooking water. Puree the drained beans until a fine texture is obtained. Blanch the chard in boiling water and then immediately cool them in cold water or with ice to maintain their color. Puree the green chard leaves with a little of the bean cooking water. Reserve the stalks for decoration. Keep the chard cooking water at a simmer. Cut the turnips and the pumpkin into cubes, cook them, and brown them in a pan. Set them aside for later. Cook the rice with the chard cooking water, as if it were a risotto. Plate it by placing the green rice in the center and the bean cream around it. Decorate with the chard stalks and the turnip and pumpkin.
notes: White beans or kidney beans. Recipe adapted from Cuinatur. It is a very simple, economical, and at the same time complete and balanced dish. With a side salad, it can be an excellent single course. It can also be a good second course if combined with a more abundant salad as a first course. It can be complemented with a poached or fried egg in the center, on top of the rice.

title: Tender spinach salad with goat cheese, honey vinaigrette, walnuts and hazelnuts

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil, parsley, black pepper

preparation: Wash the spinach and lettuce leaves well and drain them. Roughly chop the larger leaves. Peel and cut the onion into julienne. Wash and slice the cucumber (or radishes). Wash and cut the tomatoes in half (or carrots into slices). Crumble the goat cheese. Mix the spinach with the lettuce and the rest of the vegetables. Distribute the salad into 2 or 3 plates and place the raisins, cucumber (or radishes), tomato (or carrots), onion, and goat cheese on top. Dress it with the honey vinaigrette and the toasted and crushed nuts. Toast the hazelnuts and walnuts in the oven at 180 °C for 10 minutes and let them cool. You can also buy pre-toasted hazelnuts. In a bowl, combine the extra virgin olive oil, sherry vinegar, honey, pepper, and salt if desired. Whisk until an emulsion is achieved. Add the walnuts and hazelnuts, lightly crushed, and mix well.
notes: This spinach salad is an original recipe, as they are usually consumed cooked. However, like other tender green leafy vegetables, they can also be eaten fresh and raw. This way, they better preserve their properties and provide protective substances for health. The salad can be an appetizer or a side dish.

title: Escarole, pomegranate and pine nut salad

ingredients.name: vinegar (low acidity, such as Modena type)

preparation: Break up the pomegranate seeds and set them aside. Prepare a vinaigrette dressing with the oil, vinegar, wine, pepper and, if desired, a bit of salt. Mix the dressing with the pomegranate. Add the pine nuts or almonds and let it rest for a while. Arrange the clean and well-drained escarole on a plate. Dress with the previously prepared sauce.
notes: This is a salad with autumn-winter ingredients such as pomegranate and escarole, very visually appealing and light. This salad provides a good supply of fiber and micronutrients provided by the escarole and the pomegranate. It can be complemented with a second course based on legumes, or fish, egg, or meat with a side of potato or cereal (pasta, rice, couscous, etc.).

title: Radish and Cucumber Salad
preparation: Wash the radishes well. Peel the cucumber and slice both the radishes and the cucumber. Arrange them in a salad bowl. In a small jar or bowl, pour the oil, vinegar, lemon juice, oregano, pepper to taste and, if desired, a bit of salt. Shake well. Pour the vinaigrette over the vegetables. Serve immediately.
notes: This simple and refreshing salad welcomes us to summer. Radishes are available all year round, but the combination with cucumber—a vegetable very rich in water and fiber that starts appearing in markets in June—makes this recipe very suitable for the hot months. The acidic dressing contributes to the feeling of freshness. You can decorate the salad and add aroma with some fresh mint leaves. We suggest a meal with this salad accompanied by grilled sardines and bread with tomato.

title: Fish, Cardoon and Swiss Chard Asparagus Soup
preparation: Thaw and cut the monkfish into dice. Place the cardoons in water and salt, and clean and cut the asparagus into pieces. Peel and finely chop the onion and spring garlic, then sauté them in a saucepan with the two tablespoons of oil over low heat. Once the onion and garlic are golden, add the asparagus and then the monkfish. Sauté everything while stirring constantly. Season with the chopped parsley and paprika (stir well so it doesn't stick). Add the glass of white wine and let it evaporate slightly. Next, add a glass of fish stock. Stir until it begins to boil. Meanwhile, steam the cardoons and add them to the preparation along with the rest of the stock. Let everything cook for about ten minutes and adjust the seasoning with salt.
notes: It is a flavorful and very light soup dish that already incorporates a portion of fiber. The fish and cardoons provide practically no fats. The rest of the ingredients are vegetables. The asparagus are quite rich in fiber, in addition to being very tasty. This recipe is recommended for low-energy diets, as well as for people who want to control fats, sugars, or carbohydrates (this dish provides practically no carbohydrates) and also for people with high blood pressure (if salt is not added).

title: Stuffed Butternut Squash Trunks
preparation: First, boil the egg. Clean, chop, and mince the mushrooms, onion, and leek (if not in season, the leek can be omitted). Set them aside. Clean the butternut squashes, cut them into three equal-sized pieces, and boil them for five to seven minutes. It is advisable for them to remain firm and whole. Let them cool and hollow them out, leaving a cavity for the filling. Reserve the extracted squash. In a pan with oil, sauté the onion, mushrooms, and leek over low heat. Five minutes later, add a bit of parsley and, if desired, the finely chopped ham, and let it cook for a few more minutes. Season with pepper, nutmeg, and, if desired, a bit of salt. Add the rest of the reserved squash and the hard-boiled egg, finely chopped. Mix well and stuff the butternut squash trunks with the sautéed mixture. Sprinkle the grated cheese on top and bake in the oven for about ten minutes. To serve, place three pieces of squash vertically on each plate and garnish with grated carrot or a mixture of lettuce.
notes: This recipe provides a significant vegetable intake, and both the appearance and flavor are very attractive. If one or two more eggs are added to the recipe, it could be considered a main course, thanks to the protein contribution from the eggs (as well as the ham and grated cheese). The ham, specifically, is optional and can be replaced with dried fruit (such as toasted and chopped almonds).

title: Falafels

ingredients.name: dried chickpeas soaked overnight in water

preparation: Drain the soaked chickpeas, mix in the cooked chickpeas, and blend them in a blender or electric mixer (it doesn't need to be a very fine paste). Peel and chop the onion and garlic. Mix the chickpea paste with the onion, garlic, and spices. Season with salt and pepper. Store and let rest in the refrigerator for at least one hour. To make the accompanying salad, wash and chop the vegetables and sauté them with salt, oil, and lemon juice. Take the chickpea paste out of the refrigerator and form portions of about 20 g with your hands and dust them lightly with flour. In a saucepan with hot oil, fry the falafels until they are golden. Drain them on absorbent paper and serve them hot with the salad on the side.
notes: Source: Agència Catalana de Seguretat Alimentària / Fundació Alícia

title: Lentil soup
preparation: Cook the cleaned and finely sliced leek and the peeled and minced garlic in a large saucepan with the oil, without letting them brown. Add the lentils, grated tomatoes, 3/4 of the thyme, and three times the volume of cold water. Cook everything for about 30 minutes once it starts boiling. Season with salt halfway through the cooking. Once the lentils are cooked, add the lemon juice, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve topped with the remaining thyme.
notes: It is an ideal dish for cold seasons, although the presence of lemon and thyme gives it a refreshing and Mediterranean touch. It is a first course very low in fats and rich in carbohydrates and proteins, the main nutrients of lentils, along with fiber and minerals such as iron, the absorption of which can be improved by choosing an orange for dessert, for example.

title: Guacamole with nachos
preparation: Peel the avocados and place them cut into a bowl. Mash them with a fork and add the lemon juice so they do not oxidize and change color. Add the finely chopped onion and the unpeeled tomato, also finely chopped. Chop the coriander as finely as possible and add it to the previous mixture. Mix everything well and season with salt, and if desired, add a teaspoon of extra virgin olive oil to make the sauce less thick. Place the nachos on a plate and serve them with the resulting sauce in the center.
notes: Adapted from: Receptes

title: Chickpea Gazpacho
preparation: Wash and peel the cucumber. Dice it, salt it, and let it drain in a colander for about 10 minutes. Wash and peel the tomato. Peel and mince the garlic. In a deep container, blend the chickpeas with the cucumber, tomato, garlic, salt, lemon juice, and a glass of cold water. Add the oil and more cold water until you achieve the desired consistency.
notes: Chickpeas and vegetables provide fiber, vitamins, and minerals. It is a good option for both lunch and dinner. On a hot day, it can be served in a mug or a soup bowl with some ice cubes to keep it cold. You can also add some toasted whole wheat bread cubes to give it a crunchy touch.

title: Gratinated onion soup

ingredients.name: tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil
small slices of stale bread (preferably whole wheat baguette)
tablespoons of grated cheese (mixture of gruyère and manchego)

preparation: Slice the onions into thin rings. In a saucepan, heat the olive oil. Add the onion and cook over low heat until well golden, taking care not to burn it, for approximately 25 minutes. Add a little salt, pepper, and the tablespoon of flour, and stir until dissolved. Incorporate the white wine and stir until reduced, increasing the heat slightly for about two or three minutes. Add the broth, wait for it to boil, and maintain the boiling for 10 minutes. Remove from heat. Optionally, you can season the soup with a pinch of thyme. To gratin the soup, preheat the oven to 200 °C. Distribute the onion and broth into individual heatproof containers. Decorate each container with one or two slices of previously toasted bread, and cover the surface with a tablespoon of grated cheese. Place the soup in the oven until the surface is golden, and serve immediately.
notes: Gratinated onion soup is a traditional winter dish. The main ingredients are onion and broth. To ensure the soup is easily digestible, use a fat-free broth or a vegetable broth. The toasted bread and cheese add flavor and consistency to the soup; however, if these ingredients are used only for flavor, the energy value of the dish is low. Due to the characteristics of the ingredients, it can be considered a suitable dish for both adults and children. Since it is a fairly light first course, it can be combined with a more substantial second course.

title: Red lentil, carrot and coriander cream
preparation: Begin by sautéing the peeled and finely chopped onion and the peeled and sliced carrots in oil in the pot where the soup will be made. When the onion starts to color, add the cleaned and sliced leek (if it is not in season, the leek can be omitted), the coriander leaves (reserve a few for garnish), and let it cook for about 5 minutes. Add half of the broth, the pepper, and if desired, a bit of salt, and cook for about 15 minutes. After this time, blend it. Add the rest of the broth and the lentils, and let it cook for about 20 minutes until the lentils are cooked. Decorate each bowl with chopped coriander.
notes: If you like spicy food, you can add a chili pepper to the sauté, which can be removed before blending. This cream is a very good option for the winter season, being nice and warm, but also for warmer periods, as its ingredients are available all year round. With this cream, you eat legumes with a more exotic touch than a classic stewed lentil dish, and it can be accompanied by a salad as a first course, or a vegetable second course, such as spinach or pumpkin fritters.

title: Pumpkin cream
preparation: Peel the carrots, clean them, and cut them into slices. Peel the pumpkin and cut it into cubes. Sauté the peeled and finely chopped onion in a saucepan with oil until soft. Add the carrots along with the pumpkin and the broth. Cover and let it cook for about 20 minutes. Season with pepper, nutmeg and, if desired, a little salt. Blend until it reaches a smooth cream consistency.
notes: A very simple, smooth and tasty recipe, typical of autumn. Due to its texture and easy digestibility, pumpkin, and especially this cream, is very well accepted at all ages. You can garnish the cream with some pumpkin seeds lightly toasted in the oven. As it is a dish composed of vegetables, the menu can be completed with a protein-based second course based on meat, fish, egg, or legumes, with potatoes or rice as a side dish.

title: Cold melon soup with Iberian ham shreds and mint
preparation: Peel the melon and remove the seeds. Reserve a couple of slices, cut the rest of the pulp into chunks, and blend it until you obtain a very fine cream. Season it with black pepper and, if desired, a little salt, and set it aside. Keep it in the refrigerator. When it is time to serve the cream, add the natural yogurt and, if desired, a couple of tablespoons of heavy cream, and stir everything together. Cut the reserved melon pieces into small cubes or make balls and add them. Serve the cream very cold, garnished with the Iberian ham shreds, the melon cubes, and the fresh mint leaves, either whole or chopped.
notes: This is a very refreshing and light recipe, easy and quick to prepare, which you can have ready before the meal. Including fruit not only in desserts but in different courses of the meal helps guarantee adequate intake. This recipe includes ham, which, like other processed meats, is recommended not to be consumed habitually. You can substitute this ingredient and add, for example, cucumber or toasted pine nuts. A good way to complement this recipe to create a complete menu would be with a second course containing starches (paella, fideuà, potato and egg or tuna salad, legume salad, etc.).

title: Spirals with pumpkin and basil
preparation: Cook the pasta in plenty of boiling water with a bit of oil and salt. Clean the pumpkins and cut them into half-slices. Peel the garlic and slice them into thin pieces. Sauté the pumpkins, garlic, and pine nuts in a wok or pan with oil for about 3 minutes. Add the yogurt, grated cheese, basil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice, and mix well. Mix in the cooked and drained pasta and serve immediately.
notes: The main ingredients of this recipe are pasta and pumpkin. Pumpkin is a vegetable with very few calories and contains fiber. Pasta is a recommended carbohydrate-rich food, also for the diet of people with diabetes and overweight, in a certain amount depending on each person's diet. In this case, about 60 g of raw pasta per dish is used. If you find it convenient, in order to reduce the energy intake of the dish, you can reduce the amount of pasta and add more volume to the dish with vegetables; that is, increase the amount of pumpkin and decrease the amount of oil. You can also use whole wheat pasta to increase the fiber content of the meal. The saturated fat and cholesterol content of the preparation is very low.

title: Green bean salad with tomato and garlic-scented aroma
preparation: Cook the tender green beans (whole and without the tips), preferably steamed, trying to keep them crunchy. Cool them down and set aside. Grate the tomato and season it with black pepper, extra virgin olive oil and, if desired, a little salt. Warm the serving dish in the oven for a few moments. Remove it and rub it energetically with a raw garlic clove. Let it cool. Arrange the beans and cover them with the prepared tomato sauce without cooking it. Drizzle the dish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
notes: This dish is characterized by its vegetable content and by being very easy and quick to prepare. Since the cooking is very short, some of the ingredients are raw and it is served cold, it can be considered a very refreshing salad. The recipe is original and tasty, and provides a different way to eat tender green beans. The fact of rubbing the dish with raw garlic aromatizes it in a very subtle way. You can have everything prepared in the fridge and assemble the dish at the moment of eating. To complement the menu, we suggest a second course based on rabbit or baked fish with a garnish of potato and sliced onion, also baked. If you prefer to make a single and very complete dish, you can add about 100-150g of cooked legumes to the green beans, such as chickpeas or white beans. For dessert, a good fruit salad with the ripest fruits you have.

title: Rustic tomato, fish and stale bread salad

ingredients.name: grilled white fish fillets (about 250 g) or two tins of blue fish (mackerel, sardines, etc.)

preparation: Crumble the bread into pieces of about 2 cm and wrap them in a damp cloth so they become moist. Peel the tomatoes and cut them into large pieces. Clean the peppers and peel the onion. Chop everything into pieces that are not too small. In a large salad bowl, mix the bread, tomatoes, pepper, onion, and crumbled fish. If you have opted for canned fish in olive oil, you can add the oil. If not, add about 6 tablespoons of oil. Season with salt and pepper and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
notes: To serve it cold, it is best to leave the cleaned vegetables in the fridge for a few hours before preparing the salad. It can be served as a main course for a light dinner.

title: Coques with tomato, sardines and mató cheese
preparation: Making the coques: Mix all the ingredients until you obtain a homogeneous dough. Roll it out with a rolling pin and cut it into 4 individual portions (rectangles of approximately 15x10 cm). Bake them at 180 °C for 20 minutes and let them cool. Making the garnish for the coques: Fillet and devein the sardines. Beat the mató cheese with a drizzle of oil and, if desired, a pinch of salt. Spread a little mató cheese on the coques, and place two sardine fillets on top. Slice the tomato as thinly as possible and place a couple of slices on top of the sardines. Bake at 180 °C for 10 minutes, just enough for the sardines and tomato to cook. Remove them from the oven, and once out, using the mató cream in a pastry bag, decorate the surface of the coca with some dots. Garnish the dish with a bit of watercress.
notes: In cherry season, it can be decorated with pieces of pitted cherries. In summer, peach can be used, and in other times, other seasonal fruits can be selected. This coca is an original variation of the traditional coca de recapte with summer products. It can be part of an appetizer, a first course, or even a second course. Thanks to the diversity of ingredients, it results in a complete proposal, even though in a small quantity, therefore, mild and very tasty. Incorporating fruits into different meals is a very good way to increase consumption and obtain more original and diverse dishes. The menu can be completed with, for example, a cold tomato cream with croutons and hard-boiled egg. For dessert, we suggest a peach fruit salad with mint.

title: Pumpkin and basil fritters
preparation: In a deep container, mix the grated pumpkin well with the rest of the ingredients. Let the mixture rest for about 30 minutes. Place a frying pan over the heat with the oil. When the oil is hot, drop in tablespoons of the batter one by one, making sure to flatten them slightly and ensuring they do not touch each other. Let the fritters brown for a few minutes and flip them once so they cook on the other side. As they cook, remove them and place them on a plate lined with paper towels so the excess oil is absorbed.
notes: The fritters can be accompanied by tomato sauce or sliced tomato salad. Regarding the preparation, 50 g of crushed almonds can be replaced by 50 g of grated hard cheese. In this case, do not add salt. They can be served as a second course, for example, after a legume dish.

title: Chickpeas with cod and spinach

ingredients.name: boiled chickpeas (if you cooked them yourself, reserve the cooking water)
ripe tomatoes (canned crushed tomato, if it is not tomato season)
tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil

preparation: Boil the spinach with a little water (and, if desired, a bit of iodized salt). In a pan, make a sauté with the garlic, chopped onion, and tomatoes. Add the chickpeas and the cod. Shake the pan and add a little broth from cooking the chickpeas (if you did not cook them yourself, vegetable broth can be added). Let it come to a boil and at the last moment add the spinach. The spinach can be added raw and allowed to finish cooking inside the pan with the chickpeas and cod.
notes: The dish we present to you is a good option for a single-course meal, which can be accompanied by a salad. It is a complete dish, providing carbohydrates from the chickpeas, proteins from the cod and chickpeas, and the fiber, vitamins, and minerals present in all the ingredients, especially from the chickpeas and the spinach.

title: Rice with artichokes and mushrooms
preparation: Soak the mushrooms in cold water over heat. When the water boils, remove them and drain them. Peel and finely chop the onion, and also clean and cut the artichokes. Place the oil, the onion, and a little later the artichokes in a heavy-bottomed pan and let them cook over low heat with a lid. When the onion is well transparent, add the mushrooms, sauté them, and later add the rice and stir it. Add the mushroom water (approximately twice as much water as rice) and place the pan in a preheated oven for about fifteen or sixteen minutes. Remove it from the oven, cover it, and let it rest for five to eight minutes. In this preparation, fresh mushrooms can also be used: sunchokes, porcini, oyster mushrooms, maitake, and even better if you have different types of mushrooms available.
notes: In this preparation, fresh mushrooms can also be used: sunchokes, porcini, oyster mushrooms, maitake, and even better if you have different types of mushrooms available. Menu proposal: Rice with artichokes and mushrooms, Stewed pork loin with prunes, Orange slices with hot chocolate and pine nuts. The dish we propose is a preparation rich in micronutrients from the rice and also in minerals and fiber provided by the mushrooms and artichokes. Apart from the oil used, the ingredients do not provide fats, so we can consider it a very low-fat dish. To decrease the energy content of the preparation, you can use a smaller amount of rice and increase the proportion of vegetables (artichokes and mushrooms), add less oil to the sauté, and let it cook more by steaming. It is a suitable dish for people who need to control fat and salt intake, and also for diabetics, as long as they measure the amount of rice. It can be a recipe very well accepted by both adults and children in the house.

title: Potato and vegetable omelet
preparation: Dice the pumpkin into small cubes and cook them in their own juice. Peel and dice the potatoes in the same way, and boil them until they are soft. Beat the eggs and add salt to taste. Mix the pumpkin, potatoes, and eggs. Prepare a frying pan with oil, and once it is hot, pour in the mixture and cook it until it sets.
notes: As a serving suggestion, cut the omelet into squares and serve with toothpicks to make it easier to eat at parties. Be careful with the sticks if it is for small children.

title: Spinach Cannelloni

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil and salt
butter or extra virgin olive oil
iodized salt, white pepper and nutmeg

preparation: After boiling the spinach (with little water), set them aside, well drained. Heat the oil in a pan and toast the pine nuts. Add the raisins so they swell. Set everything aside and, in the same pan, chop the garlic into very small pieces. Next, add the spinach and the nuts, mixing well. Cook the pasta and let it cool, each piece separately, on a very clean surface. Fill the cannelloni with the prepared spinach mixture and roll them up. Place them in a baking dish —previously greased with a little oil— and pour abundant béchamel (not too thick) over them. Sprinkle the grated cheese on top and brown in the oven. To make the béchamel: Melt the butter or add extra virgin olive oil in a saucepan over low heat. Add the flour (wheat or corn) and cook for 3-4 minutes over low heat while stirring with a hand whisk or a wooden spoon. The mixture will change color and darken, a sign that the flour is toasting. Let it cool to room temperature. In another saucepan, heat the milk or plant-based drink. When the milk is about to boil, lower the heat and incorporate the previous roux while stirring with a hand whisk. Let it cook for 10 minutes over low heat without letting it stop boiling, stirring the whole time to prevent the béchamel from sticking to the bottom of the pan and so that the roux is well integrated with the milk. You will see that, gradually, the béchamel thickens. Important: if it seems a bit liquid to you, do not worry. It will become much thicker as it cools. After 10 minutes, when the béchamel is ready, you can season with salt to taste, grate nutmeg over it, and stir again.
notes: In our home, roasted meat cannelloni are more traditional, but considering that during these days a very high consumption of meat and fish often occurs, this is a very good alternative; lighter and very tasty. Given the amount of milk and cheese the dish contains, with a broth and a good refreshing salad, the spinach cannelloni can also be a single course, or they can be accompanied by a light second course. Due to the composition and texture of the dish, it is very suitable for all diners. A vegan version of this dish can be made by substituting the milk with a plant-based drink, the butter with extra virgin olive oil, and the cheese with breadcrumbs.

title: Coca de recapte with herring

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil and iodized salt
herring (fresh sardine fillets can also be used)
extra virgin olive oil, parsley, black pepper

preparation: Clean the bell peppers, eggplants, pumpkin and peel the onions, to roast them in the oven for 45 minutes or 1 hour, approximately. Once the vegetables are cooked, let them cool outside the oven. Next, prepare the dough for the coca. Place the flour in a large bowl. Make a hole in the center of the bowl (like a volcano) and add the yeast, the egg yolks and a little water, stir it, adding more water if necessary. Once the dough is made, roll it out on a clean marble surface and work it with your hands and a little extra virgin olive oil. Then let it rest for about 10 minutes in the refrigerator. Meanwhile, peel the cold vegetables, cut them into strips and slice the tomato. Keep everything in the refrigerator. Take the coca dough out of the refrigerator and work it again, flatten it with a rolling pin and place it on a baking tray. Brush it with a little extra virgin olive oil, add the raw tomato, the sliced vegetables and, if desired, the herring cut into pieces. Finally, put it in the oven with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil at 190 °C for about 25-30 minutes.
notes: Coca de recapte is one of the most traditional recipes of Catalan cuisine, especially in the Lleida area, and many variants can be found. It is a clear example of "utilization and seasonal cooking"; that is, in summer, when there is a large production of tomatoes, bell peppers, and eggplants, various preserves and preparations are made such as cold creams, empedrats, gazpachos, and savory cakes. All these preparations incorporate a large amount of vegetables, legumes, and some also include small amounts of fish, meat, or egg, with extra virgin olive oil as the dressing fat. Coca de recapte can be a very complete cold dish, accompanied by a tomato soup, melon soup, or a good salad.

title: Eggplant pâté

ingredients.name: oregano, iodized salt and extra virgin olive oil

preparation: Peel the eggplants and onions, cut them into small pieces and cook them with a bit of olive oil. When they begin to brown, add the garlic and the bread, both cut into small pieces. When all the ingredients are cooked, add oregano to taste and, if desired, adjust the salt. Blend everything until a homogeneous paste is obtained and let it rest until it cools.
notes: Eggplant pâté is a classic recipe of Mediterranean cuisine. In other food cultures, it can be prepared with tahini (sesame paste) and spices such as cumin. In this case, a very simple and flavorful recipe is proposed that can be prepared with very few ingredients. It is an ideal preparation for snacking with breadsticks or vegetable sticks (carrot, pepper, celery, etc.) or for spreading on sandwiches or toast. It is a plant-based alternative to conventional pâté, easy, quick to make, and economical.

title: Pizzas
preparation: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Clean the mushrooms well and slice them. Cut the cooked ham into medium pieces. Make a sofrito of ripe tomatoes with a bit of extra virgin olive oil and salt. Once the sofrito is made, spread it evenly over the dough, and place the ham and mushrooms on top. Add a thin layer of cheese over the entire surface and season with oregano to taste. Bake the pizza for 15 to 20 minutes depending on the desired degree of cooking.
notes: Adapted from: Recetasdiarias

title: Strawberry, mató and basil skewer
preparation: Cut the mató into cubes and clean the strawberries well and cut them in half. Skewer half a strawberry, a basil leaf, and a cube of mató. Repeat the operation until all the skewers are filled. Before serving, add a few drops of sherry vinegar over the mató.
notes: This simple and easy recipe is an original way to eat fresh fruit for dessert. Although it is a simple preparation, it turns out to be very elegant and cheerful due to the presentation with a variety of colors and textures. Strawberries provide fiber, vitamins, minerals, and other compounds beneficial to health, mató enriches the dish with nutrients such as calcium and proteins, and basil adds color and an intense aroma. As the seasons change, fruits can be varied according to the most seasonal and local production.

title: Pear textures
preparation: Wash and peel the pears. Pear granita: Puree one pear and place it in the freezer. Stir it occasionally so it becomes grainy. Pear compote: Cook two pears with a little water and a piece of vanilla. When the pears are cooked, remove the vanilla from the preparation, puree, and let cool. Cut the remaining pear into small cubes, splash with lemon juice, and keep in the refrigerator. Assemble the desserts in a glass or cup, in this order: Pear cubes as a base, a layer of pear compote on top, and finally the pear granita on top.
notes: Fruit-based desserts are always a light and refreshing option. In this recipe, ripe pears can be used to prepare a delicious compote, while it is recommended to reserve a firmer pear to cut into cubes. Another option is to mix several fruits to enrich the dish. For example, you can use: an apple for the compote, peach for the cubes, and melon for the granita. This adds different textures and flavors and makes the desserts more attractive.

title: Apple and pear compote
preparation: Peel and core the apples and pears. Cut them into small pieces and cook them with the lemon zest, cinnamon, and 100 ml of water until they are soft. Remove the cinnamon stick and the lemon. Mash the mixture with a fork or an electric blender until a homogeneous mixture is obtained. Let it rest in the refrigerator until cooled and then serve.
notes: Apples and pears are two typical fruits of late summer and autumn, very common in our surroundings. Although it is recommended to consume whole and fresh fruit, compotes are a good option to vary and make use of ripe fruit. If the fruit is very ripe, there is no need to add sugar. The cinnamon and lemon zest already provide a sweet and aromatic touch. This recipe is also a useful and tasty way to reduce food waste when we have a few old pieces of fruit left. This compote can also be used to accompany roasted meats.

title: Figs with curd cheese and a drizzle of honey
preparation: Wash the fresh figs and dry them well. Cut them in half and then into thick slices (about 4 slices per fig). Chop the toasted hazelnuts with a food processor or a mortar. Place about 50 g of curd cheese on each plate and arrange a couple of sliced figs around it. Sprinkle the chopped hazelnuts on top and finish with a drizzle of honey.
notes: These desserts combine fresh fruit (figs), a dairy product (curd cheese), and dried fruit (hazelnuts), creating a very tasty and Mediterranean recipe. Moreover, it is very healthy. It is recommended to reserve these desserts to finish a light menu, as they are more complete desserts than those composed only of fresh fruit. The drizzle of honey provides a sweet touch that balances the flavors and enhances the nuances of the dish, providing a delicate and harmonious contrast.

title: Seasonal fruit skewer with mint leaves

ingredients.name: skewers for preparing the fruit skewers

preparation: Peel and dice the oranges (keep them covered in the refrigerator). Seed the pomegranate (keep it covered in the refrigerator). Wash and dry the grapes well (keep them covered in the refrigerator). Shortly before starting the meal, alternate the grapes, orange, and dried plum on the skewers until 8 skewers are prepared. At the time of serving, arrange the pomegranate on a platter and place the fruit skewers on top, then decorate the platter with the fresh mint leaves.
notes: This is an excellent proposal based on fresh winter fruits in combination with dried fruit, the plum. Fresh fruits are always the best desserts and refreshments and, besides eating them whole, they can occasionally be presented in different formats, like this proposal. The mint and pomegranate end up providing a touch of freshness and very striking colors to this recipe. These are desserts that are easy to prepare, light, and very suitable for closing a celebratory meal. For meal desserts, choose fresh, seasonal, and local fruit!

title: Autumn desserts
preparation: Present two slices of oven-baked sweet potato on a dessert plate. Add the thin slices of codonyat and the boiled chestnuts on top. Drizzle the two "turróns" with a little melted dark chocolate, and garnish them with four or five toasted pine nuts and the mint leaf.
notes: The main characteristic of this dish is the use of typical autumn products, as well as the ease of preparation. Since this proposal is quite energetic, we recommend it as a dessert for a rather light meal, for example, a first course of endive and pomegranate salad and a second course of fish en papillote, or as a festive dessert. Enjoy this little pleasure, but remember that these are not desserts to make very often. In everyday life, the best desserts are whole or sliced fresh seasonal and local fruits.

title: Banana, almond and yogurt ice cream

ingredients.name: natural yogurts or fresh whipped cheese

preparation: You can use ripe bananas that you have frozen in pieces. If you don't have any, cut the bananas and place them in a closed container and freeze them for 2 hours. Mix the frozen bananas, the yogurt, and the almonds. Blend until creamy. Serve immediately or place in a closed container and keep in the freezer.

title: Strawberry, banana and milk smoothie
preparation: Remove the inedible parts of the fruit and cut them into pieces. Mix the fruit and the milk and blend everything with a blender until a smooth mixture is obtained. It is ready to serve. If the consistency of the smoothie is too thick, add more milk, and if it is too liquid, you can add more fruit.
notes: Although fruit is better consumed whole, this is a very simple preparation that can be enjoyed from time to time. It is a good option for a snack, for example, which children usually enjoy very much. The addition of milk provides a higher energy and nutritional contribution than usual fresh fruit desserts, but if a light meal has been eaten, it can also be a recipe to finish a lunch or a dinner.

title: Peach sorbet

ingredients.name: natural yogurt or fresh whipped cheese

preparation: Blend the frozen peaches with the yogurt and lemon juice until creamy. Serve immediately or transfer to an airtight container and keep in the freezer.

title: Frozen fruit juice cubes
preparation: This preparation consists simply of making the fruit juice of your choice, putting it into an ice cube tray and letting it freeze. You can use fun-shaped molds to make the ice cube more attractive. They can be served in wide glasses to pick them up while they are still frozen, or let them turn into fresh juice if they are not eaten immediately.

title: Winter fruit mille-feuille
preparation: Peel the pear and slice it vertically or horizontally (removing the core and seeds). Peel the kiwis and cut them into slices. Peel and seed the pomegranate. Slice the quince paste. In each plate, arrange 1-2 pieces of quince paste at the base, then 2-3 slices of pear on top, and 2-3 slices of kiwi on top. Finish the layers with a spoonful of pomegranate. Decorate the preparation and the plate with a drizzle of dark chocolate and a pinch of icing sugar.
notes: It is also important to include desserts based on fresh fruit during celebrations. Fruit in holiday meals can be prepared in different ways, adding small amounts of ingredients that give the dish a festive distinction. This way, a high systematic consumption of sweet desserts with high sugar and fat content can be avoided. These winter fruit-based desserts are easy and quick to prepare, but they have a very striking and festive final appearance. Choose seasonal and local fruits!

title: Orange slices with walnuts and a drizzle of dark chocolate
preparation: Peel the oranges and cut them into slightly thick slices. Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie and when it starts to melt, add two tablespoons of hot water and stir everything until it is smooth. Peel the walnuts and chop them. Drizzle the orange slices with a little hot chocolate and garnish them with the chopped walnuts.
notes: The period when oranges are best and sweetest is from the end of the year (November-December) until approximately the months of March-April. Oranges, like mandarins, are fruits rich in vitamin C and fiber. In order to ensure the preservation of fiber, it is advisable to prioritize consuming the whole orange and avoid regular intake in juice form. The combination of orange and dark chocolate flavors forms a good pairing, which is why we often find this combination in different formats (dark chocolate with orange, orange peel sticks dipped in dark chocolate, chocolate cake with orange, etc.). In order not to increase the energy value of these desserts too much, the dark chocolate and chopped walnuts should only be a small garnish for the dish.

title: Orange, grape and pomegranate fruit salad with fresh mint
preparation: In a large bowl, peel and dice the oranges. Deseed the pomegranate and mix it with the orange. Add the grapes, cut in half and without seeds. Pour the juice over the fruit. Cover and keep refrigerated. At the moment of serving, add some fresh mint leaves.
notes: This is an excellent proposal based on fresh autumn fruits. Fresh fruits are always the best desserts and refreshments, and besides eating them whole, they can occasionally be presented in different formats like this proposal. The mint adds the final touch of freshness to this recipe.

title: Watermelon and yogurt gelato
preparation: Cut the watermelon into pieces, remove the seeds, and freeze it for at least 3-4 hours. Blend half of the watermelon until it has a homogeneous texture. Decant it towards the sides of the container and add the yogurt. Add the rest of the watermelon and mix until it has a smooth and creamy texture. It can be eaten immediately or frozen for 2-3 hours for a firmer texture. In this case, leave it out for 30 minutes before eating so that it is creamier.

title: Pear, hazelnut and yogurt gelato

ingredients.name: natural yogurts or fresh whipped cheese
vanilla bean or a few drops of essence (optional)

preparation: Peel and core the pears, cut them into small pieces and place them in a saucepan. Add the lemon zest, two tablespoons of water and the vanilla (optional). Cover and cook them gently until they are soft and no liquid remains. Once cooked, remove the lemon zest and the vanilla bean, and blend. Let it cool. Mix it with the yogurt and place it in the freezer for an hour. Add the hazelnuts and blend well. Return it to the freezer. Repeat the procedure three times to break the ice crystals so that it becomes creamy.

title: Strawberry and orange fruit salad with spiced gelatin
preparation: Wash and chop the fruit into pieces. Hydrate the gelatin sheets in cold water for a few minutes. In a saucepan, combine the 300 ml of water, sugar, juice, and spices. Stir and bring to a boil for a few seconds. Set aside. Drain the gelatin and add it to the hot liquid. Stir everything together until completely dissolved. Strain the mixture. Pour it into a large container and place it in the refrigerator for a few hours until it sets. Take the gelatin and stir it so it reaches a sauce-like consistency. Arrange the chopped fruit on a plate and cover it with the stirred gelatin. Decorate with fresh mint leaves and grate a little citrus zest over the top.

title: Melon and watermelon balls
preparation: Make balls of watermelon and melon using a melon baller. Place them in a large bowl and keep them in the refrigerator. Heat the plant-based drink or milk with the spices over low heat for 4 minutes. Cover and let it cool in the refrigerator. Just before serving, mix the liquid with the fruit and distribute into individual bowls.
notes: Watermelon and melon are two of the quintessential summer fruits. The most common and recommended way to eat fruit is whole or cut into pieces, but occasionally, recipes can be prepared that do not involve the addition of ingredients such as sugar, cream, etc. In this recipe, the base liquid is a plant-based drink or milk with spices, which practically does not modify the low caloric value of the desserts.

title: Lemon or Lime Sorbet
preparation: Make the juice from the lemons (or limes). Heat the water and dissolve the sugar in it until a syrup is created. Immediately after, add, while mixing, the lemon (or lime) juice, and let it rest in the freezer for a couple of hours. Beat the two egg whites to stiff peaks, then mix with the lemon mixture. Adjust the acidity with salt if necessary, and serve.

title: Cantaloupe melon granita
preparation: Cut half of the cantaloupe melon into chunks and freeze it overnight. The next day, add the other half and blend it. To make it sweeter and creamier, you can add a ripe banana (that you have frozen in chunks).
notes: To make it sweeter and creamier, you can add a ripe banana (that you have frozen in chunks).

title: Apricot Cake (Coca d'albercocs)

ingredients.name: whole wheat or mixed wheat flour

preparation: Clean the apricots, cut them in half and remove the pits. Preheat the oven. If the mold is removable, cover the mold with parchment paper and grease it with oil. If the mold is not removable and is non-stick, no paper is needed, but it should still be greased with oil. Sprinkle the bottom of the mold with sugar and place the apricot halves open-side down, covering the entire bottom of the mold. Bake in the oven at 180 °C for about 10 minutes. Meanwhile, place the rest of the ingredients in a bowl and stir until the batter is smooth and homogeneous. Pour the batter into the mold over the fruit. Bake in the oven for about 30 min at 180 °C.
notes: Although the most recommended way to eat fruit is, without a doubt, without transforming it, that is, clean and fresh, from time to time fruit can be a good ingredient for special desserts, such as homemade cakes.

title: Potato, onion, and carrot omelet without egg (with chickpea flour)
preparation: Wash, peel, and slice the potatoes into thin rounds. Fry them in a pan with olive oil over medium heat. Peel and chop the onion. Wash and slice the carrot into thin rounds. Add the two vegetables to the pan. Fry everything together until golden. Once cooked, drain to remove excess oil, season with pepper, and set aside. Sift the flour and starch into a bowl, add the water, vinegar, and salt, and stir the mixture ensuring there are no lumps. Add the necessary amount of the mixture to the sautéed potato, onion, and carrot as if it were beaten egg. Place it in a non-stick pan with a drizzle of oil and cook over low heat for 10-15 minutes until it begins to firm up. Flip it, add a drizzle of oil, and let it brown for a few more minutes until fully cooked. Let it cool, and serve.
notes: It can be baked in the oven at 180 °C for about 20 minutes. In this case, there is no need to flip it. This "omelet" is a plant-based alternative to egg, as it is replaced by chickpea flour; since legumes also belong to the protein food group, this preparation can serve as a plant-based main course with a protein contribution. Thanks to the accompaniment of onion and carrot, it is also a recipe enriched with vegetables, and the potatoes guarantee the presence of starchy foods, rich in carbohydrates. Therefore, it is a complete dish that can be accompanied by a vegetable cream, a bowl of gazpacho, or a salad.

title: Lentil and walnut faux pate
preparation: Peel and chop the garlic. Puree the lentils together with the walnuts, garlic, lemon juice, oil, cumin, salt, and pepper. A little water can be added to improve the consistency, as well as more lemon juice if needed.
notes: Legumes are foods with such a complete nutrient density and provide so many health benefits that it is recommended that they be present in the diet at least two or three times a week. Lentils have a high content of fiber, protein, phosphorus, and iron. Lemon is an extraordinary source of vitamins, especially vitamin C, which is found especially in the pulp, and it is very good for increasing the absorption of the plant iron abundant in lentils. The walnut is composed of fat rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids (omega 3). It also has strong proteins, carbohydrates, fiber, calcium, potassium, and other minerals. It is a high energy density food. This preparation, in addition to being very tasty, is a very good alternative to pâtés or cold cuts when preparing sandwiches. This preparation can be served as a first course with salad and bread or to prepare sandwiches.

title: Chickpeas with curry
preparation: Cook the onion, peeled and finely chopped, in a clay pot with oil until it is soft. Add the curry (and a bit of salt, if desired) and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato and let it cook for about 5 minutes. Add the pumpkin cut into small cubes and cook for about 8-10 minutes. Add the chickpeas and cook everything for about 5-8 more minutes. Decorate with clean, chopped coriander.
notes: This recipe constitutes a legume stew with vegetables, but with an exotic touch provided by the presence of curry and coriander. It is a dish rich in carbohydrates and proteins, and especially abundant in protective elements provided by the chickpeas, pumpkin, onion, and tomato (fiber, minerals, vitamins, etc.). It also contains antioxidant compounds found in spices such as curry and coriander, in the beta-carotene of the pumpkin, in the lycopene of the tomato, or the vitamin E of the olive oil. If you want the dish to be juicier, you can add water or vegetable broth.

title: Baked sea bass with fennel and lemon aroma
preparation: Season the sea bass and coat them with oil. Clean the lemon and cut half of it into slices. Peel and chop the garlic and mix it with the fennel. Stuff the sea bass with the fennel and a slice of lemon. Place them in a baking dish. Pour the wine, the juice of half a lemon, and the water over them. Bake in an oven, preheated to 250 °C, for about 20 minutes. Halfway through the cooking, baste them with the juices they release.
notes: This dish should be eaten as soon as it comes out of the oven. Prepared in the oven, the sea bass is a low-calorie food but rich in protein. Fennel has a sweet and mild flavor, similar to celery, with an aniseed note. The proposed vegetable garnish and condiments enhance the mild flavor of the fish and enrich the dish with regulatory nutrients (vitamins and minerals) and energy-providing ones (carbohydrates from potatoes) without significantly increasing the calories of the dish. You can buy the fish fresh and freeze it in advance to avoid the substantial price difference that can occur in the days leading up to the Christmas holidays.

title: Baked sea bream with potatoes, sweet potatoes and sliced onions

ingredients.name: iodized salt, white pepper and fennel

preparation: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes, sweet potatoes, and onions. Arrange them in a large baking dish, with the onion on top. Add salt and pepper, a good drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, and 1/2 glass of white wine. Place in the oven at 180-200 °C for approximately 30 minutes. Remove the dish from the oven. Add the whole sea bream, previously cleaned of scales and viscera and seasoned with salt and pepper, on top of the bed of potatoes, sweet potato, and onion. Place some very thin slices of lemon on top. Let it cook for approximately thirty more minutes. Serve the potatoes, sweet potato, and onion at the base of the plate, and on top, half a sea bream with a couple of lemon slices and a pinch of fennel (optional).
notes: This is a main course with a very mild flavor, easy to prepare and suitable for the whole family. Be very careful to separate the sea bream loins well, especially for children and also for people with low visual acuity. When served with a good side of potatoes, sweet potatoes, and onion, it can be combined with a milder first course, such as a vegetable cream, broth, or a salad with fresh ingredients and dried fruit. To complement the meal, we suggest a good fresh fruit salad for dessert.

title: Gratin of chopped green beans
preparation: Clean the peppers and cut them into small dice. Put 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan and sauté the peeled and finely chopped onion until soft. Add the peppers and sauté while stirring for about 2 minutes. Add the grated tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Let it cook for about 15 minutes. Make a paste (picada) with the garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper, and add the remaining oil and the breadcrumbs. Add the green beans and olives to the pan and mix well. Pour everything into a clay dish and cover it with the paste. Place in a preheated oven to gratin until golden.
notes: Given its composition, this dish can be part of anyone's diet, even in slimming or fat-control diets. In these cases, the amount of olives and oil added to the dish can be reduced. A more economical version is to serve them without gratinating, as a stew: add water or vegetable broth in step 7, and let it boil for about 10 minutes. A few minutes before finishing the cooking, add the garlic and oregano paste. It can be accompanied by toasted bread.

title: Roasted goat ribs with warm salad of dried green beans and artichoke with rosemary
preparation: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Season the meat with pepper (and salt, if desired). Place it in the oven along with the head of garlic rubbed with oil. Cook for 20-25 minutes. Meanwhile, steam the artichoke hearts. Peel and sauté the garlic in a pan with oil and chopped rosemary. Add the green beans and the sliced artichokes. Cover and cook over low heat for a few minutes, then stir in the yogurt and mustard. Adjust the pepper (and salt, if desired) and, if necessary, add the cooking water from the artichokes. Slice the ribs and serve them on top of the green bean and artichoke salad. Decorate the dish with fresh rosemary.
notes: This recipe is juicy and original, thanks to the combination of goat with dried green beans and artichokes. Although goat is a red and fatty meat that should not be overconsumed, presenting it with legumes and artichokes is a good way to enrich the dish's content. A light first course (such as a vegetable consommé with julienned vegetables) and fruit for dessert help balance the menu.

title: Fish and Potato Patties
preparation: Peel the potatoes, clean them, and cut them into large cubes. Cook them in cold water and salt until they are soft. Once cooked, drain them well and pass them through a potato masher. Steam the fish for about 8-10 minutes. Remove the skin and bones and crumble the fish. When the puree is ready, mix in the lemon zest and juice, the chopped parsley and garlic, the fish, salt, and pepper. Once cooled, using slightly damp hands, form the patties (hamburger style). Cook them in a non-stick pan with very little oil until they turn golden, or bake them in the oven.
notes: Suggestion: Instead of eel, you can use other types of white fish or even salmon. If you like spicy food, you can add a fresh chili, chopped and without seeds, to the puree. Menu proposal: They can constitute a single dish accompanied by a nice salad and dessert, such as cooked pear with white wine. Another option could be to accompany them with a tomato, carrot, and zucchini sauce and, for dessert, fresh fruit in the form of fruit salad, for example. Dietary comment: Eel is a white fish with a mild flavor and delicate texture, which is why it pairs well with other foods of a more pronounced flavor. It provides high-quality proteins and little fat, and it is a very digestible food. Potatoes provide a variable amount of energy, depending on the quantity consumed and the cooking method. The potato is a tuber rich in carbohydrates and also contains vitamins B and C, as well as various minerals. In this recipe, the potatoes are the main ingredient and will largely determine the nutritional value of the dish. This type of preparation is an attractive alternative for offering fish to children.

title: Crispy lamb with pea puree and mint

ingredients.name: boneless lamb loin chops, in one or two cuts

preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Crush the dry bread with some fresh mint leaves, salt, and pepper. Coat the meat in beaten egg and then in the bread and mint mixture. Bake in the oven for about 20 minutes. Turn off the oven and leave the lamb inside for another 5 minutes. Meanwhile, boil the peas in salted water for about 4-5 minutes. Puree the peas with the fresh cream cheese, a handful of fresh mint, salt, and pepper. Serve the meat cut into slices about 2 cm thick with the pea puree and whole grain bread.
notes: Menu proposal: Mixed lettuce salad, radishes, and spring onion. Crispy breaded lamb with pea puree and mint. Fresh pineapple. Dietary comment: This hearty recipe provides a good dose of the numerous nutrients that the body needs daily. Peas are a source of carbohydrates due to their high starch content. They also contain fiber and folic acid. The lamb meat complements the recipe with proteins and iron. The mint, which provides an original counterpoint with its refreshing flavor, softens the dish, as the lamb, being a fatty food, can be strong and heavy to digest. The balance of the menu is achieved with the salad and fresh fruit, in this case pineapple, which contains vitamins C, B, and A, and various minerals. Since it is a highly proteinaceous dish, it should be accompanied by foods rich in carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, and minerals, such as the mixed lettuce salad, radishes, and spring onion proposed as a starter and the fresh fruit as dessert.

title: Salt-crusted pork loin with apple compote
preparation: In an elongated baking dish with high sides, place a base of salt, put the pork loin on top, and cover it completely making sure it is well compacted (if necessary, moisten the salt with a bit of water). Place it in a preheated oven and let it cook until the salt begins to crack. Break the salt crust and remove the pork loin. Peel the apples and remove the cores, cut them into quarters, and place them in a saucepan over low heat with a finger of water, the lemon zest, and the cinnamon stick. Let them cook until they are very soft. Remove the lemon zest and the cinnamon stick and puree the apples. You can add a bit of nutmeg and pepper. Slice the pork loin into very thin slices and garnish it with the apple compote using a pastry bag.
notes: This is a simple and tasty preparation. Pork is a red meat that should not be overconsumed (it is recommended not to eat it more than 2 times a week). Salt-crust preparation does not require the addition of fat for cooking and allows the pork loin to remain very tender. The apple compote garnish provides a very interesting flavor contrast to the dish, and it is a different way to incorporate seasonal fruits into menus. It is suitable to complete this dish with a first course that provides a good portion of vegetables, as well as containing some food from the starch group, such as rice, pasta, couscous, bread, potato, or even legumes.

title: Lentil and wheat lasagna
preparation: Make a sauté with all the vegetables. Boil the lentils and the whole wheat with a bay leaf, and once cooked and drained, mix them with the sauté and set aside. Using the previously boiled pasta sheets and the lentil and wheat filling, assemble the lasagna, cover it with béchamel and cheese, and gratin it in the oven.
notes: Recipe provided by Ecomenja

title: Escudella i carn d’olla

ingredients.name: pig's foot split in half and pieces of ear, snout and tail
meatball made of minced pork and beef

preparation: Wash all the meats well and submerge them in a large pot with the water (from six to eight liters). As soon as it reaches a boil, skim off the foam that has formed and add the previously soaked chickpeas. When the pot has been boiling for approximately one and a half hours, add all the vegetables, the cleaned and cut potatoes, as well as the meatball and the blood sausage. When everything is cooked, separate the meats to one side of a tray and the vegetables, potatoes, and chickpeas to the other. If you want to degrease the broth, you must let it cool. Upon cooling, the fat will become compacted on the top of the pot. Remove all this fat with a spatula. Bring the broth back to a boil and add the Christmas galets. Before the pasta finishes cooking, add the pine nuts. If you want to add salt, it is advisable to add it towards the end and in a small amount, so the broth does not become too strong. After the first course of broth with Christmas galets, bring the tray with all the ingredients of the broth preparation to the table and serve each person a small portion of each food.
notes: Escudella i carn d’olla is very suitable for cold weather, and you can accompany it with a good salad of escarole, lettuce, celery, or radish which will help to refresh the meal a bit. We recommend not including another dish in this meal (stuffed chicken, stewed meats, or baked fish), as it is quite complete in itself. The energy value of this meal may vary depending on the amount of meat, the fat accompanying the meats, and also the amount of pasta, potatoes, and chickpeas. Degreasing the broth before cooking the pasta lightens it considerably.

title: Langoustines with orange salad
preparation: Place a saucepan with water on the heat and add some peppercorns and bay leaves. When the water boils, add the langoustines, remove them when the water boils again, and let them drain. Peel the oranges, cut them into slices, and arrange them in a circle. Add the black olives, pine nuts, and mix everything. Serve the orange salad in the center of the plate and the langoustines around it (with the antennae slightly trimmed).
notes: This recipe clearly constitutes a main course. The orange salad accompaniment gives it an original touch and is a way to increase fruit consumption; although in our environment it is more common to have it for dessert, it can also be part of starters and main courses. This dish can be completed with a first course containing starches (pasta, rice, other cereals, potato, etc.) or legumes and vegetables.

title: Fish and Pea Pie
preparation: Peel the potatoes and boil them with water and salt (if you have pre-boiled potatoes, you can use them). When the potato is cooked, add the frozen peas to the water, wait for it to boil again, and drain everything. Mash the potato and peas, add oil, grated lemon zest, salt, and pepper, and set aside. Chop the onion and carrot into pieces and cook them in a pan with oil. When the vegetables are browned, add a tablespoon of flour, and once toasted, moisten with the milk (or water) while stirring continuously. Add the shredded fish, a small teaspoon of mustard, and the juice of half a lemon. Add the cheese, stir the mixture, and season to taste. Place this mixture in a deep baking dish and top it with the mashed potato. Gratin the mixture in the oven for about 20 minutes at 160 °C or until the surface is browned.
notes: Source: Agència Catalana de Seguretat Alimentària / Fundació Alícia

title: Rabbit casserole with peas, artichokes, and fennel
preparation: Peel and chop the onion. Grate the tomatoes (or use crushed tomato). Peel the artichokes by removing the outer leaves and trying to leave only the tenderest leaves. Cut off the stalks and about 2-3 cm of the tips. Cut them into wedges and soak them in water and lemon juice. In a casserole with the oil, brown the rabbit seasoned with pepper (and a little salt, if desired). Set it aside, and in the same oil, cook the onion, tomato, and wine for about 10 minutes over low heat. Add the rabbit and a glass of water, and let it cook for about 15-20 minutes. Add the artichokes, peas, fennel, and bay leaf, and cook everything for about 8-10 more minutes.
notes: Menu suggestion: Pumpkin cream, Rabbit casserole with peas, artichokes and fennel, Orange slices. Dietary comment: Rabbit stands out for being a lean white meat. This recipe incorporates vegetables such as artichokes and fresh legumes such as peas, making it a very complete dish.

title: Ganxet bean with cuttlefish
preparation: In a saucepan with the oil, sauté the chopped onion and grated tomatoes. Add the cleaned cuttlefish cut into thin strips. Cover with water and let it cook until the cuttlefish is tender. Add the beans and cook for about 10 more minutes. Meanwhile, make a picada (paste) with the garlic, parsley, salt, and almond. Add the wine. A few minutes before the cooking is finished, add it to the saucepan.
notes: The ganxet bean is closely linked to various traditional dishes of Catalan cuisine. Although they are often eaten sautéed in a pan with cansalada, with sausage, stewed with a sofrito and cold cuts or meats, in empedrat, etc., they are also used in the form of a puree or to make vegetarian meatballs and burgers.

title: Potatoes with red pepper
preparation: Boil the whole potatoes with the skin on. Peel them and cut them into thick slices. Arrange them on a plate that has been previously heated and rubbed with a raw garlic clove, and season them with a good drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, coarse salt, and a pinch of spicy or sweet red pepper. You can complete the dish with some watercress, lettuce, escarole, or sprouts leaves. You can even turn it into a good main course if you add some chicken pieces, slices of boiled octopus (the classic Galician-style octopus), or even some bites of marinated meat.
notes: Potatoes are an interesting source of carbohydrates. Boiling them with the skin on ensures better preservation of the nutritional value of the potatoes. Steaming, baking, grilling, or boiling them whole are the most appropriate methods regarding the best preservation of the nutritional value of these tubers. Extra virgin olive oil and red pepper will provide enough flavor and aroma so that salt can be dispensed with if necessary (for people who are recommended to eat with little salt). If you want the preparation not to be too caloric, reduce the amount of potato and give more volume to the base of lettuce, escarole, tender spinach, or sprouts. The combination of potatoes with octopus and red pepper (a typical preparation from Galicia) is very tasty, low in energy (depending on the amount of potato and oil) and also appropriate for people with high cholesterol or diabetes. If you make the preparation with marinated meat, sauté the meat in a pan with a drizzle of oil and add it to the potatoes, but remember that this meat is a bit fattier and, moreover, is already salted and peppered.

title: Chickpea flour, carrot and leek omelet
preparation: Julienne the carrot and the leek, setting aside a portion to decorate the dish. Sauté everything with a drizzle of olive oil (and a bit of salt, if desired). Dice the potato and fry it. Then, add it to the previous vegetables. Mix the chickpea flour, vinegar, rice flour, yeast, and a pinch of salt, and stir it with a whisk. Let it rest for one hour so the yeast can take effect. In a well-heated non-stick pan, add a drizzle of olive oil and cook the omelets just like egg omelets. Using the vegetables we set aside earlier, make a flour tempura: cut them into somewhat large pieces, coat them in flour, and fry them in very hot oil. Plate the flour omelet and decorate with the vegetable tempura.
notes: Chickpea flour has the same nutritional composition as dried legumes, so it provides a very interesting protein contribution. This recipe helps increase legume consumption with a different presentation. It can serve as a main course, just like an egg omelet, and in this case, it is also accompanied by a significant portion of vegetables.

title: Chickpea casserole with curry
preparation: Cook the onion, peeled and finely chopped, in a clay pot with the oil until it softens. Add the cleaned and finely sliced celery, the diced potatoes, and the curry (and a bit of salt, if desired). Let it cook for about 5 minutes. Add the chickpeas, the broth, and the olives, and cook for another 5-8 minutes. Serve in individual ramekins decorated with chopped parsley.
notes: The base of this dish is legumes and vegetables, making it very healthy and nutritious. It can be served as a main course, for example, with some toasted country bread triangles. If accompanied by a salad as a first course and some fresh fruit-based desserts, it can result in a very complete and balanced menu.

title: Vegetable stew with tofu
preparation: Peel and cut the onions into large chunks. Clean the leek, remove the outer layer, clean it, and cut it into slices about 2 cm thick. Peel and clean the carrots and turnips and cut them into slices 1 cm thick. Trim the artichokes by removing the outer leaves, trying to leave only the tender ones. Cut off the stalks and about 2-3 cm of the tips. Cut them into about 8 pieces and soak them in water and lemon juice. Clean the mushrooms and cut them into quarters or eighths, depending on the size. Cut the tofu into cubes about 2 cm. In a pan with oil, cook the onion, leek, carrots, and turnip for about 5 minutes, with the pan covered and stirring occasionally. Add the mushrooms, tofu, herbs, and a bit of salt, if desired, and let cook for another 5 minutes. Add a finger of water to the pan, cover it, and let it cook for about 10 minutes over low heat. Add the artichokes and peas and let cook until tender, about 7 minutes. Meanwhile, make a picada (paste) with the almonds, garlic, and bread. Add the picada to the pan along with the soy sauce. Stir and remove from heat. Let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
notes: Vegetable stew with tofu usually constitutes a second course, as the way it is presented makes it more typical to eat after a starter (preferably with carbohydrates, such as pasta, rice, potato, or other less known cereals such as millet, couscous, quinoa, or bulgur). Tofu, being a soy derivative, provides protein to the dish; the vegetables provide vitamins, minerals, and fiber, as well as the almonds which also provide cardio-healthy fats. As suggested, to complete the meal it can be accompanied by baked potato or a mound of rice, and a piece of fruit for dessert. Tofu is a soy-derived food that looks like fresh cheese. It can be made at home, but it is easy to find in any shop. It is obtained after soaking the soybeans, boiling them, crushing them, filtering them, curdling the resulting liquid, and pressing it. Since it is quite bland, cooking it with other foods (vegetables, sauces, spices, etc.) significantly improves the taste. For sandwiches or salads, it can be marinated with spices, herbs, garlic, tamari (soy sauce), ginger, oil, etc.

title: Calçots fritters (Bunyols de calçots)

ingredients.name: chickpea flour or corn flour (suitable for people with celiac disease)

preparation: Place a saucepan over heat with the milk. When it reaches a boil, remove from heat and add the oil, flour, paprika, and mushroom meat all at once. Using a spatula, mix well until you achieve a thick, cohesive dough that separates from the sides of the pan and the spatula. Let the dough cool down, then add the eggs one by one. The mixture should have the consistency of a very thick pastry cream. Clean the calçots that have already been grilled or baked. Remove the green part and slice the white part into thin rounds. Once prepared, add them to the reserved dough. Heat a frying pan (or ideally a pot) with abundant extra virgin olive oil. When the oil is hot (but not smoking), use a spoon to take portions of the dough and fry the fritters until golden brown. Remove and place on absorbent paper to remove excess oil. They can be served accompanied by romesco sauce.
notes: Recipe by Josep Martín. Restaurant “El Palau Vell” (Sant Andreu de la Barca). This recipe offers a new way to eat calçots, different from the traditional method and well-adapted to home cooking possibilities. Increasing vegetable consumption, one of the objectives of the International Year of Fruits and Vegetables, requires incorporating new vegetables and different ways of cooking them into our daily lives. Calçots fritters can serve as a very complete second course, since in addition to the vegetable content of the calçots themselves, the milk, eggs, and flour (especially if it is chickpea flour) provide a very interesting protein contribution. The fritters can be accompanied by a nice salad or with some artichokes baked in the oven, taking advantage of the calçots cooking.

title: Eggs in sauce with peas
preparation: Clean and grate the tomatoes. Cook the peas in boiling salted water for about 7 minutes. In a saucepan with oil, sauté the chopped spring onions until they begin to brown. Add the peas, tomato, salt, and pepper, and cook everything for about 10 minutes. Divide the preparation into four small ovenproof dishes. Add one egg white to each dish and bake in a preheated oven at 190 °C until set, for about 3-4 minutes. Add the yolk and let it cook for about 2 more minutes.
notes: This recipe, with eggs as the central ingredient, can become a very complete and simple main course to prepare. Its richness in proteins is determined by the eggs and the legumes (peas), which are accompanied by two vegetables typical of sautés, tomatoes and spring onions, which provide a significant amount of antioxidant compounds. To form a balanced meal, one could introduce a first course rich in carbohydrates (pasta, rice, potato, couscous, quinoa, millet, etc.) and a salad.

title: Rabbit in vinaigrette

ingredients.name: medium rabbit, cut into small pieces

preparation: Place a good amount of oil in a pot, preferably earthenware, and sauté the peeled and sliced garlic over low heat. Remove them from the oil once they are well golden and set them aside. In the same oil, brown the chopped rabbit until it is well browned. Remove it and wait a few moments until the oil temperature drops. Add a small glass (coffee cup size) of balsamic vinegar. Crush the garlic in a mortar and reduce it to a puree. Add them to the vinaigrette and incorporate the rabbit and the handful of aromatic herbs. If necessary, add a small glass of broth. Let it cook for about six to ten minutes over very low heat so that everything mixes well. Serve with a garnish of endive and pomegranate.
notes: Rabbit is a lean meat with low fat content and a high protein contribution, similar to chicken. To complement this dish, we suggest pairing it with a first course of gratin onion soup. For dessert, some orange slices with walnuts and a sliver of dark chocolate!

title: Broad beans with squid and mint aroma
preparation: Clean the squid and cut them into equal pieces. Peel the spring onions and garlic, and chop them. Pour a drizzle of oil into a saucepan and sauté the onion and garlic over low heat. Add the squid and, if desired, a bit of salt, and cook over low heat. Incorporate the aromatic herbs and the broad beans, reserving some mint leaves for decoration. Stir and add the liqueur. Add a little water and cover the saucepan. Cook for about 10-15 minutes, depending on the size and tenderness of the broad beans. Serve hot, with the mint leaves on top.
