notes: Stewed broad beans are an ideal spring dish. Their combination with squid offers a very tasty dish, which can be considered a main course. It could be complemented with a side salad. It is a preparation that might require a piece of bread to dip and leave nothing on the plate!

title: Roasted chicken stuffed with fruit

ingredients.name: bay leaves, salt and black pepper

preparation: Clean the inside of the chicken and season it with salt and pepper inside and out. Macerate the prunes, apricot halves, raisins, apple (peeled and diced), and pine nuts with the muscat wine in a bowl. Also add the onion sliced into thin rings, the bay leaves, and the cinnamon stick. Let it macerate for at least two hours. After this time, stuff the chicken with the drained macerated fruit mixture and reserve the rest of the muscat wine. To keep the stuffing inside the chicken, sew the cavity with thread and a needle. Arrange it in an oven-safe dish that you have previously preheated. Gradually pour the juices released during cooking and the muscat wine reserved from the fruit maceration over the chicken. Depending on the size of the chicken, the cooking time varies between one and a half and two hours. Serve the whole chicken (without the closure) at the table.
notes: Chicken is one of the leanest meats, meaning it has a lower fat content and a protein value similar to other meats. For this stuffed chicken, we recommend serving portions smaller than a quarter: fillet it into smaller pieces and accompany them with the sweet stuffing. To complement the chicken, we suggest a side dish of endive and green leaves with orange, well dressed with oil and vinegar reduction, which turns out very light and refreshing. This chicken recipe is very mild and suitable for young and old alike.

title: Cuttlefish Stew with Tarragon
preparation: Peel the onion and chop it finely. Peel and dice the carrots. In a clay pot, cook the onion with the oil. When the onion is transparent, add the whole garlic cloves, the carrots, and the cuttlefish. Let it cook for about 5 minutes over high heat. Immediately after, add the wine and the grated tomatoes, and season with salt and pepper. Cover and let it cook over low heat for about 20 minutes. Peel and dice the potatoes. After 15 minutes, add the potatoes, peas, tarragon, and hot water to the pot, making sure it is half covered. Let it cook for another 15-20 minutes. Adjust the salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Menu suggestion: Green bean salad with tomato and a hint of garlic. Cuttlefish stew with tarragon. A glass of seasonal fruit with vanilla-flavored yogurt. Dietary comment: Cuttlefish is a low-fat seafood, but rich in high biological quality proteins, iron, magnesium, sodium, phosphorus, and B, A, and E vitamins. The vegetables, which do not increase the caloric value of the dish, provide a variety of colors to the recipe, as well as vitamins and minerals. The potatoes complement it with carbohydrates. Tarragon is digestive and carminative. The preparation method combines perfectly with the cuttlefish and offers a very flavorful and juicy dish, suitable for all age groups. A very light dish, and fruit as a dessert is sufficient to complete the menu.

title: Tuna with mustard with tomato and ricotta garnish
preparation: Put a few drops of oil in a pan and when it is well heated, cook the tuna fillet previously spread with mustard on both sides. Cook it quickly so that it does not get overcooked, so that it turns out very juicy. Cut the tomato into two thick slices and season it with salt and a drizzle of oil. Also add a pinch of rosemary leaves previously crushed in a coffee grinder. Place the fresh or ricotta cheese on top of the tomato and season it also with salt, crushed rosemary and a few drops of olive oil. Serve everything on a large plate: the tuna fillet with mustard and on the side the tomato and cheese garnish.
notes: Tuna is a blue fish, with an interesting fat content in relation to the prevention of circulatory diseases (polyunsaturated fatty acids rich in omega 3). It has a very quick preparation that does not require much additional fat and, moreover, the garnish is very fresh, rich in fiber (provided by the tomato) and with a very Mediterranean aroma. If you want to reduce salt consumption, you can perfectly substitute the salt and significantly increase the rosemary.

title: Chicken with samfaina
preparation: Cut the chicken into large cubes. Clean the bell peppers and the eggplant and cut them into cubes. Peel the garlic and slice them into thin strips. Place the garlic to cook in a clay pot with oil and when they begin to color, add the chicken. Cook it covered and over low heat for about 15 minutes. Add the bell peppers and the bay leaf and let it cook for 2 minutes. Add the eggplant, the grated tomatoes, the wine, the salt, and the pepper. Cook it uncovered, stirring occasionally until the eggplant is tender. You can adjust the salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Chicken, being a type of meat with a soft texture and delicate flavor, is one of the most consumed and accepted by the population. It is rich in excellent quality proteins and contains little fat. Chicken breast, especially, is one of the parts cooked most frequently and its mild flavor allows for very diverse accompaniments. In this dish, samfaina is a way to incorporate vegetables as a side dish in main courses, thus enriching the diet with minerals, vitamins, antioxidants, and fiber. It results in a dish suitable for all ages.

title: Turkey breast fillets with spicy peach sauce

ingredients.name: ripe and firm peaches (yellow or nectarines)

preparation: Dice the peaches into very small cubes. Peel the onions, clean them, and slice them into very thin rings. In a small bowl, mix the peach, onion, rosemary, chopped chili, lemon juice, 2-3 tablespoons of oil, pepper and, if desired, a bit of salt. Season the fillets with pepper and, if desired, a bit of salt. Cook them on a heated griddle coated with oil, 2-3 minutes per side. Arrange the fillets on a plate or in a dish topped with the prepared sauce. It can be served immediately or cold.
notes: Turkey is a white and lean meat that, along with chicken and rabbit, can be part of our menus a couple of times a week. In this case, thanks to the sauce that accompanies them, featuring summer seasonal fruits, it results in an original, light, and very refreshing dish. The fillets could be complemented with a side of rice, pasta, potato, or legumes, perhaps also with an escalivada, and plan a first course with a soup or cold cream or a good salad.

title: Leftover style Swiss chard, spring onions and prawns
preparation: Wash and cut the swiss chard and spring onions into chunks. Place them in a thick-bottomed pan and cook them over low heat, with two or three tablespoons of water. Cover them. When the water has almost evaporated and the chard and onions begin to become quite tender, add the prawn tails, stir everything, cover, and let cook for a couple of minutes. When the prawns are half-cooked, add black pepper (and a bit of salt, if desired), stir, and uncover. Immediately after, add a drizzle of olive oil and stir carefully. Beat an egg and add it to the pan. Cook over low heat stirring with a wooden spoon until the egg has set. Serve on a plate, garnished with a slice of toasted sourdough bread cut into two triangles and some julivert leaves.
notes: On this occasion, we present a recipe with egg. This food, which in recent years has fallen into a certain discredit, besides offering many gastronomic possibilities and being well accepted by all age groups, has a very notable nutritional quality. Its protein content makes it an excellent substitute for meat and fish. Accompanying egg preparations with vegetables such as swiss chard and spring onions is a very typical tradition of the Mediterranean diet, and allows one to complete the daily intake of this very healthy food group.

title: Lentils with rice and mushrooms
preparation: Soak the lentils for at least 6 hours. Once soaked, pour them into a pot with the celery, bay leaf, leek, and carrot, peeled, cleaned, and cut into large pieces. Cover with water (double or triple the volume of water compared to the lentils) and, when it starts to boil, lower the heat so the boil is gentle. Stir occasionally. After one hour, separate the leek, celery, and carrot and blend them. Then, return the vegetable puree to the pot. Add the rice and let it boil gently for 15-20 minutes (depending on the type of rice). In a pan, sauté the cleaned mushrooms with oil. Add the minced garlic and chives. Stir and set aside. When the rice is cooked, add the mushrooms and a bit of salt, if desired. Decorate the dish with some crispy fried chive leaves.
notes: This dish can serve as a main course that can be accompanied by an autumn salad, a cream, or a vegetable broth. The combination of lentils with rice is an excellent option to obtain a balanced, flavorful, and very versatile dish. Depending on the vegetables and spices added, it can be adapted to all seasons: warm in winter and cold in spring or summer. To complete the meal, seasonal fruits such as tangerine, pear, apple, fig, grapes... can be served.

title: Roasted pork loin with orange and pine nuts

ingredients.name: pine nuts (instead of pine nuts, chopped or sliced almonds or hazelnuts can be used)
different types of salad leaves (arugula, watercress, endive, oak leaf)

preparation: Season the loin with salt and pepper and brown it in a pan. Preheat the oven to 180 °C, place the loin in a baking tray and drizzle it with a little oil. Bake it for approximately 20 minutes. In a 250-300 ml glass, prepare a mixture with the juice of one orange, two fingers of muscatel and two fingers of water. Add the pine nuts (or your preferred nuts) so they can macerate. Turn the loin and pour the mixture from the glass over it. Bake for another 20 minutes, continuously moistening the meat with its own juices. Cut some very thin slices of orange and 10 minutes before finishing the cooking, place them on top of the meat. Slice the meat into thin slices. Serve it with the orange and pine nut sauce from the tray and garnish the dish with the salad leaf mixture.
notes: This recipe is a flavorful, easy-to-prepare, and original second course, thanks to the use of orange as an ingredient. Loin is a lean piece of pork meat, a red meat that is recommended to be consumed at most twice a week. The salad leaf garnish helps to incorporate vegetables into the menu. It is recommended to accompany this dish with a first course consisting of a combination of carbohydrates (rice, pasta, legumes, or potato) and vegetables. For dessert, seasonal fresh fruit is recommended.

title: Assorted seafood skewers

ingredients.name: green olives stuffed with anchovy or pepper

preparation: Clean the octopus well and boil them for about twenty minutes in salted water. Drain and cool them. Fill each one with an olive and skewer them, alternating with another olive until the skewer is full. Place it on a tray, season with salt, chopped parsley, and olive oil, and let it marinate until serving time. Separately, clean the mussels well and open them over high heat in a covered pan. Separate the shells and skewer them, alternating with a black olive and a tomato. Season them as with the previous skewer and place them on the tray. To prepare the cuttlefish skewers, first finely chop the bread crumbs, add the parsley and the finely minced garlic, and season slightly. Add the beaten egg so that a very compact dough is formed, which you will use to fill the cuttlefish. Then thread them onto the skewers, alternating with pieces of green and red pepper. Drizzle them with a little oil and pass them over a very hot griddle.
notes: You can also cook the skewers with other types of seafood or fish. Fish requires little cooking time, so it is advisable to cook the food "al dente" to avoid burning it, to maximize nutrient intake, and to respect its organoleptic properties (flavor, aroma, texture, color). Nutritionally, you can consider this preparation rich in high-quality proteins, minerals, vitamins, and fiber. It can be a perfect main course after a good varied salad to which you can add some cubes of seasonal fruit (orange, apple, pineapple, kiwi, among others), a bit of rice, slices of boiled potato, lentils, or pasta (fusilli, lasagna). It is a very low-fat and low-calorie proposal, therefore appropriate for situations in which you must control fat consumption and also for slimming diets. It is also very appropriate for people with diabetes, as this dish does not provide carbohydrates unless you add them to the side dish. If you have to restrict salt intake, simply do not add any and replace the olives with some vegetable to reduce sodium.

title: Red bean burgers

ingredients.name: black pepper and cumin to taste

preparation: Grate the carrots, chop the garlic, and finely slice the onion. Puree the beans and mix them with the rest of the ingredients. Form about 12 burgers and coat them with breadcrumbs. Fry them in a non-stick pan or bake them in the oven.
notes: Suggestion: They can be accompanied by a carrot, leek, and thyme sauce. Dietary comment: Red beans, like other legumes, share a high concentration of nutrients. The recipe has the advantage of being very economical and nutritious, as it stands out for its low fat content, mainly due to the olive oil. Complex carbohydrates are the most abundant nutrient, followed by proteins, which improve in quality if combined with cereals (in this case, pasta in the salad). It is also a dish rich in fiber. If these burgers are preceded by a salad of pasta and vegetables accompanied by a fruit for dessert, a balanced, complete, and very healthy menu is obtained.

title: Salmon supremes with green olive crust and fresh herbs

ingredients.name: chopped fresh herbs (parsley, chives, fennel, tarragon)

preparation: Clean the herbs well. Crush the olives with the herbs, salt, and pepper. Add the olive oil and breadcrumbs until a paste is obtained. Spread this paste over the salmon, on the skinless side. Heat the pan, and place the salmon with the skin touching the pan. Cook over high heat until the salmon is almost cooked, until the color has changed in 2/3 parts. Finish cooking in the oven broiler for about 5 more minutes.
notes: Menu proposal: Leek and pumpkin cream. Salmon supremes with green olive crust and fresh herbs, accompanied by sautéed tagliatelle with olive oil and garlic. Fresh fruit skewer. Dietary comment: The combination of ingredients makes this simple recipe an exquisite dish. The carefully selected seasonal foods and easy preparation make the menu an example of tasty and balanced choice. Salmon is a blue fish rich in polyunsaturated fat, high biological value proteins, and iron. The seasoning with olives and herbs and the pasta garnish (rich in carbohydrates) offer a contrast of flavors and textures and improve the presentation of the dish. This recipe meets the requirements of a very healthy menu due to its fat profile, in which the unsaturated fats of the salmon and olives predominate. In addition, the first course provides regulatory nutrients (fiber, minerals, and vitamins).

title: Red kidney bean gratin
preparation: Dice the eggplant and leave it in water with salt for about 10 minutes, then drain and dry. Clean the pepper, remove the seeds, and cut it into fine strips. Cook the peeled and finely chopped onion in a saucepan with 4 tablespoons of oil for 5 minutes. Add the pepper and minced garlic, and let it cook covered for about 5 minutes. Grate about 200 g of tomato and add it to the saucepan along with the eggplant, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper, and let it cook uncovered for about 10 more minutes. Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Add the beans to the saucepan and place the whole mixture into an ovenproof dish. Slice the remaining tomatoes and place them on top. Season with pepper and brush with the remaining oil. Bake in the oven at 180 °C for 40-45 minutes. Remove the dish from the oven, sprinkle with parmesan, and bake for about 10 more minutes.
notes: The dish we propose can constitute a main course due to its protein content from the legume and cheese, which improves the protein quality of the beans. It can be considered that the side dish for the main course is integrated, as it incorporates a significant amount of vegetables. Due to the ingredients, especially the legumes and vegetables, it is a dish very rich in fiber, as well as in minerals such as calcium, enhanced by the presence of cheese. The olive oil, oregano, and cumin add a very Mediterranean touch to the recipe. A main course so substantial and rich in key nutrients only needs a light first course to serve as an appetizer (vegetable cream, salad, broth or consommé, etc.) and a piece of fruit for dessert.

title: Chicken stew with red wine

ingredients.name: chicken cut into eighths and skinless

preparation: Peel and cut the onions into quarters. Clean the tomatoes and cut them into quarters. Peel the head of garlic and cut off the tips of the cloves, taking care not to separate them. In a clay pot, place the chicken pieces, onions, tomatoes, head of garlic, oil, and bay leaves. Season with salt and pepper and pour in the wine until everything is covered. Cover, leaving a 1 cm opening so that the steam can escape. Cook over low heat for one hour.
notes: Menu suggestion: Tagliatelle with asparagus and mushrooms. Chicken stew with red wine. Raw pear balls dipped in vanilla pear compote. Dietary comment: Since chicken has a mild flavor, it is one of the most consumed and appreciated meats. This meat is valued for being a good source of protein and for being lean, with little fat. The wings, being covered in skin, are the parts of the chicken that contain the most fat; therefore, they are the least recommended parts.

title: Cod and spinach paella

ingredients.name: desalted cod loin, skinless and boneless

preparation: Clean the spinach and cut it into large pieces. Clean the cauliflower and cut it into florets. Cut the cod into cubes. Cook the peeled and finely chopped onion in a saucepan with 2 tablespoons of hot oil for about 5 minutes. Add the grated tomato, cover, and let cook for about 5 more minutes. After this time, add the spinach, cauliflower, cod, red pepper, pepper (and a little salt, if desired), and let cook for 5 more minutes. Add double the volume of hot water relative to the amount of rice. In a paella pan, sauté the rice with two tablespoons of oil, season with pepper and red pepper (and a little salt, if desired), and stir for a few minutes. Add the broth with the vegetables and the cod. Let cook for about 15-20 minutes, until the rice is cooked.
notes: Rice is a cereal that accepts the combination of flavors from many different foods, such as spinach and cod in this case. Due to the combination of ingredients, it constitutes a complete and balanced dish: the carbohydrates from the rice, the proteins from the cod, and the fat from the olive oil. The vegetables enrich the dish with nuances of flavor, texture, and color, in addition to vitamins, minerals, and fiber. If a salad is added as a starter and a portion of fruit as dessert, the menu is complete. Menu proposal: Lamb's lettuce, beetroot, and grated carrot salad. Cod and spinach paella. Baked apples with pears and pine nuts.

title: Strawberry, curd cheese and fig skewers
preparation: Cut the curd cheese into cubes and the strawberries in half. Take a skewer and pierce half a strawberry, a fig leaf, and a cube of curd cheese. Repeat the process until all skewers are filled. Before serving, add a few drops of sherry vinegar over the curd cheese and a few drops of cava vinegar.
notes: This simple and easy recipe is an original way to eat fresh fruit for dessert. Although it is a simple preparation, it turns out very elegant and cheerful due to the presentation with a variety of colors and textures. The strawberry provides fiber, vitamins, minerals, and other beneficial compounds for health, the curd cheese enriches the dish with nutrients such as calcium and proteins, and the fig adds color and an intense aroma. As the seasons change, the fruits can be varied according to the most seasonal and local production.

title: Pine nut panellets
preparation: Main dough: Boil the sweet potatoes or potatoes. In a bowl, mix the sugar, almonds, sweet potato or potato, egg yolks, and tartaric acid. Work the dough until it is homogeneous. Let it rest for 12 hours. Shape the panellets: Use a tablespoon to take some dough. Form small balls with clean hands. Roll the balls in the pine nuts until covered. Beat the egg. Using a pastry brush, coat the panellets with the egg and place them on a tray to go into the oven. Preheat the oven to 180ºC. Place the panellets in the oven and bake for 15 minutes. You can make panellets of different flavors by adding different ingredients to the dough, such as coffee, jam, cocoa, etc.
notes: We are facing traditional sweet desserts for the All Saints' Day festival, made mostly from nuts, sugar, and sweet potato. Sweet potato is a very useful sweet tuber for making sweet desserts like this one. The base of sweet potato, nuts, and sugar makes for very energetic desserts that should be eaten in moderation. They are usually eaten as a snack/supper accompanied by sweet wine!

title: Mandarin, pomegranate and yogurt cup
preparation: Peel and deseed the pomegranate and the mandarin. Place the mandarin segments and 2 tablespoons of pomegranate in a martini-style glass. Top with the creamy yogurt, add the other tablespoon of pomegranate, drizzle with a stream of honey and garnish with the fresh mint leaves.
notes: These desserts are an original and refreshing way to combine yogurt with autumn fruits. Yogurt is a probiotic, source of calcium, and very easy to digest. Mandarin and pomegranate are fruits especially rich in fiber due to how we eat them. We eat mandarin in segments wrapped in a thin fibrous layer, and we eat pomegranate without removing the inner seeds, which are very fibrous and contain essential fats.

title: Vegetable timbale with a brie heart
preparation: Each vegetable is cooked differently: The peppers and spring onions are roasted (escalivada style). The zucchini and eggplants are sliced and grilled. The leeks are blanched, cooled, and finished on the grill. Assembly: Use a 9cm round mold. First, create a base with eggplant, then a layer of zucchini, place the cheese in the middle, add the spring onion and pepper on the sides, and finally another layer of zucchini with the two leeks on top in the shape of a cross.
notes: This recipe is an original way to eat different vegetables in a single dish. In it, we find five different vegetables cooked in different ways to try to maintain the organoleptic and nutritional qualities of each one. For this reason, the preparation of this recipe is a bit slower, but it makes the final result of the dish ideal. Vegetables are one of the characteristic food groups of the Mediterranean Diet and are characterized by being foods with high water content but low caloric contribution. They are also rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making this dish a little nutritional "bomb" and fundamental for maintaining a balanced diet. Brie cheese is a soft cheese made with raw cow's milk and of French origin. This ingredient nutritionally complements the vegetables in this dish, providing mainly proteins, fats, calcium, and phosphorus, making this dish a good alternative for vegetable intake.

title: Baked false vegetables
preparation: A very simple recipe. Place all the vegetables in a baking tray, season with salt and pepper, add a finger of water, the white wine and the olive oil. Cover the tray with aluminum foil and place it in the oven at 115º for 1 hour and 30 minutes. Keep an eye on the vegetables in case you need to add a little more water. When they are cooked, serve on a plate. No sauce needs to be added, as the vegetables have absorbed all the flavor from the oil and wine.
notes: A very healthy recipe with low calorie content as it is made from a wide variety of vegetables, which provide a high content of vitamins, minerals, and fiber; on the other hand, they also give the dish a variety of colors that make it very visually appealing. By being prepared in the oven covered with aluminum foil, it allows flavors to be maximized and reduces nutritional losses.

title: Green asparagus and walnut tagliatelle with nectarine vinaigrette
preparation: Wash the asparagus and discard the woodiest part. Next, using a vegetable peeler, slice the asparagus into strips until you obtain tagliatelle. Then, place the tagliatelle in a container with very cold water and prepare the vinaigrette. To make the vinaigrette, put the olive oil, white vinegar, and one nectarine in a glass and blend everything until you obtain a smooth sauce. To present the dish, rinse the asparagus tagliatelle well and dress with the nectarine vinaigrette. Finally, place 25g of walnuts and one or two nectarines per plate, and add the flaky salt.
notes: The origin of green asparagus is located near the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Here in Catalonia, Baix Llobregat is one of the main asparagus cultivation areas in the country. Nectarines are a type of peach that comes from two American species that were mixed during cultivation upon arrival in Europe. This is a low-calorie dish rich in folic acid, fiber, and antioxidants. Additionally, walnuts provide plant-based proteins and a considerable amount of fats rich in omega-3 with anti-inflammatory and anticoagulant action, which contributes to lowering blood cholesterol levels. Thanks to the contribution of fruit and vegetables, it is a digestible and refreshing dish perfect for spring and summer.

title: Stuffed pepper with meat and vegetables

ingredients.name: cabernet sauvignon wine (or white cooking wine)

preparation: In a saucepan, fry the garlic cloves without peeling them to aromatize the oil, then set them aside. In the same oil, sauté the ground meat until it changes color. Dice the onion, celery, and half of the red bell pepper (reserve the other half to use as the stuffing). Sauté everything together with the meat. Add the glass of cabernet sauvignon (or white cooking wine), let the alcohol reduce, adjust the salt, and add a bit of oregano and nutmeg. To stuff the pepper, put in a little melting cheese followed by the mixture of meat and vegetables and a little more cheese. Place it in the oven, preheated to 200°C, for approximately 15 minutes. Check that the cheese melts and that the pepper remains al dente to make it easier to present in a volcano shape. Presentation: When plating, place the walnuts around the pepper and on top, along with a bit of oregano and nutmeg powder.
notes: Very good combination of vegetables and meat. This dish provides us with proteins of animal origin (meat) and vitamins, minerals, fiber, and water (vegetables). The final cooking in the oven is one of the most recommended culinary techniques, as it is a fat-free and mild cooking method. This ensures the food maintains all its color, aroma, and nutrients. This dish can perfectly be a first course, a second course, or even a single-course dish. It can be perfectly combined with a second course based on fish or eggs. It can also be complemented with a salad.

title: Vegetable couscous

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables, coriander, turmeric and ginger powder

preparation: Soak the chickpeas with the broth made with one and a half liters of water and the broth ingredients. Once made, strain the vegetables and the chickpeas from the broth. Make the compote: peel the onions, chop them, and sauté them in a pan with olive oil until they turn golden. Add the raisins and 1 tablespoon of honey. Season with salt, add cinnamon, lower the heat, and cover for about 20 minutes. Wash the vegetables to make the couscous: the zucchini, carrot, and turnip. Cut them into large pieces and cook them with water and salt for 15 minutes. Wash the eggplant, dice it, and fry it in a pan with olive oil. Once done, remove the excess oil using absorbent paper towels. Prepare the couscous (or quinoa, or rice,...) according to the package instructions. Once the couscous is ready, mix it with the rest of the ingredients: the vegetables, the compote, and the chickpeas.
notes: This mixture of vegetables, cereals, legumes, and olive oil provides richness in nutrients to this dish, making this recipe a complete and healthy option. Couscous is a cereal prepared from wheat semolina and can be an alternative to rice, pasta, or potato. Being a source of complex carbohydrates, it provides the dish with the energy component necessary to carry out all daily activities. The legumes (chickpeas) also provide carbohydrates, with starch being the most abundant. This food provides an important amount of fiber and folic acid, which is essential for the formation of red and white blood cells. The eggplant and zucchini stand out, being very rich in water and potassium, a mineral necessary for the transmission and generation of the nerve impulse in the brain. The touch of honey and raisins will give a sweet taste to the recipe. Introducing small amounts of dried fruits will enrich your diet with unsaturated fatty acids, which have the capacity to decrease blood cholesterol levels. Thus, with this recipe made from plant-based foods, you achieve the consumption of those basic foods from the Mediterranean eating pattern that protect our health.

title: Vegetable sauté with prawns and a drizzle of mild pepper oil
preparation: To make this preparation, wash the vegetables and roast the pepper. Peel the carrots and cut them into julienne using a mandoline (a tool used to cut vegetables and potatoes into sticks, slices, julienne, or fry-style cuts) or with a knife. Cut the zucchini into julienne as well, without peeling it, as the green part will add a lot of color to the dish. Peel the onion and cut it into julienne. Mix all the raw vegetables and ensure there is a balanced contrast of colors, making sure there isn't more onion than carrot or zucchini. Everything should be in the same proportion. Peel the roasted pepper and remove the seeds. Place it in a container, cover it with oil, and blend it. Season lightly with salt and cool it in the refrigerator. Peel the prawns and set them aside. Next, in a pan or a wok, add a drizzle of olive oil and heat it well. Then, add the seasoned prawn tails and a handful of vegetables and cook over high heat, stirring continuously. Try to keep them at the right cooking point, not overcooked; it is better if they remain crunchy. Place it on a plate and surround it with a little oil, red pepper, and parsley. This is a dish that should be "made and eaten"; therefore, it is better not to cook it in advance (we can have everything cut and kept in the refrigerator before cooking).
notes: Vegetables and legumes are fundamental allies of all healthy diets. Currently, there is scientific evidence regarding the advantages of consuming them when preventing diseases such as obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer. Vegetables and legumes are a source of fiber, which increases the feeling of satiety, in addition to their water and mineral salt content. This is a low-calorie dish, with a fiber contribution and rich in antioxidants and high-quality proteins from the prawns.

title: Escalivada
preparation: First, start by making a good almond wood fire; the embers must be very lively to roast the peppers, which should end up a little crispy. Once the embers have started, place the onions inside without covering them, as the first layers should be allowed to char while the onion cooks inside. To check if they are well cooked, pierce them with a knife, as the time varies depending on the amount of embers and the size of the onions. On the other hand, place a grill over the embers to cook the peppers; the skin must be charred on all sides (the pepper should be roasted, not cooked). Once all the pepper skin is charred, place it on a tray. Next, pierce the eggplant with a knife about 6-7 times, place it on the embers and turn it; once it is soft, remove it and place it on the same tray as the pepper. Finally, peel the onions, peppers, and eggplants. Cut them into strips and serve on a tray with salt (if desired) and extra virgin olive oil. Finish by decorating the dish if desired with some black olives and a hard-boiled egg.
notes: A typical first course for the autumn season in Catalan cuisine, though it can also serve as a side dish for many other courses. The high proportion of vegetables with the moderation of animal product represented by the egg is the essence of the Mediterranean diet that makes it so healthy. If desserts are a portion of fruit, we will provide even more fiber, and if they are a dairy product (mató, curd, yogurt...), we will provide a little more high biological value protein.

title: Roasted Vegetable and Provolone Lasagna
preparation: Cook the lasagna sheet in plenty of salted water. Drain and set aside. Cut the red pepper, eggplant, and zucchini into slices, roughly the same size as the lasagna sheet. Place them in a baking dish with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast until everything takes on color. Blanch the tomato, peel it, and remove the seeds and juice. To assemble the dish, place the lasagna sheet at the base and spread the olive paste over it; top with the tomato and the other vegetables, alternating with a slice of provolone each time, and finish with cheese. Ensure the lasagna sheet does not protrude to prevent it from burning. Gratin it until the cheese melts. Crush the olives with the olive oil until a fine paste is formed.
notes: A dish originating from the Greeks, adapted by the Romans and spread throughout Europe during the expansion of their empire, becoming rooted in British and Italian gastronomy from the 14th century onwards. The cooking method for this dish, oven-roasting, is one of the most recommended techniques as it does not use grease, is very mild, and results in food retaining all its properties, especially flavor and color. Thanks to the vegetables, this recipe provides plenty of water, fiber, vitamins, and minerals. The cheese will add aroma and texture to this dish, in addition to the calcium contribution.

title: Mallorcan Trempó
preparation: Clean all the vegetables. Cut them into small cubes or julienne. Immediately after, add the tuna and a handful of stuffed olives. Once everything is well mixed, place it in the fridge to keep it fresh until serving. Before serving, dress with a good drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a bit of vinegar.
notes: Here is a salad from the Balearic Islands. Trempó Mallorquí, pronounced 'trampó', is a perfect summer alternative that uses fresh, seasonal garden produce, cleaned, cut, and dressed raw with a good drizzle of olive oil. The structure of the dish is given by three vegetables: tomato, green pepper, and sweet onion; from there, every household makes and breaks it with the best of intentions, offering variations that are accepted with generosity, and in this recipe, they include canned tuna and stuffed olives. Trempar means to mix and season so that all the ingredients and aromas combine to create a good mixed salad. If we accompany it with a slice of country bread to soak up the remaining juice, we will taste the essence of the oil, soothe our hunger, and satisfy the palate.

title: Gaspatxo
preparation: Blend the tomato for about 15 seconds in a blender; add the vinegar, oil, and salt. Chop and add the green pepper, red pepper, cucumber, and the slice of bread. Blend everything for 10 minutes. Add water until the desired texture is achieved and blend again for 1 minute. Adjust the salt if necessary.
notes: Gaspatxo is a typical soup from southern Spain, which reflects the tradition of providing foods with significant amounts of water for people working in the fields during the summer, allowing them to better withstand high temperatures in a simple way using cheap, seasonal ingredients. The main ingredient of this dish is tomato, a food that provides significant amounts of fiber, minerals (potassium and phosphorus), vitamins (C, E, provitamin A and B group), and a high content of carotenoids, such as lycopene, a natural pigment that gives the tomato its characteristic red color. All this makes it an important source of antioxidants, substances with a protective function for our organism.

title: Vegetable timbal with goat cheese and romesco
preparation: Cut the zucchini into thick slices. Sauté them on a griddle with a bit of oil and set aside. At the same time, roast the bell pepper, snow peas, and potato. Once cooked, peel them and cut the potato into strips, and make strips with the bell pepper and snow peas. Slice the mushrooms and sauté them in a pan with oil, salt, and pepper. Subsequently, caramelize the onion by cutting it very finely and cooking it over low heat with oil and salt until it takes on some color. Finally, assemble the timbals using a cylindrical ring mold without a base. Form layers, placing the potato at the base. On top of everything, place a round slice of goat cheese and an asparagus spear. Place in the oven to gratin for about 10 minutes, until the cheese is golden. Serve with romesco sauce on top or around it, according to individual taste.
notes: Recipe with a presentation that recalls a Peruvian pastús made from different vegetables, which makes it a colorful dish rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber. The dish is finished with a layer of gratinated goat cheese and an asparagus. Goat cheese tends to have a more citric taste than other cheeses and is richer in fat. As for the asparagus, they are wild plants with low calorie intake, rich in fiber and with low salt content.

title: Artichokes with langoustines

ingredients.name: fish stock (sea bream, sea bass, etc...)

preparation: Place the whole artichokes in the oven unpeeled at 180º for 30 minutes. Make the fish stock using different fish. Prepare a separate sofrito with olive oil, diced tomato, and very finely chopped garlic. In a pan, add four tablespoons of olive oil and once hot, add the peeled langoustines. Next, add the peeled artichokes cut in half and sauté them slightly. Add 150 ml of fish broth and let it reduce. Serve on a plate with a bit of chopped parsley.
notes: Dish made based on artichokes, a vegetable deeply rooted in the Baix Llobregat and Ebro Delta areas and highly appreciated in Mediterranean cuisine. Regarding the nutritional composition of the artichoke, its fiber contribution is highlighted. On the other hand, it contains langoustines, crustaceans especially rich in different essential nutrients, notably their high protein and low fat content. Finally, the recipe is accompanied by a sofrito based on different vegetables, which end up enriching the dish in terms of vitamins and minerals.

title: Seasonal vegetable sauté, escalivada sausage, and black olive and anchovy sauce
preparation: Roast the artichokes and open them by cutting them on the board. Add salt and olive oil, close them, and tie them with a string. Cook in the oven at 170°C. Sweet potatoes are cooked in the oven at 175°C. Slice the eggplants into strips and sear them in a pan on both sides. Blanch the thyme sprigs, peel them, remove the seeds, and cut them into four pieces. Blanch the cauliflower and refresh it in cold water after two minutes. Place all the vegetables inside a silicone "papillote" (putting all the vegetables together), before closing, drizzle with a bit of olive oil, add a pinch of salt, close it, and put it in the oven at 180°C for approximately 10 minutes. Cook the sausage in the oven at 180°C for about 10 minutes. Separately, in a blender, add about 100g of olive oil, one clove of garlic, the anchovies, and the black olives with the pit removed, and blend everything. Assemble the dish with the vegetables as a base, the sausages on top, and finish by seasoning with the olive sauce or garum.
notes: The vegetables in this recipe: artichoke, eggplant, cauliflower, and sweet potato are good sources of vitamins, minerals, and fiber; when combined with olive oil, rich in oleic acid and vitamin E, they make this recipe a very healthy choice. Using garlic is a good way to season because it provides a characteristic aroma to the dish. In oven cooking, the loss of nutrients is small and allows for better preservation of the ingredients' flavor compared to other culinary techniques. Although the sausage has a high content of saturated fats, it is a good source of protein. As it is a first course, it is recommended to include it in small portions to add flavor to the dish. To complete the nutritional profile of the dish, it can be accompanied by cereals, for example, bread. It is an ideal dish for dinners; low in calories and providing one of the 2 recommended vegetable servings per day.

title: Grilled vegetables
preparation: Clean, peel, and slice the vegetables. Place them on a griddle with a little extra virgin olive oil until they are golden brown. Remove them and they are ready to serve, seasoned with a little extra virgin olive oil and salt.
notes: Since this dish is mainly composed of vegetables, it is a healthy option to be consumed frequently as a first course in any season of the year. From a nutritional standpoint, this mixture is fundamentally composed of water, fiber, minerals, and vitamins, ideal for meeting the daily recommendations for vegetable consumption, "two or three times a day". Its content of carotenoids, present in colored vegetables, and potassium, a mineral that helps maintain muscle functionality, is notable. The food used for seasoning is olive oil, an energetic component of the recipe, which with moderate use, provides a very healthy fat for health. To obtain a balanced menu, the meal could be completed with a protein source such as lean meat or fish.

title: Pumpkin cream
preparation: Sauté the garlic and onion with a little oil. Add the previously chopped pumpkin. Let it cook for three minutes and add the broth. Continue cooking for ten more minutes. Blend the mixture and place it over heat until a cream texture is obtained. Once off the heat, add the cream and parmesan. Adjust salt and pepper.
notes: Creams are an easy way to ingest vegetables. In this case, the pumpkin is the main vegetable of the dish; its slight sweetness and orange color make it very suitable for children's meals and comforting for the whole family as a first course in autumn or winter. It is a simple recipe based on the quality of the vegetables, which, when cooked correctly, offer their full original and delicate flavor, enhanced according to preference with pepper or other spices such as nutmeg. The fiber content, indispensable for good intestinal transit, is ensured, as are vitamins and minerals. We recommend that the contribution of dairy in the form of cream and parmesan cheese be done in moderation; finishing the dish with yogurt or kefir can be considered as an alternative.

title: Stuffed Peppers with Meat and Rice
preparation: Initially, place the onion in a pan to fry it, together with the rice and 2 tablespoons of tomato. Next, cut the pepper in half and fill it with the ground meat (without frying it). Then, place everything in a casserole with a bit of water and let it cook. Finally, make the sofrito with the rest of the raw tomato, without the seeds or the skin, and add it to the casserole. You can put it in the oven for about 5-10 minutes so that the entire stuffed pepper finishes cooking.
notes: The red pepper is native to Mexico, Bolivia, and Peru. It was introduced to Europe in 1493, and currently, pepper production in Spain is centered in the Murcia and Almeria regions. As for rice, its origin dates back more than 7,000 years to Asia. Muslims introduced it to our country, and the region with the most production currently in Catalonia is Terres de l'Ebre. The red pepper is a vegetable that mainly contains water, carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, especially folic acid, vitamin C, and beta-carotene (lycopene), and minerals such as potassium, which confer antioxidant properties and benefits for cardiovascular health. Rice is a cereal with a high content of easily digestible and absorbable carbohydrates and a moderate fiber content if consumed whole grain. This is a typical summer dish, easy to prepare and original, which at the same time makes it a very complete nutritious dish, typical of the Mediterranean, with a high presence of plant-based foods and a moderate presence of animal-based products. This dish can serve very well as a main course or as a second course after a salad.

title: Apple and gorgonzola omelet
preparation: In a non-stick pan, sauté the apple -peeled and cut into fine slices- with a bit of olive oil. Add the cheese and, over low heat, let it melt. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, add the apple and cheese, and make the omelet to your liking.
notes: This main course is very rich in different nutrients, all of them essential for a good dietary balance. Eggs are a very good source of protein and very good value, the apple provides us with fiber and carbohydrates, though we lose vitamins during cooking. With gorgonzola cheese we will obtain calcium, a very important mineral, especially for the formation and maintenance of our bones, in addition to the characteristic aroma of this strong-tasting blue cheese.

title: Roasted Rabbit
preparation: In a saucepan with oil, brown the chopped and seasoned rabbit. Add the herbs and the onions (2 chopped and 5 whole). Once the rabbit and onion are browned, add the tomatoes (2 chopped and 5 whole). Stir and add the rancio wine. Let it cook gradually until the rabbit is tender. Add water bit by bit, preventing it from running dry. Once the rabbit is tender, remove the pieces and place them in another saucepan along with the onions and the whole tomatoes. Pass the remaining sauce through a chinois strainer. For each diner, serve 3 pieces of rabbit, with one onion and one tomato.
notes: The protagonist of this dish is the rabbit. This is a lean meat, with low fat content compared to other meats such as veal, lamb, or pork. Therefore, its cooking must be carefully managed, as it easily dries out and becomes tough. It is a game meat, rich in proteins and B group vitamins. The presence of vegetables completes the dish, providing color, taste, and aroma, as well as fiber and some vitamins and minerals. The dish can be accompanied by boiled rice, to be mixed with the sauce, or with potatoes to make it an excellent ethnic dish.

title: Beef Tagine with Prunes
preparation: Soak the prunes in hot water. Cut the meat into small pieces, chop the garlic and the onion, and place everything in an earthenware casserole with the oil and salt. Cook the meat over low heat and stir it occasionally. Add the lemon, parsley, black pepper, ginger, half of the cinnamon, and the saffron, stir it a little more, then cover it with cold water, cover it, and let it cook over low heat until tender (approximately one hour and fifteen minutes). Remove a little of the broth and set it aside. Drain the prunes and heat them in the reserved broth, adding the rest of the cinnamon and the three tablespoons of sugar. Presentation: In a tagine (a typical Moroccan earthenware pot), place the meat with the prunes and decorate with sesame.
notes: The tagine, also called tayán or tajine depending on the French pronunciation, is a typical dish of Moroccan cuisine that takes its name from the utensil used to prepare it. It is one of the favorites in the Maghreb and therefore in Mediterranean cuisine, as its ingredients, although with various combination possibilities, respond perfectly to the dietary pattern that defines the Mediterranean diet. A very aromatic dish that contains many foods: meat, vegetables, and fruits, in addition to spices and aromatic herbs. Beef is a red meat, rich in iron and proteins. Prunes have laxative properties and constitute a good source of energy. It is a very complete main course, which can be combined with a light first course such as a salad or escalivada.

title: Seaside Lasagna with Fresh Cheese and Olive Dressing

ingredients.name: very thin slices of green tomato

preparation: First, boil the cannelloni pasta al dente. Place it in a bowl with cold water. Add a drizzle of olive oil so it doesn't stick. Begin assembling the lasagna in layers of ingredients: At the base, cannelloni pasta. Over the pasta, thin slices of green tomato. Over the tomato, corn. Over the corn, the tuna. Over the tuna, a slice of fresh cheese. Over the cheese, 4 pickled pilchard fillets. On top, another cannelloni pasta sheet. To finish, simply pour the black olive vinaigrette over it. Place the 5 ingredients into a blender and blend them all together. The vinaigrette is now ready.
notes: It is a very suitable dish for summer, refreshing and easy to make. Nutritionally, it is worth noting the contribution of polyunsaturated fatty acids through the blue fish in the recipe: the tuna and the pilchards. Very healthy fats with cardiovascular protective effects. The green tomato and the corn help to add color to the dish, in addition to their contribution of fiber, vitamins, water, and minerals. Light contribution of complex carbohydrates through the cannelloni pasta and the corn. Final touch of olive dressing with a contribution of color and more healthy fats, in this case monounsaturated fatty acids, also with cardiovascular protective effects. Accompanied by a salad, it can be a very practical single dish during hot periods.

title: Crispy Chanterelle and Chive Ravioli with Orange Reduction and Muscovado Sugar
preparation: Sauté the chanterelles without garlic and let them cool. Once cold, add the chives to them. Separately, cut the filo pastry into five by five centimeter squares. Place the chanterelles in the center and tie it up like a small parcel. Next, place them in the oven for approximately fifteen minutes at 150°C. Pour the orange syrup over the parcels once they have been removed from the oven. Reduce the orange juice and sugar until a syrup is achieved. To achieve this, mix the juice with the sugar in a saucepan and let it cook over low heat, watching carefully that it does not burn, until a liquid texture is obtained.
notes: Ravioli, a classic within the group of stuffed Italian pastas. It seems that the original recipe, from the mid-12th century, featured a mixture of fresh cheese like ricotta and leaves flavored with different spices. In this recipe, however, the cook explains how to prepare a vegetarian filling with a fundamental ingredient: chanterelles (Cantharellus Cibarius); highly appreciated mushrooms in Catalonia, yellow and funnel-shaped, that appear like spots of light amidst the dark earth of shady forested areas. Their flesh is compact, with a mild and pleasant scent, fine and fragrant, reminiscent of fruits like apricot or plum. On the other hand, the pre-made puff pastry made of wheat flour may contain olive oil or lard, egg, and salt, so it is advisable to read the product label. Parsley, garlic, or pepper often used to season mushrooms are replaced in this dish by delicate chives, also known as chives (ciboulette), which provide a subtle aroma that adds a touch of originality pairing well with the orange juice reduction. Complex carbohydrates from the pasta, and fiber, vitamins, and minerals from the mushrooms, healthy vegetable fats from the olive oil, and a touch of added sugar from the brown cane sugar (muscovado), make these ravioli an elegant first course.

title: Mashed potatoes with black blood sausage and mushrooms

ingredients.name: garlic and parsley pound (with a bit of salt and pepper)

preparation: In a pan, sauté the mushrooms with olive oil and the garlic and parsley pound. They should take on a golden color and a soft texture; do not cook them over very high heat. Once done, set them aside along with the garlic and parsley pound. Cook the potatoes with little water and a bit of salt. Set them aside. In a pan, add a bit of olive oil and fry the cansalada until well cooked. Place the cansalada on paper towel to remove excess oil. Cut it into strips and set aside. In the same pan used to fry the cansalada, fry the blood sausage, adding a little olive oil if necessary; if there is still enough leftover oil from the cansalada in the pan, do not add more. Once cooked, cut it into small pieces until it is crumbled and broken down. Take the potatoes, cut them into pieces, and mash them with the help of a fork. Add the cansalada, the crumbled blood sausage, and the mushrooms with the garlic and parsley. Mix everything well until a homogeneous mixture is achieved. Lightly sauté it in the pan previously used for the cansalada and the blood sausage until the surface is golden; this golden surface can also be achieved with a touch in the oven. Before serving, drizzle a thin line of olive oil over the top.
notes: A characteristic autumn dish because it contains fredolics, a type of mushroom very typical during this time of year. The most notable part of this recipe is the potato, which besides being the base of this recipe, is a good source of carbohydrates. In recent times, potato consumption has decreased in Spain, so it is good not to forget dishes like this one. This dish can be a good option to reach the daily serving numbers for this food group. On the other hand, we have the cansalada and the blood sausage which, besides providing a characteristic flavor to the dish, contribute to increasing the saturated fat content. These foods also contain potassium, which is essential for the functionality of many components of the body. The use of olive oil for frying is more appropriate as it is more resistant than other oils at high temperatures. Also, by adding garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper to the dish, it becomes full of flavor. Since it is a recipe with a high energy content and contains saturated fats, it would be preferable to consume it on holidays.

title: Sun-dried tomato risotto with mascarpone pesto
preparation:
Finely chop the onion and sauté it with a little oil and the bay leaf; when it is golden, add the white wine and let it reduce until all the alcohol has evaporated. Add the rice and finish sautéing everything together for a couple of minutes. Add the boiling broth. Incorporate the sun-dried tomatoes cut into julienne and cook for 13 minutes, adding more broth if necessary. At the end of the cooking and off the heat, add the butter, pesto sauce, and mascarpone and mix it.

The Sauce:
Peel the garlic and chop it very finely. Add the basil leaves, removing the stems if they have any, the pine nuts, and the salt. Chop everything well until it becomes a paste. Place everything in a mixing bowl and add the olive oil. Blend everything with a mixer until a fine and uniform texture is obtained. Then add four tablespoons of warm water to thin it out a bit, otherwise, it will be too dense a paste. Grate the parmesan, add it to the sauce, and mix well.
notes: Typical Italian dish, risottos are characterized, mainly, by being a source of complex carbohydrates, which are classified in the cereal group, which should be ingested approximately five times a day. The rice used is arborio, a variety with a high starch content indicated for preparing this dish. This type of rice is characterized by absorbing a lot of liquid during cooking, without becoming mushy, providing a very creamy texture to the dishes. Pesto sauce, based on extra virgin olive oil, pine nuts, parmesan cheese, and basil, is a flavorful concentrate of micronutrients and energy. Along with the tomato, this sauce, in addition to enriching the dish with vitamins and minerals, will confer an attractive coloring based on greens and reds. The creaminess of the risotto comes from the mascarpone cheese, a typical Italian food and the main source of calcium in this dish, as well as saturated fats, the intake of which should be moderated in the diet. This dish, due to the ingredients that compose it, makes it a good choice in any season of the year.

title: Fresh pasta sauté with peeled shrimp and sage sauce
preparation: Put water in a pot with a bay leaf, salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. When the water boils, add the pasta and stir. Let it boil for 4 to 5 minutes. Finely chop the sage and place it in a saucepan where we have previously added the liquid cream and olive oil. Let it reduce. Take the shrimp and sauté them in a pan with olive oil and some previously chopped garlic and parsley. Once the pasta is cooked, set it aside. Take a ladle of the sage sauce and add it to the pan where we sautéed the shrimp. Add the pasta, sauté everything together, and it is ready to be plated.
notes: Fresh pasta (spaghetti, macaroni...) are cereal derivatives and are located at the base of the food pyramid of the Mediterranean diet, as it is recommended that the consumption of these foods and derivatives be daily. It is a very complete dish. The shrimp stand out, crustaceans rich in high-quality protein and minerals. They practically contain no fat because it is a considerable amount of cholesterol. The combination of the different components of this dish gives a result that provides us, thanks to the pasta, energy that is easy for the organism to use, plus the animal proteins provided by the shrimp. And we must not forget the olive oil, which as an additive fat has a high quality due to its contribution of vitamin E (antioxidant) and healthy fats (monounsaturated). It is a recipe that can be consumed regularly. If the pasta is whole grain, we will gain nutritionally as it is richer in fiber and minerals. It is a very aromatic and refreshing dish thanks to the sage.

title: Coca with porcini mushrooms and roasted vegetables

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil D.O. Garrigues
extra virgin olive oil D.O. Garrigues

preparation: Roast the peppers and eggplants directly over the fire until they are well charred and tender. Let them rest covered. Wrap the onions and tomatoes individually in aluminum foil and roast them at the edge of the fire: 12 minutes for the tomatoes and about 30 minutes for the onions. Clean the charred skin from the vegetables. Cut the peppers and eggplants into 1 cm thick strips. Then peel the onions and cut them into half-centimeter julienne, mince the garlic with the parsley, and grate the roasted tomatoes after peeling them. Clean the porcini mushrooms with a brush and cut the stem leaving approximately half a centimeter. Arrange the vegetables harmoniously over the coca. Arrange the porcini mushrooms with the slices facing up and the cap facing down. Season the whole assembly, especially the porcini mushrooms, with the garlic and parsley mince; season the roasted vegetables with the roasted tomato. Season the whole assembly with salt and pepper and drizzle with extra virgin oil. Bake in the oven at 180ºC for 30 minutes.
notes: Porcini mushrooms are one of the best-known mushrooms in Catalonia and are highly appreciated in Catalan gastronomy; they can be used in countless dishes as they are one of the most versatile foods thanks to their organoleptic properties. On the other hand, escalivada is also a traditional dish of Catalan cuisine, which is usually served accompanied by toast. Overall, it is a typical recipe for the autumn season in the Catalan territory; it is a dish rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber, and has a low fat content. When accompanied by a bread coca, it provides energy in the form of carbohydrates.

title: Sautéed beach squid with spinach and romesco
preparation:
Wash the squid and set aside the body and the legs; save the ink to make another recipe. Wash the spinach leaves well, removing the longest stems and any remaining dirt. Place them on absorbent paper to remove excess water. Cut the squid and sauté for a couple of minutes. Season with a little salt and add the spinach (for 30 seconds to prevent overcooking). Plate, decorating with romesco and a few drops of extra virgin olive oil.

The Sauce: Roast the tomatoes, almonds, and the garlic clove in the oven on a baking sheet for 30 minutes at 175 degrees. At the last moment, add some slices of day-old bread. Remove from the oven and let cool. Peel the tomatoes, remove the seeds, and place only the tomato flesh in a colander. Peel the garlic and set aside. In a blender or thermomix, add the tomatoes (preferably cold), the roasted garlic, the nuts, the bread, and a splash of Sherry vinegar. Blend, adjust salt and pepper, and emulsify the sauce by pouring in the oil slowly.
notes: Over the last few years, spinach has been increasingly introduced into Catalan gastronomy, used for both cold dishes like salads and hot dishes like omelets, casseroles, etc. They are a very good source of dietary fiber and vitamins. At the same time, squid is a mollusk with low fat content and is very rich in proteins and minerals. The dish is accompanied by a sauce very typical of the Camp de Tarragona region, romesco sauce. A high-calorie sauce made from olive oil and nuts, among other ingredients.

title: Sea bass supreme with apple compote and al dente vegetables
preparation: Clean the vegetables, peel the carrots and the turnips. Cut the three vegetables into thin sticks and season them slightly with salt. In a saucepan, bring water to a boil, add the vegetables separately and blanch them for a few minutes (4 or 5 minutes). They should be al dente. Once blanched, they must be cooled immediately in a bowl with ice water. This way, you stop the cooking process and the vegetables maintain their color. Place a pan over the heat with a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the vegetables for a very short time, just enough to sear them, and adjust the salt. Set them aside. In the same pan, add a little olive oil and when it is hot, sear the sea bass supremes, first on the skin side so it becomes crispy, and when they are golden, turn them and sear the other side. Place the vegetables in the middle of a plate, making a bed upon which we will place the sea bass supreme. Drizzle with a bit of olive oil and use the compote to make a ring around the plate. The dish is ready. For the compote: Peel and cut the apples into pieces and boil them with water and sugar (syrup) and two cinnamon sticks. Once cooked, remove the cinnamon from the water and blend everything.
notes: White fish such as sea bass stand out for their high biological value proteins, richness in certain minerals like iodine, and low fat content. Vegetables provide us with vitamins, minerals, fiber, and water, especially if they are blanched rather than boiled. The best way to preserve these characteristic vegetable nutrients is in raw form; if not, the blanching option is always better than boiling. This is a very well-achieved main course, as the main ingredient is the fish, accompanied by vegetables that add plenty of color in addition to their own nutrients. Olive oil is a great treasure of the Mediterranean diet that provides us with vitamin E and very healthy monounsaturated fats. Finally, there is also a small contribution from the fruit in the form of a compote.

title: Stuffed sea bream with prawn and its sauce
preparation:
Take the bread strips and place the sea bream fillets on top. Next, place 2 prawn tails on them. Roll everything up and secure it with a toothpick so it maintains a cylindrical shape. Place it in the oven in a deep dish at 180°C for 10 minutes with the sauce on top.

The Sauce: Rub the prawn heads and skins with the leek. Next, add the water and Cointreau and let it reduce. Blend everything and strain it. Make sure it reaches a thick consistency.
notes: The flavor of this dish comes from the fish and shellfish, which are sources of proteins and nutrients that participate in many regulatory processes of the organism and, moreover, are necessary for the formation and repair of different organs and tissues. Prawns are characterized by their important content of mineral salts such as, for example, potassium and phosphorus. This is a light recipe with low-fat cooking, as the oven is one of the least aggressive and most recommended cooking methods.

title: Rossejat de Calafell

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil and salt

preparation: For the picada: Fry the garlic and the bread in hot oil, then remove them. Blanch the peppers on the side to make the picada with the splash of brandy and the small glass of rosé wine, then blend everything with an immersion blender. Quick with potatoes: Make a sauté with the onions and tomatoes, add the roughly cut potatoes and sauté them for five minutes with the sauté. Boil the potatoes with the stock for about 20 minutes and add the monkfish for the last 8 minutes. Remove some of the liquid to add the picada. Let it cook for 5 more minutes once it has finished boiling. Rossejat noodles: Cook the noodles, which should have been previously toasted in oil, using the liquid that was removed. At the end, add the allioli.
notes: Monkfish is a white, lean fish, highly valued from a gastronomic point of view for being very versatile. Accompanied by noodles, it creates a complete dish deeply rooted in Mediterranean food culture. It is a dish rich in proteins and carbohydrates that provides satiety and interesting nutrients. Accompanied by a good salad and fresh fruit for dessert, we will obtain a traditional healthy menu.

title: Longline conger eel with Prat artichokes, fresh spinach and chard

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil from Celler d'Ullastrell

preparation: Choose a conger eel close to 3 kg and prepare clean loins. Separate only the spinach leaves and discard the stems. Next, clean them thoroughly and blanch them for a few seconds, then quickly cool them in ice water. Choose only the chard leaves and cut off the stem vein at the end. Clean them like the spinach and boil them for 5 minutes, then quickly cool them in ice water. Peel the artichokes until only the heart remains. To prevent them from darkening, reserve them in water with a squeeze of lemon. Fry the artichokes until they are well browned and place them on absorbent paper to remove excess oil. Make a tomato concassé and mix it with oil, salt, and pepper. Grill the eel starting with the skin. It is important that it remains juicy and not overcooked. Finally, sauté the spinach on one side and the chard on the other, and plate all the ingredients together.
notes: Conger eel is a very consumed fish in our area due to its proximity to Mediterranean waters and its acceptance because of its almost lack of bones. Spinach, chard, and artichokes provide fiber and antioxidants with low caloric content. Some fresh fruit desserts will increase the fiber in the meal, now slightly reduced by the lack of chard stems.

title: Sardines a la llauna with oyster mushrooms
preparation: The night before, soak the oyster mushrooms. The next day, in the morning, change the water and boil them for approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes. You can buy the mushrooms already cooked. Prepare the sardines, clean them, and cut them into fillets without removing the head. Chop the garlic and the parsley. Season the sardines with salt and pepper and place them on a tray to go into the oven, along with the garlic, parsley, and a bit of olive oil. The skin of the sardine should be in contact with the tray. Bake them for 5 minutes at about 150°C. Once cooked, remove them, add a spoonful of sweet paprika over them and a splash of vinegar. Shake it well and it will be ready.
notes: The sardine is a blue fish of great nutritional interest due to its high content of Omega-3 fatty acids, which are very healthy fats. The mushrooms are a good complement to accompany the sardines, as they belong to the legume food group and will provide us with fiber, protein, and carbohydrates. The cooking method for this recipe is the oven, a very advisable culinary technique to be low in fat and gentle; it maintains the taste, smell, and color of the food. It is a very complete dish, which can be accompanied by a cream, a broth, or an escalivada.

title: Tuna loin with candied onion
preparation: To confit the onion, slice it into julienne and place it in a pan with olive oil, letting it warm up slowly. Add a bit of salt so it releases all its juices and leave it for one hour over very low heat until it is well cooked. Season the tuna with salt and place it on the pan, being careful not to overcook it as it can become too dry. To finish, take the cooked tuna and mix it with the onion in the pan; add some chopped garlic and parsley, squeeze 1/4 of a lemon over it, and it is ready to be served on a plate accompanied by a mix of colorful lettuce.
notes: The nutritional value of this dish lies primarily in the importance of its fats: oleic acid from the olive oil and omega-3 from the tuna (blue fish), both very beneficial for our organism due to their cardio-healthy effect. It is a light and very healthy main course that provides us with high biological value protein through the fish and is very well complemented by the salad accompaniment, as this way we obtain fiber, water, and mineral salts.

title: Sautéed artichokes with baby squid
preparation: Clean the artichokes, cut them, and sauté them together with the squid in a pan with hot extra virgin olive oil. Add a little salt and it is ready to serve.
notes: The main ingredient of this dish is the artichoke. For this reason and because it is a hot dish, it makes it a more appropriate option for autumn days. Artichokes are nutritionally rich in potassium and have diuretic properties, so they have a purifying and detoxifying effect on the body. By opting to sauté them with olive oil, a very heart-healthy fat, the dish is filled with vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Moreover, the sautéing technique does not lead to a great loss of the nutritional properties of the foods. Another food present in this recipe is the squid, which after being sautéed, the meat remains firm and flavorful. By choosing this dish, one achieves ingesting part of the recommended daily proteins in a healthy way. To complete the dish and make it more balanced, it is recommended to accompany it with some toast or bread.

title: Mediterranean hake supremes with olive oil and Lleida apple on a bed of ratatouille
preparation: Cut the apple into wedges and sauté it with olive oil, sugar, and apple liqueur. Cut the vegetables into small dice and make the ratatouille. Sear the supremes on the grill. Place the garlic and olive oil on top, along with the Lleida apple wedges arranged like a fan. Put everything in the oven to gratin. When plating, place a base of ratatouille in the shape of a ring. On top, place the gratinated hake supremes and decorate the dish with a swirl of romesco oil.
notes: This is a very balanced main course since through the hake (white fish) we obtain a portion of high biological value proteins as well as a high amount of iodine, a mineral very common in saltwater fish. The ratatouille and the apple as accompaniments provide us with fiber, vitamins, water, and minerals. Olive oil plays a discreet but important role in this dish, as it provides us with monounsaturated fats, recognized for their cardiovascular protection effect, in addition to the contribution of vitamin E, a characteristic antioxidant of olive oil, as well as the taste and aroma that ultimately profile the dish. This dish can be complemented with a first course based on raw vegetables such as a colorful lettuce salad with lentils and dried fruit.

title: Tuna steak with salt-crusted potatoes and summer lentils with olive juice

ingredients.name: dill, rosemary, bay leaf and thyme

preparation: Marinate the tuna by making a light mixture of spices: dill, rosemary, and bay leaf (reserve it in the fridge for one hour). Place the potatoes (with skin) in a deep dish that can be placed in the oven; dampen them slightly with water, cover them completely with sea salt, and place them in the oven at 180°C for approximately 45 minutes. Once done, set them aside. Next, cook the lentils together with a sprig of fresh thyme, two or three garlic cloves, and an orange peel. After boiling for approximately 40 minutes over low heat, remove and set aside. Remove the pits from the arbequina olives and crush them together with 20 cl of extra virgin olive oil until a vinaigrette is achieved. Finally, cut the potatoes into medallions without peeling them and place them on a plate. Sauté the lentils with a bit of olive oil and onion and distribute them over the potatoes. Sear the tuna in the pan (turning it over and over). Place the tuna on the plate with the potatoes and lentils and drizzle with the arbequina vinaigrette. Serve at room temperature.
notes: Tuna is a blue fish of great nutritional interest due to its high content of omega-3 fatty acids. These substances are beneficial for the cardiovascular system, as is the oleic acid we obtain through olive oil. It is a very complete and aromatic dish, with a good supply of protein, both of animal origin (tuna) and vegetable (lentils), and other nutrients such as carbohydrates and fiber from the potatoes and lentils. It can perfectly be an ethnic dish accompanied with a bit of salad.

title: Shrimp with paddy straw mushrooms
preparation: Boil the mushrooms (previously soaked for 6-8 h) with water, 1 carrot, 1 onion, and the bay leaf. Sauté the shrimp with a little oil. Heat the already cooked and drained mushrooms with the two tablespoons of sauce. Top with the shrimp, a pinch of coarse salt, and chopped parsley. The Sauce: In a saucepan or heavy-bottomed pot, add a splash of oil and sauté the shrimp. Next, add the mixture made with the vegetables and the white wine. Once browned, add 2 l of water and reduce over low heat until it reaches half its volume. Pass through a Chinese strainer.
notes: This recipe could perfectly be a main course as it is nutritionally very complete; the shrimp will provide high-quality proteins and low fat. The mushrooms, belonging to the legume group, are also a very good source of protein (in this case, of plant origin), rich in fiber which will help regulate intestinal transit, and complex carbohydrates, which will allow us to obtain energy slowly and gradually to work for the rest of the day.

title: Chickpeas and spinach sautéed with virgin olive oil
preparation: Initially, soak the chickpeas the night before. The following day, continue by placing the chickpeas in a pressure cooker with a pinch of salt. Once cooked, drain them and set aside. Next, blanch the fresh spinach. Once the spinach is blanched, take a frying pan and sauté them together with the chickpeas using virgin olive oil. Separately, make a sofrito with the onion, garlic, and parsley using olive oil and set aside. Finally, serve the dish with the chickpeas sautéed with spinach and a spoonful of sofrito.
notes: A versatile dish to consume all year round, as it can be eaten cold in spring and summer and hot in autumn and winter. A recipe rich in fiber from the legumes and vegetables, which is satiating and helps intestinal motility. If served as a main course, it can be accompanied by dairy desserts to complement the plant-based protein from the legumes.

title: Broad bean pods Catalan style
preparation: Cut the cured sausage into small squares and sauté it with a drizzle of olive oil. Next, chop the spring garlic and onions and add them to the sauté until heated. Add the peeled and chopped tomatoes to this sauté. Then, cut the broad beans in half and into four or five pieces each from the pods and immediately incorporate them into the sauté. Add the glass of wine, the glass of water, and salt to taste, letting it simmer over very low heat for one hour. When the beans begin to appear tender, add the diced sausages and four mint leaves to aromatize the dish. Adjust the salt and turn off the heat once everything is cooked. Finally, to serve the dish, you can decorate with some mint leaves.
notes: Broad bean season begins in January, starting with the green beans, which, if very tender, can be eaten along with the pods. This dish is rich in proteins of both plant origin (the broad beans are fresh legumes) and animal origin. The onions and tomatoes help balance the amount of saturated fat from the sausage and cured sausage and improve digestion.

title: Meatloaf with apples and warm salad with grains and root vegetables

ingredient_sections.section_name: Salad with grains and root vegetables

ingredients.name: whole grains, e.g., wheat, spelt or barley

preparation: Meatloaf: Mix the meat thoroughly with salt. Stir the egg into the meat. Add oats, grated onion, and pepper. Stir the milk into the meat mixture. Cut the apples into 1/2 cm thick slices. Remove the cores from the middle slices. Form a meatloaf with apple slices in two layers: Place a little of the meat mixture at the bottom of an ovenproof dish. Place a layer of apples on top, a layer of meat, another layer of apples, and finally meat. Smooth the sides and top of the meatloaf with your hands. Sprinkle thyme on top of the meatloaf and bake it in the oven at 200 degrees for 45 minutes. Salad with grains and root vegetables: Boil the grains until tender in lightly salted water, and let them drain well in a sieve. Peel the root vegetables and cut them into long strips with a peeler. Whisk oil and vinegar together, and toss the dressing with the root vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly toss the root vegetables with the grains and sprinkle with cress. Slice the meatloaf into thick slices and serve with the grain salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 80 g. Protein: 36 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Whole grain pasta with parma ham, spinach and ricotta
preparation: Boil the pasta as indicated on the packaging and drain. Save a little of the cooking water. Shell the peas. Slice the radishes. Rinse the spinach. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and cut them into strips. Steam the asparagus for about 2 minutes. Steam the spinach with the last minute. Drain and toss with radishes and ricotta. Stir so that the ricotta melts, and then toss with the pasta. Thin it out with a little of the cooking water to make the consistency more creamy. Sprinkle the peas on top and serve with parma ham. Season with flaked salt and pepper.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 30 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Spring rolls with minced beef and sweet and sour sauce
preparation:
Spring rolls: Peel the carrots and grate them coarsely on a grater. Shred the cabbage very finely. Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the curry powder in it. Add the pressed garlic, ginger, carrots, and cabbage and fry it over high heat for a couple of minutes. Add the meat and brown it well. Stir well so the vegetables do not burn. Season the filling with salt and pepper. Cut each sheet of phyllo pastry into two equal parts, so there are 12 pieces in total. Fold each piece of phyllo pastry along the long edge. Distribute 2 tbsp of filling in the middle of the dough. Brush the egg white all the way around. Fold the edges in and roll the dough tightly around the filling, like a roulade.
