Place the spring rolls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush the rolls with oil and bake them in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes, until they are golden.

Sweet and sour sauce: Place water, sugar, vinegar, tomato paste, and pressed garlic in a small saucepan. Boil it over low heat for approx. 3 minutes. Dissolve the cornstarch in a little cold water to make a slurry and stir it into the sauce. Boil the sauce for an additional 3 minutes and let it cool. Season the sauce with salt. Serve the spring rolls with sweet and sour sauce.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 52 g. Protein: 22 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Chicken balls in curry
preparation: Chicken balls: Peel and coarsely grate the onion. Mix the meat with salt, egg, onion, oats, and milk to form a meatball mixture. Season with pepper and let the mixture rest covered in the refrigerator for approx. 30 minutes. Bring a pot of bouillon to a boil. Shape the mixture into small round meatballs and cook them in the bouillon. They are done when they float on the surface of the water. Remove them with a slotted spoon and keep them warm. Strain the bouillon and save it. Sauce: Peel and coarsely chop the onion. Slice the celery. Cut the apples into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apples into thin wedges. Rinse the spinach and let it drain. Divide the broccoli into florets. Heat the oil in a large deep non-stick pan. Add curry and sauté the onion and celery for a few minutes. Add bouillon and broccoli and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Now add cooking cream, spinach, apples, and meatballs to the sauce and bring to a boil until the spinach wilts slightly. If the sauce is too thick, thin it with more bouillon. Side dish: Cook the whole grain rice as indicated on the packaging. Serve the rice with the chicken balls in curry.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrates: 80 g. Protein: 35 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Chicken with pumpkin and bell peppers in Thai coconut sauce
preparation: Cut the chicken fillets into cubes. Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds, and cut the pumpkin flesh into small triangles. Cut the bell peppers into cubes. Sauté the pumpkin and bell peppers in the oil in a large pot for 3-4 minutes. Add the chicken and fry for a few minutes. Add the curry paste, coconut milk, and bouillon and bring the sauce to a boil. Let the dish simmer for 10 minutes. Season the sauce with salt or fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice. Finely slice the spring onions and stir them into the sauce just before serving. Serve with cooked rice.
notes:
Tip! Instead of hokkaido pumpkin, you can use butternut squash.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 77 g, Fat: 20 g, of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Heart Association's green lasagna
preparation: Finely chop the onions and bell peppers and slice the mushrooms. Sauté the onions and bell peppers in oil in a pot. Add the chopped, peeled tomatoes and mushrooms to the pot. Boil over medium heat until the filling thickens, approx. 10-15 minutes. Add cottage cheese, minced garlic, fresh, chopped or dried marjoram, basil, salt, and pepper. Grease an ovenproof dish with oil. Layer the lasagna sheets and filling. Start with sheets and end with filling. Place the lasagna in the refrigerator and let it rest for at least ½ hour, preferably longer. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Sprinkle the cheese over the lasagna and bake for approx. 30 minutes on the middle rack of the oven.
notes: Tip! 300 g of diced ham can be added. Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 300 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 2000 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates 47 g. Protein 26 g. Fat 11 g. Of which saturated fat 3 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Egg cake with salmon and summer greens

ingredients.name: thick slices of whole grain rye bread

preparation: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees. Chop the onion. Remove the core and the outer leaves of the cabbage, and slice it finely. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Slice the potatoes. Cut the salmon into smaller pieces. Heat the oil in a pan that can be placed in the oven. Sauté the onion, pressed garlic, cabbage, and potatoes for about 5 minutes while stirring gently. Add the spinach and peas, and let the spinach wilt. Remove the pan from the heat and add the pieces of salmon. Whisk the eggs together and pour the mixture into the pan. Turn gently and season with salt and pepper. Place the pan in the hot oven and bake the egg cake for about 25 minutes until it has a firm consistency. Serve with a sprinkle of chives and rye bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Crispy chicken with herb dip and lentil salad
preparation: Lentil salad: Rinse the lentils and boil as indicated on the packaging. While the lentils are boiling, prepare the rest. Remove the outer leaves and the "silk" from the corn, and halve the corn. Boil them in lightly salted water for about 5 min. Drain the corn and cut the kernels from the cobs. Set aside a little corn for the open-faced sandwiches. Peel and chop the onion. Cut the tomatoes into quarters and the bell pepper and cucumber into small cubes. Drain the lentils and toss with onion, corn, tomatoes, bell pepper, and cucumber. Herb dip: Rinse and chop the herbs and mix with ricotta, flaked salt, and pepper. Set aside 25 g of herb dip for the open-faced sandwiches. Crispy chicken: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees fan air. Pound the chicken fillets slightly flat, cut into smaller pieces, coat with flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs seasoned with flaked salt and pepper. Spread the chicken pieces out on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush with a little olive oil. Bake the chicken pieces in the oven for about 20 min. until they are crispy. Turn them halfway through. Save 1/3 of the chicken for the open-faced sandwiches. Serving: Serve the crispy chicken with herb dip and lentil salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 48 g. Protein: 42 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 4.5 g.

title: Fish rolls with roasted potatoes, cauliflower and blueberries

ingredients.name: nordic crisp – crunchy salad, can be replaced by other salad

preparation: Roasted potatoes: Halve the potatoes. Divide cauliflower into small florets. Rinse and dry the blueberries. Rinse the salad and toss it dry. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and roast potatoes together with cauliflower until they take color. Season with flaked salt and pepper, and remove the pan from the heat. Gently fold in blueberries and chopped almonds. Fish rolls: Rinse and chop the parsley. Spread a little mustard on the fish fillets, and sprinkle some parsley over. Roll the fish up and season with flaked salt and pepper. Gently place the fish rolls on a pan, and add water or bouillon until it covers about 1 cm of the fish. Squeeze the juice of 1/2 lemon over, and place a lid on the pan. Steam the fish for approx. 6 min., until the fish flakes easily when you press it with a finger. Serving: Arrange salad, roasted potatoes and fish rolls on plates and serve with lemon.
notes: Fruit and vegetables approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 35 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Thai fish dish with coconut milk

ingredients.name: red curry paste (ready-made in a jar)
white fish, e.g., pollock or redfish

preparation: Slice the onions. Put bouillon, curry paste, and onions in a pot and bring to a boil. Add cornstarch stirred into coconut milk. Add fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and freshly grated ginger. Bring to a boil while stirring. Add fish cut into 3×3 cm pieces to the dish and bring to a gentle boil. Let it simmer for about 3-4 minutes. Place the dish in a bowl or deep dish. Slice the pointed cabbage and steam it in lightly salted water for 3-5 minutes. Drain the cabbage in a sieve. Distribute the cabbage over the dish. Sprinkle chili in small cubes over it and garnish optionally with fresh mint and lime wedges.
notes:
Tip! Instead of curry paste, you can briefly sauté 2 tsp of curry powder in 2 tsp of oil and then add the bouillon. You can replace the fish with large prawns that are pre-cooked and have the tails on. They should be thawed and then boiled in the same manner as the fish.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise specified.
Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrate: 24 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Cod bake with tomato and black beans

ingredients.name: cod fillet without skin and bones

preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Cut the squash, bell pepper, and aubergine into cubes. Chop the onion and press the garlic. Rinse and drain the beans. Heat oil in a pan. Sauté the onion and garlic and then add the squash, bell pepper, aubergine, and oregano and fry for a few more minutes. Cut the cod into portions. Place the vegetables, drained beans, and cherry tomatoes in an ovenproof dish and make small indentations in the tomato sauce. Place the cod in the dish and season with salt and pepper. Cover the dish and place it in the oven for approximately 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily when you press it with a finger. Remove the dish from the oven. Warm the bread. Top with basil and serve with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 380 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrate 60 g. Protein 49 g. Fat 8 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Asian noodles with summer vegetables and marinated king prawns

ingredients.name: cabbage without stalk, e.g., white cabbage or pointed cabbage

preparation: Marinated king prawns: Press the garlic. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Remove the tails from the prawns. Place the prawns in a bowl with olive oil, garlic, and chili. Toss well and let the prawns marinate for about 30 min, or longer if preferred. Asian noodles: Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain. Peel the carrots and cut into long thin strips. Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage and finely shred it. Snap the woody bottom end off the asparagus and cut the asparagus into smaller pieces on a diagonal. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the carrots and cabbage for 2-3 min. Add the asparagus and spinach, and fry until the spinach wilts slightly. Add the tamari or soy sauce and toss the vegetables with the noodles. In another pan, roast the prawns in the marinade over high heat for about 5 min, until they change color from grey to pink. Squeeze lime juice over them. Cut the mango into cubes. Serving: Serve the Asian noodles with prawns, mango, and a sprinkle of cashew nuts.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 2400 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 28 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person.

title: Pollock in curry with cabbage salad and brown rice

ingredients.name: white cabbage, pointed cabbage or red cabbage without core
pollock fillet without skin and bone

preparation: Rinse the rice and cook as indicated on the packaging. Finely shred the cabbage. Coarsely chop the kale. Mix the cabbage together if using different types, and sprinkle with salt and sugar. Peel the oranges and cut into slices or segments. Toss the cabbage with the oranges and sprinkle the crumbled salad flakes over it. Cut the fish into portions. Put bouillon in a sauté pan. Carefully place the fish in the pan, cover with a lid, and gently steam the fish for about 8 minutes until it flakes when you press it lightly with a finger. Carefully remove the fish and keep it warm. Save the bouillon. Peel the onion, peel the carrots and cut into small cubes. Heat the oil in a sauté pan and sauté the curry. Add onion, ginger and carrots and fry for about 1 minute. Pour in the milk and heat up. Shake the flour with a little of the bouillon to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the sauce while it boils up under stirring. Boil for about 3 minutes, and season the sauce with flaked salt and pepper. If the sauce is too thick, thin it with more bouillon. Serve according to the downsize-plate model, where one quarter of the plate is pollock in curry, one quarter is brown rice and half of the plate is cabbage salad. Top with parsley.
notes: TIP Instead of pollock, you can use e.g. cod fillet or ling.

title: Asian chicken meatballs in noodle salad
preparation: Chicken meatballs: Finely chop the onion. Mix the meat with onion, curry paste, egg, and salt. Let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes. Shape the chicken meat into small balls (golf ball size) and place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bake the meatballs in the oven at 220 degrees for about 12 minutes. Turn them halfway through. Let the meatballs cool slightly before glazing them with teriyaki sauce. Noodle salad: Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Make a dressing from soy sauce, finely chopped chili, and lime juice. Peel the carrots and cut them into small thin sticks. Make beautiful shavings of the cucumber with a vegetable peeler, and slice the radishes into thin slices. Rinse the spinach and sprouts well, and shake them dry. Toss the vegetables with the dressing. Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain. Toss the noodles with the vegetables and serve with the chicken meatballs. Sprinkle sesame seeds and coriander over the top.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 56 g. Protein: 35 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Falafel with pita, crispy creamy cabbage, and pickled red onions
preparation: Day 1: Dried chickpeas must be soaked the day before you want to make falafels. Put chickpeas in a bowl and pour cold water over them. Let them sit on the kitchen counter for approx. 10 hours. If you soak more chickpeas than you need, they can be boiled and frozen for later use. Canned chickpeas are pre-soaked and can therefore be used directly in cooking. Day 2: Pickled red onions: Put vinegar and sugar in a pot and bring to a boil until the sugar is dissolved. Remove the pot from the heat. Peel the onions and cut them into very thin slices – e.g., using a mandoline. Place the onions in a jar along with bay leaves and peppercorns, and pour the brine over. Close the lid and let the onions steep until the rest is prepared. The pickled red onions can be usefully saved, for example, for lunch another day. They keep well for a long time if stored in the refrigerator. Falafels: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees fan air. Peel and chop the onion. Press the garlic. Drain the chickpeas and place them in a blender along with onion, garlic, and spices. Blend into a paste. Add eggs and blend again. Add lemon juice and chickpea flour, and place the paste in the refrigerator for approx. 30 min. Shape the paste into 16 round falafels and place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Press them slightly flat. Dab/brush with oil and bake them crispy in the oven for approx. 20 min. Turn them halfway through so they become crispy on both sides. Crispy creamy cabbage: Shred the cabbage. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apple into thin wedges. Mix yogurt with sweet mustard and chopped mint, and then toss with the cabbage and apples. Sprinkle with snipped chives. Remove half of the falafels and save them for lunch another day. Warm the pita breads and serve with the falafels, crispy creamy cabbage, and pickled red onions.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 100 g. Protein: 24 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Cauliflower curry with almonds and whole grain bulgur
preparation: Peel and chop the onion. Crush the garlic. Divide the cauliflower into small florets. Rinse the spinach and shake it dry. Slice the bell pepper. Slice the spring onions. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apple into thin wedges. Heat the oil in a pot and brown the onion briefly. Add curry and stir. Add garlic, cauliflower, and bell pepper, and pour in the bouillon. Let the vegetables simmer under a lid for 5 min. Add spinach and let it just wilt. Pour coconut milk into the pot, and add lentils and apples. Heat up and season the dish with flaked salt and pepper. Chop the almonds. Rinse and chop parsley. Arrange bulgur in two bowls and top with the cauliflower curry. Sprinkle the almonds over and serve with parsley.
notes: Side dish: Rinse bulgur and boil as indicated on the packaging. Take half and save for day 5. Energy distribution per person: 550 kcal. Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 21 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g.

title: Pizza with eggs, tuna and bell pepper

ingredients.name: whole grain durum flour or regular whole grain wheat flour

preparation: Dough: Dissolve the yeast in the water in a bowl. Add the whole grain flour, salt, and most of the wheat flour. Knead the dough well until it is soft and elastic – add more wheat flour along the way if necessary. Let the dough rise covered for 1 hour. Tomato sauce: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in the oil in a pot. Add the tomatoes, pressed garlic, oregano, and salt, and let the sauce simmer for 15 minutes. Topping: Cut the broccoli into small florets and the stem into cubes. Boil the broccoli in lightly salted water for 4 minutes, and let it drain well in a sieve. Cut the bell peppers into large pieces. Drain the tuna. Pizza: Preheat the oven to 250 degrees with a baking sheet inside. Divide the dough into 4, and roll each piece out into a round pizza base. Spread the tomato sauce evenly on each base. First distribute the cheese and then the bell peppers, broccoli, and tuna evenly over the bases, but leave the center without topping. Crack an egg in the center of each pizza. Transfer one pizza at a time onto the baking sheet and bake for about 15 minutes until the cheese has melted, the edge of the pizza is light brown, and the egg white has set. Sprinkle with fresh oregano or basil before serving.
notes: Tip! If you have a baking stone, use it, as it provides crispier pizza crusts. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 372 g per person. Energy distribution: 2894 KJ (689 kcal). Carbohydrates: 85 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Egg cake with potatoes, spinach and tomato
preparation: Egg cake: Slice the onions into narrow wedges and sauté them in the oil in a pan until they are translucent. Cut the potatoes into large cubes and fry them with the onions for a few minutes. Add the spinach and sauté it until it has fully wilted. Halve the tomatoes and toss them with the other vegetables. Whisk the milk into the flour to make a smooth mixture. Then, whisk in the eggs and add salt and pepper. Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and potatoes in the pan. Let the egg cake simmer over low heat until it has set. Using a lid will help it cook faster. Herbs: Rinse and dry the herbs. Pluck the parsley and cut the chives into long pieces. Toss the herbs with apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper, and sprinkle the salad over the egg cake before serving. Serve rye bread and mustard with the egg cake.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 63 g. Protein: 26 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Autumn Stew with Root Vegetables and Mushrooms

ingredients.name: mushrooms e.g. oyster mushrooms, shiitake and button mushrooms
beer 33 cl, e.g. Brown Ale or other dark beer

preparation: Autumn Stew: Chop the onions. Peel the carrots and celeriac and cut into small cubes. Clean the mushrooms. Cut the meat into cubes and toss in flour. Heat half of the oil in the pot and sauté onions, pressed garlic, carrots, celeriac, and mushrooms. Remove the vegetables. Pour the rest of the oil into the pot and brown the meat. Add the vegetables back into the pot, and pour in the beer and bouillon. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves, and let the meat simmer at low heat under a lid for approx. 1½ hours. Season the dish with salt, pepper, and balsamic vinegar. Mashed Potatoes: Peel the potatoes and cut into cubes. Boil the potatoes in a pot of water until they are well tender. Drain the cooking water. Save a little. Mash the potatoes with warm milk and optionally thin it out with a little of the cooking water. Season the mash with salt and pepper. Serve the mashed potatoes with the autumn stew. Garnish with fresh thyme.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 2800 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 71 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 8.5 g.

title: Olivie salad – Iranian potato salad with chicken

ingredients.name: whole grain bread, e.g., Arabic whole grain flatbread, whole grain pita bread, rye bread or coarse wheat bread

preparation: Olivie salad: Place the chicken fillets in a small pot, add 2 dl of water, and let them boil under a lid for 10 minutes. Let the meat soak in the water for 5 minutes, then remove it and let it cool down. Dice the carrots and boil them in the chicken broth for 5 minutes. Remove them and let them cool in a sieve. Shred the chicken meat into small pieces with your fingers. Coarsely grate the potatoes, eggs, and pickled cucumbers using a grater. Mix them in a bowl with the peas, carrots, chicken, mayonnaise, and yogurt. Gently fold everything together. Season with pepper, lemon juice, and optionally a little salt. Side: Serve the salad with whole grain bread.
notes: Tip! You can save some of the filling to use as garnish. The salad can be used as sandwich filling. Olivie can be eaten both warm and cold; it is lightly spiced and has a fantastic flavor. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 39 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Risotto with chicken, celeriac and gremolata
preparation: Chop the onion. Peel the celeriac and parsnips and cut them into small dice. Cut the chicken breasts into small dice. Heat half of the oil in a pan and fry the pancetta until almost crispy. Remove it from the pan and drain on a piece of paper towel. Heat the rest of the oil in the pan and fry the celeriac, parsnips, and crushed garlic for a moment, without letting them take color. Add the chicken and rice and stir well. Pour the white wine into the pan and let it evaporate. Add rosemary, and gradually add the bouillon, letting the rice simmer while the liquid is slowly absorbed. This takes about 20 minutes. Add the grated parmesan cheese and fried pancetta and stir. Season the risotto with salt and pepper. Chop the parsley, grate the lemon zest, and mix with the crushed garlic. Serve the risotto topped with the gremolata.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 220 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 78 g. Protein: 26 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Minced Beef Patties with Brussels Sprout Salad and Grandmother's Dressing

ingredients.name: small bunch of herbs, e.g., parsley, basil, or lovage

preparation: Brussels Sprout Salad: Boil the potatoes until tender, and peel them. Remove any outer dirty leaves and the stem of the brussels sprouts. Divide half of the brussels sprouts into leaves. Finely shred the rest. Steam the brussels sprout leaves and the shredded brussels sprouts for about 2 minutes, and drain them. Peel the carrots, and cut them into ribbons with a vegetable peeler. Toast the almond flakes until golden in a dry pan. Cut the potatoes into smaller pieces, and toss them with the brussels sprouts, carrots, and almond flakes. Grandmother's Dressing: Mix the ingredients for the dressing together, and season with pepper. Minced Beef Patties: Rinse the herbs, dry them well, and chop them. Knead the meat with the herbs, shape it into 4 minced beef patties, and season them with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and fry the patties for about 3 minutes on each side. Serve the beef patties with the brussels sprout salad, and drizzle the grandmother's dressing over them.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (470 kcal). Carbohydrates: 54 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Medium-rare duck breast with crispy red cabbage salad, roasted rosemary potatoes, fennel and port wine glaze
preparation:
Duck breast: Score the skin on the duck breasts and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and brown the duck breasts on the skin side. Drain the duck breasts and place them in an ovenproof dish. Roast the duck breast pieces in the oven at 180 degrees for 15-20 minutes.

Crispy red cabbage salad: Shred the red cabbage finely, e.g., using a mandoline. Place the cabbage in a bowl and sprinkle with salt and sugar, then massage the cabbage well. Rinse and chop the parsley. Cut the oranges into segments and gently toss them in the cabbage along with the chopped parsley. Massage the pomegranate, halve it, and press the juice and seeds over the salad.

Roasted rosemary potatoes: Rinse the potatoes and dry them. Cut the top and bottom off the fennels and cut them into quarters. Toss the potatoes and fennel with oil and spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Season with chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper and bake in the oven at 220 degrees for about 20 minutes, until they are well crispy.

Port wine glaze: Put balsamic vinegar in a saucepan and boil down to half. Add bouillon and boil down again to half. Add port wine and boil down to half, until the sauce thickens and is completely glossy. Season the glaze with salt and pepper.

Slice the duck breast and serve with crispy red cabbage salad, roasted rosemary potatoes, and port wine glaze.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 46 g. Protein: 31 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Grilled vegetables with gremolata
preparation:
Gremolata: Chop the basil. Crush the garlic. Finely chop the capers/anchovies. Finely grate the parmesan cheese. Toast the pine nuts until golden. Toss the basil with garlic, capers, parmesan cheese, pine nuts, and lemon zest.

Grilled vegetables: Prepare the vegetables. Cut the broccoli into large florets, the bell pepper into large pieces, and the zucchini and eggplant into slices. Spray or brush the vegetables with olive oil, and grill them on a grill or a grill pan until they are tender on both sides. Break the grilled broccoli into small florets.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 9 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 2.5 g.

title: Wok with beef and noodles
preparation: Halve the cabbage, remove the outer leaves and the core, and finely shred the cabbage. Divide the broccoli into smaller florets. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Slice the bell pepper. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a wok. It should be smoking hot. Add the curry paste and brown the meat. Remove the meat and heat the rest of the oil. Fry the pointed cabbage, broccoli, and bell pepper at high heat until they get some color. Add the meat, chili, pressed garlic, and ginger and toss well. Pour the soy sauce, fish sauce, and lime juice into the pan and bring to a quick boil. Add the spinach and remove the pan from the heat. Sprinkle with coriander and black sesame and serve with cooked noodles.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 51 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Pasta with broccoli and mushroom ragout

ingredients.name: mushrooms, e.g., oyster mushrooms, button mushrooms or mixed mushrooms
pasta, e.g., fusilli, shells or shells

preparation: Slice the onions into strips and sauté them in the oil in a sauté pan or wide-bottomed pot, without letting them brown. Cut large mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and cut the broccoli into small florets. Sauté the vegetables in the pan together with the onions. Add bouillon and thyme to the dish and let it simmer for about 5 minutes. Stir the cornstarch into cold water and add the thickening to the dish. Bring to a quick boil. Add the cream just before serving and heat the dish through. Season the ragout with salt and plenty of freshly ground pepper. Cook the pasta according to the instructions on the packaging, drain it, and toss it in the vegetable ragout. Serve the pasta dish immediately.
notes: Tip! The dish is suitable as a side dish for, for example, roasted salmon, fried chicken breast and fried ham schnitzel. If you serve the dish as a side, you can reduce the amount of pasta to 320 g. Energy distribution: 2300 KJ (500 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 77 g, Protein: 22 g, Fat: 13 g, of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: White fish with whole wheat spaghetti, oven-baked root vegetables and romesco sauce

ingredients.name: root vegetables, e.g., beetroot, Jerusalem artichokes, parsnips and carrots
white fish fillets without skin and bones
whole wheat spaghetti or other whole grain pasta

preparation: Preheat the oven to 225 degrees fan. Peel the root vegetables and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Toss with olive oil and spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Season with oregano, salt, and pepper. Bake the roots in the oven for approx. 20 min. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Toss the spinach with the roots. Make a small slit in the middle of the fish fillet and fold the fish together so it gains some height. Place the fish in an ovenproof dish with parchment paper and drizzle lemon juice over it. Season with salt and pepper. Place the dish in the oven 10 min. before the roots are finished. The fish is done when it flakes easily when pressed lightly with a finger. Boil the pasta as indicated on the packaging and drain. Toss with romesco sauce and then with the root vegetables and spinach. Arrange and serve with the fish.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 66 g. Protein: 42 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Chicken salad with dill, potatoes, cabbage, melon and asparagus

ingredients.name: large pointed cabbage – sliced and massaged
green asparagus (approx. 250 g) – steamed and sliced into strips

preparation: Chicken salad: Scrub the potatoes and boil them until just tender. Cool the potatoes and set half aside for day 4. Halve the potatoes. Boil the chicken breast pieces for 12 min. Drain and shred with two forks. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Cut the melon into small cubes. Dill dressing: Mix the ingredients for the dressing together with the chopped dill and toss with the potatoes and chicken. Serving: Distribute the pointed cabbage and spinach at the bottom of two bowls and top with asparagus, melon, potatoes and chicken. Sprinkle with cress and season with flaked salt and pepper.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 500 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 72 g. Protein: 42 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Rich mushroom soup

ingredients.name: lemon, only the zest of this

preparation: Peel the potatoes and cut them into large cubes. Peel the garlic and onion and chop them coarsely. Boil the potatoes and onion in bouillon until tender, ensuring it covers them, under a lid. Blend or purée the soup and return it to the pot. Cut the mushrooms into smaller pieces and sauté them in the oil in a warm non-stick pan. Add them to the pot, add the cream, and bring everything to a boil. Adjust the consistency with water if necessary. Season the soup with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Chop the parsley. Serve the soup very hot with a sprinkle of chopped parsley, grated lemon zest, and bread.
notes: Tip! Milk can replace cooking cream if you want the soup to be less fatty. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 120 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 2150 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 81 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: One pot tagliatelle
preparation: Cut the chicken into strips. Chop the onion and press the garlic. Cut the zucchini into cubes. Warm the oil in a large pot and sauté the chicken for about 5 minutes. Remove the chicken, and then sauté the onion, garlic, and zucchini for about 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, vegetable bouillon, and pasta. Boil under a lid according to the package instructions. Add the chicken during the last 2 minutes. Season the dish with lemon zest and juice, salt, and pepper, and then toss with fresh spinach until it wilts slightly.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Ca. 300 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 2000 KJ (500 kcal) Carbohydrate 58 g Protein 30 g Fat 11 g Of which saturated fat 2 g * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Pork tenderloin with mushrooms and vegetables a la creme

ingredient_sections.section_name: Mushrooms and vegetables a la creme

ingredients.name: mushrooms e.g. porcini, oyster mushrooms, beech mushrooms or shiitake
sherry vinegar, can be replaced with balsamic vinegar

preparation: Pork tenderloin: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Trim the tenderloin and season it with salt, pepper, and thyme. Heat the oil in a pan and brown the tenderloin well on all sides. Place the tenderloin in an ovenproof dish and roast in the oven for approximately 20 minutes. Mushrooms and vegetables a la creme: Clean the mushrooms and cut them into smaller pieces if necessary. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the mushrooms over high heat. Add the pressed garlic and vinegar and bring to a boil. Pour the cream and bouillon over the mushrooms. Add spinach and thyme, and bring the sauce to a boil. Season with salt and pepper. Divide the broccoli into smaller florets and steam them until tender. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging and drain. Slice the meat and serve with the mushrooms and vegetables a la creme, steamed broccoli, and freshly cooked pasta.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 59 g. Protein: 46 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Quick-fried chicken with vegetables and roasted cashews
preparation: Cut the chicken fillets into finger-sized strips. Cut the broccoli florets into small bouquets. Peel the stalk, cut off the dry end, and slice it. Cut the bell peppers into thin strips and cut the onions into thin wedges. Finely chop the ginger. Split the cashew nuts and roast them in a dry pan over medium-high heat until they are golden brown. Place them on a plate. Heat half of the oil in the pan and quickly brown the chicken over high heat until they are golden on all sides. Place them on a plate. Heat the rest of the oil in the pan and sauté all the vegetables while stirring for about 5 min until they are tender, but still have a bit of bite. Add the chicken, ginger, and soy sauce, and toss everything together. Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging, and let them drain in a sieve. Arrange the noodles with the chicken and vegetables on top, sprinkle with cashew nuts, and serve immediately.
notes: Tip! Instead of chicken, you can use turkey or ham. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 79 g. Protein: 43 g. Fat: 23 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Burning Love with Jerusalem artichokes
preparation:
Potato and Jerusalem artichoke mash: Peel the potatoes and Jerusalem artichokes, and cut them into large chunks. Place them in a pot, cover with water, and boil them until both the potatoes and Jerusalem artichokes are completely tender. Drain the water, but save a little of it. Mash them into a coarse mash. Thin it out with some of the cooking water or warm milk until the mash has a good consistency. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

Onion and bacon: Dice the bacon and fry it in a pan over medium heat. Place it on a piece of fat-absorbing kitchen paper on a plate. Chop the onions and fry them in the fat in the pan until they are clear and golden. Rinse the thyme and pluck the leaves off. Mix the bacon and onion with the thyme.

Cut the apple into wedges. Arrange the mash on 4 plates, distribute the onion-bacon mixture on top of the mash, and serve with apple wedges.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (480 kcal). Carbohydrate: 76 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 4.4 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Gazpacho with green crunch
preparation: Gazpacho: Split the cucumber lengthwise. Remove the seeds with a teaspoon and cut the cucumber into small cubes. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Cut the bell peppers into small cubes. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and chop the chili and garlic. Put all the vegetables, tomato juice, and basil in a blender and blend until a smooth consistency is reached. Season the gazpacho with vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Green crunch: Cut the bell pepper and celery into small cubes. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Toss the bell pepper and celery with the spinach leaves. Pour the gazpacho into glasses, distribute the green crunch over it, and serve the soup with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 391 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1223 KJ (291.3 kcal). Carbohydrates: 46.3 g. Fat: 9.8 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Oven-baked fish with vegetables

ingredients.name: light bouillon, e.g., fish or vegetable bouillon

preparation: Chop the onion. Slice the carrots. Clean the leeks and slice them. Slice the tomatoes. Arrange the vegetables at the bottom of a greased ovenproof dish. Cut the cod into portions and place them on top of the vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Mix the bouillon with cream and curry, and pour it over. Place the dish in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 20 minutes. Serve the dish with boiled rice and sprinkle with chervil.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2250 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 71 g. Protein: 39 g. Fat: 8.5 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Panzanella Soup/Italian tomato soup with bread

ingredients.name: day-old wheat bread, preferably whole grain bread

preparation: Chop the onion and garlic, and sauté them in the oil in a large pot. Cut the tomatoes into coarse cubes, mix them with the onions, and sauté at high heat for about 5 minutes while stirring, until they begin to smell and release liquid. Add water or bouillon, and boil the soup for 20 minutes. Break the bread into smaller pieces and boil it in the soup for 5 minutes until it softens slightly and thickens the soup. Coarsely chop the basil or oregano, add it to the soup, and season with salt and pepper. Serve the soup with coarsely grated parmesan to sprinkle on top and bread on the side.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1800 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 19 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Fish Frikadeller with Kale Salad

ingredients.name: cod fillet without skin and bones
herbs, e.g., parsley, dill, chervil and chives

preparation: Kale Salad: Finely shred the kale and place it in a bowl. Sprinkle the kale with salt and sugar and massage it lightly. Let the kale stand while the beets are boiled. Scrub the beets and boil them in water until covered for approx. 45 minutes until tender. Cool the beets and rub off the skin. Cut the beets into smaller pieces. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apple into cubes. Toss the kale with the beets and apple. Stir the vinegar, mustard, honey, and oil together. Toss the dressing into the salad. Fish Frikadeller: Chop the fish and place it in a food processor. Sprinkle with salt and blend the fish coarsely. Peel the onion, grate it coarsely, and mix it with the fish along with the egg, oats, and milk. Season the fish mince with freshly ground pepper and place it covered in the refrigerator for approx. 30 minutes. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Form frikadeller with a spoon dipped in cold water, and fry them slowly until golden and cooked through on the pan for 6-7 minutes on each side. Green Remoulade: Chop the herbs and place them in a blender together with 1/2 dl of sour cream. Blend it into a green cream. Stir the cream with the rest of the sour cream along with the mustard and pickles. Season the remoulade with salt. Side Dish: Peel the potatoes and boil them until tender. Serve the fish frikadeller with the kale salad, boiled potatoes, and green remoulade.
notes: Tip! You can make the fish mince from a mixture of cod and salmon. Cod fillet can also be replaced with, for example, pollock, ling, or monkfish fillet. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 64 g. Protein: 36 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Buddha bowl with whole grain rice and steamed salmon
preparation: Pickled red onions: Peel the onion and cut into thin wedges. Put vinegar and sugar in a small pot with peppercorns and bay leaves and bring to a boil, until the sugar is dissolved. Add the onions, and remove the pot from the heat. Let the onions cool in the brine. Buddha bowl: Rinse the rice and cook as indicated on the packaging. Drain the rice and cool. Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage and shred it finely. Sprinkle with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Shell the peas. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and steam for 2 min. Drain and cut the asparagus into smaller pieces diagonally. Rinse and pluck the strawberries. Halve them if desired. Toast sesame in a dry pan until it takes color. Steamed salmon: Place the salmon in a pan without fat, and pour water on until it covers 1 cm of the salmon in height. Add lemon juice, put a lid on the pan, and turn on the heat. Steam the salmon for approx. 5 min., until it flakes when you press lightly on it with a finger. Remove the salmon from the pan, and let it drain before finely shredding it. Serving: Divide rice, cabbage, peas, cucumber, asparagus, and strawberries into two bowls together with the salmon and pickled red onions. Drizzle olive oil over, and sprinkle with toasted sesame.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 450 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 75 g. Protein: 34 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Lentil soup with curry, chicken, and lime-marinated apple cubes

ingredients.name: flatbread or slices of wheat bread

preparation: Bring the chicken legs to a boil in lightly salted water until covered. Cook the meat until tender, about 30 minutes. Remove the meat and let it cool slightly. Shred the meat from the legs into fine strips. Strain the soup. Split the chili and remove the seeds. Finely mince the chili and garlic. Dice the onion and bell pepper into cubes, approx. 1×1 cm. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the curry paste in it for a moment. Add the vegetables and sauté them until the onions are translucent at the edges. Add the strained soup, lentils, and spices. Supplement with water or bouillon if necessary. There should be approx. 1½ l of soup. Cook the soup for about ½ hour until the lentils begin to break down. Add the shredded chicken meat, heat the soup through, and season with salt and pepper and potentially more curry paste and ginger. Lime-marinated apple cubes: Cut the apple into small cubes and squeeze the lime juice over them. Serve the soup very hot with the lime-marinated apple cubes on top and garnish with fresh coriander leaves if desired. Eat with bread.
notes: Tip! Instead of whole chicken legs, you can use a whole chicken or chicken drumsticks or thighs. The fastest way is to use chicken fillet or chicken tenderloin and ready-made chicken broth. Cut the meat into small cubes and add it when the soup is almost finished after approx. ½ hour, and cook it with the soup for about 10 minutes.

title: Chicken Thighs with Cauliflower Tabbouleh and Strawberry Dressing
preparation: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, and place them in a greased, ovenproof dish. Roast the chicken thighs at 200 degrees for approximately 30 minutes, until they are cooked. Break the cauliflower into florets. Rinse the parsley and shake it dry. Place the cauliflower in a food processor along with the parsley, and process until a grainy consistency is reached. It should not be finely minced too much. Rinse and hull the strawberries. Clean the radishes. Cut the cucumber, radishes, melon, and strawberries into small cubes and toss with the cauliflower. Season with salt and pepper. Toast the almonds until golden in a dry pan, and chop them. Fold the almonds into the tabbouleh. Rinse and hull the strawberries. Place the strawberries, vinegar, oil, and honey in a blender and blend into a dressing. Plate the chicken thighs with the cauliflower tabbouleh and drizzle with the strawberry dressing. Serve with bread.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 66 g, Protein: 45 g, Fat: 18 g, of which saturated fat: 3 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 450 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Chicken with eggplant and pomegranate
preparation: Chicken in dish: Cut the onions into wedges. Cut the eggplant into cubes. Clean the chicken and cut it into 6 pieces. Arrange the onion, eggplant, and chicken in an ovenproof dish. Season with salt, pepper, and ground fennel. Pour in the bouillon, and bake the chicken in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 40 minutes. Rinse the parsley and chop it. Massage the pomegranate. Cut it through and remove the seeds and juice with a spoon. Remove the chicken. Toss the parsley and pomegranate seeds and juice with the eggplant and onion. Fennel tzatziki: Grate the fennel on the coarse side of a grater. Mix the fennel with Greek yogurt and pressed garlic, and season with salt and pepper. Serve the chicken with cooked bulgur, vegetables, juices, and tzatziki.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2200 KJ (510 kcal). Carbohydrates: 73 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Plaice in spicy soy sauce
preparation: Cut the bell peppers and pumpkin into triangles. Cut the zucchini into large pieces. Sauté the vegetables in oil in a large pot for 5 minutes, without letting them brown. Split the chili, remove the seeds, and chop it finely. Grate the ginger and garlic finely. Pour the bouillon over the vegetables and add the chili, ginger, and garlic, then bring to a boil. Dissolve the cornstarch in the soy sauce and thicken the sauce with the mixture. Roll the plaice fillets up, sprinkle them with salt, and place them on top of the vegetables. Put a lid on the pot and let the fish steam over medium heat for 5 minutes. Serve the fish with the vegetables, sauce, cooked rice, and a sprinkle of fresh coriander.
notes: Tip! Instead of pumpkin, you can use sweet potatoes. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 67 g. Protein: 36 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Tandoori chicken with Asian pointed cabbage
preparation:
Tandoori chicken: Preheat the oven to 225 degrees. Remove bone and skin from the chicken thighs. Wrap them slightly together and place them in an ovenproof dish lined with baking paper. Brush the chicken thighs with oil and season with Tandoori, salt, and pepper. Bake the chicken thighs in the oven for approx. 15 minutes, until they are golden and the meat is cooked through.

Asian pointed cabbage: Halve the pointed cabbage, remove the core and the outer leaves, and thinly slice the cabbage. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Slice the radishes. Halve the cucumber lengthwise and slice it. Cut the mango into wedges and chop the coriander. Mix a dressing of lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar and toss it with the cabbage along with the radishes, cucumber, mango, and coriander.

Mix the yogurt with ginger, chopped mint, salt, and pepper.

Serve Tandoori chicken with Asian pointed cabbage, naan bread, and yogurt dressing.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 45 g. Protein: 40 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Turkey in curry sauce with cabbage, grapes and apple
preparation: Chop the onion. Halve the cabbage. Remove the outer leaves and the core from the cabbage. Finely shred the cabbage. Take a large handful of cabbage and mix with carrots and raisins for a raw salad. Halve the grapes. Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the core, and cut the apples into thin slices. Place a pot over heat with a little water. Steam the cabbage for a few minutes and drain. Heat the oil in a pot. Add curry and brown it well. Add onion and turkey meat and fry at high heat. Add 3 dl of milk. Shake the rest of the milk with flour to make a slurry. Add the slurry to the pot and boil for a few minutes. Add cabbage, grapes and apple and heat through. Season with salt and pepper. Cook the rice as indicated on the packaging. Peel the carrots and grate them using the coarse side of a grater. Mix the carrots with raisins. Serve the turkey in curry sauce with whole grain rice and raw salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 88 g. Protein: 40 g. Fat: 11 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Lasagne with minced beef and Mediterranean vegetables
preparation: Mediterranean vegetables: Cut eggplant, zucchini, and bell pepper into bite-sized pieces. Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, and vegetables. Let it simmer for about 5 minutes until the vegetables feel tender. Meat sauce: Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion together with the meat. Add oregano and chopped tomatoes and let it simmer for about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Bechamel sauce: Heat 3 dl of milk in a pot. Shake the rest of the milk together with the wheat flour to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the pot while stirring and boil while stirring for about 3 minutes. Add cheese and nutmeg. Let the cheese melt in the sauce and season with salt and pepper. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Layer lasagna sheets, Mediterranean vegetables, meat sauce, and bechamel sauce in a greased ovenproof dish. Continue and end with a layer of bechamel sauce. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and cheese and bake the lasagna in the oven for about 30 minutes. Side dish: Cut tomatoes into wedges and onion into rings. Toss tomatoes with onion and fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper. Serve the lasagna with tomato salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 430 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2872 KJ (684 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 87 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 8 g.

title: Pita bread with hummus, cucumber and coriander
preparation: Rinse and drain the chickpeas and place them in a blender or food processor together with the pressed garlic, cumin, tahini, and the grated zest and juice of the lemon. Blend and thin with 1 dl of water a little at a time until the hummus has a soft, smooth consistency. Season with olive oil and salt. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Toss the cucumber with the chili, pressed garlic, and chopped coriander. Distribute the hummus, cucumber salsa, and crisp lettuce leaves into warm pita breads.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 42 g, Protein: 13 g, Fat: 7 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Roast duck breast with baked hokkaido
preparation:
Roast duck breast: Rub the duck skin with salt, freshly ground pepper, and finely grated lemon zest. Place the roast in a roasting pan and put it in the oven at 150 degrees for 1 hour. Pour off the melted fat from the roasting pan and add the bouillon. Continue roasting the duck breast for 30 minutes – until the internal temperature of the breast meat is approx. 62 degrees. Set the oven to 200 degrees fan air, and roast the duck breast further for approx. 30 minutes – until the skin is crispy. Let the roast rest for 15 minutes. Carve the meat off the bone and slice it.

Baked hokkaido pumpkin and radicchio: Wash the pumpkin and cut it into quarters. Scrape out the seeds and divide the pumpkin into large pieces. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, drizzle with ½ tbsp. olive oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and place the tray in the oven along with the duck roast for the last half hour at 200 degrees. Divide the radicchio salad into wedges and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and place them in the oven together with the pumpkin pieces once the duck has been removed, and bake them for 10-12 minutes. Arrange the pumpkin and radicchio together, drizzle with lemon juice, and sprinkle with thyme leaves.

Sauce: Strain the juices into a saucepan, skim off the fat, and thicken the sauce with cornstarch dissolved in a little cold water. Season the sauce with lemon juice, honey, salt, and pepper.

Side dishes: Boil the potatoes until tender in lightly salted water, and peel them. Keep them warm, or roast them until golden in a pan with olive oil. Optionally sprinkle with chopped parsley.

Serve slices of duck breast with baked pumpkin and radicchio, sauce, and potatoes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 53 g. Protein: 47 g. Fat: 18 g (including 5 g saturated fat).

title: Cauliflower gratin with cauliflower salad
preparation: Cauliflower gratin: Cut the cauliflower into large florets, and let the stem remain attached. Place the cauliflower in a saucepan, sprinkle with salt and add water to the bottom. Let the cauliflower boil under a lid for 4 minutes. Remove the cauliflower from the water and let it drain in a sieve. Grease an ovenproof dish with oil and sprinkle it with breadcrumbs. Whisk the flour and milk together, and whisk in the cooking water from the cauliflower. Cook the sauce thoroughly while whisking, and let it boil for 4-5 minutes until it is thick and smooth. Thin with a little extra milk if necessary if the sauce is so thick that it is difficult to whisk with a whisk. Add pepper and finely grated nutmeg. Separate the eggs and whisk the whites until stiff. Stir the egg yolks into the sauce, and then gently fold in the whites. Place the cauliflower in the dish and spread the mixture over it. Sprinkle the gratin with breadcrumbs and bake it in the oven at 180 degrees for approximately 30 minutes, or until it is fully cooked and crispy golden on top. Cauliflower salad: Slice the cauliflower, carrot, and radishes into thin slices. Finely chop the chives. Mix the oil and lemon juice together, and toss the vegetables and chives in the dressing. Season the salad with salt and pepper. Serve the cauliflower gratin with salad, bread, and mustard.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (750 kcal). Carbohydrates: 100 g. Protein: 28 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Wok with beef and vegetables in oyster sauce
preparation: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until they are fragrant and
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 74 g. Protein: 39 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Mexican pancakes with green salsa

ingredients.name: chili or pickled jalapeno chili (can be omitted)

preparation:
Chop the onions. Finely grate the carrots. Sauté the meat in a pot without fat until it has changed color. Add the onion and carrots and sauté for a few minutes. Add the taco sauce and simmer together until most of the liquid has evaporated, 5-10 minutes. Stir the pot regularly. Season with salt and pepper.

Cut the avocado in half and remove the flesh. Clean the bell pepper by removing the stem and seeds. Cut the bell pepper into smaller pieces. Place the avocado and bell pepper in a blender or food processor and mix until smooth. Season with garlic, lime juice, salt, and optionally freshly chopped or pickled chili.

Warm the pancakes according to the instructions on the packaging. Fill the pancakes with the meat sauce, green salsa, and sliced iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, and cucumber, and corn kernels.
notes:
Tip! Green salsa also tastes good as a dip for vegetable sticks.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 57 g. Protein: 33 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Beef in dark beer with mashed potatoes

ingredients.name: lean beef slices, e.g., sirloin or rump
dark beer, e.g., Brown Ale or porter

preparation:
Beef in dark beer: Pound the beef slices flat and season them with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a pot and brown the meat slices, possibly in several batches. Remove the meat. Peel the onions and cut them into strips. Brown the onions in the pot and add the meat back in. Add beer, bay leaves, thyme sprig, and beef bouillon until the meat is covered. Let the dish simmer under a lid for approx. 45-60 minutes. Peel the carrots, cut them into slices, and add them to the dish when the meat is almost tender. Cook the dish for another approx. 10 minutes, and season with salt and pepper. Stir the cornstarch into a little cold water and thicken the dish to the desired consistency. Optionally adjust the color with a few drops of caramel color.

Mashed potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut them into large pieces, and boil them until tender in water without salt. Drain the potatoes and steam off the remaining liquid over the heat. Whip the potatoes into a coarse mash with a stiff whisk or a potato masher, and season with salt and pepper.

Serve the dish with the mashed potatoes and steamed broccoli or green beans.
notes:
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrate: 92 g, Protein: 41 g, Fat: 17 g, of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Millionbøf with mashed potatoes

ingredients.name: salt, pepper and optionally a little nutmeg

preparation: Millionbøf: Peel onions and carrots. Blend onions, carrots, and white cabbage in a food processor, or grate them coarsely. Brown the meat in oil in a pot. Add the vegetables and brown them with the meat for 4-5 minutes. Mix the tomato paste with bouillon and cornstarch, and stir the mixture into the meat and vegetables. Add bay leaf, bring to a boil, turn down to low heat, and let the dish simmer for 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Mashed potatoes: Peel potatoes and parsnips. Cut them into large pieces, place them in a pot and cover with water. Boil until completely tender. Drain the water, but save a little of it. Mash the potatoes and parsnips into a coarse mash and thin it with the cooking water until the mash has a good consistency. Season with salt, pepper, and optionally finely grated nutmeg. Serve the millionbøf with the mash and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
notes:
Tip! Instead of parsnip, you can use parsley root, celeriac, kohlrabi, or sweet potatoes.
Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 77 g, Protein: 30 g, Fat: 16 g, of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Beetroot patties in crunchy salad with sweet potatoes
preparation:
Beetroot patties: Rinse the lentils well and boil them until tender. Drain the lentils. Chop the onion and press the garlic. Peel the beetroots and grate them on the coarse side of a grater. Optionally blend the lentils slightly before mixing them with onion, garlic, beetroots, cumin, egg, and chickpea flour. Season with salt and pepper. Shape the mixture into 4 patties and place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper and bake in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 25 min.

Salad with roasted sweet potatoes: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into large pieces. Toss the sweet potatoes with oil and spread them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Season with salt and pepper and bake the potatoes in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 30 min. Finely chop the kale. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apple into thin wedges. Squeeze the juice and seeds out of the pomegranate. Toss the roasted sweet potatoes with the de-stemmed kale and arrange on a platter with apples and pomegranate seeds. Crumble feta cheese over the top and drizzle with hoisin sauce. Top with coriander and serve with the beetroot patties.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 20 g. Fat: 9 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Pumpkin soup with crispy croutons and leeks

ingredients.name: pumpkin flesh e.g. hokkaido or butternut

preparation: Pumpkin soup: Cut the pumpkin flesh into cubes and chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion without letting it brown. Add the pumpkin, pressed garlic, and spices. Mix everything well. Add chicken stock/bouillon and let the soup simmer under a lid for approx. 20 minutes. Blend the soup and season with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Crispy croutons: Cut the bread into cubes and toss with the oil. Spread the bread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and toast the bread in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 8 minutes, until the croutons are golden. Leeks: Cut the leeks into strips and steam them for 1 minute. Drain the leeks. Serve the soup with croutons, leeks, coriander, and bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1700 KJ (410 kcal). Carbohydrate: 69 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Kale salad with black beans and falafel
preparation: Mix yogurt with chives, sweet mustard, and pressed garlic to make a dressing. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Sprinkle the kale with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Peel the oranges and slice them. Squeeze the juice from the peel over the kale. Rinse and drain the beans. Toss the kale with oranges and beans and arrange in two bowls. Warm the falafel and distribute them in the salad. Top with pickled red onions and drizzle with the dressing.
notes: NOTE: This dish uses leftovers from the recipe for falafel with red onions. Fruit and vegetables approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate 63 g, Protein 20 g, Fat 15 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: New potatoes with lamb, crispy cabbage and dill
preparation: Season the lamb fillet with chopped rosemary, pressed garlic, salt and pepper. Squeeze lemon juice over it and let the meat marinate for a couple of hours. Scrub the potatoes and boil them until they are just tender. Halve the potatoes. Grill the meat on a hot grill pan for about 4 minutes on each side depending on how red you want the meat. Remove the meat from the pan. Halve the cabbage, remove the core and the outer leaves. Finely shred the cabbage. Sprinkle with sugar and salt, and massage it well. Slice the cucumber diagonally and the red onion into thin wedges. Toss the potatoes with cabbage, cucumber, onion, crumbled feta cheese and chopped dill. Stir a dressing of oil, vinegar, honey and mustard and drizzle over the salad. Slice the meat and arrange the salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1300 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 30 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Teriyaki marinated pork chops

ingredients.name: pork chops without fat edge, approx. 125 g

preparation: Teriyaki marinated pork chops: Mix the teriyaki sauce with ginger and put it in a freezer bag along with the pork chops. Tie a knot on the bag and massage the marinade into the meat. Let the meat marinate for approx. 30 minutes. Heat the oil in a pan. Take the pork chops out of the marinade, pat them dry, and brown them on both sides. Turn down to medium heat and fry the pork chops for approx. 3 minutes on each side. Remove the pork chops and keep them warm. Vegetables: Chop the onion. Cut the bell peppers into strips, and divide the broccoli into small florets. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Sauté the onion and vegetables in the pan over high heat while stirring for approx. 3 minutes. Add teriyaki sauce and bouillon and bring to a boil. Season the sauce with salt and pepper and fold in the spinach. Herb rice: Cook the rice as indicated on the packaging and fold in chopped herbs. Serve the teriyaki pork chops with vegetables and rice.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 70 g. Protein: 41 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Harira – Moroccan soup with chickpeas

ingredients.name: whole grain bread e.g. batbout (Moroccan bread)

preparation: Soak the chickpeas in a large bowl of water in the refrigerator overnight. Peel and chop the onions. Peel the carrots and cut the carrots and celery into small cubes. Optionally, blend all the vegetables finely in a food processor or mini chopper. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the vegetables for a few minutes. Cut the tomatoes into small cubes and mix with the vegetables. Drain the soaking water from the chickpeas. Chop the parsley and coriander and add to the pot. Grate the ginger finely and add it along with the turmeric, tomato puree, lentils, chickpeas, salt, pepper and bouillon. Bring the soup to a boil, turn down to low heat and let it simmer for 1½ hours under a lid. Mix the wheat flour and water together to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the soup and let it simmer for 10 minutes while stirring. Optionally thin the soup with a little water if it has become too thick. Season the soup with lemon juice, salt and pepper and sprinkle with chopped herbs. Serve with whole grain bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrate: 70 g. Protein: 26 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Green pasta with spinach, beans and broccoli
preparation: Green pasta: Thaw the vegetables. Boil water for the pasta. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging and drain. Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the broccoli, beans, and edamame beans for a couple of minutes with the chili flakes. Add the spinach and let it wilt. Add the bouillon and stir. Season with lemon zest, flaked salt, and pepper. Serving: Toss the cooked pasta with the sautéed vegetables and cottage cheese. Arrange and top with fresh basil.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 55 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Spinach waffles with shrimp, avocado and spinach

ingredient_sections.section_name: Spinach waffles (8 pcs. 4 double Belgian waffles)

preparation: Thaw the spinach and mix it with the eggs. Blend the oatmeal into flour and fold in the whole wheat flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir the flour mixture into the spinach-egg mixture along with the milk, and let the batter rest for about 30 min. Preheat your waffle iron. Brush with a little olive oil and pour ¼ of the batter onto the iron. Close the waffle iron and bake the waffles until they are golden. Repeat with the rest of the batter. Rinse and squeeze the spinach dry. Slice the bell pepper. Halve the avocado and remove the stone. Slice the avocado into thin slices and squeeze lemon juice over it. Top the waffles with spinach leaves, green pepper, avocado, and shrimp, and sprinkle chives over it. Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1200 KJ (300 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 20 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Pork in sweet and sour sauce
preparation: Mix water, vinegar, sugar and tomato paste in a pot and bring the mixture to a boil. Turn down to low heat so the sauce does not boil. Stir potato starch into cold water, and add it in a thin stream while stirring. Remove the pot from the heat. Heat 1 tbsp oil in another pot and brown the pork. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the meat. Cut pineapple, bell pepper and onion into cubes and slice the carrots. Sauté the vegetables in the remaining oil. Add the meat and the sweet and sour sauce and heat the dish through. Season the dish with salt and pepper. Serve with cooked rice.
notes: Tip! Fresh pineapple can be replaced with 250 g canned pineapple. Cornstarch can replace potato starch. The sauce should boil for a couple of minutes after the potato starch has been added. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (650 kcal), Carbohydrate: 94 g, Protein: 34 g, Fat: 11 g, of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Potato salad with pointed cabbage, blueberries and dill cream
preparation: Potato salad: Scrub the potatoes and boil them until just tender. Cool the potatoes. Halve the cabbage. Remove the outer leaves and the core, and shred the cabbage very finely – possibly using a mandoline. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Let it sit on the kitchen counter for at least 20 minutes. Feel free to massage it a little along the way. Rinse the blueberries. Dill cream: Mix the yogurt with mayonnaise and season with salt and pepper. Rinse and chop the dill and fold it into the dressing. Toss the potatoes with the dill cream and then with the pointed cabbage and blueberries, and arrange the salad in a large bowl or on a platter.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1300 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 47 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Risotto with pumpkin, roasted pumpkin seeds and crispy ham

ingredient_sections.section_name: Pumpkin, roasted pumpkin seeds and crispy ham

preparation:
Risotto: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in the oil in a pot until it is translucent without browning. Add the rice and sauté for a moment. Add the bouillon and bring to a boil while stirring. Turn down to low heat and let the rice simmer under a lid for approx. 15 minutes. Stir occasionally. If the rice is still not tender, add a little boiling water and cook for a bit longer – however, they should still retain a slight bite. Add a little water before serving so the consistency is like a smooth porridge. Season with salt and pepper.

Pumpkin, roasted pumpkin seeds and crispy ham: Peel the pumpkin, halve it, and remove the seeds. Cut the pumpkin flesh into cubes and fry them in the oil in a large pan along with whole sage leaves until the pumpkin flesh is brown and tender. Stir often and season with salt. Place the pumpkin seeds on a baking sheet and roast them in the oven at 180 degrees until the shell cracks slightly. Place the ham slices on a baking sheet with parchment paper and bake them at 180 degrees until they are crispy. Serve the risotto topped with pumpkin, pumpkin seeds, and crispy ham.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 70 g. Protein: 26 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Vegetarian patties with beetroot quinoa salad

ingredients.name: whole grain sandwich bread without crust

preparation: Vegetarian patties: Cut the bread into cubes and soak it in milk. Clean the vegetables. Grate the celeriac, carrots, leek, and onion in a food processor and pour into a bowl. Chop the parsley. Add half of the parsley – save the rest for the quinoa salad – along with the soaked bread, eggs, and egg white, and season with salt and pepper. Form the mixture into 16 patties and fry them until crispy in oil in a non-stick pan for about 5 minutes on each side. Beetroot quinoa salad: Cook the quinoa as indicated on the packaging and drain it. Peel the celeriac, beetroots, and carrots, and grate the root vegetables on the coarse side of a grater. Rinse and spin the arugula. Toss the quinoa with the root vegetables, arugula, parsley, and salad greens. Season with salt and pepper. Clean the leek and cut it into rings. Steam the leek for 1 minute and drain it. Sprinkle the leek rings over the quinoa salad and serve it with the vegetarian patties.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 21 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Cod in spicy green curry
preparation: Rinse the rice well and boil as indicated on the packaging. Peel and chop the onion. Press the garlic. Rinse and snap the beans. Rinse and slice the sugar peas. Heat the oil in a pan and add the green curry paste. Sauté the onion, garlic, and green beans for 2-3 min. Pour the bouillon into the pan and place the cod pieces in the pan. Cover with a lid and steam for approx. 5 min, until the cod is tender and flakes easily when pressed with a finger. Season the dish with soy sauce, lime, and fish sauce. Arrange the rice in bowls and serve with the cod in green curry, coriander, and sliced sugar peas as a crunchy topping.
notes: Energy distribution: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g, Protein: 40 g, Fat: 8 g (of which saturated fat: 1.5 g). Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g. Per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Salad tacos with cod rillette and cucumber
preparation: Season the cod with salt and pepper and squeeze lemon juice over it. Place it in an ovenproof dish lined with parchment paper, and bake in the oven at 170 degrees for approx. 12 minutes. Cool the fish before gently breaking it into flakes. Peel and finely chop the onion. Chop the chives. Mix the skyr with mayonnaise, onion, capers, and chives, and season with salt and pepper. Gently fold in the cod. Separate the lettuce into leaves. Rinse and spin them dry. Use a vegetable peeler to shave the cucumber into long, thick strips. Arrange the salad on a platter and top each leaf with a little "cod rillette" and cucumber strips. Serve with toasted rye bread – optionally as a crunch.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 125 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 700 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrates 14 g. Protein 17 g. Fat 3 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Buddha bowl with chicken, beans and guacamole

ingredients.name: beans, e.g. black beans or kidney beans

preparation: Buddha bowl: Place the chicken pieces in a pot with enough water to cover them, and boil for approx. 12 minutes. Drain the chicken and shred it with two forks. Rinse the beans thoroughly in a sieve and drain. Vegetables: Finely shred the cabbage. Prepare the broccolini. Remove the outermost leaves and the corn silk. Halve the corn and place them in a pot with enough water to cover them. Boil the corn for approx. 5 minutes. Add the broccolini to the pot for the last minute of boiling. Drain the vegetables and cut the corn off the cobs. Halve the tomatoes. Guacamole: Halve the avocados, remove the pits, and mash the avocados in a blender. Add pressed garlic, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and yogurt, and blend into a guacamole. Arrange the cabbage, beans, chicken, broccolini, corn, tomatoes, and guacamole in bowls. Top with cress and herbs.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 45 g. Protein: 42 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Bulgur salad with plaice, new carrots, spinach and spicy chickpeas

ingredients.name: chipotle (can be replaced by e.g. chili flakes)

preparation: Plaice rolls: Season the plaice with salt and pepper, and roll them up from the tail upwards. Place them in an ovenproof dish and add bouillon. Steam the plaice at 180 degrees for approx. 15 minutes, until they flake when you press lightly on them with a finger. Crispy chickpeas: Drain and dry the chickpeas. Heat oil in a non-stick pan, and fry the chickpeas with chipotle until they are well crispy. Season with salt. Bulgur salad: Cook the bulgur as indicated on the packaging and drain. Place the carrots on a baking sheet with parchment paper and season with salt and pepper. Bake them in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 15 minutes until they are well crispy. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Arrange the bulgur on 4 plates with the roasted carrots, spinach and fish rolls. Drizzle the juice from the fish over and top with watercress. Sprinkle the spicy chickpeas on top.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 43 g. Protein: 37 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Cod lasagna with spinach and fresh tomatoes

ingredient_sections.section_name: Cod lasagna with spinach and fresh tomatoes
