preparation: Cod lasagna with spinach and fresh tomatoes: Cut the fish into bite-sized pieces. Slice the tomatoes. Finely chop the onion and garlic. Clean and rinse the spinach. Spin it dry. Heat the oil in a pot, and brown the onion with the garlic for a few minutes. Add the spinach, and let it wilt. Season with salt and pepper. Bechamel sauce: Mix 1 dl of the milk with the cornstarch to make a slurry. Heat the rest of the milk in a pot, and stir in the slurry. Bring the sauce to a boil while stirring, season it with nutmeg, salt, and pepper, and melt half of the cheese into the sauce. Remove the pot from the heat. Layer the lasagna sheets, spinach, cod, tomatoes, and bechamel sauce in 4 greased dishes. Finish with a layer of sauce and tomatoes, and sprinkle the rest of the mozzarella cheese on top. Season with salt and pepper. Bake the lasagnas in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 30 minutes, until they are golden on the surface. Side dish: Rinse the lettuce, and spin it dry. Slice the bell peppers. Toss the lettuce with the bell peppers and balsamic vinegar. Serve the lasagna with the salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 57 g. Protein: 50 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Cod in tomato sauce with kale, capers and soft polenta
preparation: Cod in tomato sauce: Cut the aubergine into small cubes. Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pan, and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, and aubergine in it. Add the chopped tomatoes, vinegar, and sugar, and let the sauce simmer for about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Strip the kale and chop it finely. Add the kale to the sauce and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Cut the fish into smaller pieces and place them on top of the sauce. Turn them when the fish is almost white. Sprinkle capers over the sauce. Soft polenta: Pour boiling water into a pot with salt. Sprinkle in the polenta while stirring, and let it boil for about 5 minutes. If necessary, thin it out with more boiling water. The polenta should be like a smooth porridge. Serve the soft polenta with the cod in tomato sauce.
notes: Tip! The dish can also be prepared with meatballs made of minced pork and/or veal. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal), Carbohydrates: 54 g, Protein: 35 g, Fat: 11 g, of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Duck breast with cabbage salad, small roasted potatoes and cranberry sauce

ingredients.name: cabbage, e.g. white cabbage, savoy cabbage or red cabbage

preparation:
Roasted potatoes: Wash the potatoes and dry them well. Toss the potatoes with the oil and spread them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Chop the rosemary and sprinkle it over the potatoes. Season with salt and pepper and bake the potatoes in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 30 minutes, until they are golden and tender.

Duck breast: Score the skin on the duck breast fillets. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and brown the duck meat on the skin side. Place the meat in an ovenproof dish with the skin side facing up and season it with salt and pepper. Cook the meat in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 15 minutes.

Cabbage salad: Halve the head of cabbage. Remove the core and the outer leaves. Shred the cabbage very finely. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar and massage it well into the cabbage. Let it sit and soften for about 20 minutes. Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the core and cut the apples into wedges. Peel the oranges and cut them into segments. Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Toss the apples, oranges, and almonds with the cabbage and drizzle orange juice over it.

Cranberry sauce: Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion in it. Add balsamic and honey and let it simmer for a few minutes. Pour in the bouillon and bring to a boil. Add the cranberry juice and simmer the sauce over low heat for about 3 minutes. Add the cranberries and boil for about 5 minutes. Mix the cornstarch with a little water, pour the slurry into the sauce while stirring carefully, and let it boil for about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Serve the duck breast sliced with the cabbage salad, roasted potatoes and cranberry sauce.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2750 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrates: 64 g. Protein: 39 g. Fat: 25 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Oven-baked whiting with cumin carrots and mint yogurt
preparation:
Cumin carrots: Split the carrots and cut them into 1/2 cm thick diagonal slices. Boil the carrots with water and oil. Boil them without a lid until all the water has evaporated, add the cumin and pressed garlic, and sauté the carrots while stirring for 1 minute. Season with salt.

Oven-baked whiting: Slice the fennel into paper-thin slices, spread them in the bottom of an ovenproof dish, and drizzle with 1/2 dl water. Cut the whiting fillet into 4 pieces and sprinkle them with curry. Place the fish on top of the fennel and season the fish and fennel with salt. Place a slice of lime on each piece of fish and place the dish in a 200 degree oven for approx. 12 minutes.

Mint yogurt: Roughly chop the mint leaves. Mix the yogurt with the mint and season with salt and pepper.

Cook the couscous as indicated on the packaging and serve it with the oven-baked whiting and the carrots with the mint yogurt.
notes:
Tip! Instead of whiting, you can use any other fish in the cod family, e.g., pollock, grenadier, cod, saithe, ling, and plaice, as well as salmon or trout.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 60 g. Protein: 34 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Meatballs with mustard-braised cabbage

ingredients.name: minced veal and pork, max 10% fat
rapeseed or olive oil for frying
large pointed cabbage or summer cabbage
apple cider vinegar or light balsamic
large pointed cabbage or summer cabbage

preparation: Meatballs: Mix the meat with salt and pepper. Stir egg and grated onion into the meat, followed by oatmeal. Thin with milk until the mixture is soft but still firm enough to form meatballs. Optionally, let the mixture rest for a while. Form the mixture into approximately 12 meatballs using a tablespoon, and fry them until golden in a pan with the oil. Cabbage Salad: Finely shred the cabbage. Slice the spring onions into thin slices. Mix the cabbage and spring onions with vinegar, salt, and pepper, and let the salad marinate for at least 15 minutes. Mustard-braised Cabbage: Cut the cabbage into 2-3 cm thick slices and boil them in lightly salted water for 3-4 minutes until they are tender with a slight bite. Remove the cabbage from the cooking water. Whisk milk and flour together in a pot, and bring to a boil while stirring. Thin with the cabbage water until the sauce has a good thick consistency. Let the sauce simmer over low heat for 5 minutes. Stir the mustard into the sauce and toss in the cabbage. Season the sauce with salt, pepper, and possibly more mustard. Serve the meatballs with the mustard-braised cabbage and boiled potatoes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 2900 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 64 g. Fat: 30 g. Of which saturated fat: 9 g.

title: Steamed salmon with leeks, parsley sauce andJerusalem artichoke salad

ingredients.name: salmon fillet without skin and bones

preparation: Jerusalem artichoke salad: Scrub the Jerusalem artichokes thoroughly and slice them as thinly as possible. Slice the spring onions thinly, and cut the apples into small cubes. Mix the Jerusalem artichokes, onion, and apple with oil and lemon juice. Season the salad with salt and pepper. Steamed leeks and salmon: Rinse the leeks thoroughly. Cut the leeks into 8 cm pieces and place them in a wide-bottomed pot or pan. Cover halfway with water and steam the leeks under a lid for 8 minutes. Remove the leeks from the water with a slotted spoon, place them in a dish, and keep them warm. Cut the salmon into 4 pieces, season them with salt and pepper, and place them in the cooking water from the leeks. Steam the salmon under a lid for approx. 8 minutes, remove it, drain it slightly, and place it on top of the leeks. Parsley sauce: Rinse and pluck the parsley. Blend the parsley with the cooking water from the leeks and salmon, and season the sauce with salt and pepper. Serve the salmon with Jerusalem artichoke salad, leeks, parsley sauce, and boiled potatoes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 80 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Flatbread with pork, couscous salad and herbs
preparation: Couscous Salad: Prepare the couscous as indicated on the packaging and let it cool. Rinse and chop the lettuce. Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into small cubes. Fluff the couscous with a fork, and toss in the lettuce, tomato, cucumber, olives, and chopped parsley. Pork: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the meat with chopped rosemary for about 5 minutes until tender. Season the meat with salt and pepper. Yogurt Dressing: Mix the yogurt with garlic salt and chopped herbs. Season with pepper. Warm the tortillas and serve them with the couscous salad, pork, and yogurt dressing.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 80 g. Protein: 36 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Chickpea patties with sweet potatoes in crunchy cabbage salad with apple
preparation: Chickpea patties: Drain the chickpeas. Mix the flaxseeds with the water and let it sit for 10 minutes until it becomes a thick and gel-like consistency. Coarsely chop the onion, peel the sweet potatoes and grate them coarsely. Place half of the chickpeas in a food processor together with the coarsely chopped onion, flaxseed mixture, cumin, salt and pepper, and blend it to a smooth and creamy consistency. Place the mixture in a bowl and fold it together with the rest of the chickpeas, coarsely grated sweet potato, flour and finely chopped parsley. Let the mixture rest and bind for 20-30 minutes. If your mixture is very wet and loose, add more flour. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Shape the mixture into 8 patties and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake the chickpea patties in the oven for approximately 30 minutes until they are golden. Crunchy cabbage: Shred the cabbage and massage it with sugar and salt. Cut the apple into thin slices and toss with the cabbage. Garlic yogurt dressing: Mix the ingredients and season with pepper. Arrange the cabbage in 4 bowls and serve with chickpea patties, yogurt dressing and coarse bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 100 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 31 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Salmon Salad with Croutons

ingredients.name: thick slices of coarse wheat bread

preparation: Salad: Rinse the lettuce and spin it dry. Slice the lettuce crosswise into 2 cm wide strips. Rinse and snap the beans. Boil them in lightly salted water for 2 minutes. Rinse the beans in cold water and drain them. Finely chop the celery. Toast the bread and cut it into small cubes. Dressing: Stir the yogurt with the mayonnaise and mustard. Add the pressed garlic and the drained, chopped anchovy fillets. Season the cream with salt and pepper. Salmon: Brush the salmon with the oil and grill it on a hot grill pan for approximately 3 minutes on each side. Flake the salmon. Arrange the romaine lettuce with the beans, celery, and bread croutons. Distribute the salmon and freshly grated parmesan cheese into the salad. Drizzle the dressing over the salad.
notes: Tip! The anchovies cannot be replaced by spice-salted Danish "ansjoser" – it is a completely different product with a significantly different taste and consistency. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 42 g. Protein: 23 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Jerusalem artichoke soup with apples and crispy potato bread
preparation:
Jerusalem artichoke soup: Finely chop the onion. Peel the Jerusalem artichokes and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Peel the apples, remove stems and cores, and cut them into smaller pieces. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, Jerusalem artichokes, apples, and rosemary for a few minutes. Pour in the bouillon and let the vegetables simmer over low heat under a lid for approx. 30 minutes, until the Jerusalem artichokes are tender. Blend the soup to a smooth consistency. If the soup is too thick, thin it out with more bouillon if necessary. Season the soup with salt and pepper, and top with apples and fresh thyme.

Potato bread: Place the bread slices on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Top with cheese. Slice the potatoes into ultra-thin slices and arrange them in layers on the bread. Drizzle with olive oil and bake the bread in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes. Sprinkle with chopped rosemary and serve the bread with the soup.
notes:
Tip! Need some variation? Replace the amount of Jerusalem artichokes with celeriac and make a celeriac soup instead.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 84 g. Protein: 19 g. Fat: 16 g (of which saturated fat: 4 g).

title: Chicken tikka masala – Chicken in tandoori sauce
preparation: Marinated chicken: Make a few small incisions in each chicken breast. Peel garlic and chop it. Mix yogurt with spices, pressed garlic, ginger and tandoori masala. Toss the chicken well in this and let it marinate for at least 2 hours – preferably longer. Spread chicken and marinade in an ovenproof dish and bake in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 20 minutes. Sauce: Peel onion and garlic and chop them. Cut the tomato into cubes. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion. Add all spices and let them fry for a few minutes until the aromas are released. Add garlic and ginger. Add tomatoes and bell pepper in cubes and the chopped tomatoes and let the sauce simmer under a lid at medium heat for approx. 10 minutes. Blend the sauce until completely smooth. Toss the cooked chicken in the sauce and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Add cream and bring to a boil. Salad: Rinse and dry the lettuce and chop it coarsely. Shred the cabbage finely. Cut the cucumbers into slices and mix with lettuce and cabbage. Toss the vegetables with lemon juice. Sides: Garnish the dish with the green bell pepper cut into strips and fresh coriander and serve with salad and cooked rice as sides.
notes:
Tip! Instead of mango powder, you can use half a lime. Scrape the flesh and juice out of the lime with a teaspoon. Swap chicken breast for chicken thighs and bake the dish in the oven for approx. 40 minutes in total. Without the sauce, the chicken thighs can easily go into children's lunchboxes or be served with a tomato and onion salad for a quick lunch.

Fruit and vegetables*: Approx. 400 g (* per person, unless otherwise stated)

Energy distribution*: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate 68 g, Protein 40 g, Fat 16 g, thereof saturated fat 4 g (* per person, unless otherwise stated)

title: Salmon with spinach salad and grandma's dressing
preparation: Spinach salad: Boil the potatoes until just tender and let them cool. Optionally, cut them in half. Rinse the spinach and toss it dry. Snap off the woody bottom ends of the asparagus, and steam the asparagus for 2 minutes. Cool and slice the asparagus into strips. Peel and cut the onion into thin wedges. Halve the avocado and drizzle lemon juice over it. Cut the avocado into cubes or wedges. Peel the melon, remove the seeds, and cut the melon into cubes. Gently toss the potatoes with spinach, asparagus, onion, avocado, melon, and peas. Grandma's dressing: Stir the cream with lemon juice, sugar, and pepper until the cream thickens slightly. Salmon: Season the salmon with lemon pepper and salt and fry on a hot grill or grill pan for 3-5 minutes on each side. Serve the salmon with lime wedges and spinach salad, and drizzle the dressing over.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 47 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g.

title: Stuffed bell peppers with tomato sauce
preparation: Tomato sauce: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in the oil. Add the pressed garlic, tomatoes, paprika, and salt. Let the sauce simmer for 10 minutes. Stuffed bell peppers: Boil the rice for 10 minutes. Drain them in a sieve and let them cool. Finely slice the leeks. Mix the meat with the rice, leeks, salt, pepper, and oregano or thyme. Cut each bell pepper into 4 thick slices. Gently push the stems out through the stem ends. Spread the tomato sauce on the bottom of a large ovenproof dish. Place the bell pepper slices in the dish, and distribute the stuffing into the bell peppers. Smooth the surface with a spoon and brush with oil. Cover the dish with foil and bake the bell peppers in the oven at 200 degrees for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and bake the dish for another 10-15 minutes until the stuffing has gained some color and is fully cooked. Sprinkle the dish with chopped parsley and serve with bread.
notes: Tip! Instead of whole grain jasmine rice, you can use whole grain basmati rice which has the same cooking time. You can also use regular brown rice, but boil it for about 20 minutes first. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person. Energy distribution: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Veal Rump with Tarragon Potatoes, Garlic Dip and Vegetables
preparation:
Veal Rump: Trim off the fat edge. Season the rump with salt and pepper. Place it in a baking tray lined with parchment paper and place it in a preheated oven at 200 degrees. Roast the rump for approx. 30 minutes. Take it out of the oven and let it rest for 15 minutes.

Garlic Dip: Press the garlic. Mix the skyr or fromage frais with the garlic and season with salt and pepper.

Vegetables: Trim the beans. Cut the celery and carrots into approx. ½x½ cm thick sticks, the same length as the beans, about 5 cm. Boil the vegetables in lightly salted water until they are tender but still have a bite. Remove them from the water and let them cool.

Tarragon Potatoes: Boil the potatoes until tender in lightly salted water. Finely chop the shallots and sauté them in the oil in a pan. Toss the potatoes with the shallots and add the tarragon and wine vinegar. Pour the meat juices from the baking tray over the potatoes and heat everything through.

Slice the rump into thin slices. Serve the meat with the potatoes, vegetables, and garlic dip.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 208 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2139 KJ (509 kcal). Carbohydrate: 66 g. Fat: 9 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: One pot Italian whole grain pasta
preparation: Chop the onion. Cut the zucchini and bell peppers into cubes, and crush the garlic. Heat the oil in a large pan. Sauté the red onion with garlic, then add the zucchini, bell pepper, chicken fillet, and rosemary and fry for another couple of minutes. Add bouillon and pasta to the pan and stir. Place a lid on the pan and let it all simmer for approx. 12 minutes until the pasta is tender. Season with salt and pepper and top with basil.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 130 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 1800 KJ (400 kcal) Carbohydrate 55 g Protein 25 g Fat 10 g of which saturated fat 1 g * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Roasted cauliflower with black rice, apricots and almonds

ingredients.name: black whole grain rice (can be replaced with other whole grain rice)

preparation: Rinse the rice and cook it as indicated on the packaging. Drain the rice. Divide the cauliflower into smaller florets. Toss the cauliflower florets with oil, spices and salt, and spread them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake the cauliflower in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 25 minutes. Turn them halfway through. Mix the cauliflower with the rice, chopped apricots, chopped coriander and almonds.
notes: Tip! Instead of dried apricots, you can use raisins. And if you are not fond of coriander, use parsley instead. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1400 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrate: 50 g. Protein: 13 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Rye bread tartlets with summer salad
preparation:
Rye bread tartlets: Break the bread into smaller pieces. Crush the bread in a food processor or mini chopper. Add egg and 1 tbsp oil and blend into a uniform dough. Grease silicone or metal muffin molds with a little oil. Wet your hands slightly, and press the dough thinly into the molds. Bake the tartlets at 175 degrees for 20-25 minutes. Carefully remove them from the molds, and bake them for another 4-5 minutes in the oven so they become fully baked. Let them cool down.

Summer salad: Whisk the smoked cheese together with the skyr. Slice the cucumber and radishes into thin slices, and toss them in the dressing. Season with pepper and perhaps salt.

Distribute the summer salad into the rye bread tartlets just before serving. Garnish with pea sprouts. Sprinkle with finely chopped chives and freshly ground black pepper. Rinse and dry the lettuce, and break it into large pieces. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Mix the salad and tomatoes and serve with the tartlets.
notes:
Tip! Serve the rye bread tartlets as an appetizer, or use them on a buffet.
Approx. 16 pieces.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 28 g, Protein: 16 g, Fat: 10 g, of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Chicken Skewers with Summer Slaw and Grilled Corn
preparation: Chicken Skewers: Cut the meat into strips and place it in a freezer bag along with the spices, salt, olive oil, and lemon juice. Tie a knot in the bag and rub the marinade well into the meat. Let the meat marinate for about 1 hour. Place the meat on skewers and grill them for about 4-5 minutes. Turn the skewers during cooking. Summer Slaw: Remove the outer leaves and the core of the pointed cabbage. Shred the pointed cabbage very finely. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Let the cabbage rest for about 30 minutes. Cut the top and bottom off the fennel and slice it into ultra-thin slices. Chop the lovage. Mix the yogurt with mayonnaise, pressed garlic, and lovage. Toss the pointed cabbage with fennel and drizzle the dressing over it. Season with pepper. Grilled Corn: Grill the corn with the husks on for about 15 minutes until they are well charred. Remove the husks and halve the corn. Fried Potatoes: Wrap the potatoes in foil and grill them for about 15 minutes until they are golden. Serve the chicken skewers with summer slaw, grilled corn, and fried potatoes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 56 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Chicken Lasagna

ingredients.name: chicken fillet without skin and bone

preparation: Filling: Cut squash and bell pepper into small cubes. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Peel and chop the onion. Cut the chicken into small cubes. Heat the oil in a pot, and sauté the chicken with squash, bell pepper, and onion. Fry for approximately 5 minutes. Add pressed garlic, chopped tomatoes, and chopped thyme, and let the sauce simmer for about 5 minutes. Fold the spinach into the sauce, and season with salt and pepper. Remove the pot from the heat. Bechamel Sauce: Heat 4 dl of milk in a pot. Shake the remaining milk with the wheat flour to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the milk while stirring, and boil the sauce for about 2 minutes. Add nutmeg and mozzarella cheese, and season the sauce with salt and pepper. Layer lasagna sheets, filling, and bechamel in a greased ovenproof dish. Repeat and finish with a layer of bechamel. Sprinkle with mozzarella, and bake the lasagna in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 25 minutes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 65 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Shakshuka with beans and eggs

ingredients.name: kidney beans (250 g drained cooked beans)

preparation: Rinse and drain the beans. Peel and chop the onion, press the garlic. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Cut the bell pepper and zucchini into cubes. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Heat the oil in a large pan, and sauté onion, garlic, chili, and spices until the onions are translucent and the spices are fragrant. Add bell pepper and zucchini and stir. Next, add tomatoes and bouillon until it becomes a rich sauce. Let it simmer under a lid for about 5 minutes. Add the drained beans and spinach, and let the spinach wilt slightly. Crack the eggs into the sauce. Place a lid on, and let the eggs poach for 5-6 minutes, until the egg white is firm. Rinse and chop the parsley and sprinkle over the dish. Serve directly from the pan with coarse whole grain bread.
notes: Energy distribution* per person: 2200 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 62 g, Protein: 32 g, Fat: 13 g (including 3 g saturated fat). Fruit and vegetables* per person: Approx. 250 g.

title: Whole grain rice salad with vegetables, hot-smoked salmon and coriander dressing
preparation: Whole grain rice salad: Rinse the rice and cook it according to the instructions on the package. Place them in a sieve and let them drain. Snap the beans. Cut the broccoli into small florets. Boil the beans and broccoli in lightly salted water for about 3 minutes, until they are tender but still have a slight bite. Let the vegetables cool. Optionally, halve the beans. Slice the avocado into thin wedges and drizzle with lemon juice. Rinse the salad and spin it dry. Slice the spring onions and set them aside for later. Rinse the parsley and chop it. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Finely chop the garlic. Toss the rice with beans, broccoli, avocado, salad, parsley, chili, garlic and olive oil. Season the salad with wine vinegar, salt and pepper. Divide the salmon into smaller pieces and distribute it through the salad. Coriander dressing: Stir the yogurt with the mayonnaise and season with salt and pepper. Chop the coriander and stir it into the dressing. Top the rice salad with spring onions, drizzle with coriander dressing and serve with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 302 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 34 g. Fat: 30 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Cauliflower Gazpacho with Bread Croutons
preparation: Cauliflower Gazpacho: Divide the cauliflower into small florets. Take about ¼ of them and set aside for later. Peel the outer part of the cucumber in wide strips using a peeler. Set them aside for later. Cut the rest of the cucumber into small cubes. Cut the apple into quarters. Remove the core and cut the apple into small cubes. Steam the cauliflower in half of the bouillon until it is tender. Place the cauliflower and bouillon in a blender along with the cucumber, apple, and pressed garlic. Blend until it becomes a thick soup. Adjust the consistency with the rest of the bouillon. Season the soup with salt and pepper, and let it cool. Heat the oil in a pan. Add the curry powder and sauté the remaining cauliflower florets for a few minutes. Bread Croutons: Cut the bread into cubes and toss them with the oil. Spread the bread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Sprinkle with salt and thyme, and bake the croutons in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 10 minutes. Serve the soup with the croutons, cucumber strips, and sautéed cauliflower.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1400 KJ (350 kcal). Carbohydrate: 43 g. Protein: 11 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Thai tomato soup with curry-fried vegetables
preparation: Thai tomato soup: Chop the onion. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds and finely chop the chili. Heat the oil in a pot, and sauté the curry paste, onion, chili, pressed garlic, and ginger for a few minutes. Add the chopped tomatoes and bouillon, and let the soup simmer under a lid for approx. 10 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and blend the soup. Season the soup with salt and pepper. Curry-fried vegetables: Slice the leeks and clean them well. Slice the sugar peas. Heat the oil in a pan and brown the curry. Sauté the leeks and sugar peas in the pan over high heat for approx. 5 minutes while stirring. Serve the soup topped with the curry-fried leeks and sugar peas with bread as a side.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 57 g. Protein: 15 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Baked savory pancake with spinach, mushrooms, and quinoa
preparation: Preheat the oven to 220 degrees fan, and let two small pans (or one large one) get hot in the oven. It should be a steel or cast iron pan that is oven-safe. Put the flour in a bowl and whisk in the eggs. Dilute with milk and season the batter with chopped herbs, flaked salt, and pepper. Take the hot pans out of the oven and brush them gently with olive oil. Distribute the batter into the pans and place them back in the oven. Bake them for about 15 min. until they are golden. Meanwhile, prepare the topping. Rinse the quinoa and cook as recommended on the packaging. Clean the mushrooms and cut them in half, depending on the size. Peel the onion and slice it. Press the garlic. Cut the zucchini into small cubes. Rinse the spinach and shake it dry. Heat the oil in a pan, and sauté the mushrooms, onion, and zucchini over high heat for about 5 min. until the mushrooms get some color, while shaking the pan well. Add garlic and spinach, and remove the pan from the heat as soon as the spinach wilts slightly. Toss the filling with the cooked quinoa. Top the savory pancakes with the filling and serve with grilled or toasted bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 34 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Meatballs with kale and celeriac-potato gratin
preparation: Meatballs: Rinse and grate the kale, and boil it for 3-5 minutes in lightly salted water. Place the kale in cold water. Remove the kale and drain well. Squeeze the water out of the kale, and chop it with a knife. Mix the meat thoroughly with salt, and stir in finely grated onion, egg, and oats into the mixture. Add the milk gradually, and season with salt, allspice, and pepper. Stir in the chopped kale, and place the mixture in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. Celeriac-potato gratin: Cut the celeriac and potatoes into ½ cm thick slices. Cut the slices into strips, and blanch them in boiling, lightly salted water. Drain in a sieve. Whisk milk and flour together in a pot, and boil through for 5 minutes. Season with thyme or rosemary, grated nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Toss the drained strips of celeriac and potatoes well with the sauce, and fill an ovenproof dish or 4 ovenproof bowls. Grate the cheese over the top, and place the dish in the oven at 200 degrees fan oven for 30 minutes – until the gratin is fully cooked and the surface is golden brown. Shape the mixture into meatballs, and brown them in a hot pan with butter and oil. Place the pan in the oven, and finish cooking them for approx. 10 minutes. Serve the meatballs with the gratin.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 580 kcal (2400 KJ). Carbohydrates: 66 g. Fat: 19 g (of which saturated fat: 7 g).

title: Protein bowl with eggs and mexi-style beans
preparation: Pour boiling water over the edamame beans and drain. Halve the avocado, remove the pit, and slice the avocado. Drizzle with lemon juice. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Peel the mango and cut into small cubes. Rinse and drain the black beans. Boil the eggs for approximately 7 minutes until they are soft-boiled. Peel the eggs and halve them. Mix the skyr with flaked salt and pepper. Set aside some coriander for garnish. Rinse and chop the rest of the coriander and stir it into the skyr mixture. Distribute the cabbage at the bottom of two bowls. Top with small mounds of avocado, mango, cucumber, black beans, edamame beans, eggs, and dressing. Top with fresh coriander.
notes: Fruit and vegetables approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1800 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 33 g. Protein: 30 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g. Dietary fiber: 5.3 g.

title: Spicy Root Vegetable Soup with Cabbage Topping

ingredients.name: root vegetables e.g. potatoes, parsnips, carrots, parsley roots and celeriac

preparation: Root Vegetable Soup: Peel the root vegetables and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Peel and chop the onion. Heat the oil in a large pot, and sauté the onion and root vegetables in curry paste for about 5 minutes. Stir well throughout the process. Add ginger and pressed garlic and pour in the bouillon. Let the root vegetables simmer under a lid for about 20 minutes. Cabbage Topping: Remove the core and the outermost leaves of the cabbage, and finely shred the cabbage. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Heat the oil in a pan, and fry the cabbage in curry paste for a couple of minutes while stirring, until it wilts slightly. Add spinach and season with salt and pepper. Remove the cabbage from the heat. Blend the soup and season with salt and pepper. Serve the soup with the cabbage topping, a sprinkle of sesame, and coarse bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 50 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Tuscan pasta

ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes (can be replaced with canned chopped tomatoes)

preparation: Peel and finely chop the onion. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Cut the zucchini into cubes and slice the bell pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the onion, chili, zucchini, bell pepper, bacon, pressed garlic, and spices in it. Add the meat and brown it well, stirring the pot along the way. Add the cherry tomatoes and sugar, and let the meat simmer under a lid at low heat for about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging. Serve the pasta with the meat, grated parmesan cheese, lemon zest, and chopped parsley.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 285 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 64 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 4.5 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Thai salad with rice and beef
preparation: Rinse the rice and cook it in water with added pressed garlic as indicated on the packaging. Cool the rice. Season the steaks with salt and pepper, and grill the steaks for approx. 3 minutes on each side. Rinse and snap the beans, and steam them for 3 minutes. Drain the beans. Cut the avocado into wedges and drizzle lemon juice over it. Finely slice the leek and rinse it well. Dice the onion, and chop the mint and coriander. Toss the rice with the vegetables, mint, and coriander, and season the salad with salt and pepper. Slice the meat and top the salad with the meat. Drizzle chili sauce over.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate: 38 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Blue mussels in tomato
preparation: Scrub the mussels clean with a stiff brush under running cold water. Discard damaged mussels and mussels that do not close when tapped firmly against the edge of the table. Finely slice the onion and garlic. Cut the tomatoes into coarse cubes. Chop the parsley. Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil without letting them take color. The pot must be large enough to accommodate all the mussels. Add the tomatoes and sauté them for about 5 minutes. Add the mussels and steam them under a lid at high heat for about 5 minutes, until the mussels have opened. Fold in the parsley and serve the mussels with bread.
notes: Tip! Discard mussels that have not opened! Use a mussel shell to eat the soup with. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 160 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 17 g. Protein: 23 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Bhindi salan – Okra casserole with tomato and onion
preparation: Peel and cut the onions into wedges. Cut the ends off the okra. Split them so they are half length. Cut the tomatoes into large cubes. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and sauté the onions for about 5 minutes. Add all the spices and fry for 1 minute. Add the okra and tomatoes, and toss them well with the onions. Let the dish cook over medium-high heat for about 15 minutes. Stir the vegetables occasionally. Season with salt.
notes: Okra is a popular vegetable used in East Asian, Turkish, Arabic, Pakistani, and African cuisines. Okra pods are green, angular, long pods that taper at the ends and can resemble fingers. In English, they are therefore called ‘ladyfingers’. Turks know it as ‘bamiyan’ and in Persian it is called ‘bamiyeh’. The taste is slightly bitter, but otherwise quite neutral. Okra can be found fresh all year round at many specialty grocers. It is very important to rinse the okra in cold water and pat it dry before cutting off the ends and stems. If you cut the okra first and then rinse it, the cut pieces will fill with water. Okra tastes best when cooked in its own juices. Tip! The dish can be served with whole grain basmati rice or roti. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 425 KJ (100 kcal), Carbohydrate 8 g, Protein 4 g, Fat 5 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Iprax dolma – Stuffed vegetables

ingredients.name: whole grain jasmine rice or whole grain brown rice
celery stalks (the inner stalks with leaves on)
grape leaves (from a jar or package)

preparation:
Stuffed vegetables: Rinse the rice thoroughly. Boil them in 3 dl of water for 15 minutes. Place them in a sieve, let them drain, and cool down.

Peel the onion and boil it in water for about 10 minutes until it becomes soft. Let it cool. Save the cooking water. Make a cut through all the layers of the onion on one side, and carefully separate the layers from each other.

Cut the tops off the tomatoes and bell peppers, and save the tops to use as lids.

Cut the stems off the eggplants and zucchini and peel the potatoes. Carefully hollow out all the vegetables, including the tomatoes, using a corer. Save everything you have scooped out, including the center of the boiled onion.

Chop all the vegetable and potato pulp. Chop the celery and spring onions. Coarsely grate the carrots. Mix everything with the rice, tomato paste, salt, citric acid, and spices. Season with salt.

Put the rice filling into all the vegetables and into the onion layers. Put lids on the tomatoes and bell peppers. Save a little of the filling for the grape leaves.

Stuffed grape leaves: Wash the grape leaves, place them in a bowl, and pour boiling water over them. Let them steep in the water for 10 minutes, take them out, and let them drain.

Spread the grape leaves out and carefully cut the stem away. Distribute 1-2 tbsp of rice filling on each leaf. Fold the sides over the filling and roll them up.

Place the grape leaves at the bottom of a medium-sized pot. Place the stuffed vegetables tightly on top.

Mix the cooking water from the onion with oil and pour it over the vegetables. Dilute with extra water until it stands slightly below the surface. Place a plate on top so the vegetables are pressed down slightly. Put a lid on and bring to a boil. Turn down to low heat and let the dish simmer until the rice is tender, about 40-50 minutes. Lift the vegetables with a fork occasionally during cooking to prevent anything from burning.

Carefully pour off the water and turn the dish out onto a platter. You can place a large Arabic bread at the bottom to soak up some of the liquid.

Side: Serve the dish with Arabic whole wheat bread.
notes:
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 400 g per person, unless otherwise specified.
Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates 72 g, Protein 14 g, Fat 6 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Homemade fish meatballs

ingredients.name: cod or other lean fish, e.g., pollock, dark- or light scrod

preparation: Chop the fish meat coarsely in a blender or food processor together with the other ingredients for a short time, so the mixture does not become warm. Let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for half to a full hour. Warm the fat in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Remove the pan from the heat. Shape the meatballs with a spoon and place them on the pan. Put the pan back on the heat and fry the meatballs over medium heat for approximately 8 minutes on each side.
notes: Tip! You can make your own remoulade by mixing four tablespoons of pickles with 2 tablespoons of mayonnaise. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate: 14 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 11 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Grilled tenderloin in salad with summer berries

ingredients.name: summer berries e.g. strawberries, raspberries and blueberries

preparation: Grilled tenderloin: Season the tenderloin with salt, pepper and rosemary. Brown the tenderloin on the grill, and then place it over indirect heat and close the lid. Grill the tenderloin for approx. 10 minutes – turn it during the process. If it feels very soft, it needs a little longer. Remove the tenderloin from the heat and let it rest for approx. 10 minutes before slicing. Salad with summer berries: Scrub the potatoes and boil them until just tender. Cool the potatoes before slicing them. Rinse the lettuce and spinach, and spin them dry. Cut the cauliflower into very small florets. Rinse and pick the berries. Halve them. Chive cream: Mix yogurt with mayonnaise and chopped chives and season with salt and pepper. Toss the salads with potatoes, cauliflower, berries and peas. Distribute the meat into the salad, and drizzle the dressing over before serving. Top with dill.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 39 g. Protein: 32 g. Fat: 11 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Beetroot Carpaccio with Feta
preparation: Peel the beetroots and cut them into slices as thin as possible, preferably using a sharp mandoline. Finely chop the garlic with the fennel seeds and mix them together with oil, vinegar, and salt in a large bowl. Toss the beetroots thoroughly with the dressing so that all slices are coated. Let them marinate for 30 minutes or more. Spread the beetroot slices out on 4 large plates. Crumble the feta over the beetroots and sprinkle with finely chopped chives. Serve with bread.
notes: Tip! The beetroots only get better by marinating, preferably until the next day in the refrigerator. Serve the beetroot carpaccio as an appetizer or a small lunch dish. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person. Energy distribution: 1500 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate: 45 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g per person.

title: Niçoise Salad with Smoked Mackerel and Eggs

ingredients.name: whole grain pita bread at 80 g

preparation: Boil the eggs for approximately 8 minutes, and cool. Peel the eggs and cut them in half. Trim the beans and boil them in lightly salted water for 4 minutes. Drain and pour cold water over them. Wash the lettuce and spin it dry. Slice the potatoes. Halve the tomatoes. Whisk the dressing ingredients together and toss with the salad. Grill the pita breads on a grill pan for about 3 minutes on each side. Arrange the gem lettuce with eggs, potatoes, beans, and tomatoes. Distribute the mackerel over the salad and top with cress. Season with pepper and serve with pita bread.
notes: A crisp salad with smoked mackerel, boiled eggs, and leftover boiled potatoes is appetizing, filling, and heart-friendly. If you have leftovers, it tastes wonderful for lunch the next day. Fruit and vegetables approximately 270 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate 55 g, Protein 30 g, Fat 24 g (including 5 g saturated fat), Dietary fiber 10 g.

title: Karniyarik – Beef-stuffed eggplants
preparation:
Eggplants: Turn the oven to grill at 250 degrees. Split the eggplants. Place them with the round side facing down in a large ovenproof dish or in a baking tray with parchment paper. Brush them with 1 tbsp oil. Roast the eggplants under the grill in the oven at 250 degrees until they are golden brown on the surface, approx. 15 minutes. Lower the oven heat to 200 degrees without grill. The eggplants are now completely soft inside. Press them in the middle with a fork to make room for the filling.

Filling: Peel the onion and chop it. Heat oil in a pan and fry the onion at medium heat until it is slightly soft. Add the meat and brown it with the onions. Cut the peppers and tomato into small cubes. Finely chop the garlic. Fry the vegetables and garlic with the onion and meat, and season with salt, chili, and plenty of pepper. Distribute the filling onto the eggplants.

Topping: Cut the pepper into strips and place them on top of the filling. Garnish with tomato slices. Mix the tomato puree with ¾ dl boiling water. Drizzle the mixture over the stuffed eggplants. Bake the eggplants in the middle of the oven for 20-30 minutes until they are brown on the surface.

Side Dish: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into wedges. Toss them with oil on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bake them in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 30 minutes. Season with salt. Serve the baked eggplants with potato wedges.
notes:
Tip! Instead of long thin green peppers, you can use thick strips of regular green pepper. You can serve the dish with a bowl of salad.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 400 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 59 g, Protein: 25 g, Fat: 20 g (including saturated fat: 4 g).

title: Christmas salad with red cabbage and orange

ingredient_sections.section_name: Christmas salad with red cabbage and orange

preparation: Remove the stem and the outer leaves from the christmas lettuce. Cut the lettuce into strips. Remove the stem and the outer leaves of the red cabbage and shred it finely. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar and massage it well. Cut the orange into segments, and the red onion into thin rings – e.g., sliced with a mandoline. Arrange the christmas lettuce and red cabbage at the bottom of a dish and top with orange, cranberries and red onion. Drizzle balsamic vinegar and olive oil over the top.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 160 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 350 KJ (100 kcal). Carbohydrates: 10 g. Protein: 2 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Æggekage (Danish Egg Cake)
preparation: Fry the bacon until crispy in a pan without fat and let the fried bacon slices drain on a piece of paper towel. Pour most of the frying fat away, but leave about 1 tsp in the pan. Slice the potatoes into thick slices and sauté them in the pan for a couple of minutes. Mix eggs, potato starch, milk, salt, and pepper together in a bowl and pour the mixture over the potatoes. Turn down to medium heat and cover the pan with a lid or aluminum foil. Let the egg cake fry for 10-15 min until all the egg mixture has set. Slice the tomatoes into wedges and place them and the bacon slices on top of the egg cake. Sprinkle with finely chopped chives.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 75 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1225 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrate: 46 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g (per person, unless otherwise stated).

title: Everyday chicken with potatoes and vegetables

ingredients.name: herbs e.g. parsley, chives or coriander

preparation: Chicken in dish: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees fan air. Optionally debone the chicken thighs – it is not strictly necessary. Peel the onion and cut into thin wedges. Press the garlic. Peel the carrots, scrub the Jerusalem artichokes and potatoes and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Place the potatoes, vegetables and chicken in an ovenproof dish and toss with olive oil. Season with herbs, and pour the bouillon into the dish. Season with a little flaked salt and pepper. Place the dish in the oven and bake for approx. 40 min., until the chicken and vegetables are tender. Turn gently along the way. Yogurt dressing: Press the garlic, rinse and chop the herbs. Mix the yogurt with mustard, garlic and herbs. Serving: Serve the chicken, potatoes and vegetables in the dish with a drizzle of the yogurt dressing. Season with pepper.
notes: The dish is also suitable for those who want to lower their blood pressure and eat less salt. Rosemary, garlic and thyme give the chicken a wonderful flavor, allowing you to use less salt. Chicken thighs with coarse vegetables served with a dip made of lean dairy products is a delicious option for dinner. Quick and easy to make. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 55 g, Protein: 29 g, Fat: 15 g (of which saturated fat: 2.5 g). Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person.

title: Seafood Risotto with Summer Greens
preparation: Seafood: Clean the mussels and remove the beard. Discard any mussels that do not close when you tap them lightly against the edge of the sink. Steam the mussels in white wine until they open. Remove approximately half out of the shells. Keep the rest in the shells. Strain the liquid and save it for the risotto. Risotto: Chop the onions and press the garlic. Cut the top and bottom off the fennel and dice it into small pieces. Snap off the woody bottom ends of the asparagus. Heat the oil in a large sauté pan and fry the langoustine tails and prawns for about 1 minute over high heat. Remove the seafood, and sauté the onions, pressed garlic, fennel, and risotto rice until the rice is golden. Add the liquid from the mussels. Gradually add bouillon, and let the rice simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes until they are tender and the bouillon has reduced. If the risotto is too dry, add a little more bouillon. Rinse and chop the parsley. Fold the chopped parsley, grated parmesan cheese, asparagus, fresh shelled peas, langoustine, tiger prawns, and all the mussels into the risotto. Season the risotto with salt and pepper and serve with lemon.
notes: Fruit and vegetables approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates 82 g, Protein 35 g, Fat 10 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: Grilled plaice with beans and herb dressing
preparation:
Grilled plaice: Clean the plaice and pat them dry with paper towels. Brush them with oil. Place them on a hot grill. Using a grill net is recommended so the fish does not stick. Season with salt and pepper. Grill the fish for approximately 5 minutes on each side, depending on how thick they are.

Herb dressing: Rinse the dill and chives. Pick the dill and roughly chop the chives. Blend the herbs with the creme fraiche until the herbs are finely minced. You can thin it with a little water if the dressing is too thick. Season with salt and pepper.

Trim the beans. Boil them in a pot with a little water at the bottom for 4 minutes under a lid. Let them drain.

Serve the fish with boiled potatoes, beans, and herb dressing.
notes:
Tip! Instead of plaice, you can use other flatfish such as flounder or lemon sole. If you do not have a grill net, the best way to ensure the fish does not stick is to make sure the grill grate is very hot from the start, and avoid moving the fish before it has developed a beautiful, firm grill pattern; it will often release on its own. Use a long, thin metal spatula to loosen the fish gently and to flip it carefully. Never clean the grill grate with soap, as this can cause fish and other items to stick.

Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 150 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 54 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Grilled saithe and carrots with potato salad
preparation:
Cold potato salad: Boil the potatoes until tender in lightly salted water. Let them cool, and slice them. Clean the radishes and spring onions, and slice them. Mix skyr, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, pepper, apple cider vinegar, and honey together. Toss the potatoes, radishes, and onions in the dressing. Season with salt and possibly more pepper, mustard, vinegar, and/or honey. 

Grilled saithe and carrots: Cut the heads and tails off the fish, and clean it inside. Clip off the fins. Cut each saithe into 4 large pieces. Scrub or peel the carrots, and split them. Toss the carrots with 1 tbsp of oil, and brush the fish with the rest of the oil. Grill the carrots and saithe on a well-heated grill. Grill the fish until it has a nice grill pattern, and the carrots until they are tender but still have a bit of bite. Season with salt and pepper, arrange on a platter, and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve with potato salad.
notes:
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. 
Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 56 g. Protein: 44 g. Fat: 23 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Spiced pork sirloin with oven-roasted root vegetables, honey potatoes and mustard dressing

ingredients.name: white root vegetables, e.g., celery root, parsley root and/or parsnip

preparation:
Spiced pork sirloin: Trim almost all the fat off the sirloin. Leave at most 1 mm of fat remaining. Lightly dice the fat. Season with salt and pepper. Coarsely crush the spices with a knife on the cutting board, and sprinkle them on both sides of the roast. Place the roast in a small ovenproof dish, and roast it at 200 degrees for 35-40 minutes.

Oven-roasted root vegetables: Peel the root vegetables and cut them into coarse, bite-sized pieces. Toss them with oil and spread them out on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake them in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 30 minutes. Toss the root vegetables with coarsely chopped parsley and season with salt.

Honey potatoes: Boil the potatoes until tender in lightly salted water and drain them in a sieve. Heat the honey in a pan until it bubbles, and fry the potatoes in the honey until they are golden brown. Add chopped thyme.

Mustard dressing: Mix the mustard with farin and possibly thin it out with a little cold water to a thin dressing.

Slice the sirloin into thin slices and serve with honey potatoes, root vegetables, and drizzle with mustard dressing.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 89 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Pulled chicken burger

ingredients.name: skinless and boneless chicken breast fillet

preparation: Pulled chicken: Boil the chicken in water with added bouillon for about 15 min. Remove the chicken from the water and shred it. Mix with a little of the cooking water so that it remains juicy. Coleslaw: Finely shred the two types of cabbage. Peel the carrots and grate them on the coarse side of a grater. Mix yogurt with mayonnaise and mustard and season with salt and pepper. Toss the dressing with the cabbage, carrots, and chopped parsley. Barbecue sauce: Put ketchup, vinegar, sugar, and chili sauce in a saucepan. Simmer over very low heat for about 5 minutes and let cool. Halve the burger buns and fill with coleslaw, chicken, sliced pickled cucumbers, and barbecue sauce. Serve the remaining coleslaw as a side dish.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrate: 55 g. Protein: 37 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Green pearl barley risotto with spinach, asparagus, peas and dill
preparation: Rinse the pearl barley. Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a sauté pan and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, and pearl barley for a couple of minutes. Pour in the stock and let the pearl barley simmer under a lid at low heat for about 30 minutes, until it is tender. Rinse the spinach and let it drain. Snap off the woody bottom ends of the asparagus. Cut the asparagus into strips. Add the spinach, asparagus, and peas to the pearl barley and let it simmer for another couple of minutes until the spinach wilts. Gently fold in the cream cheese until it is melted and the pearl barley risotto is creamy. Season with chopped dill, salt, and pepper. Serve with crusty bread.
notes: Tip! Instead of pearl barley, you can use pearl spelt or risotto rice. Fruit and vegetables approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (476.2 kcal). Carbohydrates 75.1 g. Fat 15.5 g. Of which saturated fat 5.5 g.

title: Whole grain pizza with ricotta, potatoes, zucchini and rosemary
preparation: Dough: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt, and knead the durum wheat first and then the wheat flour into the dough. Knead until the dough is smooth and supple. Place the dough covered to rise in a warm place for about 1 hour. Topping: Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin slices. Slice the zucchini. Cut the onion into thin wedges. Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each piece out into a round pizza. Place each of them on a piece of baking paper. Spread the bases with ricotta. Subsequently top with potatoes, zucchini, onion and chopped rosemary. Drizzle olive oil over the pizzas, and season with salt and pepper. Bake the pizzas one at a time – preferably on a baking stone – in the oven at 250 degrees fan at approx. 8 minutes, until they are crispy. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Top the pizzas with spinach.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 71 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Pan-fried halibut with roasted fennel and sage potatoes
preparation: Sage potatoes: Scrub the potatoes and dry them well. Chop the sage leaves. Toss the potatoes with oil and sage and spread them in an ovenproof dish. Season with salt and pepper. Roast the potatoes in the oven at 200 degrees for approximately 30 minutes. Pan-fried halibut: Scale the fish skin so it can be eaten after being fried. Cut the fish into 4 roughly equal pieces. Score the skin lightly with a sharp knife. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the fish skin-side down for approximately 1 minute at high heat. Turn down to medium heat and fry for approximately 3-4 minutes. Flip the fish and fry it until finished, approximately 1 minute, at high heat. Roasted fennel: Cut the top and bottom off the fennel bulbs and cut them into quarters. Cut the carrots into slices or cubes. Rinse and drain the spinach. Heat the oil in a pan and fry the fennel and carrots at high heat until they are almost tender. Add the orange juice and spinach, and let the spinach wilt. Remove the vegetables from the heat and season with salt and pepper. Serve the halibut with roasted fennel and sage potatoes.
notes: Tip! Instead of halibut, you can use cod, pollock, or red mullet.

title: Teriyaki chicken with vegetable noodles
preparation: Teriyaki chicken: Mix the teriyaki sauce, ginger, pressed garlic, and lime juice, and pour the marinade over the chicken. Let the chicken marinate while the vegetables are prepared. Heat the oil in a pan, and fry the chicken and marinade for approximately 5 minutes at high heat until it is cooked through. Vegetable noodles: Cut the leek and carrots into strips. Chop the kale coarsely. Boil the vegetables in lightly salted water for about 2 minutes and drain. Cook the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain. Toss the noodles with the vegetables, chicken, and fresh coriander.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate: 47 g. Protein: 27 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Pot-roasted lamb culotte with shallots and carrot salad

ingredients.name: bouillon, e.g., lamb, chicken or veal bouillon

preparation:
Pot-roasted lamb culotte with shallots: Trim the fat layer off the culottes. Peel the onions and garlic. Halve the garlic. Heat the oil in a pot and brown the meat on all sides. Remove the meat and brown the onions in the pot for 4-5 minutes. Place the meat back into the pot and season with salt and pepper. Add garlic, thyme sprigs, white wine, and bouillon and bring to a boil. Turn down the heat and let the meat and onions simmer for 15 minutes under a lid. Remove the meat and let it rest under foil. Bring the sauce and onions to a boil, dissolve the cornstarch in water and thicken the sauce. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Carrot salad: Peel the carrots. Slice the carrots into thin slices using a potato peeler. Also cut thin strips of celery using a peeler. Place all strips in a large bowl of ice-cold water and let them soak for 20 minutes until they curl slightly. Dry the vegetables well in a kitchen towel. Mix olive oil and lemon juice in a large bowl. Pick the leaves off the thyme and mix them into the dressing along with the vegetable strips, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Slice the lamb culottes into thin slices and serve them with the onions and sauce, boiled potatoes, and carrot salad.
notes: Tip! Instead of lamb culotte, you can use veal culotte. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 239 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2408 KJ (573 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 63 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Rice pilaf with beef and raita
preparation: Rice pilaf: Cook the rice as indicated on the packaging. Coarsely chop the onions. Cut the cabbage, bell pepper, and zucchini into small cubes, approx. 1×1 cm. Cut the beans into 2 cm pieces. Halve the tomatoes. Sauté the meat in oil in a large pan until browned. Add all vegetables except the tomatoes and sauté them with the meat for about 10 minutes while stirring. Add tomatoes, finely grated ginger and garlic, garam masala, curry, and salt. Sprinkle with chopped parsley or coriander. Raita: Stir the yogurt with cumin and salt. Serve the pilaf with raita, mango chutney, and lemon wedges.
notes: Tip! Feel free to use leftover rice for this dish. You can use any other kinds of vegetables; this dish is a true 'empty the fridge' meal. Energy distribution: 2800 KJ (700 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 79 g, Protein: 38 g, Fat: 18 g, of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Salmon with stir-fried vegetables

ingredients.name: cabbage, e.g. kale, white cabbage or savoy cabbage

preparation: Vegetables: Remove the outer leaves and the core of the cabbage and finely shred the cabbage. Slice the carrots into diagonal half-slices. Slice the bell pepper into strips. Rinse and spin the spinach. Split the chili, remove the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Heat the oil in a wok or a wide-bottomed pan and fry the cabbage and carrots with the chili and pressed garlic for about 3 minutes. Add the bell pepper to the wok and fry for an additional 2 minutes. Fold in the spinach and let it wilt. Chop the coriander and add half of it, then season the vegetables with fish sauce and lime juice. Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain them. Toss the noodles with the remaining coriander. Salmon: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the salmon for about 3 minutes on each side. Season with salt and pepper. Serve the salmon with noodles and stir-fried vegetables.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 64 g. Protein: 33 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Chili sin carne
preparation: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water for 10-12 hours. Drain the soaking water and boil the beans in plenty of lightly salted water for about 45 minutes. Drain the beans in a colander or sieve. Split the chili lengthwise. Remove the seeds and finely chop the chili. Chop the onion. Slice the celery and bell pepper and cut the tomatoes into wedges. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, and celery without letting them brown. Add the bell pepper, tomatoes, oregano, and cumin and stir everything well. Add the canned tomatoes and tomato paste to the pot and let the vegetables simmer for 5 minutes without a lid. Add the beans and let everything simmer for about 10 minutes without a lid. Season the chili with salt, pepper, and optionally more chili. Finely chop the onion. Cut the bell pepper into small cubes and the cucumber into slices. Serve the chili with onion, bell pepper, cucumber, chopped coriander, sour cream, and bread.
notes: Tip! The dried beans can be replaced with 1 can of drained beans. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (451 kcal). Carbohydrates: 55 g. Protein: 22 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Rice noodles with beef and vegetables

ingredients.name: whole grain rice noodles or other whole grain noodles

preparation: Slice the carrots, leeks, and celery. Halve the bell peppers and cut them into slices. Brown the meat in a large pan in 1 tbsp of oil, and place it on a plate. Fry the vegetables in the remaining oil for 4-5 minutes while stirring. Finely chop the garlic and toss it with the vegetables along with the meat and peas or edamame beans. Add the bouillon. Mix the cornstarch with the soy sauce and 2 tbsp of water. Stir the mixture into the vegetables and bring to a boil while stirring. Chop the coriander and sprinkle over the dish. Cook the noodles as indicated on the packaging and serve with the sauce.
notes: Tip! This recipe contains a little meat and many vegetables. The amount of meat is only 200 grams, which corresponds to approximately half a pack. You can freeze the rest of the meat and use it another day, or you can use all the meat in the sauce. You can use all kinds of vegetables in the sauce; feel free to empty your vegetable drawer for what you have, or replace one or more vegetables in the recipe with others. Energy distribution: 2200 KJ (600 kcal) per person. Carbohydrate: 57 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Lightly Cured Veal Brisket with Horseradish Sauce
preparation:
Brine: Put water, salt, and sugar in a pot and boil it until the salt and sugar are dissolved. Cool the brine. Place the veal brisket in the brine under pressure, so the meat is covered by the brine. Place the meat in the refrigerator for 1-2 days.

Lightly cured veal brisket: Rinse the meat well under cold water. Put the meat, herbs, and spices in a pot and add enough water to just cover it. Bring the meat to a boil over even heat, skim off the foam, and then turn down the heat. Let the meat simmer at low heat for approx. 1½-2 hours until the meat is tender.

Horseradish sauce: Put vinegar and sugar in a pot and bring to a boil. Add the cooking liquid and milk. Stir cornstarch with a little cold water to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the sauce while it is boiling. Season the sauce with pepper and boil it through for approx. 5 minutes. Add horseradish to taste.

Slice half of the meat into slices and serve it with boiled potatoes, steamed broccoli, steamed green beans, and horseradish sauce. Garnish optionally with chopped chives.
notes:
Tip! Serve the rest of the meat cold with a horseradish cream: Mix 2 dl of 9% sour cream with 1 tsp of mustard and 1 tbsp of low-fat mayonnaise. Add freshly grated horseradish to taste. Season the cream with salt and pepper.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution: 1900 KJ (450 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 50 g. Fat: 9 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Potato omelet with pea mash and hot-smoked salmon

ingredients.name: frozen peas (if using fresh shelled peas, you do not need to boil them first)

preparation: Pea mash: Put the peas in a pot and bring to a boil. Drain the peas and blend with pressed garlic and creme fraiche. Potato omelet: Whisk eggs with milk and season with salt and pepper. Peel and finely chop the onion. Lightly mash the potatoes and fold them into the egg mixture along with the onion. Add 1 tsp. of oil to a non-stick pan, and pour about a quarter of the egg mixture onto the pan. Fry until the egg mixture has set. Gently turn the omelet onto a plate and keep it warm. Repeat with the remaining oil and egg mixture, so you fry 4 omelets in total. Topping: Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Remove the skin from the salmon and shred it with a fork. Top the warm omelets with baby spinach, pea mash, salmon and chives and fold together. Serve the omelets with rye bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (590 kcal). Carbohydrate: 40 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 29 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g.

title: Pointed cabbage salad with spring greens, lentils and smoked mackerel
preparation: Pointed cabbage salad: Rinse the lentils and boil as indicated on the packaging. Drain the lentils and save half for day 2. Halve the cabbage, remove the core and the outer leaves. Shred the cabbage finely. Sprinkle with sugar and salt and massage the cabbage. Set half aside and save in a freezer bag for day 3. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus. Steam them for 2 min. and drain. Set half aside and save for day 3. Slice the asparagus into strips. Rinse and dry the blueberries. Slice the spring onions and chop the dill. Save the rest of the dill for day 3. Mustard dressing: Mix the ingredients for the mustard cream together and fold in the cabbage so it becomes slightly creamy. Serving: Cut the head and tail off the mackerel. Open it carefully like a book, and remove the bone and the dark part of the meat. Divide the light meat into fine pieces. Distribute the lentils into two deep bowls. Top with the creamy pointed cabbage, asparagus, and blueberries. Place pieces of mackerel on top of the salad, and sprinkle with spring onions and dill.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2800 KJ (670 kcal). Carbohydrates: 41 g. Fat: 35 g. Of which saturated fat: 8 g. Small smoked mackerel can be replaced by store-bought Keyhole-labeled fish cakes.

title: Bean salad with anchovies

ingredients.name: sherry vinegar or red or white wine vinegar

preparation: Soak the beans in a large bowl with plenty of cold water. Place the beans in the refrigerator overnight or for a minimum of 10 hours. Drain the soaking water. Place the beans in a pot, cover them with fresh water, and let them boil for 30-90 minutes until they are tender without being overcooked. Pour the beans into a sieve and cool them down. Finely chop the garlic and chop the parsley very coarsely. Remove the seeds from the chili and chop it finely. Slice the spring onions into thin rings and cut the bell peppers into small cubes. Slice the celery into slices 1/2 cm thick. Cut each anchovy fillet into 2-3 diagonal strips. Mix the oil and vinegar together in a large bowl. Toss all the vegetables, beans, garlic, parsley, chili, and anchovies together with the dressing. Season the salad with salt and pepper. Let the salad sit for 1/2-1 hour before serving. Serve with crusty bread.
notes: Tip! Butter beans are also called "butterbeans". Canned beans can replace the dried beans. Calculate 2 cans. Rinse them in cold water and let them drain in a sieve before mixing them with the other ingredients. Energy distribution per person: 400 kcal, Carbohydrate 42 g, Protein 14 g, Fat 15 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: Daal with yogurt and chili-roasted chickpeas
preparation: Daal: Peel and chop the onion. Press the garlic. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Halve the bell pepper, remove the seeds, and cut the bell pepper into cubes. Heat the oil in a pot, and sauté the onion with garlic and ginger for about 1 min. Add curry, cumin, coriander, chili, and bell pepper, and sauté for a few minutes. Rinse the lentils and add them to the pot along with the bouillon and cherry tomatoes. Let it simmer for about 30 min under a lid. Stir the pot regularly, and add a little more bouillon if the consistency becomes too dry. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Roasted chickpeas: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and roast the chickpeas over high heat until they are golden. Season with chili flakes and flaked salt. Serve the daal in bowls topped with yogurt, roasted chickpeas, and chopped parsley. You can optionally make a double portion and freeze the rest. That way, you have easy and healthy food for another day.
notes: Well-spiced, filling, and delicious daal is perfect winter food. The dish is both cheap, healthy, and packed with green proteins. You can also use chopped or peeled tomatoes instead of cherry tomatoes.

title: Mini fish cakes with potato salad
preparation: Homemade corn remoulade: Remove the outer leaves of the corn and boil them for approximately 5 minutes. Cut the corn from the cob. Divide the cauliflower into small florets. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Chop the parsley. Mix the skyr with mayonnaise, mustard, capers, parsley, and vegetables and season with salt and pepper. Mini fish cakes: Sprinkle the cod with salt and chop the fish in a food processor or blender. Peel the onion, grate it coarsely, and stir it into the mixture along with the egg, oats, and chopped parsley. Stir in the water little by little, and season the mixture with freshly ground pepper. Place the mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Form small fish cakes using a spoon dipped in cold water, and fry them slowly until golden and cooked through in the pan – 6-7 minutes on each side. Potato salad: Scrub the potatoes and boil them until they are just tender. Cool the potatoes and slice them. Slice the cucumber. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus. Steam the asparagus for 2 minutes, drain, and slice into strips. Cut the tomatoes into quarters. Mix the yogurt with mustard and season with salt and pepper. Toss the yogurt with the potatoes, cucumber, asparagus, and tomatoes. Sprinkle with cress. Serve the fish cakes with corn remoulade and the potato salad with summer vegetables.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 36 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Bean salad with cauliflower, chicken and avocado dressing
preparation:
Bean salad: Brown the chicken on both sides in the oil in a pan. Turn down the heat and let the chicken simmer for 5 minutes on each side. Season with salt and pepper, and let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Trim the beans and boil them in lightly salted water for 4 minutes. Let them drain in a sieve. Slice the cauliflower into thin slices. Rinse and dry the lettuce, and break it into large pieces, leaving the small inner leaves whole. Slice the chicken into thin slices. Mix the lettuce, cauliflower, chicken, and beans in a large bowl or on a platter.

Avocado dressing: Scoop the avocado flesh out of the skin with a spoon. Finely chop the chives. Blend the avocado with 2/3 of the chives and the lemon juice. Thin with water until the dressing has a good dressing consistency. Season with cayenne pepper and a little salt. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and sprinkle with the remaining chives.

Serve the salad with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 400 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2800 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 40 g. Fat: 28 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Baked sweet potatoes with garlic skyr, chickpeas and root vegetable salad

ingredients.name: root vegetables e.g. carrots, Jerusalem artichokes, beets

preparation: Baked sweet potatoes: Scrub the potatoes and dry them well. If they are large, halve them. Place the potatoes in a greased ovenproof dish and bake them in the oven for approximately 20 minutes at 200 degrees convection, until the skin is dark and the potatoes are tender. If they are very large potatoes, bake them a little longer. Root vegetable salad: Peel the root vegetables and cut into long diagonal slices. Peel the onions and cut into wedges. Toss the vegetables with olive oil and spread on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle thyme over and season with flaked salt and pepper. Roast the vegetables in the oven at 200 degrees convection for approximately 15 minutes. Drizzle honey over and roast for an additional 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Rinse the salad and spin it dry. Toss the arugula with the root vegetables. Roasted chickpeas: Drain the chickpeas and dry them well. Roast them in a dry pan with cumin and a little chili until they are golden. Sprinkle with flaked salt and remove from the pan. Garlic skyr: Stir the skyr with mayonnaise, mustard, pressed garlic, flaked salt, and pepper. Cut a slit in the warm potatoes and serve with garlic skyr, coriander, root vegetable salad, and roasted chickpeas.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 260 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (525 kcal). Carbohydrate: 85 g. Protein: 19 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Egg cake with chicken, bacon and crispy vegetables
preparation:
Spread the bacon on a baking sheet with parchment paper and bake it until crispy in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 10 minutes. Place the bacon on a piece of grease-absorbing paper to drain.

Boil the chicken meat for approx. 20 minutes until it is tender. Shred it with a fork. Optionally add a little of the cooking water so the chicken remains juicy.
