Peel the asparagus – starting from the head. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and steam the asparagus for approx. 5 minutes until tender. Drain the asparagus and slice them into smaller pieces.

Halve the pointed cabbage, remove the core and the outer leaves, and finely shred the cabbage. Slice the radishes. Toss the pointed cabbage with asparagus, radishes, and peas.

Whisk eggs, milk, potato starch, and chopped chives together well – save a little for garnish – and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan that can go into the oven, and pour the egg mixture onto it. Place the pan in the oven and bake the egg cake at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes until the egg cake is golden and fully cooked.

Top the egg cake with the crispy vegetables, chicken, and bacon, and sprinkle the remaining chives over it. Serve with rye bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 338 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2511 KJ (598 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 74 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Mexican vegetable stew with yogurt and whole grain pasta

ingredients.name: root vegetables, e.g., carrots, Jerusalem artichokes and parsnips

preparation: Peel the onions and chop them. Press the garlic. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds and chop the chili finely. Peel the root vegetables and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Cut the zucchini and bell pepper into cubes. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic, chili and spices for a couple of minutes. Add the root vegetables and let them fry for a moment. Then add the zucchini and bell pepper to the pot along with the cherry tomatoes and bouillon, and let it all simmer under a lid for approx. 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender. Rinse the beans and drain. Add the beans to the pot and heat up. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging. Serve the vegetable stew with whole grain pasta, yogurt and fresh coriander.
notes: Fruit and vegetables approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1800 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate 64 g, Protein 19 g, Fat 5 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Duck breast with a twist
preparation: Duck breast: Score the skin on the duck breasts and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and brown the duck breasts on the skin side. Place the duck breasts in an ovenproof dish. Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the core and cut the apples into wedges. Toss the apples with prunes and cinnamon, and place them in the dish. Bake the duck breast pieces with apples and prunes in the oven at 180 degrees for 15-20 minutes. Kale salad: Rinse the pearl barley and boil as indicated on the packaging. Cool the pearl barley. Finely shred the kale. Sprinkle with salt and sugar, and massage the kale very well. Clean the mushrooms. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and sauté the mushrooms with pressed garlic over high heat. Shake the pan during the process. Remove the mushrooms from the pan. Filet the oranges and cut into smaller pieces. Halve the pomegranate, and squeeze out the juice and seeds. Toss the kale with pearl barley, mushrooms, oranges, and pomegranate seeds and juice. Slice the duck breast. Arrange the salad with duck breast, apples, and prunes, and drizzle a little hoisin sauce over it.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 190 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 40 g. Protein: 30 g. Fat: 26 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Slow-roasted beef with polenta
preparation: Slow-roasted beef: Cut the meat into cubes. Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the meat. Season with salt and pepper and set aside. Clean the vegetables and cut them into small cubes. Finely chop the red onion and garlic. Sauté the vegetables and red onion in the pot, and add garlic, chopped tomatoes, red wine, rosemary, and bay leaves. Add the meat, and let it simmer under a lid until it is completely tender, approx. 2 hours. You can add a little bouillon along the way if needed. Season with balsamic vinegar and pepper. Polenta: Bring the water to a boil and add salt. Remove the pot from the heat and whisk the polenta flour into the water a little at a time. Place the pot back on the burner and turn down to low heat. Let the porridge simmer while stirring for approx. 5 minutes, until it is smooth and soft. You can add more water to adjust the consistency if needed. Season with freshly ground pepper. Top the meat with olives and parsley, and serve with velvety polenta.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 180 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2400 KJ (560 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 56 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Parmesan-gratin leeks and root vegetable mash

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar or white balsamic

preparation: Root vegetable mash: Peel the potatoes, parsnips or parsley roots and celery and cut them into large pieces. Boil the potatoes and root vegetables until tender in unsalted water. Drain the cooking water, but save it. Mash the potatoes and root vegetables with a potato masher or a whisk. Thin with the cooking water until the mash is smooth and airy. Season with salt and pepper. Parmesan-gratin leeks: Rinse the leeks thoroughly to remove dirt. It is easier if you split the green top, which can be filled with dirt. Cut the leeks into pieces of about 10 cm. Boil the leeks in lightly salted water until they are tender. Remove the leeks from the water with a slotted spoon and let them drip dry on a kitchen towel. Place the leeks in a dish, possibly with the green tops on top of each other, so the gratinated leeks have a uniform height. Grate the parmesan. Pick the leaves off the thyme, chop them slightly and mix them with breadcrumbs and parmesan. Sprinkle the mixture over the leeks. Drizzle with oil and gratin the leeks under the oven's grill until the surface is golden brown and crispy. Tomato-carrot vinaigrette: Cut the carrot and tomatoes into tiny cubes. Mix the tomatoes and carrots together with finely chopped parsley, vinegar or balsamic and oil and season with salt and pepper. Serve the leeks with the herb mash and the vinaigrette.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Ca. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 64 g. Protein: 14 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Sac kavurma – Lamb stew with bell peppers
preparation: Cut the meat into very small cubes. Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan. Fry the meat over medium-high heat for about 30 minutes until the meat is browned on all sides. Peel the onions and chop them coarsely, finely chop the garlic, and cut the bell peppers into small cubes or slices. Toss them with the meat and continue frying. Dice the tomatoes, toss them with the meat and vegetables, and fry for another 5 minutes. Season with salt, plenty of pepper, and chili powder. Boil the whole grain bulgur as indicated on the packaging. Serve the dish with a sprinkle of chopped parsley and the cooked bulgur.
notes: Tip! You can serve the dish with salad. Instead of bulgur, you can serve cooked whole grain rice. A little scrambled egg can be added to the dish as a garnish. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (550 kcal), Carbohydrate 56 g, Protein 35 g, Fat 16 g, of which saturated fat 4 g.

title: Asian cabbage salad with spicy chicken topping
preparation:
Cabbage salad: Place the cabbage in a bowl, sprinkle with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Place the edamame beans in a small bowl and pour boiling water over them. Slice the avocado into strips and squeeze lemon juice over it. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, and slice the apple into wedges. Drain the chickpeas, rinse, and drain again. Optionally, warm the chicken meat in the microwave or in a pan with a little oil.

Asian dressing: Mix the ingredients for the dressing together.

Serving: Distribute the cabbage into a bowl and toss well with the dressing. Arrange the salad in two bowls and top with edamame beans, avocado, apple, and drained chickpeas. Top the salad with chicken and coriander.
notes:
NOTE: This recipe contains leftover chicken from this recipe. You can either choose to make both dishes, or you can fry fresh chicken meat. The dish will therefore take a little longer than the specified 20 minutes.

TIP If you buy a whole head of red cabbage, remove the outer leaves and the stalk, and shred the cabbage, for example, using a mandoline slicer. Put the rest of the cabbage in a freezer bag and store it in the refrigerator, so it stays fresh for several days. If you are in a hurry, buy cabbage that is already shredded.

title: Japanese curry with beef and carrots
preparation:
Curry sauce: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in oil in a pot for a few minutes. Add curry powder and flour and sauté for a minute. Add garam masala and thin with the bouillon. Boil the sauce while you prepare the meat and vegetables.

Meat and vegetables: Roughly chop the onions and brown them with the meat in a pot in oil. Pour the curry sauce into the pot with the meat and vegetables, and let the dish simmer for 30 minutes. Peel the carrots and potatoes, cut them into cubes, and add them to the sauce. Let it simmer for another 30 minutes. Season the sauce with finely grated garlic and ginger, salt, and cayenne pepper. Add the edamame beans just before serving.

Serve the dish with cooked rice.
notes:
Tip! Japanese curry is characterized by having a relatively large amount of sauce. The sauce is thickened in the same way as a Danish curry sauce (used for dishes like meatballs in curry), and then seasoned with the Indian spices garam masala, ginger, and garlic.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2900 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrate: 94 g. Fat: 20 g (of which saturated fat: 5 g).

title: Minced beef patty with grilled Mediterranean vegetables
preparation: Grilled Mediterranean vegetables: Cut the bell peppers into wedges. Slice the eggplant and courgette. Cut the onions into wedges. Gently toss the vegetables with the oil. Grill the vegetables until they are tender and colored. Tarragon dressing: Mix the ingredients for the tarragon dressing together and season with salt and pepper. Minced beef patty: Shape the meat into 4 patties and season them with salt and pepper. Grill the patties on a grill or a very hot grill pan for 3-4 minutes on each side until the meat is well done. Serve the beef patties with grilled Mediterranean vegetables, tarragon dressing, and boiled potatoes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2229 KJ (531 kcal). Carbohydrates: 62 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Chana chaat – Warm chickpea salad
preparation: Slice the onions into rings. Dice the bell pepper, tomatoes, and cucumber. Finely chop the chili. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and sauté the onions. Add the spices and fry for approximately another 1 minute. Scrape the lime flesh out with a spoon and toss the flesh and juice with the onions. Drain the chickpeas and add them to the pan. Turn off the heat and finally toss the bell pepper, tomatoes, cucumber, chopped coriander, and finely chopped chili into the salad.
notes: Tip! Can be used as an extra dish for the dinner table or as a healthy lunch salad, served with a dollop of drained yogurt and naan bread. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate: 44 g, Protein: 13 g, Fat: 8 g, of which saturated fat: 0.5 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person.

title: Minced Beef Patties with Asparagus Salad and Dill Cream
preparation: Asparagus Salad: Boil the potatoes until just tender. Cool them down and halve the potatoes. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and steam them for about 2 minutes. Drain and slice the asparagus into strips. Cut the cucumber lengthwise and slice it. Toss the potatoes with asparagus, cucumber, grated parmesan cheese, and chopped almonds. Season with salt and pepper, and top with pea sprouts. Dill Cream: Mix yogurt with mayonnaise, mustard, chopped dill, salt, and pepper. Minced Beef Patties: Knead the meat and form into 4 patties. Season the patties with rosemary, salt, and pepper. Fry the patties on a grill for about 3 minutes on each side. Serve with asparagus salad and dill cream.
notes: Energy distribution: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 47 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Baked marinated salmon with roasted bell peppers and noodles with pointed cabbage

ingredients.name: bell peppers, red, green and yellow

preparation:
Roasted vegetables: Cut the bell peppers and onion into thick slices. Toss them with oil and salt, and spread them out on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake the vegetables in the oven at 200 degrees for 15 minutes.

Marinated salmon: Coat the salmon with ketjap manis on all sides. Sprinkle with salt, sesame seeds, and finely chopped chili. Place the salmon among the vegetables, and bake everything for another 10 minutes.

Noodles with pointed cabbage: Finely chop the garlic, squeeze the limes, and mix both with fish sauce and salt. Shred the pointed cabbage finely. Pick the coriander. Boil the noodles in a large pot of lightly salted water as indicated on the packaging. Drain them in a sieve, and place the pointed cabbage into the warm pot. Toss the pointed cabbage, dressing, coriander, and noodles together in the pot.

Serve the salmon with the noodles and roasted vegetables.
notes:
Tip! Ketjap manis is an Indonesian soy-based sauce that is thicker, sweeter, and slightly more spiced than soy sauce. You can find it in bottles on supermarket shelves with Asian goods or at an Asian specialty store. Instead of ketjap manis, you can use oyster sauce or soy sauce.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 52 g. Protein: 31 g. Fat: 28 g (of which saturated fat is 3.5 g).

title: Potato Pizza
preparation: Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm water with salt. Add the flour gradually and knead the dough. Let the dough rise covered for approx. 45 minutes. Slice the potatoes into very thin slices and finely chop the onion. Finely chop the mozzarella cheese. Roll out the dough to the size of a baking sheet – approx. 30 x 40 cm. Rub olive oil over the pizza dough and sprinkle with finely chopped onion. Distribute potato slices, spinach, air-dried ham, rosemary, and mozzarella on the pizza. Bake at 250 degrees for approx. 25 minutes.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 20 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Rejecocktail asian style

ingredients.name: little chinese cabbage or iceberg lettuce

preparation: Rejecocktail: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage and slice it finely. Snap the woody bottom ends off the asparagus and steam them for about 2 minutes. Drain them, pour cold water over them, and cool them down. Slice the asparagus into strips. Finely slice the spring onions. Split the cucumber lengthwise, remove the seeds, and slice the cucumber into rounds. Halve the avocados, remove the stones, drizzle with lemon juice, and cut them into thin wedges. Dressing: Whisk the dressing ingredients together. Arrange the chinese cabbage, asparagus, spring onions, cucumber, avocado, and shrimp. Pour the dressing over and serve with toasted bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1800 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate: 45 g. Protein: 23 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Broccolini salad with crispy parma ham and almonds
preparation: Grilled parma ham: Spread parma ham on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and grill it until crispy in the oven. Broccolini salad: Cook the bulgur as indicated on the packaging and let it cool. Cut off the small bottom piece of the broccolini, and steam them in water with the juice of 1/2 lemon for about 3 min. (save the other half for serving), until they are tender but still have a bite. Drain the broccolini. Chop the almonds. Serving: Spread the bulgur on a platter with the broccolini, and top with semi-dried tomatoes, raisins, and chopped almonds. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over it. Crush the parma ham and sprinkle it over the salad. Drizzle with olive oil.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 30 g. Protein: 15 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person.

title: Lemon-marinated salmon with onion and basil

ingredients.name: salmon fillet (it is recommended to freeze the fish before eating it raw)

preparation: Lemon-marinated salmon: Slice the salmon fillet as thinly as possible with a sharp knife. Slice the onion into very thin slices. Pick 2 handfuls of basil leaves. Squeeze the juice of the lemon and mix it with oil, salt, and pepper. Place the salmon slices in layers in a container with a lid. Sprinkle some onion and basil between the layers and drizzle with the lemon-oil mixture. Let the fish marinate for at least 5 hours, preferably until the next day. Bean salad: Trim the beans and boil them for 4 minutes in lightly salted water. Cool them under cold water and let them drain in a sieve. Rinse and dry the lettuce and break it into large pieces. Place the beans on top of the lettuce. Finely chop the garlic and cut the sun-dried tomatoes into thin strips. Mix the garlic and tomatoes into the yogurt and drizzle it over the salad. Arrange the salmon on a platter and sprinkle it with fresh basil. Serve the salmon with the bean salad and bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 49 g. Protein: 33 g. Fat: 27 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Whole grain wraps with hummus and grilled vegetables

ingredients.name: sesame oil or extra virgin olive oil

preparation: Hummus: Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Toast the cumin in a dry pan, and crush it in a mortar. Place chickpeas, coriander, cumin, pressed garlic, and tahini in a blender, and add bouillon. Blend until a thick hummus is formed. Season with lemon juice, salt, and pepper, and stir in the oil at the end. Grilled vegetables: Cut the bell peppers into wedges. Slice the eggplant and courgette. Brush a grill pan with oil and heat it well. Grill the vegetables until they are tender and colored. Rinse the lettuce and shake it dry. Warm the wraps and fill them with lettuce, hummus, and grilled vegetables.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Börek – Dough rolls with beef filling
preparation:
Börek
Peel the onions and grate them coarsely. Cut the bell peppers into very small dice. Heat oil in a non-stick pan and sauté the onions and bell peppers over medium heat until they are translucent.

Add the meat and sauté it with them for 5 minutes.

Finely chop the parsley and cut the tomatoes into small dice. Toss them with the meat in the pan. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika, and let the mixture cool.

Leave the yufka sheets in a damp tea towel while you make the börek.

Place one piece of dough on the table at a time. Place a little meat filling on the wide end of the dough triangles. Fold the sides in slightly, and roll the dough together around the filling from the wide end towards the tip like a cigar. Put a little water in a small bowl, and dip the tip of the dough into the water for a moment before finishing the roll – so the roll does not open up during baking.

Preheat the oven to 250 degrees.

Place the rolls on baking sheets with parchment paper. Whisk the egg yolk and yogurt together, and brush the rolls.

Bake the börek just before serving. Bake them for 15-20 minutes, or until they are golden brown and crispy.

Side Dish
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumbers into slices. Separate the lettuce into leaves, rinse and dry them.

Börek is served on a platter together with vegetables.
notes:
Tip! For these rolls, special yufka dough sheets are used, which can be purchased in Turkish specialty stores in chilled or frozen packs. If you cannot find the triangular pieces of dough, you can buy large sheets of dough and cut them into triangles yourself. Wrap the dough in a damp tea towel 30 minutes before use to make the dough sufficiently soft and flexible.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

Energy distribution per person: 1300 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 27 g. Protein: 20 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Chicken burger with romesco sauce

ingredients.name: whole grain kamut flour, coarse spelt flour or graham flour

preparation: Burger buns: Dissolve the yeast in the water and add salt, kamut flour, durum flour and half of the wheat flour. Knead the dough well while adding more flour until the dough just barely releases from your fingers. Let the dough rise covered for about 1 hour. Punch down the dough on a floured surface. Divide it into 12 pieces. Shape each piece into a bun. Arrange the buns on two baking sheets lined with parchment paper and press them down so they are about 1 cm high. Let the buns rise covered in a warm place for about 30 minutes. Brush the buns with milk and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake the buns at 200 degrees for about 20 minutes until they are golden brown. Romesco sauce: Light the grill or start the oven's grill function. Halve the bell peppers, remove the seeds and place the halves skin-side up. Grill the bell peppers until they are well darkened and charred. Remove the bell peppers and place them in a freezer bag. Tie a knot on the bag and let the bell peppers rest for about 15 minutes. Peel the skin off the bell peppers. Put the bell peppers in a blender or mini chopper along with almonds, pressed garlic, vinegar and olive oil. Blend to a coarse, thick consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Filling: Gently flatten the chicken breast pieces. Brush them with oil and season with thyme and pepper. Grill the meat for about 4 minutes on each side until cooked through. Slice the lettuce. Cut tomatoes and cucumber into slices. Warm 4 buns and cut them through. Fill with lettuce, chicken, romesco sauce, cucumber and tomato.
notes: Tip! The remaining burger buns can be frozen. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 298 g per person. Energy distribution: 2377 KJ (566 kcal). Carbohydrates: 62 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Tuna patties with coleslaw and rosemary roasted potatoes
preparation:
Rosemary roasted potatoes: Scrub the potatoes and dry them well. Cut the potatoes into wedges and toss them with the oil. Spread the potatoes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, sprinkle with chopped rosemary and season with salt and pepper. Bake the potatoes in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 30 minutes.

Tuna patties: Finely slice the spring onions. Chop the capers. Drain the tuna and mix it with eggs, breadcrumbs and milk. Chop the dill and chives and add them to the mixture along with the spring onions, capers and mustard. Season the mixture with salt and pepper. Shape the mixture into 16 small patties the size of golf balls. Dip the patties in beaten egg and then in breadcrumbs. Place the tuna patties on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Drizzle the oil over them and bake them in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 20 minutes, until they are crispy.

Coleslaw: Peel the carrots. Cut the apples into quarters and remove the core. Grate the apples and carrots on the coarse side of a grater and drizzle lemon juice over them. Finely shred the cabbage. Chop the parsley. Mix yogurt with mayonnaise and mustard and season the dressing with salt and pepper. Toss the dressing with carrots, apple, cabbage and parsley. Serve the tuna patties with coleslaw, rosemary roasted potatoes and lemon wedges.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrate: 78 g. Protein: 42 g. Fat: 27 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Lasagne with chicken and spinach

ingredients.name: finely grated zest of an untreated lemon
fresh lasagna sheets, preferably whole grain

preparation: Meat and spinach filling: Chop the onion and sauté it in the oil in a pan. Add the meat in small pieces and brown it together with the onion. Rinse the spinach thoroughly. Place it in a large pot over high heat and stir until the spinach collapses completely. Cook the spinach until it is tender and most of the liquid has evaporated. Mix the meat and spinach, and season with salt, pepper, and lemon zest. Milk sauce: Whisk milk and flour together in a pot, and bring to a boil while stirring. Let the sauce simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, and season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Lasagna: Layer the lasagna sheets, meat and spinach filling, and milk sauce in an ovenproof dish. Ensure there is enough sauce and filling for all the lasagna sheets. Save a little milk sauce for the top and sprinkle with cheese. Cover the dish with foil and bake the lasagna for 25 minutes at 200 degrees. Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes until the lasagna is light brown on top. Side dish: Rinse and dry the lettuce, and break it into large pieces. Slice or wedge the tomatoes. Mix oil and balsamic together, toss the dressing with the lettuce and tomatoes, and season with salt and pepper.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 45 g. Protein: 40 g. Fat: 21 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Greek Chicken Bake with Tzatziki
preparation: Greek Chicken Bake: Preheat the oven to 225 degrees. Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices. Toss the potatoes with the oil and distribute them in a greased baking dish. Season with salt and pepper and bake the potatoes in the oven for about 20 minutes. Cut the zucchini and bell pepper into small cubes. Cut the tomatoes and onion into wedges. Finely chop the rosemary. Mix the vegetables together with the pressed garlic. Grill the chicken breast fillets on a hot grill pan on both sides. Arrange the vegetables and chicken breast fillets over the potatoes. Bake in the oven for about 15 minutes. Spread feta cheese, soaked sun-dried tomatoes in strips, and pine nuts over the dish and bake for an additional 5 minutes. Tzatziki: Coarsely grate the cucumber. Sprinkle the cucumber strips with salt and let them sit for about 15 minutes. Squeeze the cucumbers free of liquid. Stir the yogurt with the pressed garlic and fold in the cucumbers. Season the tzatziki with pepper. Garnish the dish with fresh rosemary if desired and serve with tzatziki.
notes: Tip! Use olive oil instead of sunflower oil. Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 300 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 34 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Pasta carbonara with sautéed mushrooms, spinach and roasted tomatoes
preparation:
Roasted tomatoes: Preheat the oven to 150 degrees. Rinse and dry the tomatoes. Halve the tomatoes and toss with olive oil. Spread the tomatoes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Season with flaked salt, pepper, and chopped rosemary. Bake the tomatoes in the oven for approx. 1 ½ hours.

Pasta carbonara: Set a pot of water to boil for the pasta. Cook as indicated on the packaging. Drain and reserve some of the cooking water. Peel and chop the onion. Press the garlic. Clean the mushrooms. Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion with garlic and mushrooms over high heat until the mushrooms are tender. Stir the milk with cornstarch and add to the pan. Let it simmer over low heat for approx. 5 min. If necessary, thin the sauce with a little of the pasta cooking water. Lower the heat. Rinse the spinach and drain. Add the spinach to the pan and let it wilt. Season the sauce with grated lemon zest, parmesan cheese, and flaked salt. Serving: Toss the sauce with the linguine and serve with the roasted tomatoes. Season with pepper.
notes:
Carbonara is normally made with cream and bacon and is not known as heart-healthy diet. In this version, the sautéed mushrooms are the dish's "bacon", which contributes plenty of umami flavor. 

Energy distribution per person: 550 kcal, Carbohydrate: 67 g, Protein: 25 g, Fat: 20 g (including 5 g saturated fat).

title: Baked cauliflower and pork tenderloin with bacon
preparation: Tomato sauce: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in 1 tbsp of oil in a small pot. Add the tomatoes, pressed garlic, bay leaf, and thyme. Let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes and season with salt and pepper. Stir the olives into the sauce and place it at the bottom of an ovenproof dish. Divide the cauliflower into smaller florets and place them in the tomato sauce. Brush the cauliflower with the remaining oil. Bake the dish in the oven at 200 degrees for 30-40 minutes until the cauliflower is golden and tender. Sprinkle with coarsely chopped parsley before serving. Pork tenderloin with bacon: Trim the fat and sinew off the tenderloin. Season the meat with salt, pepper, and rosemary. Roll the bacon around the tenderloin, place it in an ovenproof dish or on a piece of parchment paper, and roast at 200 degrees for approximately 40 minutes. Let the tenderloin rest for 5 minutes, then slice it. Side dish: Cook the couscous as indicated on the packaging. Fluff it with a fork before serving. Serve the tenderloin with the baked cauliflower and couscous.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 56 g. Protein: 44 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Nordic winter stew with apple-mushroom topping

ingredients.name: root vegetables, e.g., Jerusalem artichokes, parsnips, carrots and beetroot
fresh rosemary (can be replaced by thyme)
fresh rosemary (can be replaced by thyme)

preparation: Peel and chop the onion. Peel and prepare the root vegetables and cut them into smaller bite-sized pieces. Heat the oil in a large pot, and sauté the bacon with onion, pressed garlic, root vegetables, rosemary, cloves and juniper berries for 2-3 min while stirring. Add beer and tomatoes, and let it simmer over low heat for approx. 20 min, until the root vegetables are tender. Meanwhile, cook the pearl spelt as indicated on the packaging. Brush the mushrooms clean, halve them if they are large. Halve the apples, remove the core and cut the apples into wedges. Heat oil in a pan, and fry mushrooms with apples and rosemary until they are golden. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Serve the Nordic winter stew with pearl spelt and apple-mushroom topping.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 80 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Hungarian goulash
preparation:
Cut the meat into cubes. Heat the oil in a pot and brown the meat. Stir a little of the bouillon with the tomato paste, paprika, and cumin, and pour it in. Add the rest of the bouillon and the bay leaves, and simmer the meat over low heat for 1½ hours.

Peel the potatoes, cut them into cubes, and add them to the pot. Cook the dish for about 20 minutes longer until the potatoes are tender.

Clean the mushrooms and slice them. Cut the onion into thin wedges. Cut the bell peppers into strips. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Heat the oil in a large pan and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, chili, mushrooms, and bell peppers for about 5 minutes.

Add the sautéed vegetables to the pot with the meat. Season with salt and pepper.

Sprinkle with chopped chives and serve with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2900 KJ (690 kcal). Carbohydrates: 89 g. Fat: 23 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g (per person, unless otherwise stated).

title: Butter Chicken – Chicken in curry sauce

ingredients.name: chicken breast without skin and bone

preparation:
Marinated chicken: Cut each chicken breast into 3 pieces or smaller bite-sized pieces. Toss the chicken in lime juice and let it marinate for about 10 minutes. Grate the ginger finely and mix it with the yoghurt and spices to make a marinade. Toss the chicken in the marinade. The longer it is allowed to marinate, the better the flavor will be. Place the chicken with the marinade in an ovenproof dish. Roast the chicken at 200 degrees for 15 minutes. Turn the chicken pieces over and roast for an additional 15 minutes.

Sauce: Peel the onion and garlic and chop them. Peel and grate the ginger. Cut the tomatoes into small dice. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic, tomatoes, ginger, spices, and lime juice until the onions are golden. Add the cream and bring to a boil. Blend the sauce. If necessary, thin the sauce with a little water. Toss the chicken in the sauce and let the dish simmer for about 10 minutes.

Topping: Chop the bell pepper, spring onions, and coriander. Mix them together and sprinkle over the butter chicken when serving.

Side dish: Serve the butter chicken with cooked whole grain rice mixed with peas.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 200 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 2600 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate 71 g. Protein 41 g. Fat 16 g. Of which saturated fat 4 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Fish dish with leeks

ingredients.name: scrod or cod fillet without skin and bones
apple cider vinegar or lemon juice

preparation: Fish dish: Cut the fish meat into smaller pieces. Place them in a blender or mini chopper and blend with salt and pepper. Blend the egg into the mixture, then the flour, and thin it with the milk until it forms a soft paste. Grease an ovenproof dish, approx. 16 × 22 cm, with a little oil. Spread the fish paste at the bottom of the dish. Split the leeks and rinse them thoroughly. Cut them into pieces the same length as the width of the dish. Boil them in lightly salted water for 3 minutes. Let them drain well, and press them down into the fish paste. Brush the leeks with a little oil. Bake the mixture in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 30 minutes, or until the paste is firm and the leeks are lightly golden. Salad: Rinse and dry the salad well. Toss them with oil and vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Serve the fish dish with salad and boiled potatoes.
notes: Tip! Instead of scrod or cod, you can use plaice, salmon, trout, ling, monkfish, or haddock.

title: Chicken in Sweet and Sour Sauce
preparation:
Sweet and sour sauce: Mix cornstarch, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, tomato puree, and water together in a small pot. Bring the sauce to a boil while stirring, until the sauce thickens. Remove the pot from the heat.

Chicken: Cut the chicken meat into strips. Divide the broccoli into small florets. Cut the bell pepper into strips, pineapple into cubes, and spring onions into slices.

Heat half of the oil in a pan and brown the meat. Season it with salt and pepper and remove it from the pan.

Heat the rest of the oil in the pan and fry the broccoli and bell pepper for a couple of minutes. Add the pineapple, chicken, and sweet and sour sauce and heat the dish through. Optionally thin it out with a little water if the sauce is too thick. Season with salt and pepper and serve the dish with cooked rice.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 87 g. Protein: 35 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 2.5 g.

title: Chicken Adobo – Filipino soy-marinated chicken
preparation:
Chicken adobo: Mix soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, pepper and sugar together. Coat the chicken in the marinade and let it marinate in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours. Peel the onion and finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and sauté the onion and garlic. Add the chicken thighs and marinade to the pan and pour in the coconut milk. Bring to a boil and turn down to low heat. Let the chicken simmer for approx. 30 minutes without a lid. Turn the chicken occasionally.

Stir-fried vegetables: Cut the vegetables into pieces suitable for stir-frying. Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan or wok. Sauté the vegetables while stirring until they are tender-crisp. You can add a little water during frying so the vegetables soften without burning. Season with salt.

Side dish: Serve the chicken thighs with the vegetables and cooked rice.
notes:
Tip! 1 can of coconut milk contains 4 dl of coconut milk, and you only need 1 dl for the dish. Shake the can well before opening it. Take 1 dl for the dish, and freeze the rest in 3 small portions of 1 dl each, which you can use the next time you make the dish.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 78 g, Fat: 21 g (of which saturated fat: 4 g).

title: Baked potatoes with cod roe dressing

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar or lemon juice

preparation: Baked potatoes: Scrub the potatoes well and place them on a baking sheet. Cut a cross in the top of each potato and bake them at 200 degrees for approx. 1 hour. Prick them with a small pointed knife and check if they are tender, and potentially bake them longer if they are still hard in the middle. Cod roe dressing: Wrap the cod roe individually in lunch paper or parchment paper and place them in a pot. Cover the packets with water, add 1 tsp salt, 2 bay leaves, 5 black peppercorns and ½ lemon in slices. Bring the water to a gentle boil, turn down to low heat and let the cod roe simmer under a lid for 8 minutes (small) or 15 (large). Move the pot to the side and let the cod roe steep in the cooking water for 10 minutes. Take them out, unwrap them and let them cool on a plate. Peel the skin off the cod roe with a small paring knife and cut them into small cubes. Squeeze the other half of the lemon. Mix the cod roe and capers with dill and season with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Salad: Peel the carrots. Clean the celery and cauliflower. Cut the carrots, celery and cauliflower into very thin slices. Stir oil and apple cider vinegar or lemon juice with curry and toss the vegetables and chopped cress in the dressing. Season the salad with salt and pepper. Serve the baked potatoes with the cod roe dressing and salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 170 g per person. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 62 g. Protein: 35 g. Fat: 2 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Baked egg cake with potatoes and vegetables
preparation: Peel the onion and garlic, and chop them finely. Clean the zucchini and bell pepper, and cut them into cubes. Cut the potatoes into cubes. Wash the tomatoes and cut them in half. Sauté the onion in a pan with oil without letting it brown. Add garlic, zucchini, and bell pepper, and fry under stirring for 5 minutes. Toss in the potatoes and season with salt and pepper. Distribute the vegetables in a greased ovenproof dish or in two ovenproof portion dishes. Whisk the eggs together with the flour, and add milk, salt, and pepper. Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and place the egg cake in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes – until the egg mixture is half set. Place the tomatoes on top, and continue baking the egg cake for 20-25 minutes until it is completely set. Sprinkle basil leaves over the egg cake and serve it with rye bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 33 g. Protein: 14 g. Fat: 9 g (of which saturated fat: 2 g).

title: Stew with apples and leeks
preparation: Stew: Cut the meat into cubes and season with salt and pepper. Peel and chop the onions. Peel the Jerusalem artichokes and cut into bite-sized pieces. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and brown the meat. Remove the meat, and fry the onions and Jerusalem artichokes for a couple of minutes. Add the pressed garlic and parsley, and put the meat back into the pan. Pour in the beer and bouillon, and let the meat and vegetables simmer under a lid for about 1½ hours, until the meat is very tender. Season the dish with pepper. Fried apples and leeks: Slice the leeks and rinse them well. Cut the apples into quarters, remove the core, and cut the apples into wedges. Heat the oil in a pan, and fry the leeks and apples until they are golden. Shake the pan along the way. Optionally add a little bouillon so it does not burn. Add fresh thyme and season with salt and pepper. Serve the stew with cooked whole grain rice and top with the fried apples and leeks.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 240 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 3100 KJ (740 kcal). Carbohydrate: 91 g. Fat: 25 g. Of which saturated fat: 8 g.

title: One pot cod in tomato with pearl barley and kale

ingredients.name: cod fillet without skin and bones

preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Cut the fennel into cubes. Chop the kale. Chop the onion and press the garlic. Heat the oil in a pan with a matching lid that is oven-safe. Sauté the onion and garlic, then add the fennel, kale, and thyme, and fry for another few minutes. Add the cherry tomatoes to the pan and stir. Cut the cod into portions. Make small indentations in the tomato sauce and place the cod in them. Season with salt and pepper, and put the lid on. Place the pan in the oven for 10-12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily when you press it with a finger. Rinse the pearl barley and boil as indicated on the packaging. Remove the pan from the oven and sprinkle with crumbled salattern. Top with watercress, parsley or basil and serve with the cooked pearl barley.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrate: 41 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Root vegetable soup with croutons
preparation: Root vegetable soup: Take the root vegetables out of the freezer. It is good to defrost them a little beforehand, but it is not strictly necessary. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the root vegetables with chili for a few minutes. Add the chopped tomatoes and bouillon, and let the vegetables simmer under a lid for about 10 min. Meanwhile, prepare the croutons. Blend the vegetables into a thick, creamy soup with an immersion blender – if it is too thick for your taste, thin it out with more bouillon. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Croutons: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees fan air. Cut the bread into cubes and toss with oil. Spread the bread on a baking sheet with parchment paper and season with flaked salt. Bake the croutons in the oven for about 5 min. Serving: Arrange the soup and top with croutons and basil.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 59 g. Protein: 14 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Lentil Bolognese with Cabbage Salad
preparation:
Lentil Bolognese: Peel and chop the onion. Press the garlic. Cut the zucchini and bell pepper into small cubes. Rinse the lentils and drain. Heat the oil in a pot, and sauté the onion and garlic with oregano. Add the zucchini, bell pepper, and lentils. Add the tomato paste and tomatoes to the pot and stir. Pour in the bouillon and let the dish simmer for approx. 20 min without a lid, so the sauce reduces. Meanwhile, boil the pasta as indicated on the packaging. Season the lentil bolognese with flaked salt and pepper.
Cabbage Salad: Finely shred the cabbage. Sprinkle with salt and sugar, and massage it well. Briefly boil the edamame beans and drain. Toss the cabbage with the beans.
Serving: Arrange the pasta with lentil bolognese in bowls and top with basil. Serve with cabbage salad on the side.
notes:
TIP If you have leftovers of the lentil bolognese and cabbage salad, they can easily be eaten the next day, for example in warm pita bread or as filling in a wrap.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution: 2500 KJ (600 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated.
Carbohydrates: 73 g
Protein: 32 g
Fat: 14 g
Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g

title: Thai Soup
preparation: Place chicken breast in a pot and cover with water. Boil for approximately 20 min and drain. Shred the pieces into fibers using two forks. Set aside. Clean the mushrooms and cut them into smaller pieces. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Slice the bell pepper, sugar peas, and spring onions. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the mushrooms with garlic for 1-2 min. Set the mushrooms aside. Pour chicken stock into a pot and bring to a boil. Add noodles, bell pepper, sugar peas, and finely chopped chili and cook until the noodles are tender. Season with lime juice, fish sauce, and salt. Add the chicken and garlic-sautéed mushrooms to the pot along with the edamame beans and cook for approximately 1 min. Serve the soup in bowls and top with sliced spring onions, sprouts, and coriander.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 235 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 53 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 11 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Bariis iyo suqaar – Beef with basmati rice

ingredients.name: chicken bouillon (powder) or 2/3 chicken bouillon cubes

preparation:
Meat dish: Finely chop onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion with garlic for 2 minutes. Add the meat and let it fry with it for 2 minutes. Peel the potato and cut it into cubes. Mix it into the meat and add bouillon, cumin, and coriander and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Cut the bell peppers into strips, mix with the meat and let it simmer for another 5 minutes.

Side dish: Soak the rice in a bowl of water for 30 minutes. Rinse them thoroughly and let them drain in a sieve. Peel and chop onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté onion and garlic. Add marwa and the rice and toast them for 2 minutes. Add water and bouillon and bring to a boil. Turn down the heat, let the rice simmer on low heat for 20 minutes with a lid on. Turn off the heat and let them steam to finish.

Serve meat with rice and bananas sliced.
notes: Tip! Chicken bouillon can be replaced with chicken bouillon. Marwa is a Somali spice blend, which can be found in Somali specialty stores.

title: Baked potato with beef filling
preparation: Baked potato: Wash the potatoes and dry them well. Cut a cross in the top of each potato and wrap them in foil. Bake the potatoes at 200 degrees for approximately 1 hour. Beef filling: Chop the onion. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion together with the meat. Add oregano and tomato paste, and let it simmer for about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Rinse the lettuce. Cut the bell pepper into cubes and the cherry tomatoes into quarters. Cut the cucumber into diagonal slices. Serve the baked potatoes with salad, meat filling, bell peppers, tomatoes, cucumber, and creme fraiche.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1800 KJ (430 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrate: 54 g. Fat: 12 g (including 4 g saturated fat).

title: Vegetarian Burger
preparation:
Vegetable patty: Drain the brine from the chickpeas. Blend them in a food processor or mini chopper along with the pressed garlic, soy sauce, and cumin. Grate the zucchini and carrots finely and the onion coarsely. Knead the vegetables and oatmeal thoroughly together with the chickpea mash using your hands in a bowl. Let the dough rest for 10 minutes. You can prepare the sides in the meantime. Shape 4 patties from the chickpea dough, about 1½ cm thick. Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a non-stick pan and fry the patties at medium heat for 1 minute. Turn down the heat and fry them for another 2 minutes. Flip them, drizzle with the remaining oil, and fry for approximately 2 minutes.

Split the buns and warm them under the oven grill or in a toaster. Rinse and dry the lettuce, and break it into large pieces. Slice the tomatoes, onion, and cucumber. Spread the buns with mustard to taste, and assemble the burgers with the vegetables, patty, and ketchup.
notes:
Tip! The dough for the patties can be a bit porous. You can shape each patty on a small piece of parchment paper, making it easy to turn them onto the pan one by one and then peel the paper off.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 67 g, Protein: 19 g, Fat: 18 g, of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Chicken Goulash with Mashed Potatoes
preparation:
Chicken Goulash: Cut the chicken thighs at the joint. Coarsely chop the onions. Cut the carrots into thick slices and the bell peppers into large cubes. Brown the chicken in the oil in a large pot, first on the skin side, then on the other side. Place the chicken on a plate. Sauté the vegetables in the pot. Add tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, finely minced garlic, and water or bouillon and bring to a boil. Finely chop the cumin and add it to the sauce along with the paprika. Place the chicken in the sauce and let the dish simmer for 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle chopped parsley over the top.

Mashed Potatoes: Peel the potatoes and celery root. Cut them into large pieces, place them in a pot and cover with water. Boil the potatoes and celery root until completely tender. Mash them with a potato masher or a whisk. Thin with milk and season with salt and pepper.

Serve the mash with the chicken goulash.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 600 kcal. Carbohydrates: 69 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Etli ekmek – Turkish pizza
preparation: Dough: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt, oil, and flour and knead the dough. Let the dough rise covered for approx. 1 hour. Meanwhile, prepare the filling. Filling: Peel and finely chop the onion and parsley. Cut the bell pepper into small cubes. Mix onion, parsley, and bell peppers with meat, tomatoes, lemon juice, salt, pepper, chili, tomato paste, and oil. Etli ekmek: Preheat the oven to 225 degrees. Divide the dough into 8 pieces. Press the dough out onto a piece of parchment paper with wet hands, until they are as long as the baking sheet and approx. 5 cm wide and thin. Spread the filling on top of the dough. Bake the breads until the bottoms are crispy, approx. 20 minutes.
notes: Tip! You can roll out the dough with a rolling pin instead of pressing it out with your hands. Optionally serve etli ekmek as a main course for 6 people with a large bowl of salad. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1500 KJ (350 kcal), Carbohydrate: 46 g, Protein: 17 g, Fat: 7.5 g, of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Asian noodles with chicken and vegetables
preparation: Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain. Finely shred the cabbage. Cut the broccoli into smaller florets. For the fried chicken: peel and chop the onion. Heat half of the oil in a wok and add the green curry paste. Fry the onion and chicken at high heat for approx. 5 min while stirring, until the meat is tender. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Remove the meat from the pan. Add the rest of the oil to the wok and fry the cabbage with the broccoli for 2-3 min at high heat, until it is tender but still has a bite. Add the meat and noodles and heat well. Toss everything together. Add the soy sauce and mix well. Slice the spring onions. Serve the noodles in bowls and sprinkle with spring onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Delicious and easy noodle dish with whole grains and protein. Leftovers also taste wonderful for lunch the next day. Energy distribution: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 40 g. Protein: 31 g. Fat: 21 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Avocado salad with crispy cabbage and chili

ingredient_sections.section_name: Avocado salad with crispy cabbage and chili

preparation: Halve the cabbage, remove the core, and shred the cabbage finely, e.g., using a mandoline slicer. Sprinkle the cabbage with sugar and salt and massage it well. Pour boiling water over the edamame beans and drain. Rinse the black beans well and drain. Toss the pointed cabbage with the edamame beans and black beans. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Chop the chives and toss them into the salad along with the chili and squeeze lime juice over. Season the salad with pepper. Halve the avocados, remove the pits, and cut the avocado into thin slices. Drizzle with lemon juice. Top the salad with the avocados.
notes: Tip! The salad can also be served for lunch on a piece of rye bread with a poached egg. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 29 g. Protein: 13 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Krebinetter with Creamed Kale and Carrot Salad
preparation: Creamed Kale: De-rib the kale, and grate or cut it into large pieces. Boil the kale in a pot with slightly salted boiling water for about 4 minutes. Remove the kale and let it drain in a sieve. Whisk milk and wheat flour together in a pot, and bring to a boil while stirring. Let the sauce simmer over low heat for 5 minutes while stirring. Fold the kale into the sauce and cook it through well. Season with salt and pepper. Krebinetter: Shape the meat into 4 krebinetter. Coat them in breadcrumbs. Heat half of the oil in a non-stick pan and brown the krebinetter. Turn down the heat and let them fry for 3 minutes. Turn them, drizzle with the rest of the oil, and fry them for 4 minutes over medium heat. Season the krebinetter with salt and pepper. Carrot Salad: Coarsely grate the carrots. Mix mustard, honey, and apple cider vinegar together, and fold the marinade together with the carrots and snipped watercress. Serve the krebinetter with creamed kale, boiled potatoes, and carrot salad.
notes: Tip! Instead of krebinetter, you can serve the kale with, for example, low-fat Danish sausage (medisterpølse) with 7-10% fat or meatballs (frikadeller). Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution: 2800 KJ (660 kcal). Carbohydrates: 84 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

title: Steamed fish and shrimp with stir-fried vegetables

ingredients.name: mushrooms, e.g., shiitake, button mushrooms or king oyster mushrooms
fillet of firm white fish, e.g., cod, halibut, redfish, Pacific cod or similar

preparation:
Stir-fried vegetables: Cut the red onions into thick wedges. Cut the bell peppers into strips and the mushrooms into slices. Mix the soy sauce with the vinegar, cayenne pepper, and finely chopped garlic. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry non-stick pan until they 'pop' and become fragrant. Let them cool down. Heat the oil in the pan and stir-fry the onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms over high heat for about 8 minutes while stirring. Add the peas and shrimp, and warm them together with the vegetables. Arrange the vegetables on a platter. Pour the marinade over the vegetables and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

Steamed fish: Cut the fish into pieces of approximately 3 x 3 cm, and season them with salt and pepper. Bring 2 dl of water to a boil in a pan or a wide-bottomed pot. Place the fish in the boiling water and let it simmer under a lid for 3 minutes. Remove the fish with a slotted spoon, let it drip dry on a piece of kitchen paper, and arrange it on top of the vegetables.

Serve the dish with cooked rice.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2300 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 75 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Plaice with shrimp sauce and pointed cabbage
preparation: Shrimp sauce: Whisk milk and flour together in a pot. Bring the sauce to a boil while stirring. Let the sauce simmer over low heat for 5 minutes. Add shrimp and chopped dill just before serving, and season with pepper and optionally salt. Fried plaice: Coat the plaice in the coarse flour. Heat a small amount of the oil in two non-stick pans, and brown the plaice on the dark side first. Turn down the heat and let the fish fry for about 7 minutes. Flip the plaice and drizzle with the rest of the oil. Fry the fish for another 7 minutes, and season with salt and pepper. Side dishes: Cut the pointed cabbage into wide strips. Place them in a pot with 3 dl of water. Bring to a boil, and let the cabbage steam with a lid on for 4 minutes. Season the cabbage with salt, and let it drain in a sieve. Serve the plaice with pointed cabbage, shrimp sauce, and boiled potatoes.
notes:
Tip! It can be difficult to fry whole fish in small amounts of oil without them burning. Therefore, make sure to turn down the heat during frying. You can also brown the fish on both sides, place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper, and finish baking the fish in the oven, where they should bake for about 10 minutes at 200 degrees.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (640 kcal). Carbohydrate: 75 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Moroccan stew with sweet potatoes, spices and chickpeas
preparation: Moroccan stew: Peel the potatoes and cut them into cubes. Peel and chop the onion. Crush the garlic. Cut the eggplant into cubes. Peel the carrots and cut them into slices or cubes. Heat the oil in a pot, and sauté the onion with garlic and spices for a few minutes. Add the sweet potatoes, eggplant, and carrots and stir well. Let it sauté for a few minutes. Now add the tomato paste and chopped tomatoes, and let it simmer at low heat under a lid for about 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender but still have a bit of bite. Rinse the chickpeas and drain. Warm the chickpeas in the stew and season with salt and pepper. Side dishes: Pour boiling water over the couscous as indicated on the packaging. Let it steep for about 10 minutes under a lid. Massage the pomegranate and squeeze the juice and seeds into a bowl. Serve the stew in bowls with couscous, pomegranate, and yogurt. Top with coriander or parsley.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 400 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 600 kcal. Carbohydrates: 100 g. Protein: 24 g. Fat: 9 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Braised beef cheeks in dark beer
preparation: Braised beef cheeks: Chop the onions. Press the garlic. Cut the carrot and celery into small cubes. Heat the oil in a large ovenproof pot. Brown the beef cheeks well and set aside. Sauté the onion, garlic, and carrot for a few minutes together with the spices. Add tomato paste, beer, and stock, and return the browned cheeks to the pot. Bring to a boil, and place a lid on the pot. Place the pot in the oven at 150 degrees, and let the meat cook for approximately 3 hours. Shred the meat in the pot with a fork. Drain and rinse the beans, and add them to the pot with the meat. Let it simmer further for approximately 15 minutes. Stir well and season with salt and pepper. Jerusalem artichoke mash: Peel the Jerusalem artichokes and potatoes and cut into bite-sized pieces. Boil the Jerusalem artichokes and potatoes with the pressed garlic in a pot of water, just covering them, and boil until tender. Drain the cooking water, and blend with milk, olive oil, and possibly a little of the cooking water. Season with salt and pepper. Serve the beef cheeks with Jerusalem artichoke mash. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 300 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrate: 71 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Black rice salad with egg and tuna

ingredients.name: large bell peppers or small yellow and red ones

preparation:
Boil the rice according to the instructions on the packaging, rinse them and drain them well in a sieve.
Boil the eggs soft, approximately 7 minutes, peel them and cut them in half.
Halve the bell peppers, place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and place them under the oven grill until they get black spots. Place them in a bowl and cover with film or put them in a plastic bag and close it tightly. Peel the skin off the grilled bell peppers when you can touch them, and cut them into large cubes. Slice the fennel into very thin slices, sprinkle them with a teaspoon of salt and let them sit for about ½ hour. Rinse them free of salt and drain them.
Strip the leaves from the parsley stems and rinse the leaves and the salad. Drain the tuna and cut it into smaller pieces. Whisk a dressing of oil, lemon juice and a tablespoon of water and season the dressing with salt and pepper. Cut the anchovies into small pieces.
Toss all the ingredients except the eggs with the dressing and arrange the eggs on top of the salad.
notes:
The dish can also be prepared with red or brown rice and grains.
Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 170 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 2250 KJ (525 kcal). Carbohydrate: 72 g. Fat: 19 g (of which saturated fat 3 g).

title: Chicken in Green Tabbouleh

ingredients.name: skinless and boneless chicken breast pieces

preparation: Place the chicken breast pieces in an ovenproof dish with pressed garlic and flat-leaf parsley. Add the water and cook the chicken in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes. Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Thin it out with some of the liquid, and save the rest for later. Cook the bulgur as indicated on the packaging. Finely shred the cabbage. Halve the tomatoes. Cut the cucumber and bell pepper into small cubes. Peel the onion and chop it finely. Slice the spring onions. Rinse and chop the herbs. Gently toss the bulgur with the cabbage, tomatoes, onion, cucumber, herbs, and chicken. Pour a little of the liquid from the chicken over it. Arrange the salad on a platter or in bowls, and top with spring onions. Serve with bread.
notes: Filling and satisfying salad with all sorts of delicious, crunchy vegetables. If you have leftover cooked chicken, use it in the salad, and feel free to replace the whole grain bulgur with, for example, whole grain couscous. Energy distribution per person: 500 kcal. Carbohydrates: 65 g, Protein: 40 g, Fat: 10 g (of which saturated fat 3 g), Dietary fiber: 1.5 g.

title: Kale with spicy pork
preparation: Kale with spicy pork: Chop the onions and sauté them in the oil in a large pot. Add the meat and fry with high heat until browned. Strip the kale, slice the leaves coarsely and chop the ribs into small pieces. Sauté the kale together with the meat until it wilts slightly. Add curry and water. Let the dish simmer at medium heat without a lid for about 15 minutes, until the kale is tender but still has bite and color. Season with salt and pepper. Crispy apple salad: Cut the apples into thin wedges and the onion into thin slices, and mix them with the apple cider vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Serve the dish with the apple salad on top and rye bread on the side.
notes: Tip! Instead of kale, you can use pointed cabbage. You can also use Savoy cabbage or white cabbage, which will gain both flavor and texture by being cooked for 30-40 minutes. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 59 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Plaice rolls with cold parsley sauce and steamed root vegetables
preparation: Plaice rolls: Pat the plaice fillets dry with paper towels. Spread the fillets with mustard and add a little chervil. Roll the fillets together so the mustard and chervil are on the inside. Place the fish fillets in an ovenproof dish, season with salt and pepper, and add bouillon until it covers about 1 cm of the fish. Steam the fish rolls in the oven at 175 degrees for approx. 20 minutes. Steamed root vegetables: Peel the celery, carrots, and parsley roots and cut the root vegetables into large cubes. Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the root vegetables for a few minutes. Pour in the vinegar and let it evaporate. Add the bouillon and place a lid on the pot. Steam the root vegetables for approx. 10 minutes until they are tender but still have a slight bite. Sprinkle with cane sugar and gently toss the root vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Cold parsley sauce: Stir the yogurt with mayonnaise and mustard. Rinse and chop the parsley, fold it into the cream, and season with salt and pepper. Serve the plaice rolls with root vegetables and cold parsley sauce.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 1300 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 14 g. Protein: 31 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Meatloaf with Leek

ingredient_sections.section_name: Tomatoes, onions and olives in white wine

preparation: Meatloaf with leek: Strip the thyme leaves and chop them. Mix pork, salt, pepper, egg, wheat flour, milk and thyme thoroughly together to form a meat mixture. Cut off the coarsest top and outer leaves of the leek and clean it thoroughly. Halve the leek and boil it in lightly salted water for about 6 minutes, until it is tender. Drain the leek. Form two slender meatloaves directly on a piece of parchment paper with a piece of leek inside. You can optionally wet your hands so the mixture does not stick. Sprinkle the meatloaves with breadcrumbs and bake them at 200 degrees for 25 minutes. Tomatoes, onions and olives in white wine: Cut the onions into wedges and the tomatoes into halves and mix them with the olives in an ovenproof dish. Pour in the white wine and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cover the dish with foil and bake it in the oven at 200 degrees for about 25 minutes, until the onions are tender. Remove the foil and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Oven potatoes: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into wedges. Toss them with oil and spread them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bake them in the oven at 200 degrees for 25 minutes, until they are tender and golden. Season with salt. Slice the meatloaf into thick slices and serve with oven-baked potatoes and the tomatoes and onions in the dish.
notes: Tip! Instead of white wine, you can use vegetable bouillon. Energy distribution: 2650 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrates: 92 g. Fat: 22 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person.

title: Baked fish, celery puree, lemon-marinated beans and sesame potatoes

ingredients.name: white fish fillets, e.g., cod or haddock

preparation: Sesame potatoes: Scrub the potatoes, dry them and toss with oil. Spread them in the bowl of an air fryer and sprinkle with sesame. Fry them until crispy at 200 degrees for approx. 15 min. Check that they are golden, otherwise they need a little longer. Alternatively, spread them on a baking sheet and bake for 20 min at 200 degrees in the oven. Take the potatoes out and keep them warm – set aside 100 g of cooked potatoes for this open-faced sandwich dish. Baked fish: Place the fish on a piece of parchment paper and season with flaked salt and pepper. Slice the lemon and distribute over the fish. Bake the fish in the air fryer for approx. 10 min, until it flakes when you press lightly on it with a finger. Alternatively, prepare it in the oven at 200 degrees for 12 min. Lemon-marinated beans: Rinse and trim the beans. Steam them in a pot for 5-8 min until they are tender. Drain the beans and toss with lemon zest and juice, olive oil, flaked salt and pepper. Celery puree: Peel the celery and cut into cubes. Place the celery in a pot with pressed garlic and bouillon and boil for approx. 10 min at medium heat until tender. Drain the bouillon and blend, while gradually adding whole milk and then bouillon, until you have a lovely creamy celery puree. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Serving: Arrange celery puree at the bottom of two plates, top with fish, and serve with lemon-marinated beans and sesame potatoes. Top with chervil.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 500 kcal. Carbohydrates: 46 g. Protein: 37 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Cabbage salad with quinoa, roasted pumpkin, mushrooms and pickled red onions

ingredients.name: mushrooms e.g. oyster mushrooms, shiitake and button mushrooms
shredded white cabbage or deseeded finely chopped kale

preparation: Roasted pumpkin: Preheat the oven to 225 degrees. Cut the pumpkin into wedges and toss with oil. Spread them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and season with salt and pepper, then bake in the oven for about 20 minutes until tender and golden. Be careful they do not get too burnt. Pickled red onions: Peel the onion and cut into thin slices. Put the onions, vinegar, and sugar in a pot and bring to a boil until the sugar is dissolved. Remove the pot from the heat and let the onions cool in the brine. Rinse the quinoa and cook as indicated on the packaging. Clean the mushrooms. Finely shred the cabbage. Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the mushrooms over high heat, turning them frequently so they do not burn in the pan. Season with salt and pepper, and remove the mushrooms from the pan. Toss the cabbage with the quinoa and arrange on a platter. Top with roasted pumpkin and sautéed mushrooms. Distribute the pickled onions over the top and drizzle the brine over the salad.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 38 g. Protein: 7.5 g. Fat: 7.5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Cauliflower Pizza
preparation: Divide the cauliflower into florets and put them in a blender. Blend to a cauliflower couscous-like consistency. Mix the cauliflower with eggs, psyllium husk, white whole wheat flour, oregano, and salt together to form a coarse dough. Let it rest for about 20 min. Divide it into two parts and press the dough onto two baking sheets to form 2 round thin pizza bases. Approximately 30 cm diameter. Use your palms to ensure the bases become fine. Bake them at 225 degrees convection for 15 min until they are nicely golden on the surface. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into thin slices. Slice the onion thinly. Spread the cheese on the base of the pizzas. Top with the sliced potatoes and onion and sprinkle with rosemary. Drizzle the oil over and bake in the oven for 10 min until finished. Place it on a wire rack so it does not become soft.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 190 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 1350 KJ (350 kcal). Carbohydrates: 21 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Chicken in salad with greens

ingredients.name: small iceberg lettuce or other lettuce that can be divided into leaves

preparation: Boil the chicken in a little bouillon for about 15 minutes. Drain the cooking water and shred the meat. Divide the broccoli into smaller florets. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and slice the asparagus into strips. Slice the sugar peas and spring onions. Heat the oil in a pan and add the curry paste. Sauté the broccoli, asparagus, sugar peas, garlic, and ginger over high heat for about 3-4 minutes. Shake the pan during the process so it does not burn. Add soy sauce and remove the pan from the heat. Rinse the lettuce leaves and spin them dry. Arrange the chicken and vegetables in the lettuce leaves. Top with spring onions, fresh coriander, and sprinkle sesame seeds over.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 800 KJ (200 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 10 g. Protein: 17 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Roasted chickpeas with chipotle
preparation: Dry the cooked chickpeas well. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and roast the chickpeas with chipotle until they are golden and slightly crispy. Season with salt and serve as a snack.
notes: Energy distribution* 300 KJ (75 kcal). Carbohydrate 6 g. Protein 10 g. Fat 4 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Cottage pie
preparation:
Mashed potatoes: Peel the potatoes and boil them until tender in a pot with plenty of water. Drain and place the tender potatoes in a bowl and mash them while gradually adding the milk – you can warm the milk slightly beforehand. The mash should be airy. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

Meat sauce: Chop the onion and garlic, grate the carrots, cut the zucchini into cubes, and slice the leek into thin strips. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion. Add the meat and brown it well over high heat. Lower the heat and then add the garlic, carrots, zucchini, leek, worcester sauce, tomato paste, red wine, and bouillon along with the spices, and let everything simmer for about 10 min. Season the meat sauce with salt and pepper.

Spread the meat sauce into an ovenproof dish, or 4 ovenproof bowls, and place a layer of mashed potatoes on top. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and a little parmesan cheese. Bake in the oven at 180 degrees for about 30 min until the mash is golden.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 190 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 51 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Salad pizza with minced beef, sour cream and bulgur
preparation: Spread the whole grain tortillas on two baking sheets lined with parchment paper. Spread with tomato paste. Drain the mozzarella and crumble it over the pizzas. Peel the onion and cut into thin wedges. Press the garlic. Distribute the onion, garlic, and beef in small mounds on the tortilla bases. Sprinkle with oregano and season with flaked salt and pepper. Bake the bases at 225 degrees fan for approx. 8 min. Rinse the tomatoes and cut them into halves or quarters, depending on the size. Rinse the salad. Toss the tomatoes with the salad and cooked bulgur. Top the freshly baked tortilla pizzas with the bulgur salad and sour cream.
notes:
Friday treat. Small cheat pizzas with a delicious topping of bulgur, crunchy salad and low-fat sour cream. Lightning fast to make and a guaranteed success.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 3000 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrate: 70 g. Fat: 26 g. Of which saturated fat: 14 g.

title: Pork cheeks in beer with root vegetables, apples and toasted buckwheat
preparation: Chop the onions. Peel the carrots and celery root and cut into small cubes. Coat the pork cheeks in wheat flour. Fry the bacon until crispy in a saucepan, and place it to drain on a piece of fat-absorbing paper. Heat half of the oil in the pan and sauté the onions, pressed garlic, carrots, and celery. Remove the vegetables. Pour the rest of the oil into the pan and brown the meat. Add the bacon and vegetables back into the pan, and pour in the beer and bouillon. Add the rosemary sprigs and bay leaves, and let the meat simmer at low heat under a lid for approx. 1½ hours. Toast the buckwheat until crispy and golden in a dry pan. Cut the apples into wedges. Remove the core and cut the apples into slices. Gently fold the apples into the dish and season with salt, pepper, and possibly a little balsamic vinegar. Serve the dish on kale leaves topped with toasted buckwheat and with coarse bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal). Carbohydrates: 69 g. Fat: 21 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Spaghetti carbonara with spinach, leeks and feta crumble
preparation: Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Slice the leeks into rings, rinse them free of soil, and drain them in a sieve. Fry the bacon bits until crispy together with the leeks and pressed garlic in a dry pan. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging. During the last minute, cook the spinach together with the pasta. Drain the pasta and return it to the pot. Mix the pasta with the bacon and leeks. Whisk the eggs together with the bouillon and gently fold the mixture into the pasta. Warm the dish over low heat and stir gently until it reaches a creamy consistency. Season the dish with salt and pepper and sprinkle with crumbled feta cheese when serving.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 159 g per person. Energy distribution: 2517 KJ (599 kcal). Carbohydrates: 86 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g.

title: 2 pieces of smørrebrød

ingredient_sections.section_name: Potato sandwich with egg and corn

preparation: Crispy chicken with avocado and dip: Spread the bread with herb dip and top with crispy chicken. Halve the avocado, remove the stone and skin, and slice. Squeeze lemon juice over. Arrange the avocado on the chicken and sprinkle with chopped chives. Potato sandwich with egg and corn: Boil the egg for about 6-7 min. Cool and peel it. Spread the bread with a thin layer of mayonnaise. Halve the potatoes and arrange them on the bread. Halve the egg. Top the potato sandwich with egg, and sprinkle with corn and cress. Cut the cucumber into strips with a vegetable peeler and arrange over the food before serving. Alternatively, cut the cucumber into small cubes to be sprinkled on top.
notes: NOTE: For this dish, you will need leftovers from these recipes: Crispy chicken with herb dip and lentil salad, Baked fish, celery puree, lemon-marinated beans and sesame potatoes. Energy distribution: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrate: 57 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 27 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Noodle salad with chicken and autumn vegetables
preparation: Noodle salad: Boil the chicken breast fillets for about 15 minutes. Drain the cooking water and shred the meat with two forks. Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain them. Autumn vegetables: Slice the carrots diagonally. Finely shred the kale. Boil the kale for about 2 minutes and drain it. Peel the oranges and cut them into segments. Finely slice the spring onions. Toss the noodles with the chicken and vegetables. Season with pepper. Dressing: Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Mix all the dressing ingredients together and toss it into the salad. Sprinkle the salad with sesame seeds and top with fresh coriander.
