notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 53 g, Protein: 25 g, Fat: 11 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Eggs in cocotte with potatoes and spinach
preparation: Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Slice the potatoes. Distribute the potatoes, spinach, and tomatoes into four small cocottes or ovenproof bowls. The spinach takes up a lot of volume, but will shrink during baking. Crack the eggs, one into each cocotte, season with salt and pepper, and gently swirl with a fork. Place the cocottes in the oven at 180 degrees and bake for approximately 15 minutes until the egg mixture has set. Serve them with toasted rye bread.
notes: Tip! You can add Parma ham to the cocottes. Distribute 1 slice into each cocotte, or serve Parma ham as a side dish to the cocottes. Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrate: 31 g. Protein: 14 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Moroccan lamb with plenty of spices
preparation: Cut the meat into cubes. Chop the onions. Heat half of the oil in a pot and brown the meat on all sides. Remove the meat. Heat the rest of the oil and brown the onions. Add the meat, pressed garlic, and spices to the pot and add the bouillon. Let the meat simmer under a lid at low heat for approximately 2 hours. Peel the carrots and celery. Slice the carrots and dice the celery. Add the vegetables to the pot with the meat along with the apricots, and let it simmer for an additional approximately 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Season the dish with salt and pepper. Add chopped coriander and serve the dish with steamed couscous.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 257 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2879 KJ (686 kcal). Carbohydrates: 83 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Pumpkin soup with sesame chicken
preparation: Pumpkin soup: Chop the onions. Peel the pumpkin and remove the seeds. Cut the pumpkin flesh into smaller pieces. Sauté the onions in oil in a pot for 3 minutes. Add the pumpkin and sauté for a few minutes. Add the bouillon and boil the soup for about 20 minutes until the pumpkin is completely tender. Blend the soup and season with salt. You can dilute with a little water if the soup is too thick. Sesame chicken: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until they begin to smell and pop in the pan. Place them on a plate. Cut the chicken into thin strips. Brown the meat on all sides in oil in the pan. Season with salt. Toss the chicken meat with the sesame seeds and chopped thyme. Serve the soup in bowls and sprinkle the chicken on top of the soup. Serve with bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (470 kcal). Carbohydrates: 61 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Vegetarian hash with greens and fried eggs

ingredients.name: baked, boiled or fried root vegetables in bite-sized pieces, e.g. Jerusalem artichokes, beets, parsnips, Jerusalem artichokes or celery
thick slices of whole grain rye bread

preparation: Vegetarian hash: Chop the onion. Cut the potatoes into smaller pieces. Divide the broccoli into small florets. Rinse and spin the spinach dry. Heat the oil in a large pan, and fry the onion and pressed garlic for a few minutes. Add the potatoes, root vegetables, broccoli and chopped rosemary, and fry over medium heat until the root vegetables and potatoes are crispy and tender. Add the spinach, and let it wilt slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Fried eggs: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the eggs sunny-side up. Serve the hash with fried eggs and rye bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2800 KJ (700 kcal). Carbohydrates: 97 g. Protein: 24 g. Fat: 18 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Tabbouleh with plenty of protein and steamed cod
preparation: Tabbouleh: Rinse the lentils and cook as indicated on the packaging. Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Halve the tomatoes, dice the bell pepper, peel and chop the onion. Rinse the parsley and drain. Finely chop the parsley. Chop the almonds. Toss the lentils with chickpeas, tomatoes, bell pepper, onion, parsley, and almonds. Grate the lemon zest and fold into the tabbouleh. Drizzle the oil over. Cod: Place the cod in a pan, season with flaked salt and pepper, and cover with bouillon about 1 cm above the fish. Steam under a lid at low heat for approx. 5 min, until it flakes. Carefully remove the fish. Serving: Arrange the tabbouleh and serve with the cod.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (450 kcal), Carbohydrate: 32 g, Protein: 38 g, Fat: 15 g, of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Herring with apple salad and raw pickled red onions
preparation: Raw Pickled Red Onions: Slice the onions into thin rings, e.g., using a mandoline slicer. Mix vinegar with honey and water and pour over the onions. Massage the onions well. Apple Salad: Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the core and cut the apples into thin wedges. Split the chili, scrape out the seeds, and finely chop the chili. Toss the apples with lemon juice and chili. Finely chop the coriander and fold it into the apple salad. Cut the rye bread in half. Cut the herring into smaller pieces. Arrange on rye bread with apple salad and raw pickled red onions.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 75 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 38 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 9 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Shrimp salad with cauliflower
preparation: Cut approximately 1/6 of the cauliflower into thin slices and set them aside for garnish. Cut the rest of the cauliflower into small florets and boil them in lightly salted water for 2-3 minutes until they are tender with a slight bite. Let them cool under cold water and drain well in a sieve. Remove the seeds and pith from the chili and finely chop it. Mix the mayonnaise together with the paprika, chili, and skyr, fromage frais, or quark. Set aside a few shrimp for garnish. Toss the shrimp and cauliflower florets in the dressing and season the salad with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Place 2 lettuce leaves on each slice of rye bread and distribute the shrimp salad onto the bread. Garnish with raw cauliflower slices and finely chopped chives.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 18 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1200 KJ (300 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 26 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Squash pasta with spinach and leek
preparation: Chop the onion. Press the garlic. Clean the leeks and cut them into rings. Chop the dill. Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, pressed garlic, and leek for a couple of minutes. Mix 1 dl of milk with cornstarch. Add the rest of the milk to the pot with the vegetables and heat up. Stir in the thickening agent while stirring and boil for approx. 2 min. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Add the spinach and let it gently wilt slightly. Cut the squash into strips similar to the pasta. Cook the pasta as indicated on the packaging. Cook the squash pasta with it for the final minute. Drain the pasta and squash and toss with the sauce. Serve the pasta in deep plates and sprinkle dill over top.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 160 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 19 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Cup Noodles with chicken

ingredients.name: crushed bouillon cube or bouillon powder

preparation: Cup Noodles: Boil the noodles as indicated on the packaging and drain. Place a pot over heat with water, and give the frozen vegetables a quick boil and drain. Chicken: Heat the oil in a pot and add the curry paste. Add the chicken meat and sauté the meat until it is cooked through, and season with soy sauce and pepper. Rinse and chop the coriander and mix it with the chicken meat. Save the rest of the chicken meat (half, 200 g) for another recipe. Or you can choose to only fry 200 g of chicken meat, which is intended for the cup noodles. Serving: Distribute the cooked noodles and all vegetables into two glasses or heat-safe containers. Crush the bouillon and sprinkle over. Top with the meat. Pour boiling water over right before serving and stir.
notes: There are homemade cup noodles on the menu in a much healthier version than the ones you buy. Enjoy the noodles here and now, or store all ingredients in a glass or container for the next day, and pour boiling water over right before serving. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 275 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1750 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 30 g. Protein: 6 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Tuna to go

ingredients.name: small bunch coriander, basil or parsley

preparation: Cook bulgur as indicated on the packaging and let it cool. Drain the tuna and mix with aioli and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage and slice it finely. Sprinkle with sugar and salt and massage it well. Cut the bell pepper into small cubes. Layer in a lunch box – to be taken with you – bulgur, cabbage, edamame beans, bell pepper and tuna. Top with avocado and pea dip and herbs.
notes: NOTE: This dish includes ingredients from these recipes: aioli and pea-avocado dip. * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1800 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 11 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Olive tapenade
preparation: Place the olives in a blender or mini chopper together with the sun-dried tomatoes, olive oil, pressed garlic, chopped almonds, and lemon juice. Blend together until a smooth, spreadable consistency is achieved and season with flaked salt and pepper. Place the tapenade in a jar with a lid and store in the refrigerator. Use the tapenade on toasted whole grain bread or toss it with whole grain pasta.
notes: 1 jar, approx. 175 g. Tip! Energy distribution below is per 100 g. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 15 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (250 kcal), Carbohydrate 10 g, Protein 4 g, Fat 24 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: Fatair – Bread parcels with spinach filling

ingredients.name: fresh spinach - also use the soft stems
optionally flavored with chopped parsley or garlic

preparation: Dough: Crumble the yeast into the water. Add salt, oil, and whole wheat flour. Add the wheat flour a little at a time. Knead the dough well, adding more flour until the dough no longer sticks. Let the dough rise covered for about ½ hour. Filling: Rinse the spinach thoroughly and chop it coarsely. Peel and finely chop the onion. Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the onion. Add the spinach and let it sauté until it wilts. Let the spinach cook until it becomes dry. Add the pressed garlic, salt, pepper, and season with sumac. Preheat the oven to 250 degrees. Bread parcels with spinach filling: Divide the dough into 20 small balls and roll them out into circles approximately 12-15 cm in diameter. Place about 2 tbsp of spinach filling in the center of the dough. Fold the dough together so it looks like a triangle and press the edges firmly together. Place the breads on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bake the spinach breads in the oven for about 15 minutes. Optionally, give them a little grill for a couple of minutes at the end to make them crispy. Side: Serve the breads freshly baked, optionally with yogurt flavored with chopped parsley or pressed garlic.
notes: Tip! You can make fatair in large batches and freeze them. They can be reheated in the oven for a few minutes, and then they are ready. Fatair can also be made with ground beef.

title: Herring salad with curry, beans and potato
preparation: Cut the potatoes into small cubes. Trim the beans and boil them in lightly salted water for about 4 minutes. Cool the beans under cold water and let them drain in a sieve. Cut the beans into 2 cm lengths. Halve the chili, remove the seeds, and finely chop it. Chop the parsley and finely chop the onion. Mix the skyr with curry, chili, parsley, and half of the onions. Cut the herring into pieces 1 cm wide and toss them in the dressing. Season the herring salad with salt and pepper. Serve the herring salad on thick slices of rye bread and sprinkle with the remaining onions.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 61 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 50 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Onion pâté with almonds
preparation: Chop the onions. Grate the apples with the peel on using a grater. Sauté the onions and apples in oil for 4-5 minutes without letting them take much color. Chop the almonds. Stir in the almonds and oatmeal. Stir in the milk. Boil together while stirring for a couple of minutes. Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the eggs one at a time. Stir in the soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Place the pâté in a greased ovenproof dish. Bake the pâté in the oven at 200 degrees for about 50 minutes until it is fully cooked. Serve the pâté warm with whole grain bread and tomatoes.
notes:
Tip! Any leftovers of the pâté can be used cold as a topping on rye bread.
Energy distribution: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 61 g, Protein: 26 g, Fat: 19 g, of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Kale tartare with anchovies

ingredients.name: thick slices of whole grain bread or rye bread

preparation: Rib the kale, rinse it well, and let it drain. Cut the kale into very thin strips and chop it slightly afterwards. Finely chop the red onion. Chop the anchovies very finely and mix them with the mayonnaise. Thin the mayonnaise with vinegar. Toss the kale and red onion with the mayonnaise. Season the tartare with salt and pepper. Serve the kale tartare on toasted whole grain bread or rye bread.
notes:
Tip! The kale tartare can also be used as a side dish for fried and grilled meat, fish, and poultry.
Fruit and vegetables approx. 60 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution: 950 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate 23 g, Fat 10 g, of which saturated fat 1 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Smoked salmon with horseradish cream
preparation:
Horseradish cream: Mix skyr with mayonnaise and freshly grated horseradish. Season the cream with salt and pepper.

Smoked salmon: Cut the salmon into 8 or 16 pieces and roll them up.

Toast the rye bread on both sides and cut it into halves or quarters. Top the bread with horseradish cream and arrange the salmon on top. Garnish with dill and season with salt and pepper.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 22 g, Protein 11 g, Fat 6 g, of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Whole grain bagels
preparation: Boil the oatmeal and water and remove the pot from the heat. Let it cool until lukewarm. Stir in yeast, sugar, oil, milk, and salt. Add whole wheat flour and all-purpose flour. Knead the dough until it is smooth. Let the dough rise covered for approx. 1 hour in a warm place. Divide the dough into 14 pieces. Shape them into buns. Make a hole in the middle so that rings are formed; the hole should have a diameter of 3 cm. Let the rings proof for another 15 minutes. Boil water in a deep pan. Boil the dough rings several times, 1 minute each. Remove them with a slotted spoon. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush the rings with beaten egg. Sprinkle sesame seeds over them. Bake at 200 degrees for approx. 20 minutes.
notes: Tip! These bagels are suitable for breakfast, lunch, and as a snack. For example, you can split the bagels, spread them with a little light cream cheese, and fill them with lettuce leaves and slices of smoked salmon. Another option is to spread them with mashed avocado and add slices of fried chicken breast along with slices of cucumber and bell pepper. Energy distribution per piece: 800 KJ (650 kcal), Carbohydrates 30 g, Protein 6 g, Fat 3.8 g, of which saturated fat 0.7 g, Dietary fiber 5 g.

title: Spring salad with lightly cured pork tenderloin and rhubarb
preparation:
Lightly cured pork tenderloin
Day 1: Sprinkle the meat with salt and sugar, and place it in a freezer bag. Tie a knot in the bag, and rub the brine well into the meat. Place the meat in the refrigerator until the next day.
Day 2: Rinse the meat to remove the "marinade," and dry it well. Heat the oil in a pan, and brown the tenderloin. Finish cooking it in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 15 minutes. Let the meat rest for approx. 5-10 minutes before slicing it into pieces.

Rhubarb
Cut the rhubarb into smaller pieces. Spread them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and drizzle honey over them. Bake the rhubarb at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes, until they are tender.

Spring salad
Remove the outer leaves and the core from the cabbage, and shred the cabbage finely. Halve the radicchio, remove the core and outer leaves, and chop the salad coarsely. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus, and steam the asparagus for 2 minutes. Discard the cooking water and pour cold water over. Drain the asparagus and cut into strips.

Toss the cabbage with radicchio and asparagus. Mix oil with vinegar, mustard, and honey, and drizzle the dressing over the salad. Arrange the salad with the sliced meat and rhubarb. Toast the almonds until golden in a dry pan, and chop them. Sprinkle the almonds over the salad and serve with coarse bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 65 g. Protein: 35 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Homemade rye bread
preparation:
Begin 4-5 days before use if you do not already have rye sourdough starter.

Rye sourdough starter: Mix the rye flour thoroughly with the water in a small bowl or a jar. Cover the bowl or jar with a loose lid or plastic wrap, and let it stand on the kitchen counter for 4-5 days. Stir it once a day. When the dough has bubbled and smells like beer for a couple of days, it is ready to use.

Dough: Knead all ingredients together into a good, thick, and sticky dough. Set aside 2 dl of dough for the next sourdough starter, place it in a container with an airtight lid, and store it in the refrigerator. Grease the bread tin with oil. Place the rest of the dough in the tin. Smooth the surface with a dough scraper dipped in water. Cover the tin with plastic wrap, and let it stand in a warm place for approx. 6 hours. Bake the bread at 190 degrees for 45 minutes. Remove the bread from the tin and let it cool down. Store the completely cooled rye bread in a plastic bag.
notes:
The heart loves whole grains. They have a beneficial effect on both blood pressure, cholesterol levels, weight, and blood sugar. Therefore, there are good reasons to eat rye bread and whole grain bread.

Tip! If the plastic wrap sticks a bit to the dough after rising, remove it as gently as you can so the dough does not collapse or the surface does not become pitted. The easiest way is to get a scoop of sourdough from someone you know who bakes their own rye bread. Or buy a jar of ready-made sourdough. It is sourdough that is already well underway and can be used together with it. If you cannot obtain sourdough, you can try to make it yourself. Perhaps it won't succeed the first time, but do not give up. The more freshly milled the flour is, the easier the sourdough will be to get started. Your sourdough will gradually improve as it has been used a few times.

Energy distribution per 100 g: 700 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 28 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 1 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.2 g.

title: Wraps with tuna-tomato filling and cabbage salad
preparation: Tuna-tomato filling: Coarsely chop the onions and dice the bell peppers. Sauté them in the oil in a pot, without letting them brown, for about 8 minutes. Add the tomato paste and 1 dl water, and let the sauce simmer for about 5 minutes. Drain the tuna and mix it into the sauce. Add the pressed garlic and season with finely grated lemon juice, cayenne pepper, and vinegar. Cabbage salad: Finely shred the kale and massage it with oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Let it marinate for 10 minutes. Finely shred the pointed cabbage and mix it with the kale. Serving: Warm the wraps as indicated on the packaging. Distribute the tuna filling and the salad into the wraps, roll them up, and serve.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 500 kcal. Carbohydrates: 61 g, Protein: 32 g, Fat: 12 g, of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Smørrebrød with herring and leek cream
preparation:
Marinated herring: Cut the herring in half and trim off the fins. Cut each fillet into 3 diagonal slices and place them in a dish. Slice the onion. Boil vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper in a pot. Add the onion slices to the brine and boil for a couple of minutes, then pour the brine over the herring. The herring is ready once they have cooled down.

Leek cream: Finely slice the leeks and rinse them thoroughly in a bowl of cold water. Place the leeks in a pot with the remaining water. Boil them without a lid, stirring occasionally, until they collapse and are tender, while the water evaporates. Let the leeks cool down. Mix the skyr with mustard, fold in the leeks, and season with salt and pepper.

Spread the leek cream onto the 4 slices of rye bread. Let the herring drain, and place them on top of the leek cream. Garnish with watercress and onion from the herring brine.
notes:
Tip! The marinated herring can keep for a few days in the refrigerator. Instead of marinating the herring yourself, you can use 300 grams of pre-marinated herring.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 75 g per person, unless otherwise stated.

Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate: 50 g, Protein: 27 g, Fat: 15 g, of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Club salad nicoise

ingredients.name: white cabbage, kale or red cabbage

preparation: Finely shred the cabbage. Sprinkle the cabbage with salt and sugar and massage it well. Trim the beans and steam them. Cut the cucumber into matchstick-thin strips – for example, using a julienne peeler. Slice the bell pepper. Boil the eggs and cut them into quarters. Drain the tuna and mix with yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, capers, and chopped dill. Season with salt and pepper. Toast the bread. Top half of the bread slices with cabbage, beans, tuna salad, cucumber, bell pepper, and egg. Top with the remaining slices of bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: approx. 35 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 58 g. Protein: 33 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Edible Wraps – tortilla with chicken and vegetables
preparation: Warm the tortillas according to the instructions on the packaging, and let them cool. Mix mayonnaise, tomato ketchup, and optionally worcestershire sauce. Cut cooked or fried chicken meat and red pepper into cubes and toss them in the mayonnaise mixture along with the drained corn. Season with salt and pepper. Distribute the shredded iceberg lettuce in the middle of the tortillas. Spread the chicken mixture over it. Fold the tortillas together as if you were wrapping a gift. Tie a piece of cotton butcher's twine around. Wrap the tortillas in parchment paper, optionally with a string tied around. You can also wrap a napkin. Pack the melon wedges and cucumber sticks separately.
notes:
Tip! Tortillas are Mexican flatbreads. The edible wraps are great to take with you, e.g., on a forest trip.
Fruit and vegetables approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate 36 g, Protein 8 g, Fat 5 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Spinach egg wrap with smoked salmon and crispy vegetables
preparation: Spinach egg wrap: Clean the spinach, rinse it well, and steam it in the remaining water. Squeeze the spinach free of water and chop it coarsely. Whisk the eggs with milk, whole wheat flour, and spinach, and season with salt and pepper. Heat half of the oil in a non-stick pan and pour in half of the egg mixture. Let it set, turn down the heat, and cover the pan with foil. Let it sit for a couple of minutes. Remove the foil and gently loosen the egg mixture with a spatula. Flip it onto a plate and repeat with the rest of the egg mixture. Crispy vegetables: Halve the cabbage. Remove the core and the outermost leaves, and finely shred the cabbage. Massage it well with salt and sugar so it softens. Slice the cucumber into very thin slices and toss with the cabbage. Fill the baked egg wraps with smoked salmon and cabbage salad – be careful not to overfill them – and roll them up gently. Cut the wraps through so you have 4 in total and serve with the remaining filling and rye bread as a side.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 32 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 15 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Beetroot Hummus

ingredients.name: vegetables e.g. carrots, cucumber, Chinese radish, kohlrabi

preparation: Beetroot hummus: Place the chickpeas in a bowl with cold water and let them stand covered until the next day. Rinse the chickpeas very well and place them in a pot with fresh water and boil them for approx. 35 min. Drain the chickpeas and save the cooking water. Peel and coarsely grate the beetroot. Place the chickpeas in a blender or food processor along with the coarsely grated beetroot, pressed garlic, cumin, tahini, lemon zest and juice, and olive oil. Blend and thin with the cooking water, about 1 dl at a time, until the hummus has a soft, smooth consistency. Season with salt. Accompaniments: Toast the pita breads and cut them into quarters. Peel the vegetables and cut them into sticks. Arrange the beetroot hummus in a bowl and sprinkle with parsley. Serve with toasted pita bread and crunchy vegetable sticks.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1200 KJ (300 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 40 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Pasta salad with peas, feta and ham

ingredients.name: lettuce head, e.g., frillice or hearts of lettuce

preparation: Dressing: Mix the cultured milk with curry powder. Thin it out with oil, lemon juice, and water. Season the dressing with salt and pepper. Pasta salad: Boil the pasta in a large pot of lightly salted water as indicated on the packaging. Pour the cooked pasta into a sieve and rinse it with cold water until it has cooled down. Let the pasta drain in the sieve. Cut the ham into cubes. Finely slice the onions. Cut the tomatoes into quarters, the cucumbers into cubes, and the radishes into slices. Wash and dry the lettuce and break it into smaller pieces. Shell the peas. Coarsely chop the dill. Thoroughly toss the pasta together with the dressing, ham, spring onions, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, peas, and dill. Season the pasta salad with salt, pepper, and optionally extra lemon juice. Thin it with a little water if the pasta salad seems dry. Toss the green salad into the pasta salad just before serving and sprinkle with crumbled feta.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2600 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 64 g. Protein: 33 g. Fat: 21 g. Of which saturated fat: 7 g.

title: Tart with ham and carrots
preparation: Mix wheat flour, rye flour, and oil in a bowl. Add salt and combine the dough with water, optionally in a food processor. Roll out the dough and place it in a greased tart pan approximately 22 cm in diameter. Slice the spring onions and grate the carrots. Sauté spring onions and carrots in oil in a pan for 3-5 minutes. Whisk eggs, cottage cheese, wheat flour, salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp grated parmesan cheese together. Cut the ham into strips. Fold the vegetables and ham into the egg mixture. Distribute the filling in the tart pan. Sprinkle the remaining parmesan cheese on top. Bake the tart for 50-60 minutes at 175 degrees. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Slice the spring onion and sprinkle it over the tomatoes. Optionally mix the sliced lettuce with the tomatoes.
notes: Tip! You can add cubes of boiled or fried chicken to the tart instead of ham. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person. Energy distribution: 2300 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 65 g. Protein: 26 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Heart bowl

ingredients.name: finely chopped herbs, e.g., parsley and chives

preparation:
Sweet ponzu: Whisk rice vinegar, ponzu, soy sauce, and honey together in a small bowl. Pour the dressing into a small container with a lid so it is ready for use. There is enough dressing for approx. 6 bowls (25 g per bowl, equivalent to 1.5 tbsp). Store the dressing in a container in the refrigerator. The dressing should be stirred/shaken before being poured over the salad.

Tartar sauce: Mix skyr with mayonnaise, mustard, capers, and chopped herbs. Season with pepper – the dressing does not need salt, as it gets plenty of salt from the capers. There is enough dressing for approx. 8 heart bowls (25 g per bowl). Store the dressing refrigerated in a container with a lid so it stays fresh for several days and can be used for other dishes, e.g., breaded fish and fish cakes. Alternatively, you can halve the portion so it is enough for 4 bowls.

Heart bowl: Cook the brown rice according to instructions and let it cool. Put edamame beans in a bowl, pour boiling water over them, and let them sit for a few minutes. Drain the water. Or ensure you take the edamame beans out in good time to defrost before making the bowl. Shred red cabbage and carrots into fine strips, possibly using a mandoline. Slice spring onions finely. Cut the salmon into cubes. Arrange the rice in a bowl, and mix the ponzu sauce with the rice. Top the rice with strips of carrot and finely shredded cabbage, as well as pickled red onion, edamame beans, and salmon cubes. Top with four 'strips' of tartar sauce (possibly using a piping bag or a dressing bottle with a nozzle), and sprinkle with sesame seeds and spring onion.
notes: Heart bowl was developed in collaboration between OLIOLI and the Heart Foundation's dietitian Lotte Juul. Heart bowl has a calorie content and nutritional composition corresponding to a healthy dinner and therefore stands out from other fast food. The recipe is calculated and approved according to the criteria for the Keyhole label. Please note that this recipe contains raw salmon. It is recommended that the salmon has been frozen for at least 24 hours at a minimum of -20 degrees before it is thawed and used in cooking. Energy distribution per person: 2700 KJ (650 kcal), Carbohydrate 75 g, Protein 33 g, Fat 19 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: Winter salad with Arabic roots
preparation: Cook the bulgur as indicated on the packaging together with the pressed garlic. Peel the carrots and cut them into small cubes. Peel the oranges and cut them into segments. Chop the red onion, almonds, mint, and parsley. Toss the bulgur with the carrots, oranges, red onion, almonds, and herbs. Halve the pomegranate and press the juice and seeds over the salad. Season the salad with salt and pepper and crumble the feta cheese over it.
notes: Tip! Feta cheese can be replaced with an equivalent amount of olives. Or omitted entirely. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person. Energy distribution: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 28 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g per person.

title: Savory muffins with ham and broccoli
preparation: Cut the broccoli into small florets and the stem into small cubes. Chop the onion. Sauté the broccoli and onion in 1 tbsp of oil in a pan for 2-3 minutes. Cool the mixture until it is lukewarm. Put the eggs in a bowl and stir in the parmesan cheese, milk, and wheat flour mixed with baking powder, salt, and pepper. Cut the ham into small cubes. Fold the ham and broccoli mixture in. Brush the muffin liners with the remaining oil. Distribute the batter into them. Bake at 180 degrees for approx. 40 minutes until they are golden and fully cooked. Cool them or eat them warm together with rye bread, carrots, and apples.
notes: Tip! You can place the paper muffin liners into a muffin tin so they hold their shape better. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrate: 30 g, Protein: 10 g, Fat: 10 g, of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Spring quinoa bowl with shrimp and herb cream
preparation: Quinoa bowl: Cook quinoa as indicated on the package and drain. Snap off the woody bottom end of the asparagus and steam them for one minute. Slice the asparagus. Slice the avocado into wedges and the radishes into slices. Rinse and spin the spinach dry, dice the cucumber and cut the tomatoes into wedges. Herb cream: Rinse the herbs and drain. Blend the herbs with yogurt and season with salt and pepper. Divide the quinoa, vegetables, and shrimp into four bowls. Serve the herb cream to drizzle over.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 350 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1500 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 35 g. Protein: 21 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Okonomiyaki with cabbage, salmon and spinach
preparation: Finely shred the cabbage. Sprinkle with salt and massage the cabbage well. Blend the oats into flour and whisk together with the bouillon and eggs. Fold the egg mixture into the cabbage. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, and fry two small okonomiyaki on both sides in the oil until they are well crispy. Mix the ingredients for the dressing together. Finely slice the spring onions. Rinse the spinach and shake it dry. Top the okonomiyaki with salmon, spinach, and spring onions, and drizzle the dressing over. Serve optionally with a little chervil.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1900 KJ (450 kcal). Carbohydrate: 21 g. Protein: 23 g. Fat: 16 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Gravad salmon with fox sauce
preparation: Gravad salmon: Remove the small bones with tweezers, or ask the fishmonger to do it. Dry the salmon well. Mix brown sugar with salt and distribute it over the salmon fillet. Season with pepper. Place the salmon skin-side up in a container with a tight-fitting lid, and place it in the refrigerator for at least 1 day – preferably a couple of days. Fox sauce: Whisk brown sugar, mustard, vinegar and oil together. Chop the dill and fold it into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Toast the bread. Rinse the lettuce and toss it dry. Slice the cucumber into slices and then into strips. Slice the salmon into thin slices. Calculate 75 g of sliced salmon per person. Top the bread with lettuce, salmon, cucumber, horseradish and fox sauce.
notes: Tip! Once the salmon is gravad, it can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 1 week in a container with a lid. The dish can also be served as part of a Christmas lunch, in which case it serves 8 people. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 65 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 3289 KJ (783 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 89 g. Fat: 30 g. Of which saturated fat: 6 g.

title: Mushroom Pâté

ingredients.name: cooked rice, bulgur, quinoa or similar
chopped fresh thyme or 2 tsp dried
rye bread or whole grain bread
rye bread or whole grain bread
pickled cornichons, pearl onions and/or caper berries

preparation: Coarsely chop the nuts and roast them in a dry, hot pan until they are lightly golden. Finely chop the onions. Clean the mushrooms and chop them finely. Sauté the onions in the oil over high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring along the way, add the mushrooms and continue frying until the mushrooms are dry and roasted, about 10 minutes. Mix the mushrooms with the bulgur or similar, nuts, garlic, thyme, eggs, skyr or fromage frais, salt and pepper. Place the mixture in an ovenproof dish, greased with oil, approximately 15×20 cm. Bake the pâté at 175 degrees for about 30 minutes, until the pâté is firm when pressed lightly. Serve the pâté warm with rye bread, pickled cucumbers, onions or capers or a good mixture of it all.
notes:
Tip! The mushrooms can be, for example, button mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, shiitake and portobello.
Fruit and vegetables approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated.
Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrate 64 g, Protein 19 g, Fat 16 g, of which saturated fat 2.5 g.

title: Salmon Tartare

ingredients.name: chopped herbs (e.g., dill, chervil or parsley)

preparation: Cut the fresh (raw) salmon into cubes. Finely chop the smoked salmon. Remember, the fresh salmon must have been frozen for at least 24 hours when to be eaten raw. Cut the apple into small cubes, and finely chop the onion. Peel the cucumber and remove the middle with a teaspoon. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Mix a dressing of sour cream, mustard, lemon, pepper, and herbs, and fold it into the salmon, apple, onion, and cucumber. Toast the bread. Top with lettuce leaves and salmon tartare.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 90 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1000 KJ (250 kcal) per person. Carbohydrate: 24 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Green sandwich with edamame hummus
preparation: Place the edamame beans, pressed garlic, oil, and skyr in a blender and process until a coarse cream is formed. Season with salt and pepper. Finely shred the kale and toss with lemon juice. Cut the cucumber into wide ribbons using a vegetable peeler. Slice the bread through. Fill with the edamame hummus, kale, and cucumber ribbons.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 160 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1500 KJ (355 kcal). Carbohydrates: 49 g. Fat: 11 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. The recipe is presented in collaboration with Pågen.

title: Tart with broccoli and turkey bacon
preparation: Pastry base: Mix wheat flour, rye flour, salt, and margarine thoroughly. Add the water and quickly knead the dough together. Press the dough into a tart pan approximately 25 cm in diameter and prick the bottom with a fork. Pre-bake the pastry base at the bottom of the oven for 15 min at 200 degrees. Filling: Cut the turkey bacon into cubes, chop the onion, divide the broccoli into small florets, and cut the stem into cubes. Heat the oil in a pan, sauté the turkey bacon, onion, and broccoli for 5 min, and let it cool slightly. Whisk the fromage frais together with salt, mustard, egg, flour, and milk. Fold the bacon, onion, and broccoli into the egg mixture and place everything into the pre-baked base. Bake the tart until finished for approximately 30 min at 200 degrees at the bottom of the oven.
notes: Energy distribution* 2500 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates 53 g. Protein 20 g. Fat 27 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Lunch salad with hot-smoked salmon and dill dressing
preparation: Finely shred the cabbage. Rinse the spinach and spin it dry. Slice the potatoes. Remove the skin from the salmon and flake it. Cut the cucumber into small cubes. Mix the yogurt with mayonnaise and chopped dill, and season with flaked salt and pepper. Toss the dill dressing with the cabbage and then with the spinach, potatoes, cucumber, and hot-smoked salmon. Arrange the salad and serve.
notes: Use leftover boiled potatoes for a hearty, filling lunch salad with fatty fish and crunchy cabbage. Energy distribution per person: 1300 KJ (300 kcal), Carbohydrates 25 g, Protein 20 g, Fat 13 g (including 2 g saturated fat), Dietary fiber 5 g. Fruit and vegetables: approx. 250 g per person.

title: Whole Grain Rye Bread

ingredients.name: flavor-neutral oil to grease the pan

preparation: DAY 1: Place the rye kernels in a bowl and pour boiling water over them. Let the kernels soak for 30 minutes. Put the beer and yogurt in a large bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add syrup, salt, soaked rye kernels, flaxseeds, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds. Stir well, and then stir the rye flour into the dough. Knead the dough for about 10 minutes – preferably in a stand mixer. Alternatively, use a hand mixer with dough hooks. Grease a rye bread tin (approx. 2.5 liters) with oil, and distribute the dough into the tin. Smooth the surface with damp hands, and place the tin covered in the refrigerator to rise until the next day. DAY 2: Take the tin with the dough out of the refrigerator about 1 hour before you want to bake. Preheat the oven to 170 degrees fan air. Bake the rye bread for about 1.5 hours. Let the bread cool for about 10 minutes in the tin before turning it out onto a cooling rack to cool completely.
notes: Tip! Use sunflower seeds, flaxseeds, and pumpkin seeds depending on what you have in your kitchen drawer and what you like best. The total amount of kernels and seeds should be 225 grams. Energy distribution per 100 g: 1000 KJ (250 kcal), Carbohydrate: 30 g, Protein: 8 g, Fat: 9 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g

title: Pork Roast Sandwich with Raw Red Cabbage and Cucumber Salad

ingredients.name: small pork loin with crackling without bone

preparation: Pork Roast: Score the crackling if necessary, but avoid scoring the meat itself. Carefully rub the salt down between each piece of crackling. Place the roast on a rack with a roasting pan underneath. The roast and the crackling should preferably lie horizontally during roasting. Optionally, place a piece of foil under the roast at the lowest end. Insert a meat thermometer into the center of the meat. Pour water into the bottom of the roasting pan and place the roast in the oven at 180 degrees. When the meat's core temperature reaches 50 degrees, increase the oven temperature to 250 degrees until the core temperature reaches 65 degrees. Keep an eye on the crackling so it does not get too dark. Remove the roast and let it rest for about 10 minutes. Slice the roast. For pork roast sandwiches for 4 people, you will need 8 slices. Cut the fat layer off between the crackling and the meat. Cucumber Salad: Slice the cucumber into thin slices. Sprinkle the cucumber slices with salt and let them sit for about 30 minutes. Rinse the salt off the cucumber slices and squeeze them well. Mix vinegar with water and sugar and pour the brine over the cucumbers. Season with pepper. Raw Red Cabbage: Remove the stem and the outermost leaves of the cabbage. Shred the cabbage finely. Sprinkle the cabbage with sugar and salt and toss it well. Let the cabbage sit for about 15 minutes. Dressing: Finely chop the onion. Mix yogurt with mayonnaise, onion, and mustard. Season with salt and pepper. Split the buns. Spread them with dressing and fill them with red cabbage salad, sliced pork roast, and cucumber salad.
notes: Tip! If the crackling on the roast does not become crispy, take the roast out of the oven when it has a core temperature of 65 degrees. Cut the crackling off the roast and divide it so the pieces of crackling lie individually. Place them in a roasting pan and turn the oven temperature up to 225-250 degrees. Watch so the crackling does not get too dark, and let them roast until they are crispy. Optionally, turn them a few times during the process.

title: Open-faced sandwiches with avocado butter and shrimp
preparation: Remove the peel and stone from the avocados and mash the avocado flesh smoothly with a fork. Season the avocado butter with a little freshly squeezed lemon juice and salt. Spread the avocado butter on the rye bread. Cut the rye bread in half crosswise. Chop the dill. Mix the shrimp with the dill and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Spread the shrimp on the avocado sandwiches. Sprinkle with freshly ground pepper. Clean the radishes and rinse and dry the lettuce. Serve the sandwiches with radishes and lettuce leaves on the side.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrate: 24 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Eggless tart with tomato and spinach

ingredients.name: thick slices of whole grain bread

preparation: Tart crust: Put flour and salt in a bowl, and add the oil. Combine the dough with the water. Press the dough firmly into a greased tart pan approximately 22 cm in diameter, and prick the bottom with a fork. Pre-bake the crust at 200 degrees for approx. 15 minutes. Filling: Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Rinse the spinach well, and steam it in the water clinging to it. Drain the spinach and toss with tomatoes and mozzarella. Distribute the filling onto the tart crust. Season with chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper, and bake the tart in the oven for approx. 20 minutes, until golden. Snip the beans. Cut the broccoli into florets. Steam the beans and broccoli for a few minutes until they are tender. Serve the tart with broccoli, beans, and coarse bread.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 2100 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 54 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Root vegetable chips with tartar sauce

ingredients.name: root vegetables such as parsnips, carrots and beets
herbs such as chervil, parsley, dill, basil

preparation: Root vegetable chips: Peel the root vegetables and slice them very thinly lengthwise using a mandoline slicer. Place the vegetables in a freezer bag with olive oil and massage them gently so the oil is distributed. Place the vegetables on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper – they should be spread out. Season with salt and bake them until crispy in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 15 min. Open the oven occasionally to let the steam escape. Remove the root vegetable chips as they become crispy. Cool the chips. Tartar sauce: Stir the skyr with mayonnaise and mustard. Chop the herbs and fold them into the cream along with the capers. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle the root vegetable chips with salt and serve with tartar sauce.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 750 KJ (175 kcal). Carbohydrates: 18 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Crispbread with seeds and grains

ingredients.name: various seeds for sprinkling, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds and flaxseeds

preparation: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt, oil, flaxseeds, rye flour and wheat flour, and knead the dough together until it is a soft and elastic dough. Let the dough rise covered until it doubles in size – approx. 45 minutes. Divide the dough into two, and roll each piece of dough out thinly between two pieces of parchment paper into a rectangle, approx. 20×30 cm. Remove the top piece of parchment paper, prick the dough with a fork, and cut each piece into approx. 12 pieces. Lift the parchment paper with the dough onto baking sheets. Brush with water and sprinkle with seeds. Gently run the rolling pin over the crispbread dough, and bake the crispbreads at 200 degrees fan temperature for approx. 15 minutes. Turn down to 100 degrees, and bake the breads until finished for 15 minutes, until they are crispy. Let the crispbreads cool on a wire rack, and store them in an airtight container.
notes: Tip! Energy distribution is indicated per piece. Fruit and vegetables Approx. 2 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 300 KJ (75 kcal). Carbohydrates 12 g. Protein 2 g. Fat 2 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Granola snack bar
preparation: Place the oats in a dry pan and toast until they smell slightly and gain some color. Transfer the oats to a bowl. Place the almonds, sunflower seeds, and pumpkin seeds in the pan and toast until they become golden. Add them to the bowl along with the raisins, chopped apricots, and flaked salt. Chop the dates and place them in a mini chopper or blender with 2 tbsp cold water. Blend into a paste. Place the date paste and peanut butter in the pan and melt them together over low heat while stirring for about 5 min. Fold the paste and honey into the dry ingredients. Knead the mixture together and press it down into a mold lined with parchment paper. Spread it well into the sides and smooth the surface – optionally with damp fingertips. Place the mold in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, after which it is sliced into bars.
notes: Energy distribution* per piece: 850 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 21 g. Protein: 6 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Pea-avocado dip
preparation: Halve the avocado, remove the stone, and scoop the flesh into a blender/mini chopper. Add the peas, lemon juice, pressed garlic, and olive oil and blend until a creamy dip is formed. Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: approx. 80 g per 100 g. Energy distribution per 100 g: 850 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 8 g. Protein: 6 g. Fat: 17 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Broccoli Buns

ingredients.name: semi-skimmed or skimmed milk for brushing

preparation: Divide the broccoli into florets and steam them in the water for 3-4 min. Remove the pot from the heat and blend. Place the broccoli and boiling water in a bowl together with the yogurt and cool until finger-warm, before dissolving the yeast in it. Add sunflower seeds, salt, and oats, and knead the white whole wheat flour into the liquid little by little. Knead until the dough is moist and cohesive. Place the dough covered to rise in a warm place for approx. 1 hour. Shape the dough into 10 buns and place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Let the buns rise for approx. 30 min. Brush with milk and bake the buns in a preheated oven at 220 degrees fan heat for approx. 20 min. until they are golden.
notes: Tip! White wheat is a whole wheat, and whole grain is healthy for the heart. White wheat is easy to work with and provides good flavor to your whole grain buns. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 40 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal), Carbohydrate 33 g, Protein 11 g, Fat 5 g, of which saturated fat 1 g, Dietary fiber 7.5 g.

title: Date balls with marzipan

ingredients.name: oatmeal for rolling the balls in

preparation: Place dates and oil in a blender and blend them together. Add grated marzipan, cocoa powder, chia seeds, orange marmalade, and oatmeal. Mix the mass well and adjust the consistency with water. The mass should be sticky. You can optionally add a few drops of rum essence. Roll into 40 balls and coat them in oatmeal.
notes: Approx. 40 pieces (4 pieces per person). Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 8 g, Protein: 4 g, Fat: 6 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Popcorn Bark with Chocolate
preparation: Pour the oil into a large pot and add the corn kernels. Pop them under a lid over even heat until they no longer make noise. Shake the pot during the process. Spread the popcorn onto a piece of parchment paper and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Toss the popcorn with the cranberries. Melt the chocolate in a bowl over a water bath. Drizzle the chocolate over the popcorn and toss it around so the popcorn becomes partially covered by the chocolate. Let the chocolate harden before breaking the popcorn into smaller pieces.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 18 g. Protein: 2 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 4.5 g.

title: Lemon cakes with lightly toasted meringue

ingredients.name: wheat flour + extra for the molds

preparation: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees. Grate the zest of the lemons and squeeze out the juice. Whisk eggs and sugar until they form a light, airy mixture. Mix the wheat flour with the almond flour and baking powder, then fold it into the batter along with the lemon juice and zest. Finally, stir the olive oil into the batter. Grease 8 small molds (approx. 8 cm in diameter) with a little oil and sprinkle with flour. Distribute the batter into the molds and bake in the oven for approximately 12 minutes. Use a skewer to check if the cakes are baked. If batter clings to it, bake for a little longer. Let the cakes cool. Whisk the egg white until stiff. Gradually add the sugar until it no longer granulates.
notes: Amount: 8 cakes (1 pc. per person). Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrate 25 g, Protein 5 g, Fat 8 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Whole grain crispbread with seeds

ingredients.name: seeds and kernels, e.g., sunflower seeds, flaxseeds and pumpkin seeds

preparation: Preheat the oven to 185 degrees. Combine oatmeal, whole wheat flour, seeds and kernels in a bowl along with baking powder and salt. Add water and oil and mix the dough well. The dough should be slightly sticky. Roll the dough out between two pieces of parchment paper to a thickness of approx. 3 mm. Remove the top piece of parchment paper. Cut the dough into squares of approx. 5 × 8 cm, and gently lift them onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush them with beaten egg and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds. Bake the crispbread in the oven for 20-25 minutes until they are golden and crispy. Cool the crispbread on a wire rack.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 0.5 g per person. Energy distribution per piece: 500 KJ (100 kcal). Carbohydrates: 10 g. Protein: 4 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.8 g.

title: Herbed Quick Bread

ingredients.name: fresh herbs that withstand heat, e.g., thyme and rosemary

preparation: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add the honey, and stir the chickpea flour into the liquid along with the salt. Gradually knead the white whole wheat flour into the dough, and mix for about 10 min. in a stand mixer. Let the dough rise covered on the kitchen counter for about 1 hour. Pour the dough into a greased ovenproof dish. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees fan, and let the bread rise while the oven heats up. Brush with olive oil and distribute herbs over the dough. Sprinkle with flaked salt and bake the bread for about 20 min. until it is golden.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 32 g, Protein 6 g, Fat 2 g, of which saturated fat 1 g. * per 100 g

title: Crudité with edamame cream

ingredients.name: vegetables e.g. carrots, cucumber, daikon radish, kohlrabi

preparation: Edamame cream: Place edamame beans, pressed garlic, olive oil and skyr in a blender and blend to a creamy consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Accompaniments: Toast the pita bread and cut into quarters. Peel the vegetables and cut into sticks. Serve edamame cream with toasted pita bread and crunchy vegetable sticks.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 250 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 29 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Oatmeal peaks with chocolate
preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Place the oatmeal in a bowl with brown sugar, baking powder, vanilla sugar, and cinnamon. Chop the chocolate and fold it into the mixture along with the peanut butter. Combine the dough with the egg. Moisten your fingers with a little water and shape the dough into 12 peaks, which are distributed on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Dab your fingers to smooth the peaks slightly. Bake the cookies for 10-12 min. until they are golden. Let them cool for a few minutes on the baking sheet before carefully placing them on a wire rack to cool. This allows them to achieve their crispness.
notes: Quantity: 12 pieces (2 pieces per person). Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrates 24 g, Protein 6 g, Fat 10 g, of which saturated fat 3 g.

title: Buns with spinach and tomato
preparation: Dough: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt and knead the oats, durum wheat flour, and then wheat flour into the dough. Knead until the dough is cohesive, but also slightly sticky like rye bread dough. Let the dough rise covered in a warm place for about 30 minutes, well brushed with olive oil. Filling: Clean and rinse the spinach. Steam it in the water that clings to it. Cut the tomatoes into quarters. Punch down the dough on a floured surface. Divide it into 10 pieces and shape them as well as you can into buns. Press the buns slightly flat with your hand and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Top the buns with mozzarella, spinach, and tomatoes, and season them with salt and pepper. Bake the breads in the oven at 225 degrees for about 20 minutes until they are crispy and golden.
notes: Energy distribution* 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates 34 g. Protein 10 g. Fat 5 g. Of which saturated fat 2 g. Dietary fiber 4 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Breadsticks with parmesan and oregano
preparation: Dissolve the yeast in the water. Add salt, oil, rye flour, and wheat flour and knead the dough well together. Let the dough rise for 30 minutes. Roll the dough into a log and cut it into 24 pieces. Sprinkle only a small amount of flour on the surface and roll each piece of dough into a long stick, approx. 25 cm. Place the sticks on baking sheets with parchment paper. Brush the breadsticks with water and sprinkle with oregano and finely grated parmesan. Bake the breadsticks in the oven at 180 degrees for approx. 15-20 minutes, until they are golden. Let them cool completely on a wire rack. Store the breadsticks in an airtight container.
notes: Tip! Instead of oregano, you can sprinkle with dried basil, nigella seeds, or ¼ tsp. cayenne pepper. Energy distribution per person: 1174 KJ (280 kcal). Carbohydrates: 49 g, Fat: 7 g, Of which saturated fat: 2 g, Dietary fiber: 5.3 g.

title: Lemon koldskål with rye bread crunch and summer berries

ingredients.name: zest and juice of 2 untreated lemons
summer berries e.g. strawberries, blueberries, currants, raspberries

preparation: Rye bread crunch: Cut the rye bread into very small cubes and toss it with the brown sugar. Heat a non-stick pan without fat and toast the rye bread mixture while stirring for about 5 minutes, until the sugar is caramelized. Remove the pan from the heat and spread the crunch onto a piece of parchment paper to cool. Lemon koldskål: Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Whisk the egg yolk with sugar and vanilla seeds into a light egg mixture. Add the grated zest and juice from the lemons. Then stir in the skyr a little at a time. Add the buttermilk and stir the koldskål together. Serve the koldskål with rye bread crunch and summer berries. Optionally garnish with edible flowers.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 43 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Fastelavnsboller with cream and jam
preparation: Dough: Dissolve the yeast in the milk. Add oil, 1 egg, salt, sugar, and most of the wheat flour. Knead the dough well and gradually add more flour until the dough is soft and smooth. Let the dough rise covered in a warm place until doubled in size. Pastry cream: Whisk all ingredients for the cream together in a saucepan. Bring the cream to a boil while whisking constantly, and let it cook thoroughly for a couple of minutes. Let the cream cool down, stirring it occasionally so it does not form a skin while cooling. Buns: Roll the dough out on a floured surface into a square, approximately 30 × 30 cm. Cut the dough into 16 square pieces and place a spoonful of jam and a spoonful of pastry cream in each. Fold the dough over the filling and press the seams firmly together. Place the buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper with the seams facing down. Brush with egg and let them proof for an additional 30 minutes. Bake the buns in the middle of the oven for 12-15 minutes at 200 degrees until they are light brown. Let them cool on a wire rack. Topping: Melt the chocolate, spread it on top of the buns, and sprinkle with sprinkles.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 28 g. Protein 6 g. Fat 5 g. Of which saturated fat 1.5 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Frozen yoghurt with berries

ingredients.name: frozen berries, e.g., blackberries or raspberries
fresh berries and possibly wood sorrel for garnish

preparation: Place the frozen berries in a small pot and bring to a boil for 1 min while stirring so they do not burn. Remove the pot from the heat. Add icing sugar and blend into a puree. Cool the berry puree before folding it into the yoghurt. Put the yoghurt cream in an ice cream maker and churn until it becomes ice cream. Divide the ice cream into two with a large spoon and scoop into two large balls. Place the ice cream in a container with a lid and freeze.
notes: Energy distribution* 700 KJ (170 kcal). Carbohydrates 31 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 2 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated. Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 80 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Asparagus guacamole with rye bread chips
preparation: Rye bread chips: Place the rye bread in the freezer for 1 hour. Slice the semi-frozen rye bread into 2-3 mm thin slices with a large sharp knife or using a meat slicer. Place them on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, and bake them for approx. 10-15 minutes at 180 degrees fan oven. Let them cool on a wire rack. Asparagus guacamole: Snap off the woody ends of the green asparagus and discard them. Cut off the heads and save them. Slice the asparagus into strips and steam them in a pot with 1 dl water and a little salt for 3-4 minutes. Remove them, dip them in ice-cold water, and let them cool in a strainer. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Scrape out the seeds and cut the tomato flesh into small cubes. Finely slice the spring onions. Chop the herbs together with the asparagus heads. Halve the avocado and remove the stone. Scrape the avocado flesh out of the skins and process it into a mash in a food processor along with the garlic, the drained asparagus, and yogurt. Place it in a bowl and add the tomato cubes, spring onions, and the chopped asparagus heads and herbs. Season the guacamole with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Serve the crispy rye bread chips with the guacamole.
notes: Tip! You can spice the guacamole with a little finely chopped chili or some chili sauce. You can also serve, for example, heart lettuce, celery, red bell pepper, or other raw vegetables alongside. Guacamole is suitable as a spread in a sandwich with, for example, smoked salmon and salad. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 160 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 24 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Fruit and Nut Bars
preparation: Coarsely chop the almonds, hazelnuts, and walnuts. Cut the apricots, dates, and figs into slightly smaller pieces. Sift the flour and baking powder together, and add the salt. Whisk the egg and light brown sugar until frothy, then fold in the flour mixture. Fold all the filling into the dough, and press it into a baking sheet (18 x 26 cm) lined with parchment paper. Place the pan in the oven at 160 degrees for approximately 35 minutes, until the surface is golden and the dough is fully baked. Place the pan on a wire rack and let the cake cool in the pan. Turn the cake out onto a board and cut it into 18 bars. Store the bars in a cake tin.
notes: Quantity: 18 bars (1 piece per person). Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per piece. Energy distribution per piece: 600 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrates: 17 g. Protein: 3 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.5 g.

title: Date Oat Bars
preparation:
Date filling: Blend the dates in a mini chopper or food processor, or chop them finely. Mix them with the orange juice and cardamom.

Oat dough: Coarsely chop the almonds and mix them with the oats. Put the brown sugar, oil, and honey in a saucepan, and warm it all over medium heat while stirring, until it is viscous and cohesive. Place the mixture in a large bowl. Stir the oat mixture into the still-warm sugar mass, and quickly knead it all together into a coarse and crumbly dough.

Place parchment paper in a square ovenproof dish, approx. 20 x 20 cm. Press half of the dough into the bottom of the dish. Spread the date filling on top. Distribute the rest of the dough evenly over the date filling and press it down. Bake the cake for approx. 20 minutes at 200 degrees. Let the cake cool for 10 minutes, then turn it out onto a cutting board, bottom side up. Remove the parchment paper, and cut the cake into pieces of approx. 3 x 3 cm with a heavy, sharp knife while it is warm – use firm and powerful cuts so the cake does not crumble too much. Let the bars cool completely and store them in an airtight container.
notes:
Tip! The dough for the date oat bars should be coarse and crumbly, similar to dough for krumkaker. You can optionally mix the dough in a stand mixer. If the cake gets cold, it may be difficult to cut. In that case, you can warm the cake slightly again.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per person.

Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 35 g. Protein: 3 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Herb hummus with rye bread chips and green sticks

ingredients.name: chickpeas (in a soaked state, e.g., from a can, this corresponds to 100 g)
small bunch of coriander – save a little for garnish
zest and juice of an untreated lemon
vegetables, e.g., celery, kohlrabi, cucumber, green bell pepper

preparation: Day 1: Place the chickpeas in a bowl with cold water and let them sit covered until the next day. Day 2: Rinse the chickpeas very well and place them in a pot with fresh water, and boil them for approximately 35 minutes. Drain the chickpeas and save the cooking water. Coarsely grate the apple. Place the chickpeas in a blender or food processor along with the coarsely grated apple, pressed garlic, cumin, tahini, coriander (save a little for garnish) and the zest and juice of a lemon. Thin it out with a little of the cooking water until the hummus has a soft and smooth consistency. Season with flaked salt. Rye bread chips: Spread the rye bread on a baking rack and toast it crispy in the oven at 200 degrees fan air for approximately 5 minutes. Green sticks: Clean the vegetables and cut them into sticks. Arrange hummus on a small plate. Top with olive oil and coriander. Serve with rye bread chips and vegetables.
notes: A homemade hummus of soaked, boiled chickpeas and plenty of coriander is truly delicious as a snack. Please note that the chickpeas must be soaked and boiled before use. Chickpeas from a can or carton can be used directly. Energy distribution per person: 250 kcal (1100 KJ), Carbohydrate 31 g, Protein 9 g, Fat 8 g (of which saturated fat 1 g), Dietary fiber 11 g.

title: Müsli bars with dried fruit and cornflakes
preparation: Cut the apricots into small cubes. Blend the rye bread and figs together in a food processor or mini chopper. Place the mixture in a bowl, add the apricots and the remaining ingredients, and knead everything thoroughly together. Spread the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper into a square, approximately 25×25 cm. Wet your hands slightly and press the mixture firmly together, ensuring the edges are even. Bake the mixture at 150 degrees for 30 minutes. Let the baked mass cool for 10 minutes. Cut it into 3 strips in one direction and approximately 7 in the other direction. Let the muesli bars cool completely and store them in an airtight container.
notes: Tip! If you do not have a food processor or mini chopper, the rye bread can be grated and the figs finely chopped. Energy distribution: 500 KJ (100 kcal) per piece. Carbohydrate: 19 g, Protein: 3 g, Fat: 3 g, of which saturated fat: 0.4 g.

title: Romesco sauce
preparation: Preheat the oven to 250 degrees grill. Halve the bell peppers. Remove the seeds, and place them skin-side up on a baking sheet with parchment paper and grill for 15-20 min., until they are dark and charred. Place the grilled peppers in a freezer bag and tie a knot. Let them rest for about 15 min. Rub off the skin. Place the peppers, almonds, pressed garlic, vinegar, and oil in a blender and blend to a coarse, thick consistency. Season with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
notes: 1 portion = approx. 2 dl/200 g. Fruit and vegetables: approx. 75 g per 100 g. Energy distribution per 100 g: 650 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrate: 58 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 13 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Baba ganoush – eggplant dip with tahini

ingredients.name: whole grain bread, e.g., Arabic whole grain flatbread or whole grain pita bread

preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Bake the eggplants whole in the oven for about 40 minutes, or until they are black, wrinkled, and collapsed. Let them cool down. Scrape out the flesh with a spoon, place it in a sieve, and press out the liquid. Mash the eggplant flesh. Stir the tahini with water in a small bowl. Mix it together with the eggplant, pressed garlic, and oil into a coarse cream. Season with salt and lemon juice. Spread the baba ganoush onto a flat plate and sprinkle with paprika, cumin, and finely chopped parsley. Serve with pita bread.
notes: Tip! The eggplants can also be baked on the oven grill to give the baba ganoush a slightly more smoky flavor. Prick the eggplants first, or make a few small slits in them, otherwise they may explode in the oven. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1400 KJ (350 kcal). Carbohydrate: 40 g. Protein: 14 g. Fat: 12 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Pea hummus with new carrots and tortilla chips
preparation: Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Rinse the parsley and shake it dry. Place the chickpeas, half of the peas, parsley, cumin, pressed garlic, tahini, and yogurt in a blender and blend until a thick hummus forms. Season with lemon juice, salt, and pepper, and optionally stir in a little cold water if the consistency is too thick. Fold the remaining peas into the hummus. Grill the whole wheat tortillas until they have nice grill marks on both sides. Scrub the carrots. Serve vegetables with pea hummus and tortilla chips.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 54 g. Protein: 16 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Apple Gløgg

ingredients.name: dark brown sugar or muscovado sugar

preparation: Peel the orange, being careful not to include too much of the white pith. Slice the ginger into thin slices. Bring the apple juice to a boil in a pot with the orange peel, ginger, cinnamon sticks, pepper, cloves, cardamom, star anise, and brown sugar or muscovado sugar. Bring to a slow boil under a lid, and let the gløgg simmer under the lid for 45 minutes. Remove some of the gløgg in a small saucepan and let the raisins simmer in it for 10 minutes. Let the rest of the gløgg simmer for another 10 minutes. Dice the apple into small cubes. Distribute the almonds, apples, and raisins into the glasses. Strain the gløgg, pour it into the glasses, and serve immediately.
notes: Tip! The apple gløgg is alcohol-free and can be enjoyed by everyone. You can add calvados, port wine, or apple brandy to the gløgg if you want it with alcohol. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 207 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 4 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Mint Cocktail
preparation: Put sugar and water in a pot, and boil until the sugar is dissolved. Cool the sugar syrup. Slice the cucumber into fine strips, and distribute them into two glasses along with ice cubes. Put the sugar syrup and lemon juice in a shaker and shake. Pour into the glasses with plenty of fresh mint, and top up with sparkling water. Serve immediately.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 250 KJ (50 kcal). Carbohydrate: 10 g. Protein: 1 g. Fat: 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Muesli bars with peanut butter and mixed nuts

ingredients.name: mixed nuts, e.g. almonds, hazelnuts and walnuts

preparation: Preheat the oven to 160 degrees. Chop the nuts. Cut the apricots and figs into very small pieces. Put the sugar, syrup and peanut butter in a small saucepan and bring to a boil over low heat. Add the oats, nuts, seeds and dried fruit. Remove the pan from the heat and stir well. Spread the mixture into a small ovenproof dish of approximately 20×30 cm lined with parchment paper. Smooth the surface with your palm and bake for approximately 30 minutes. Cool completely before cutting into 18 pieces.
notes: Approx. 18 pcs. Energy distribution* 600 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrate 20 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 5 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per piece.

title: Aioli
preparation: Whisk egg yolk with dijon mustard and pressed garlic. Gradually add the oil while whisking until a thick mayonnaise forms. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
notes: Energy distribution* per 100 g: 3000 KJ (700 kcal), Carbohydrates: 2 g, Protein: 1.5 g, Fat: 80 g, of which saturated fat: 10 g

title: Banana bread with chickpea flour
preparation: Whisk the oil with the brown sugar. Mash the bananas. Add the bananas to the oil-sugar mixture and whisk together. Add the eggs one at a time and mix together. Blend the oatmeal into flour and fold in the cocoa powder, chickpea flour, baking powder, and vanilla sugar. Add the dry ingredients to the batter and mix well. Coarsely chop the chocolate and fold it into the batter. Distribute the batter into a bread tin (approx. 1 ½ liters) lined with parchment paper, and bake the banana bread at 175 °C fan oven for approx. 30 min. Check with a skewer if the bread is baked. If there is batter clinging to it, bake it for a bit longer.
notes: 1 cake = approx. 14 slices (1 slice per person). Energy distribution per piece: 200 kcal, Carbohydrate 25 g, Protein 6 g, Fat 9 g, of which saturated fat 2 g.

title: Spin swirls with cheese and basil
preparation: Rinse the spinach and steam it in the water clinging to it. Wring the spinach free of water and chop it. Place it in a large bowl and add water and yogurt. Dissolve the yeast in this. Add the white whole wheat flour and salt. Stir the dough well and gradually add the wheat flour. Knead until the dough is smooth and supple. Place the dough covered to rise in a warm place for approx. 1 hour. Punch the dough down on a flour-dusted surface. Roll it out into a large rectangle of approx. 50 x 40 cm. Brush the dough with the oil and distribute the mozzarella, basil, and a sprinkle of oregano on one half of the dough. Fold the side of the dough without filling over the other part, and press the dough together slightly. Cut the dough into strips approximately 2 cm wide. Twist each strip by grabbing each end and twisting the dough in opposite directions. This is easiest to do while staying over the table so the filling does not fall out. Lift one end over the middle and fold the tip under the dough. Twist the other end around and under, then twist the dough out slightly so the filling is visible. Place the swirls on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Let them rise in a warm place for 1 hour. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees (standard oven setting). Brush the swirls with coffee and sprinkle with a little oregano. Bake for approx. 20 min. until they are golden. Cool the swirls on a wire rack.
preparation_time: 40 min. plus rising and baking time
notes: Tip: Pack the swirls in small bags and freeze them. Thaw them and take them with you on the go.

title: Risalamande with sea buckthorn sauce
preparation:
Sea buckthorn sauce: Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Put sea buckthorn, sugar, vanilla seeds, and the empty vanilla bean in a pot and simmer over low heat for about 5 minutes until the sea buckthorn bursts. Remove the sea buckthorn sauce from the heat and remove the vanilla bean.

Rice pudding: Rinse the rice and drain. Put milk in a pot and bring to a boil. Add the rice and cook for about 1 hour and 15 minutes over low heat until the rice feels tender. They should still have a bit of bite. Stir the pudding along the way so it doesn't burn. Cool the pudding.

Risalamande: Split the vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into the sugar. Mash the rice pudding with a fork and stir in the skyr a little at a time. Add the vanilla seeds mixed with powdered sugar and almond flakes. Serve the risalamande with sea buckthorn sauce.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 28 g, Protein 8 g, Fat 6 g, of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Mini date scones with chia seeds

ingredients.name: sifted spelt flour or sifted flour

preparation: 10 small scones – one per person. Combine the two types of flour in a bowl with baking powder, sugar, salt, and chia seeds. Chop the dates and add them to the dough along with the cream, and then add the buttermilk little by little. Stir until the dough is combined. Roll out the dough to a thickness of approximately 2 cm. Cut out approximately 10 scones using a glass about 5 cm in diameter. Place the scones on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush with beaten egg and bake for about 12-15 minutes at 200 degrees (standard oven). Cool on a wire rack.
notes: Energy distribution* 500 KJ (125 kcal). Carbohydrates 23 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 2 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per piece.

title: Vegetable snack with dip

ingredients.name: shelled edamame beans or thawed peas
vegetables e.g. carrots, daikon radish, cucumber, kohlrabi, bell pepper and celery

preparation: Dip: Place edamame beans/peas, pressed garlic and yogurt in a blender and blend to a creamy consistency. Season with flaked salt and pepper. Vegetable snack: Clean the vegetables and cut them into sticks. Serve the vegetables with the dip.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 450 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 27 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 2 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 11 g.

title: Banana bread with dried fruit
preparation: 1 loaf/14 slices = 1 slice per person. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Mash the bananas with a fork. Whisk brown sugar and eggs together. Add the oil. Mix white wheat with wheat flour, cinnamon, ginger, baking soda, and salt. Stir the flour mixture into the batter along with the mashed bananas, raisins, and chopped dates. Pour the batter into a loaf pan, approx. 10 x 30 cm, lined with parchment paper. Bake the banana bread in the middle of the oven for approx. 50 minutes. Check with a skewer if the banana bread is baked. If batter clings to it, bake it for a little longer. Carefully turn the banana bread out of the pan and let it cool before slicing.
