notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 33 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 4 g. Of which saturated fat 2 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Carrot Muffins
preparation: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees. Whisk muscovado sugar and oil until creamy. Add the eggs one at a time, whisking during the process. Mix wheat flour with baking powder and spices, then fold into the batter along with the grated carrots and raisins. Distribute the batter into 12 muffin molds and bake the cakes for approx. 15 minutes. Use a skewer to check if they are baked. If batter clings to it, bake them for a little longer. Cool the cakes before serving with a sprinkle of icing sugar.
notes: Tip! Energy etc. is indicated per piece. Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 29 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 6 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Oatmeal cookies with chocolate
preparation: Oatmeal cookies: Preheat the oven to 170 degrees. Mix all ingredients together. Place the cookies on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, using approximately 2 tsp. of dough per cookie, with good spacing between them. Bake the cookies for approximately 10 minutes until they are light brown. Let the cookies cool down. Chocolate glaze: Chop the chocolate and melt it over a water bath. Place the cookies close to a piece of parchment paper. Drizzle the chocolate over the cookies in thin stripes. Let the chocolate stiffen. Store the cookies in an airtight container.
notes: Amount: Approx. 24 pcs./4 cookies per person. Energy distribution* 950 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 39 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 6 g. Of which saturated fat 3 g. * per person, i.e., for 4 cookies.

title: Rye snacks with seeds and chocolate
preparation: Put the rye kernels and pumpkin seeds in a bowl and pour cold water over them. Ensure the water covers the kernels. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the kernels soak at room temperature until the next day. Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add the soaked kernels with their water, then stir in the rye flour and salt, and knead well. Gradually add the wheat flour and knead the dough for about 10 min. – feel free to use a stand mixer or a hand mixer with dough hooks. Chop the chocolate and fold it into the dough. Distribute the dough into 12 silicone muffin molds using two spoons dipped in cold water, and let them rise at room temperature for about 2 hours. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Moisten the surface with a little water and bake for about 30 min. Cool the rye snacks on a wire rack.
preparation_time: ca. 20 min. plus resting, rising and baking time
notes: Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 27 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Banana Soft Serve
preparation: Place frozen bananas in a blender with vanilla sugar, and blend for a long time (approx. 5 min.) until the bananas have reached a soft serve consistency. Divide the soft serve into two glasses and enjoy with a light sprinkle of chia seeds.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 200 kcal (800 KJ). Carbohydrates: 40 g, Protein: 2.5 g, Fat: 1 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Batbout – Moroccan flatbread
preparation: Mix salt, sugar, whole wheat flour, and semolina in a large bowl. Make a small indentation in the flour mixture and crumble the yeast into the indentation. Add a little water to dissolve the yeast, and then the rest of the water to knead the dough together. Knead the dough until it is soft and elastic and just starts to pull away from the sides of the bowl. Alternatively, it can be mixed in a stand mixer. Let the dough rise covered for about 1 hour. Divide the dough into 15 pieces – depending on how large you want the breads to be – and shape them into balls. Place them on a tea towel sprinkled with flour and place another tea towel over them. Let them rest in a warm place for 5 minutes. Roll the balls flat like pancakes – approx. 2-3 mm thick. Let them rise for another 10 minutes. Fry the breads on a hot pan, without fat, and turn them regularly in the pan. The breads should ideally rise on the pan so they become hollow inside.
notes: Tip! These breads can be made with many types of flour, and are also good with 100% whole grain of both fine and coarse types. The breads can also be made with cornmeal. The dough can be prepared the day before and slow-risen in the refrigerator. They can also be made with sourdough instead of yeast. The dough can also be divided into more pieces so you get more smaller breads. Energy per piece: 500 KJ (100 kcal). Carbohydrate: 21 g. Protein: 4 g. Fat: 1 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Homemade mini crispbread
preparation: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add oil and salt, and stir in the rye flour first and then the wheat flour into the dough little by little. Knead until the dough is smooth and supple. Roll the dough out to a thickness of 2 mm. Cut out the dough with a cutter, approx. 10 cm diameter, and place the dough on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Optionally cut a small hole in the middle of each crispbread. Brush with water and bake the crispbreads in the oven at 200 degrees for approx. 20 minutes, until they are crispy. Cool the crispbreads on a cooling rack.
notes: 16 pcs. Energy distribution* per person: 200 KJ (50 kcal). Carbohydrate: 10 g. Fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 1 g.

title: Salmon with fried noodles
preparation: Fried noodles: Ensure the vegetables are thawed. Boil the noodles according to the package instructions and drain. Heat the oil in a pan and add the curry paste. Add the boiled noodles to the curry paste along with the vegetables, until they take color and are well heated. If necessary, thin with a splash of water so they do not burn. Season with soy sauce and pepper. Fried salmon: Season the salmon with flaked salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the salmon for approx. 4 min on each side. Remove the salmon from the pan and drizzle lemon juice over it. Serving: Arrange the salmon and fried noodles on plates. Top with a little fresh coriander.
notes: TIP If you are not very fond of coriander, use parsley or basil instead. Energy distribution per person: 2200 KJ (550 kcal). Carbohydrates: 44 g. Protein: 38 g. Fat: 20 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Canjeero/laxoox – Somali pancakes

ingredients.name: finely ground whole wheat flour or sorghum flour

preparation: Pour the water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add the other ingredients and stir or blend everything well. Let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes until it has risen. Fry the pancakes on a non-stick pan. You can optionally drip a few drops of oil onto the pan before the first pancake. Put a little batter in the middle of the pan using a small ladle or a metal deciliter measure. Spread the batter out on the pan with the ladle or measure so that a spiral pattern forms in the pancake. Let the pancake fry over low heat until the batter has completely dried on the surface. Remove it from the pan and continue with the rest of the batter until you have a whole stack of pancakes.
notes: Eat the pancakes for breakfast or as an accompaniment to stews and meat sauces, instead of rice or bread. You can also dip canjeero in soup. With butter and sugar, it is a dessert, and some like to pour a little tea over it. Sorghum flour is also called durra flour. Sorghum is a grass species originally from Central Africa. Can be purchased in specialty stores. Energy distribution: 700 KJ (150 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates 36 g, fat 2 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Rye bread rolls with chocolate
preparation: Pour the beer into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add the rye kernels, seeds, cocoa, and salt and stir well together. Chop the chocolate and fold it into the dough along with the white whole wheat flour. Add the flour little by little and knead the dough well. This is best done with a stand mixer. The dough should be a bit sticky. Cover the dough and let it rise at room temperature for approx. 1 hour. Shape the dough into 12 rolls using two spoons, and place the rolls on two baking sheets lined with parchment paper. Let them proof again, covered, for approx. 30 minutes. Bake the rolls in the oven at 200 degrees fan oven for approx. 15 minutes.
notes: Tip! The energy distribution below is per rye bread roll. Energy distribution* 900 KJ (220 kcal). Carbohydrates 34 g. Fat 7 g. Of which saturated fat 2 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Spinach Balls
preparation: Spinach balls: Place the spinach in a pot and thaw over low heat. Squeeze the spinach free of water and chop it coarsely. Pour water and yogurt into a bowl, and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt, honey, and spinach. Add sunflower seeds and oats to the liquid and knead in the white whole wheat flour a little at a time. Knead the dough for a long time until it is cohesive, but also slightly sticky. Place the dough covered to rise in a warm place for approx. 1 hour. Dip a large spoon in cold water and use it to shape the dough into balls. Place the balls on a baking sheet with parchment paper – they can be a bit rustic – and let them rise covered in a warm place for approx. 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 225 degrees. Bake the balls for 15-18 minutes until they are golden, and cool on a wire rack.
notes: 10 pieces. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 30 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 850 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 29 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 45 g.

title: Banana tortilla with skyr, apples and blackberries
preparation: Blend the oatmeal into a flour. Whisk eggs with milk and fold in the oat flour. Slice the bananas. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan – or 4 smaller pans – and pour in the egg mixture. Distribute the banana slices on top, and fry the pancake over low heat until it is firm. Be careful that the bottom does not burn. Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the core, and cut the apples into thin wedges. Distribute apples, blackberries, and skyr on top of the pancake before serving.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 59 g. Protein: 20 g. Fat: 14 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g.

title: Overnight oats with raspberries
preparation: Combine oats, milk, and vanilla sugar in a container with a lid, and stir them together. Close the lid and place the porridge in the refrigerator until the next morning. Stir the porridge, add yogurt, and serve with raspberries, vanilla sugar, and mint leaves.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1700 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 61 g. Protein: 18 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Chia Porridge

ingredients.name: summer berries e.g. strawberries, blueberries, raspberries

preparation: Day 1: Place the oats and chia seeds in a container with a lid. Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Add the vanilla seeds and milk to the container with the grains and stir well. Cover the container with a lid and store in a cool place until the next day. Day 2: Stir the porridge lightly with skyr. Rinse and pick the berries. Serve the porridge with summer berries.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2000 KJ (500 kcal). Carbohydrates: 65 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Skyr with luxury topping
preparation: Luxury topping: Cut the bread into small cubes and toss it with brown sugar. Spread the rye bread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and toast it in the middle of the oven at 200 degrees for 10-15 minutes until crispy. Cool the rye bread and crumble it in a blender. Chop the almonds and toss them in the topping along with the sun-dried blueberries. Skyr with luxury topping: Peel the oranges and cut them into segments. Serve the skyr with oranges and luxury topping.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate: 30 g. Protein: 25 g. Fat: 35 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Mango smoothie-bowl
preparation: Mango smoothie-bowl: Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the stone. Cut the flesh into smaller pieces and place it in a blender along with frozen bananas, oatmeal, ginger, lime juice, and milk. Blend until a thick smoothie porridge is formed. Topping: Toast the rye bread and cut it into small cubes, or blend it into rye bread crumbs. Divide the smoothie porridge into 4 bowls and top with blueberries, chia seeds, and rye bread crumbs.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 175 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1600 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 50 g. Protein: 29 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Yoghurt with chocolate sprinkles
preparation: Grate the rye bread and chop the nuts. Warm the oil in a small pan. Add the rye bread, nuts, and sugar to the pan and toast until it is crispy and starts to smell fragrant. Pour it into a small bowl and let it cool. Grate the chocolate or chop it finely and mix it into the rye bread mixture. Pour the yoghurt into a small bowl and sprinkle the chocolate sprinkles on top.
notes: Tip! You can make a double portion and store it in a cool place. The nuts can be replaced by half a slice of rye bread. Energy distribution: 1300 KJ (300 kcal) per person.

title: Hearty muesli with skyr and berries

ingredient_sections.section_name: Hearty muesli (approx. 400 g enough for 10 portions)

ingredients.name: seeds and kernels (flaxseeds, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds and hemp seeds)
raisins (can be replaced by e.g. dried cranberries)

preparation: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Put honey and water in a small saucepan and melt over low heat. Mix oats with seeds and kernels in a bowl and stir in the melted honey water. Spread everything out on a baking sheet with parchment paper, and roast in the oven for approx. 15 min., until it is crispy and golden. Stir it halfway through. Cool the mixture on a piece of parchment paper. Chop the almonds and stir them into the muesli along with the raisins. Store the muesli in an airtight container. Divide skyr into two bowls and top with hearty muesli and berries.
notes: Energy distribution* 1400 KJ (350 kcal). Carbohydrate 31 g, Protein 29 g, Fat 9 g, of which saturated fat 1 g. * per person for 2 dl skyr with 40 g muesli and 25 g blueberries

title: Blueberry Smoothie
preparation: Give the blueberries a quick boil in plenty of boiling water. Pour them into a sieve and let them cool down completely in the sieve. Peel the bananas and pears, and cut them into smaller pieces. Put them in a blender with the oatmeal, blueberries, yogurt, milk, and ice cubes. Blend everything until it is completely finely ground and the drink is quite thin. Season with honey. Pour the smoothie into 4 glasses and serve immediately.
notes: Tip! Instead of blueberries, you can use blackcurrants, strawberries, or raspberries, or a blend. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate: 49 g. Protein: 9 g. Fat: 2 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.5 g.

title: Whole grain rolls with root vegetables

ingredients.name: root vegetables e.g. parsnips, parsley root, celeriac and/or Jerusalem artichokes

preparation:
DAY 1
Peel the root vegetables and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Boil the root vegetables in water until tender, using just enough water to cover them. Drain them well before mashing them with a fork. Cool the root vegetable mash.

Pour the water into a large bowl and crumble the yeast into it. Add salt and honey, then add the root vegetable mash, cracked rye kernels, spelt flakes, white wheat, and approximately half of the wheat flour. Mix the dough well. Gradually add more flour, and knead the dough for about 10 minutes in a stand mixer. The dough should be soft and sticky. Place the dough covered in the refrigerator to rise until the next day.

DAY 2
Roughly shape the dough into rolls using two spoons dipped in cold water. Arrange the rolls on two baking sheets lined with parchment paper, and let them rise covered for about 30 minutes at room temperature. Bake the rolls at 225 degrees for about 20 minutes. Cool the rolls on a wire rack.
notes: Energy distribution* 1100 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates 50 g, Protein 8 g, Fat 1.6 g. * per roll

title: Overnight oats with chia
preparation: Place oatmeal and chia seeds in a container with cinnamon, cardamom, and cocoa powder. Stir in milk and water, and let the porridge sit covered in the refrigerator until the next morning. Stir the porridge and add yogurt. Slice the banana and fold them into the porridge along with the blueberries. Divide the porridge into two bowls or glasses and enjoy.
notes: Fruit and vegetables*: Approx. 75 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution*: 1200 KJ (275 kcal). Carbohydrates: 41 g. Protein: 15 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Energy smoothie
preparation: Peel the bananas and put them in a blender. Halve the passion fruits and oranges, and squeeze the juice into the blender. Optionally strain the seeds from the passion fruits. Add mint and ginger and blend until it becomes a smoothie. Thin with milk and season with vanilla sugar.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 225 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 39 g. Protein: 6 g. Fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 5 g.

title: Smoothie bowl with topping
preparation: Place frozen bananas, spinach, and frozen blueberries in a food processor together with yogurt and blend until a thick liquid consistency is reached. Divide the smoothie bowl into two bowls and top with oats, chia seeds, and fresh blueberries.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 235 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 1300 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 52 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Greenie
preparation: Halve the avocado and remove the stone. Peel the orange and divide it into segments. Place the avocado, orange, lemon zest and juice, bananas, and kale in a food processor together with the water. Blend for 2-3 minutes until you have a lovely green drink.
notes: Fruit and vegetables* Approx. 235 g * per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution* 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate 33 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 8 g. Of which saturated fat 2 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Mexican breakfast

ingredients.name: serrano ham or other air-dried ham
toasted whole grain sandwich bread cut into triangles
pickled jalapeno chili or tabasco sauce

preparation:
Scrambled eggs: Whisk the eggs together in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Peel and grate the carrots on a grater. Clean the bell peppers and cut them into small cubes. Slice the spring onions. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Sauté the carrots, bell pepper, and spring onions for 2-3 minutes. Remove some vegetables to use for garnish. Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and stir until the eggs are cooked, approx. 5 minutes. Divide the scrambled eggs into 4 bowls or plates and garnish with the remaining vegetables.

Tomato salsa: Roast the whole tomatoes and the white part of the spring onions in a dry pan until they get some color. Cool the vegetables, cut them into smaller pieces, and put them in a blender or mini chopper. Add the jalapeno and blend until the salsa is smooth. Season with salt and serve in a bowl with a fine garnish of the green part of the spring onion.

Mango smoothies: Peel the mango and remove the stone. Cut the flesh into smaller pieces. Put the orange juice and mango flesh in a blender along with ice cubes, and blend until smooth. Serve the smoothies in glasses. Garnish optionally with a lime slice and mint.

Serve the eggs with serrano ham, tomato salsa, and toasted bread. Drink the mango smoothie with it.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 400 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 2400 KJ (600 kcal). Carbohydrates: 63 g. Protein: 28 g. Fat: 19 g. Of which saturated fat: 5 g.

title: Savory muffins with beetroot, ham and garlic cream
preparation:
Savory muffins: Mix the oatmeal with yogurt and milk, and let it soak for 5 minutes. Peel the beetroots and grate them coarsely. Chop the onion. Sauté the vegetables in oil in a pan for a few minutes, and let them cool slightly. Mix the eggs with the oatmeal mixture. Blend the flour, baking powder, and thyme together. Fold the mixture into the oatmeal mixture along with the vegetables and ham. Distribute the batter into 12 muffin tins, and bake them at 200 degrees for 20-25 minutes.
Garlic cream: Mix the cream cheese with pressed garlic. Place a teaspoon of garlic cream on each muffin.
Trim the beans and boil them for 3-4 minutes in lightly salted water.
Serve the muffins with the beans.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 60 g per piece. Energy distribution: 700 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 19 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g per piece.

title: Rye Triangles
preparation: Dissolve the yeast in the water. Add yogurt, salt, rye flour, and wheat flour and knead the dough. Optionally add more flour, but not more than necessary until the dough just barely releases from your fingers. Roll the dough out into a rectangle, approx. 30×20 cm, on a surface sprinkled with plenty of flour. Cut the piece into 6 pieces of 10×10 cm each. Cut each of these pieces in half across to get 12 triangles. Place the triangles on baking paper on baking sheets. Whisk the yogurt with a little water and brush the triangles. Sprinkle with flaxseeds. Let them rise in a warm place for 1 hour, and bake them at 190 degrees for approx. 10-15 minutes. Let the triangles cool on a wire rack.
notes: Energy distribution* per piece/person: 550 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrates: 20 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 2 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 4 g.

title: Green smoothie
preparation: Rinse the spinach. Cut the celery into small pieces. Remove the skin and pit from the avocado, and cut it into smaller pieces. Peel the apple and cut it into smaller pieces. Peel the ginger and grate it finely. Blend all vegetables and apple with apple juice and ice cubes until all ingredients are completely finely blended and the smoothie is thick and a beautiful green. You can optionally season with more ginger. Pour the smoothie into glasses and serve with a straw.
notes: Tip! If you do not blend the ice cubes, you can let the smoothie cool down in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes before drinking. Or use ingredients directly from the refrigerator. Energy distribution per person: 450 KJ (100 kcal), Carbohydrates 18 g, Protein 1 g, Fat 3 g, of which saturated fat 0.5 g.

title: Granola
preparation: Approx. 320 grams granola. Mix all the dry ingredients except the raisins in a bowl to make the granola. Melt the honey in a dry non-stick pan, and toast the mixture while stirring. Toast until the mixture is golden. Stir in the raisins, and let the mixture cool on a piece of parchment paper. Serve granola as a topping on sour dairy products with fruit for breakfast.
notes: Energy distribution* 1500 KJ (350 kcal). Carbohydrates 69 g. Fat 6 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. Dietary fiber 11 g. * per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Kernel Buns

ingredients.name: whole spelt flour or graham flour

preparation: Place the chopped rye and flaxseeds in a pot together with 5 dl of water. Bring to a boil. Let it simmer at low heat for 3-4 minutes while stirring. Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture cool for ½ hour until it is lukewarm. Stir in 1½ dl of water. Stir the yeast into the mixture. Add buttermilk, salt, whole spelt flour, and wheat flour. Knead the dough until smooth. Let the dough rise covered for 3 hours. Shape into 20 buns. Brush them with beaten egg. Sprinkle the buns with coarsely chopped sunflower seeds. Bake the buns at 225 degrees for approximately 25 minutes.
notes: Energy distribution* 700 KJ (150 kcal). Carbohydrates 25 g. Protein 6 g. Fat 3 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. Dietary fiber 5 g. * per piece.

title: Oatmeal with apple
preparation: Place oats in a pot with milk and boil for approx. 5 min. while stirring until it becomes a porridge. Season with a pinch of salt and ground cinnamon. Cut the apple into small cubes and fold the apple pieces into the porridge. Arrange the porridge in two bowls. Sprinkle with a little cinnamon. Serve while the porridge is still warm.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 35 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Banana pancakes with skyr and fruit

ingredients.name: berries, e.g. raspberries, blueberries and blackberries

preparation: Blend oatmeal into flour. Mash the bananas with a fork. Mix egg with skimmed milk, oat flour, a pinch of salt and the mashed banana. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry 4 small pancakes for 2-3 min on each side until they are golden and firm. Serve with skyr, berries, pomegranate seeds and fresh mint.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 90 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 750 KJ (175 kcal). Carbohydrates: 19 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Chia pudding with fruit
preparation: Day 1: Place oats, spelt flakes, and chia seeds in a container with a lid. Add milk and vanilla bean and stir. Cover the container with a lid and keep cool until the next day. Day 2: The next day, stir the pudding lightly with skyr. Serve the pudding with diced pears and blueberries.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1800 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 62 g. Protein: 24 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Overnight oats with pomegranate and coconut

ingredient_sections.section_name: Overnight oats with pomegranate and coconut

preparation: Put oatmeal and chia seeds in a container and stir with milk. Place the porridge covered in the refrigerator until the next morning. Stir the porridge and add yogurt. Divide the porridge into two bowls and top with pomegranate and toasted coconut.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 30 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 38 g. Protein: 15 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 4 g.

title: Birchermuesli
preparation: Grate the apple coarsely and place it in a container along with the oatmeal and apple juice. Stir, and place the porridge covered in the refrigerator until the next morning. Mix the skyr into the porridge and stir well. Divide the porridge into two bowls and top with raisins and sunflower seeds.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 50 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1200 KJ (300 kcal). Carbohydrates: 46 g. Protein: 12 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Cold-risen pumpkin buns

ingredients.name: pumpkin flesh without seeds and peel

preparation: Day 1: Grate the pumpkin flesh using the coarse side of a grater. Pour cold water into a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add the grated pumpkin, salt, and honey. Mix everything well. Next, add the oats and white whole wheat flour and stir well into the dough. It is recommended to use a stand mixer so the dough is thoroughly mixed. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place the dough in the refrigerator until the next day – minimum 10 hours. Day 2: Dip a large spoon in cold water and shape the dough into buns. Place the buns on a piece of parchment paper and let them proof for approximately 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 225 degrees fan oven and let a baking sheet heat up inside the oven. Gently brush the buns with whisked egg and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds. Carefully lift the buns and parchment paper onto the hot baking sheet, and bake the buns for approximately 15 minutes until they are crispy.
notes:
Approx. 10 pieces.
Energy distribution* per piece: 750 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 29 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.5 g.

title: Raspberry chia pudding with vanilla and skyr
preparation: Raspberry chia pudding Day 1: Put the frozen raspberries in a pot and boil them for at least one minute. Set aside to cool. Place oatmeal and chia seeds in a container with a lid. Add raspberries, ginger, and milk, and stir well. Place the pudding covered in the refrigerator until the next morning. Day 2: Take the pudding out of the refrigerator. Add vanilla sugar, stir into the pudding, and mash the berries. Gently fold the skyr into the pudding and arrange in bowls. Topping: Massage the pomegranate and press the juice and seeds into a bowl. Top with pomegranate seeds and chopped mint. Serve with apple wedges/cubes as a snack accompaniment.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 200 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1500 KJ (350 kcal), Carbohydrates: 52 g, Protein: 19 g, Fat: 6 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Spicy Christmas Buns
preparation: Warm the milk and pour it into a bowl. Dissolve the yeast in the milk. Add syrup, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, finely chopped candied peel, and currants. Knead the wheat flour into the dough little by little and knead until the dough is smooth and supple. Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for approx. 1 hour. Punch the dough down on a floured surface and divide it into 10 pieces. Roll them into buns and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Let the buns rise for another approx. 30 minutes. Brush the buns with whisked egg and sprinkle them with pearl sugar and hazelnut flakes. Bake the buns at 200 degrees for 12-15 minutes. Cool the buns on a wire rack.
notes: 10 pcs./10 people. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 8 g per person. Energy distribution: 793 KJ (189 kcal). Carbohydrate: 37 g. Fat: 2.4 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.4 g.

title: Mango salad with passion fruit marinade
preparation: Halve the passion fruits and scrape out the flesh. Mix the passion fruit with honey. Peel the mangoes and cut the flesh into pieces as large as possible. Slice the mango and arrange on a plate. Drizzle the passion fruit dressing over the mango. Sprinkle with coarsely chopped mint.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 180 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 600 KJ (100 kcal). Carbohydrates: 28 g. Protein: 1 g. Fat: 0.5 g.

title: Overnight oats with quinoa, chia and pomegranate
preparation: Overnight oats. The day before: Place oats, spelt flakes, quinoa flakes and chia seeds in a container with a lid. Pour the milk over. Stir the mixture together and close the lid. Place the container in a cool place until the next day. The next day: Take the porridge out of the refrigerator. Add skyr and stir. Topping. Halve the pomegranate and press the juice and seeds out into a bowl. Cut the kiwi and banana into small cubes. Divide the porridge into bowls and top with pomegranate seeds, kiwi and banana.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approximately 120 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1500 KJ (400 kcal). Carbohydrates: 52 g. Protein: 16 g. Fat: 6 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Overnight oats with berries
preparation: Evening: Place the oatmeal and chia seeds in a container with a lid along with the vanilla powder. Add milk and stir well. Place the porridge in the refrigerator covered until the next morning. Morning: Take the porridge out of the refrigerator and stir it. If it is too thick, thin it with a little water. Divide the cold porridge into four bowls and top with berries and kiwi.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrate: 34 g. Protein: 11 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Smoothie (the satiating one)
preparation: Bring the berries to a boil for at least 1 min. before using them in the smoothie. Let them cool down completely before use. Place berries, oatmeal, yogurt, grated fresh ginger, and mint in a food processor and blend until a thick smoothie is achieved. Pour into glasses and enjoy.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 35 g. Protein: 10 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Whole grain buns with oat topping
preparation: Combine water and yogurt in a bowl, and dissolve the yeast in it. Peel the carrots and grate them on the coarse side of the grater. Add the grated carrots, sunflower seeds, rye kernels, salt, and oatmeal to the liquid. Add the spelt flour and knead the dough until it is cohesive but still sticky. The best result is achieved if you mix the dough in a stand mixer. Dip a spoon in cold water. Loosely shape the dough into 12 buns. Roll them in oatmeal and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Let the buns rise covered for about 1 hour. Bake the buns in a preheated oven at 200 degrees for 20 minutes. Turn off the oven and let the buns sit for an additional 10 minutes before removing them and cooling on a wire rack.
notes: 12 pieces. Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal) Carbohydrates 36 g Fat 4 g Of which saturated fat 1 g Dietary fiber 6 g * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Chia Buns
preparation: Put the water in a bowl and dissolve the yeast in it. Add salt, honey, and chia seeds, and let it sit for about 10 min. Now stir the oatmeal, spelt flour, and then the white whole wheat flour into the liquid. Knead until the dough has the consistency of a thick porridge. Turn the oven to 250 degrees fan oven, and let a baking sheet stay in the oven. Use a spoon and carelessly shape the dough into 10 buns, which are placed on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Dab the buns with a little water and sprinkle with oatmeal and chia seeds. Take the hot tray out of the oven, and carefully lift the parchment paper with the buns onto the hot tray. Put the tray in the oven, lower the heat to 220 degrees, and bake the buns for about 20 min. Cool the buns on a wire rack.
notes: Energy distribution* per piece: 1000 KJ (250 kcal). Carbohydrates: 39 g. Protein: 8 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g. Dietary fiber: 7.5 g.

title: Cold-proofed buns with pumpkin seeds

ingredients.name: white wheat flour or graham flour

preparation: Place the cracked wheat kernels in boiling water and boil them for 2-3 minutes. Pour them into a sieve, rinse them, and let them drain. Put water in a dough bowl or a large bowl and dissolve yeast, salt, and honey in it. Add the wheat kernels, pumpkin seeds, and white wheat flour. Knead the ingredients together with the wheat flour, but do not add it all at once. Add only as much wheat flour as needed so that the dough just pulls away from the fingers. Knead the dough thoroughly and shape it into buns. Place the buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, cover them with film, and place them in the refrigerator overnight. Place the buns in a cold oven and set the oven to 225 degrees. The buns are finished after 35-40 minutes. Optionally, brush the buns with milk 5 minutes before they are finished so they get a beautiful shiny surface. If you choose to bake the buns in a warm oven, the buns must be taken out of the refrigerator an hour before baking and bake for about a quarter of an hour at 225 degrees.
notes: Tip! If you do not have space in the refrigerator for baking sheets, you can leave the dough in the dough bowl until the next morning. Pour the dough out onto the kitchen counter and cut the dough into buns without punching the dough down or working with it too much. Bake them as described in the recipe. Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal) per piece. Carbohydrates 32 g, Protein 7 g, Fat 3 g, of which saturated fat 0.4 g.

title: Honey-roasted pineapple with vanilla skyr and nuts
preparation: Split the vanilla bean, scrape out the seeds, and mash them together with the sugar. Mix the vanilla sugar well into the skyr. Roast the hazelnuts for 3-5 minutes in a dry pan. Rub off the skins and chop them coarsely. Peel the pineapple and cut the fruit into wedges or slices without the core. Melt the honey in a pan, and fry the pineapple pieces until golden brown on all sides. Serve the pineapple pieces with vanilla skyr, crushed nuts, and optionally a little fresh mint.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 800 KJ (200 kcal) per person. Carbohydrates: 28 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.3 g. per person, unless otherwise stated.

title: Strawberry Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Cream

ingredients.name: light cream cheese or fresh cheese max 11 %

preparation: Cake Layers: Whisk the eggs until white and frothy with the sugar and water. Fold in the flour, and place the batter in a springform pan 22 cm in diameter. Sprinkle almond flakes on top. Bake the cake at 180 degrees at the bottom of the oven for 20-25 minutes, until the cake is firm and elastic when you press the middle. Carefully remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan. Cut around the edge of the pan and loosen the cake from the sides and bottom. Split the cake into 3 layers with a sharp bread knife. Place the bottom layer on a serving platter or large plate. Strawberry Filling: Rinse the strawberries and let them drain well. Cut them into small cubes and mix them with sugar in a bowl. Cream Cheese Cream: Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Whisk the cream cheese until airy with the vanilla and powdered sugar. Layer Cake: Spread half of the cream onto the bottom cake layer. Distribute half of the strawberries on top. Place the middle layer on top, spread the rest of the cream on it, and place the last of the strawberries on top. Place the top cake layer with the almonds on top and press it down lightly. Let the cake set for 1 hour in the refrigerator before it is ready for serving. Serve the cake with fresh strawberries.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 100 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrates: 40 g, Protein: 6 g, Fat: 6 g, of which saturated fat: 2 g.

title: Strawberry mousse with strawberry sauce
preparation: Soak the gelatin leaves in plenty of cold water for 10 minutes. Rinse the strawberries and remove the stems. Scrape the vanilla seeds out of the vanilla pod. Blend the strawberries with powdered sugar and vanilla seeds. Set aside 1½ dl of strawberry puree for the sauce and save it for later. Take the gelatin leaves out of the water and melt them over very low heat in a saucepan. It must not boil and must be removed from the heat as soon as it is melted. Stir it into the strawberry puree. Put the skyr or fromage frais in a bowl and whisk in the strawberry puree little by little to avoid lumps. Whip the egg whites until stiff and fold them into the strawberry puree. Pour the mousse into individual glasses or into a glass bowl. Let the mousse set in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours. Toast the almond flakes in a dry pan until they are golden brown and fragrant. Let them cool on a plate. Serve the strawberry mousse with strawberry sauce and garnish with halved strawberries and almond flakes.
notes: Tip! Skyr is an Icelandic dairy product that is also produced in Denmark. Skyr has a fat content of only 0.2%, has a very fine, thick and creamy consistency and a well-balanced acidity. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 38 g. Protein: 9 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.3 g.

title: Marbled Banana Cake
preparation:
Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Whisk the oil with sugar and vanilla seeds for a couple of minutes. Add the eggs one at a time. Continue whisking for about 5 minutes.

Mix the white whole wheat flour with the baking powder and sift it over the batter. Gently fold the batter. Mash the bananas and fold them into the batter.

Chop the chocolate and melt it in a bowl over a water bath.

Take a third of the batter and fold in the sifted cocoa powder and melted chocolate.

Spread half of the white batter into the bottom of a loaf pan lined with parchment paper. Cover with the chocolate batter, and finish with the rest of the white batter. Swirl a little carelessly through the batter with a fork to create a marbled effect.

Bake the cake at 175 degrees for approximately 45 minutes on the bottom rack.

Cool the cake before slicing it into slices.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates 31 g. Protein 4 g. Fat 6 g. Of which saturated fat 1 g. * per piece.

title: Katrineblommekage
preparation: Lightly pickled plums: Halve the plums and remove the pits. Boil the water with sugar, and let the plums simmer gently until they are tender without falling apart. Remove the plums from the water and place them in an ovenproof tart dish with the rounded side facing up. Batter: Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds. Whisk the vanilla seeds, eggs, and sugar until frothy. Boil the milk, and whisk it into the egg mixture. Put everything back in the saucepan and heat while stirring until the cream thickens, but it must NOT boil. Pour the cream over the plums. Mix the cinnamon and sugar together and sprinkle it over the cake. Sprinkle with almonds and bake the cake in the oven at 175 degrees for approx. 30 minutes, until the cream is golden on top and firm when pressed. Serve the cake warm.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 60 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 1000 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 32 g, Protein: 7 g, Fat: 8 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Panna cotta with apple and burnt almonds
preparation:
Panna cotta: Soak the gelatin leaves in a large bowl of cold water for at least 10 minutes. Heat 1 dl of milk with sugar and vanilla seeds until it melts. Squeeze the water out of the gelatin leaves and melt them into the warm milk. Mix the warm milk with the cold milk and pour the milk into 4 glasses. Let them set in the refrigerator – it takes about 2 hours. 

Apple jelly: Soak the gelatin leaves in a large bowl of cold water for at least 10 minutes. Melt the gelatin leaves over very low heat in a saucepan. Stir the apple juice with the gelatin. Cut the apple into very small cubes and mix them with the apple juice. Distribute the apples and jelly onto the set panna cotta. Let the apple jelly set in the refrigerator for about 1 hour. 

Burnt almonds: Boil sugar and water in a pot with the almonds. Boil all the water away and let the sugar slowly turn into a golden, shiny caramel. When the almonds start to make a cracking sound, they are done. Spread the almonds out on a piece of parchment paper and use two forks to separate the almonds. Let them cool completely. Serve the almonds with the panna cotta.
notes:
Tip! Instead of whole milk, you can use almond milk. Almond milk can be bought in well-stocked supermarkets. They are found in the refrigerated section, typically together with rice and oat milk. If you do not use all the almond milk at once, you can freeze it.

Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 80 g per person, unless otherwise specified.

Energy distribution: 1000 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 34 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 10 g. Of which saturated fat: 3 g (per person, unless otherwise specified).

title: Apple cake with cinnamon
preparation:
1 cake = 10 pieces

Apple cake
Mix sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, baking soda, and baking powder together. Grate the ginger finely. Stir the ginger, milk, nut oil, and lemon juice together with all the dry ingredients. Remove the cores from the apples, cut them into large cubes, and fold them into the batter. Place the batter in a springform pan approximately 22 cm in diameter and sprinkle with almond flakes. Bake the cake at 175 degrees for approx. 30 minutes. Prick the cake with a toothpick; if batter sticks, the cake needs to bake longer.

Cardamom cream
Stir the skyr with cardamom.

Serve the cake with or without cardamom cream.
notes:
Tip! Instead of almond flakes, you can use hazelnut flakes, chopped almonds, or nuts. Nut oil can be purchased in well-stocked supermarkets. You can use flavor-neutral rapeseed oil instead. The cake is egg-free, and if you want to make it completely vegan, you can use all kinds of plant milk instead.

Energy distribution*
850 KJ (200 kcal)
Carbohydrate 32 g
Protein 6 g
Fat 6 g
Of which saturated fat 1 g
* per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Spice cake with candied orange peel, bitter orange, and orange

ingredients.name: dried fruits e.g. figs, prunes, raisins and dates
mixture of candied orange peel and bitter orange

preparation: Finely chop the dried fruits and place them in a bowl. Pour the rum over them and let the fruits soak for at least 1 hour – preferably longer. Preheat the oven to 160 degrees. Finely chop the nuts. Mix the whole wheat flour with baking powder and spices. Stir the brown sugar and eggs together and then add the flour with baking powder and spices, nuts, orange juice, oil and syrup. Stir until a uniform batter is formed, then add the candied orange peel, bitter orange, the dried fruits in rum and the orange zest. Pour the batter into a greased cake tin of approx. 1 liter or a springform pan of approx. 22 cm. Bake the cake in the middle of the oven for approx. 45 minutes. Use a skewer to check if the cake is baked. If batter clings to it, bake the cake for a little longer. Remove the cake and let it cool before dusting with sifted icing sugar.
notes: Energy distribution* 800 KJ (200 kcal) Carbohydrate 27 g Protein 4 g Fat 5 g Of which saturated fat 1 g * per person, unless otherwise stated

title: Panna cotta with caramelized pears
preparation: Caramelized pears: Peel the pears and remove the cores. Cut the pears into large cubes. Melt the sugar in a pan until it caramelizes, and toss the pears in the caramel. Let them simmer over low heat until they are barely tender. Remove the pan from the heat and let the pears sit until they are completely tender. Let them cool down. Distribute half of the pears into 8 serving glasses. Save the rest for later. Panna cotta: Soak the gelatin leaves in a large bowl of cold water for at least 10 minutes. Split the vanilla bean, scrape out the seeds, and mix them with 2 tsp. of the sugar. Heat 2 dl of milk with the vanilla seeds and the rest of the sugar. Squeeze the water out of the gelatin leaves and melt them into the warm milk. Mix the warm milk with the cold milk. Let the milk cool down until it thickens. Stir it occasionally so the vanilla at the bottom is distributed throughout the milk. Pour the milk into the glasses over the pears. Place the dessert in the refrigerator and let it set for approximately 2 hours. Distribute the remaining pears on top of the desserts when serving and sprinkle with chopped pistachios.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 125 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 850 KJ (200 kcal) per person, unless otherwise stated. Carbohydrates: 38 g. Protein: 3 g. Fat: 4 g.

title: Apple-pear cake
preparation: Peel pears and apples, remove the cores and cut them into wedges. Grease a tart pan with ½ tbsp melted margarine. Place the fruit in the tart pan and sprinkle cinnamon and brown sugar over it. Mix oats with crushed macaroons, the rest of the melted margarine, and honey. Spread the mixture over the fruit. Bake the cake at 200 degrees for 25-30 minutes, until the fruit is soft. Serve with creme fraiche.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 85 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 32 g. Protein: 4 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.5 g.

title: Squash cake with cream cheese icing
preparation: Whisk eggs and brown sugar until frothy. Stir in oil margarine and milk. Mix flour with baking powder and cinnamon and fold it into the batter along with squash and raisins. Pour the batter into a baking pan, approx. 25 x 30 cm, lined with parchment paper. Bake the cake in the middle of the oven at 180°C for approx. 40 minutes. Mix cream cheese with icing sugar to make an icing and spread the icing on the cooled cake.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution: 850 KJ (200 kcal). For 15 pieces, 1 piece corresponds to the energy distribution above. Carbohydrates: 35 g, Protein: 5 g, Fat: 5 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Apple cake with marzipan, orange, and cinnamon
preparation: Sift the flour, baking powder, and cinnamon together, and add the salt. Whisk the eggs until fluffy with the cane sugar and vanilla sugar, and fold in the flour. Coarsely grate the marzipan and finely grate the orange zest. Stir the marzipan and orange zest into the batter along with the greek yogurt or quark. Squeeze the orange juice into a large bowl. Peel the apples, remove the cores, and cut them into 2-3 cm pieces. Toss the apple pieces in the orange juice, and then fold them into the batter. Pour the batter into a round cake pan (22-24 cm) lined with parchment paper, and bake the cake in the middle of the oven at 175 degrees for approximately 50 minutes. Check with a wooden skewer if it is fully baked, and place it on a wire rack to cool.
notes: 1 cake/12 people. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 40 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrates: 31 g, Protein: 6 g, Fat: 7 g, of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Chocolate cake with pears in a baking tray
preparation: Separate the eggs into yolks and whites. Whisk the yolks with half of the sugar until a white cream forms. Mix the flour, baking powder, vanilla powder, cocoa, and salt, and sift the mixture. Whisk the whites until frothy, add the rest of the sugar, and whisk them until stiff. Stir half of the egg whites into the egg yolks. Fold the flour mixture into the batter along with the oil and milk. Gently fold the remaining egg whites into the batter. Peel the pears and cut them into cubes. Fold the pears into the batter, and place the batter in an ovenproof dish, approx. 20×25 cm, greased with oil or lined with parchment paper. Sprinkle almonds on top, and bake the cake at 175 degrees for 30-40 minutes. Check if the cake is done by piercing it with a toothpick. When the toothpick can be pulled out of the cake without any batter sticking to it, the cake is finished.
notes: Tip! Instead of nut oil, you can use flavor-neutral rapeseed oil. 1 baking tray = 16 pieces. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal), Carbohydrate 3 g, Protein 0.5 g, Fat 7 g, of which saturated fat 1 g.

title: Apple-lime mousse with apple salad
preparation: Mousse: Peel and core the apples for the mousse, and cut them into smaller pieces. Place them in a pot with apple juice and finely grated lime zest, and cook them until completely soft under a lid – approx. 10 minutes. Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water. Blend the apples and liquid into a fine puree, and season with lime juice and sugar. Squeeze the water out of the gelatin, and melt it into the warm apple puree. Cool down. Whip the egg whites until stiff, and whisk in the sugar until it becomes a glossy meringue. Fold the cooled apple puree into the meringue mass, and distribute the mousse into 4 dessert glasses. Place them in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours. Salad: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3-4 minutes. Let them cool, and chop them coarsely. Wash the apple, core it, and cut it into thin slices or small cubes. Toss them together with lime juice, freshly chopped mint leaves, and walnuts. Place the apple salad on top of the mousse and serve.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 150 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 33 g. Protein: 3 g. Fat: 5 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Chocolate Cake
preparation: Whisk eggs and sugar into a light egg mixture. Add cocoa and whisk again. Mix flour together with baking powder and vanilla sugar and whisk it into the batter along with milk and oil margarine. Spread the batter into a small pan of approx. 20 x 25 cm lined with parchment paper and bake the cake at 175 degrees for approx. 25 min. Cool the cake before it is sliced and sprinkled with a little powdered sugar.
notes: Energy distribution* per person: 750 KJ (175 kcal). Carbohydrates: 28 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 1.5 g.

title: Apple Muffins
preparation: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Whisk eggs with brown sugar and vanilla until a frothy mass is formed. Mix white wheat flour with the spices and baking powder, and stir it into the egg mixture along with the oil. Cut the apples into quarters. Remove the cores and cut the apples into cubes. Fold the apples into the batter, and distribute it into 10 muffin molds. Bake the cakes for approximately 20 minutes. Check with a skewer to see if the cakes are baked. If there is batter clinging, bake the cakes for a little longer. Cool the cakes and sprinkle with a little ground cinnamon.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 25 g per person, unless otherwise specified. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 34 g. Protein: 4 g. Fat: 7 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Rhubarb trifle with vanilla skyr cream and oat crunch
preparation: Rhubarb: Cut the rhubarb into small pieces of approximately 1 cm. Place the rhubarb and sugar in a small saucepan and cook into a compote over low heat for about 10 minutes. Season the compote with ginger. Let the rhubarb cool. Oat crunch: Melt the honey over low heat in a pan. Add the oats and toast them until they are golden and crispy. Stir them occasionally. Chop the almonds and toss them into the oats. Vanilla skyr cream: Mix the skyr with powdered sugar and vanilla seeds. Layer the rhubarb compote, vanilla skyr cream, and oat crunch in glasses. Finish with a layer of cream.
notes: Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 80 g per person, unless otherwise stated. Energy distribution per person: 900 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrate: 37 g. Protein: 7 g. Fat: 3 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Rhubarb snails with rum glaze
preparation:
Rhubarb compote: Place rhubarb in a pot with the water that remains after they have been rinsed. Add sugar, vanilla seeds, and the pod, and cook over low heat for approx. 10 minutes. Remove the vanilla pod, cool the compote, and blend it. 

Yeast dough: Warm the milk and pour it into a bowl. Dissolve the yeast in the milk and add oil, salt, cardamom, and sugar. Knead the white wheat and then the wheat flour into the dough a little at a time. Knead until the dough is smooth and supple. Let the dough rise covered in a warm place for 1 hour. Roll the dough out to a rectangle of approx. 40 x 30 cm. Spread the rhubarb compote on the dough, and roll it up gently along the long side, like a roulade. Carefully cut the dough into 14 pieces, and place them with the seam facing down in small foil molds. Alternatively, in one large round mold. Let the snails rise for approx. 30 minutes. Brush the snails with beaten egg, and bake them at 175 degrees for approx. 20 minutes, until they are golden. 

Rum glaze: Mix powdered sugar with a little boiling water and rum essence into a glaze. Decorate the snails with the glaze.
notes: Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 37 g, Protein: 5 g, Fat: 8 g, of which saturated fat: 0.4 g.

title: Kransekage Pieces
preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Divide the marzipan into smaller pieces and knead it together with the sugar and egg white. Roll the dough into a log and divide it into 24 pieces. Roll them into small balls and place them on a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bake the kransekage pieces for approx. 8 minutes until they are golden and slightly brown at the edges. Cool the cakes. Mix powdered sugar with egg white to create a glaze. Put the glaze in a freezer bag. Cut a small hole in one corner and decorate the kransekage.
notes: 24 pieces (3 pieces per person). Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 60 g. Protein: 19 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Chocolate Cookies with Nuts

ingredients.name: hazelnut oil or flavor-neutral rapeseed oil

preparation: Finely chop the nuts. Coarsely chop the chocolate. Scrape the vanilla seeds out of the half vanilla bean. Mix the nuts and vanilla with the other ingredients and knead the dough well together. Roll approximately 45 small balls of dough. Place the balls on baking sheets lined with parchment paper with a little space between them so they can spread slightly during baking. Bake the cookies at 175 degrees for about 12 minutes until they are golden brown. Let them cool on a wire rack and store them in a cookie jar.
notes: Approx. 45 pcs. – 4 pcs. per person. Energy distribution per person: 800 KJ (200 kcal). Carbohydrates: 28 g. Protein: 4 g. Fat: 8 g. Of which saturated fat: 0.8 g.

title: Banana Bread

ingredient_sections.section_name: 1 large loaf approx. 12 slices (1 slice per person)

preparation: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees fan air. Whisk the brown sugar and eggs until fluffy with an electric whisk. Mash the bananas with a fork. Mix the dry ingredients together and fold them into the batter along with the yogurt and mashed bananas until a soft dough is formed. Grease a pan or line it with parchment paper, and pour the batter into the pan. Halve the last banana lengthwise and place it on top of the batter with a gentle press. Bake the banana bread in the oven for approx. 25 min. until it is golden on top. Cool the bread and sprinkle with sifted powdered sugar.
notes: Tip! The banana bread can also be baked in a rye bread pan of approx. 3 liters. The baking time is extended to a total of 45 min. Fruit and vegetables: Approx. 40 g per person. Energy distribution per person: 775 KJ (175 kcal). Carbohydrates: 31 g. Protein: 5 g. Fat: 4 g. Of which saturated fat: 1 g.

title: Quinoa and adzuki bean burger
preparation: Place the quinoa in a strainer and rinse it with water. Place it in a pot with water, salt to taste, and cook until the water has been completely absorbed. It is recommended to check the instructions on the package as the water volume may vary between brands. Slice the onion into julienne, place it in a pan with hot oil and sauté for a couple of minutes, lower the heat, add the chopped garlic, and let it cook for about 15 minutes. Cover with a lid and stir occasionally. Once everything is done, place the quinoa, the adzuki beans mashed with a fork, the parsley, and the onion in a container. Mix everything well by hand and form two burgers. Place them in a pan with oil and cook to your liking. Serve with the sautéed shiitake.

title: Chickpea and spinach pancakes
preparation: Using a blender, blend the chickpea flour, water, spinach, salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. Let the batter rest in the refrigerator for 2 hours. In a pan, add a little olive oil and when hot, add a bit of batter (make small pancakes). Cook for a few minutes on one side, flip, and cook on the other side. Serve.

title: Chickpea hummus with pumpkin
preparation: Cook the pumpkin in the oven, having previously peeled and chopped it. (It can also be cooked in the microwave as if it were steamed). Mix the pumpkin, garlic clove, cooked chickpeas, natural yogurt, lemon juice, salt, and spices with a tablespoon of olive oil. Blend until a homogeneous texture is obtained.
notes: Pumpkin is in season and could be combined with boiled cabbage leaves as if it were a cannelloni.

title: Chickpeas with barley
preparation: The day before, we will have soaked the chickpeas and the barley grains. The next day, we will boil the chickpeas and the barley (we can substitute them for pre-cooked chickpeas and the barley can be substituted for brown rice, quinoa, or buckwheat). We will start making the sauté with the leek, carrots, and zucchini; once browned, we will add the fried tomato, let it simmer for a bit, add salt and pepper, and finally add both the legume and the cereal. We will add a bit of vegetable broth (150 ml) and let it cook for about 10 minutes until the broth is consumed, and then it will be ready to serve.

title: Roasted chickpeas with carrots and Greek yogurt
preparation: Preheat the oven to 200 ºC. Clean the carrots well and dry them. Drain and pat dry half a can of chickpeas. If you wish, you could peel them to improve digestibility for some people. In a bowl, mix the chickpeas with the carrots. Add a drizzle of oil, the spices (cumin, thyme, paprika) and salt. Mix well and transfer to a baking tray previously greased or lined with parchment paper. Roast in the oven for 25-30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chickpeas are crunchy and the carrots are golden. If you want the carrots to be softer, you can boil or steam them beforehand for 10 minutes (e.g., using a steamer). Meanwhile, mix the yogurt with the lemon zest, a portion of the feta, and a bit of salt. Spread this yogurt base on a plate. Serve the roasted chickpeas and carrots on top of the yogurt. Finish with pieces of feta, a drizzle of oil and, if you like, fresh coriander and toasted seeds.
notes: If you want the carrots to be softer, you can boil or steam them beforehand for 10 minutes (e.g., using a steamer).

title: Chickpeas with cauliflower and quinoa
preparation: Soak the chickpeas in water for 10-12 hours. The next day, discard the soaking water, add clean water, a bay leaf and cook until they are soft. Rinse the quinoa well in a strainer until the water runs clear, boil in a separate pot, drain and set aside. Wash and separate the cauliflower florets. Chop the onion, garlic and peppers, then immediately transfer to a saucepan and sauté with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Add 1 liter of water or vegetable broth, salt, cumin and fennel, the cauliflower and the frozen spinach, cover and cook until the vegetables are almost soft. Next, add the reserved chickpeas and quinoa, a bit of pepper and turmeric. Boil for 10-15 more minutes, then let rest before serving.

title: TIMBAL OF CHANTERELLE MUSHROOMS

ingredients.name: olive tapenade and sliced black olives
lemon and extra virgin olive oil

preparation: Dice the tomato, onion, shredded cod, and avocado. Mix with lemon juice and oil, the onion, and the avocado cubes. Take a metal plating mold and place the mushrooms first, pressing them well, followed by the onion, tomato, cod, and avocado in layers. Decorate with some black olives and some peeled prawns. Leave in the refrigerator for at least one hour. Remove the mold and garnish with an olive tapenade mixed with extra virgin olive oil.

title: LENTILS SHEPHERD'S STYLE PIE
preparation: Wash the vegetables. Peel the onion, carrot, and pumpkin. Chop them into cubes and sauté them with the olive oil for 10 - 15 minutes. Add the lentils with enough water, salt, and sweet pepper and boil until the lentils are cooked. If you like a spicy touch, you can add hot pepper instead of sweet pepper. Separately, peel and boil the potatoes with water and salt. Drain them and mash them well with a fork. In a somewhat deep baking dish, place the stewed lentils at the bottom, cover with the mashed potato and a bit of grated cheese on top. Bake for 10 - 15 minutes and the dish is ready.
notes: If you want to make the recipe vegan, simply substitute the cheese with nutritional yeast and add orange zest on top if desired.

title: Chickpea flour crackers
preparation: Mix 100 g of chickpea flour, 1 tbsp of baking powder, 1 tbsp of salt, 1 tbsp of garlic powder, 1 tbsp of rosemary, 15 ml of olive oil and 40-60 ml of water, until a compact dough is obtained. Roll out the dough with the help of a rolling pin, cut it into squares, and prick it with a fork. Bake the dough in the oven at 180 ºC for 25-30 minutes (until lightly golden) on a baking sheet lined with a sheet of parchment paper. Let it cool. Serve the crackers with guacamole (or with whichever vegetable pâté we like best).

title: Pumpkin cream with hummus

ingredients.name: white beans (you can use another legume)
unsweetened plant-based drink or vegetable broth

preparation: Blend everything together (if you want the cream less thick, add more plant-based drink until the desired texture is obtained). Add the spices you like (paprika, curry, turmeric...). For a crunchy touch, add chopped pistachios.

title: White bean curry with eggplant
preparation: Sauté a sweet onion with olive oil. When it becomes transparent, add the crushed tomato. Add the spices: cumin, turmeric, curry, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, pepper, and salt. Add the eggplant cut into cubes. Once browned, add the coconut milk. Let cook for 5 minutes. Add the previously cooked white beans and let cook for 10 minutes. Plate with a little coconut milk on top and optionally chili flakes on top.

title: Warm chickpea salad
preparation: Place a pot with water on the heat and when it starts to boil, add the eggs for 10 minutes. Mince the garlic and dice the onions, pepper, and tomatoes into small cubes. Place a frying pan with a drizzle of EVOO on the heat and once heated, add the chopped vegetables and season with salt and pepper. Drain the chickpeas and the tuna. Once the eggs have boiled, peel them and dice them into small cubes. Keep stirring the vegetables until they are as cooked as you like and adjust salt and pepper if necessary. Mix the chickpeas with the cooked vegetables, the tuna, and the hard-boiled eggs, and the dish will be ready to serve and eat.

title: Pizza with red lentil base

ingredients.name: toppings to taste (tomato, olives, goat cheese...)

preparation: Soak the red lentils for a minimum of 45 minutes. Drain the lentils. Using a food processor, blend the lentils together with 30 ml of water, a couple of pinches of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. Grease a sheet of parchment paper with a little olive oil. Spread the dough over the parchment paper. Bake in the oven at 200 ºC for 10-12 minutes. Flip the dough over, then add some tomato sauce, oregano, mozzarella, and any toppings you like. Bake in the oven for another 10-12 minutes and serve.

title: Chickpeas stewed with vegetables
preparation: In a large frying pan, sauté the chopped chicken along with the sliced sausage. Let it cook with the pan covered so that the meat releases juices and does not become dry. Season with pepper to taste. Add the chopped onion and let it cook over low heat until the onion becomes transparent. Add the chopped green and red bell peppers, stirring for about 4 minutes. Add the grated tomato and the boiled chickpeas. In a pressure cooker or a traditional pot, add the previous mixture and pour the vegetable or meat broth into the pot. Cover the pot and let it cook for 15 minutes in a pressure cooker or 35 minutes if using a conventional pot.
notes: Regarding spices, you can add pepper, but also a pinch of curry, ginger powder, and turmeric. (We always add spices at the end so they do not become bitter). You can make a larger quantity and freeze it to save time and work for other meals. You can substitute the red and green bell peppers with pieces of cabbage, since it is currently in season.

title: Lentils with rice with sherry aroma

ingredients.name: vegetable or chicken broth (at room temperature)

preparation: Slice the carrot and the leek. Chop the garlic cloves very finely. Put the oil in a saucepan and sauté the vegetables. Add the cured ham to the sauté. Incorporate the wine and stir. Add the rice and the broth and let boil. Once the rice is cooked, add the lentils. Plate the lentils and add a drizzle of sherry vinegar.

title: Chickpeas stewed with vegetables and miso
preparation: Drain the chickpeas in a colander and rinse them with tap water. Immediately prepare the vegetables. Clean, peel, and cut the carrots, onion, and tender garlic into small pieces. Clean and chop the green leaves (spinach or chard). In a pot or saucepan, add the olive oil and cook the onion and tender garlic over low heat. After a few minutes, add the rest of the vegetables and let them sauté together with the onion for a couple more minutes. Next, add the chickpeas and sauté everything for one minute. Then, add water or broth to the vegetables and chickpeas until everything is covered, add the salt, and cook for approximately 20 minutes. Check the saltiness. Once you turn off the heat, add the miso and mix.

title: Lentil meatballs
preparation: First, chop the onion, leek, eggplant, and carrots into small pieces. Sauté the onion and leek in a pan with a drizzle of olive oil over low/medium heat. Once they are transparent, add the carrots and sauté until they become slightly soft. Incorporate the chopped eggplant and season with pepper, stirring so it doesn't stick. When the vegetables are cooked, turn off the heat and let them cool for a few minutes. Open the lentil jars, drain them, mash them slightly or chop them, and put them in a bowl. Add the cooked vegetables to the bowl along with the oat flour, spices, and mix everything together so it is well integrated. Place the breadcrumbs with garlic and parsley on a plate and use the vegetable and lentil mixture to shape the meatballs; coat them in the breadcrumbs with garlic and parsley and place them on baking paper on a tray while preheating the oven to 190 degrees. Place the tray of meatballs in the oven for 40 minutes, turning them every 10 minutes so they cook evenly. Once cooked, place them in a casserole dish with tomato sauce and a hint of oregano.
notes: We can serve them on a plate with some bacon or other vegetables or mushrooms.

title: Broad bean burgers
preparation: Wash and peel the carrots. Cook the carrots by steaming or in the microwave until they are soft. Peel the onion and cut it into very small pieces or pass it through a food processor. Sauté the onion with oil in a pan over medium-low heat, adding half a cup of water so it cooks and softens slowly. Add the parsley, spices, and salt, then stir. Pour the cooked beans into a colander and rinse them under running tap water. In a bowl, using a fork or a masher, mash the carrots together with the cooked beans. Add the sautéed and spiced onion to the mixture. In a deep dish, mix the chickpea flour with half a cup of water until a homogeneous mixture is obtained, then add it to the previous dough to help bind it. In a non-stick pan, heat the extra virgin olive oil over medium heat and form burger shapes using a round mold. Cook on both sides until golden brown.

title: Black peas with artichokes and poached eggs
preparation: Soak the peas in water for 24h, making 2-3 water changes. Boil them in hot water for 1h. Meanwhile, peel and cut the artichokes to microwave them for 5 minutes. In a frying pan with olive oil, sauté a mixture of minced garlic and parsley. When golden, add the artichokes and season with salt and pepper. Drain the peas and add them to the pan so everything combines flavors. Place a pot of water on the heat and just before it boils, drop in the eggs, let them cook for 3 minutes, and remove them to plate.

title: Chickpea Madeleines
preparation: Blend the chickpeas with the banana using a blender. Afterwards, beat the eggs and mix them in. Add the cinnamon, honey, and chocolate, and finish stirring everything so it integrates well. Take some molds and grease them with a little oil. Add a bit of batter. Bake in the oven at about 180°C until cooked (to check, you can pierce them with a toothpick or the tip of a knife).

title: Endive boat with pumpkin hummus

ingredients.name: cooked chickpeas or pumpkin
ingredients.quantity: 50 g of cooked chickpeas or 25 g of pumpkin

ingredients.name: chickpea cooking water or homemade vegetable broth
salt and pepper (black or red) to taste

preparation: Peel and cut the pumpkin into small cubes. Cook the pumpkin in the oven or microwave. Blend the pumpkin, cooked chickpeas, water or broth, tahini, extra virgin olive oil, lemon, salt, and pepper until smooth. Add the mixture onto the cleaned endive leaves. Decorate with raw pumpkin seeds.

title: Red kidney bean brownie

ingredients.name: chopped walnuts or dark chocolate chunks

preparation: First, hydrate the dates with water for approximately 1 hour. Second, blend the cooked and well-drained red kidney beans with the cocoa powder. Add the room temperature butter to the mixture. Using the previously hydrated dates, blend them with a little water until a consistent paste is obtained. Finally, add the dates to the mixture. If you want to enrich the brownie with walnuts or chocolate, now is the time. Bake the brownie for 20 minutes at 180ºC.

title: Gratinated lentil cake
preparation: Peel and chop the onion into pieces, set aside. Prepare a pot with water and place it on the heat, rinse the oatmeal well and add it once the water starts to boil and cook it for 15 minutes. Once boiled, drain it and set it aside in a container. Sauté the onion in a pan adding a little EVOO and a pinch of salt and let it brown slightly. Rinse the cooked lentils and mix them in the container along with the oatmeal, adding a pinch of salt and pepper optionally. Add the browned onion and the eggs to the mixture, mix well and blend. Prepare an oven-safe dish, place parchment paper at the base lightly coated with a few drops of EVOO and add the mixture so that it is well distributed. Cover the top with grated cheese and gratin in the oven for 25 minutes. Serve hot, enjoy!

title: BEANS WITH SPINACH, GARLIC AND PARSLEY
preparation: Prepare the beans: If you are using dried beans, you must soak them overnight beforehand to soften them. If you have cooked beans (canned or frozen), you can skip this step. Cook the beans in a pot with plenty of water for about 40-50 minutes (if they are dried) or 20 minutes in a pressure cooker, until they are tender. Add a bit of salt at the end of the cooking. Prepare the spinach: Clean the spinach well and cut it if the leaves are very large. If the spinach is fresh and tender, there is no need to cook it much; just blanch or sauté it briefly in olive oil later. Sauté the garlic and onion: In a large pan or casserole, add a good drizzle of olive oil. When hot, add the peeled and finely minced garlic. Let them brown lightly. If you want to add onion, chop it finely and add it along with the garlic. Sauté until the onion is transparent. Add the spinach: Incorporate the spinach into the pan and sauté until it has reduced well and is tender. This step will only take a few minutes.
notes: (typical beans from the area) (ideally from the garden) (optional) (optional) (optional)

title: Cold chickpea salad
preparation: Boil the eggs and leave them on a plate. Desalt the cod and shred it. Take the already boiled chickpeas and add the cod, the escarole, the spring onion, the tomato and mix everything together adding the oil and the vinegar. Leave it in the refrigerator for about 3 hours so it is fresh, stirring it a couple of times. Finally, before serving, add the chopped eggs on top.
notes: Pseudonym: La Guineu

title: Beetroot hummus
preparation: Place the chopped beetroot, chickpeas, yogurt, tahini, cumin, lemon juice, and olive oil in a food processor or a blending jar. Blend until a homogeneous texture is obtained. Add the beetroot juice gradually until you achieve the desired consistency (creamier or denser). Taste and adjust with salt or lemon juice if necessary. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and almond pieces on top, accompanied by vegetable sticks, pita bread, or toast.

title: Green beans with prawns
preparation: Peel the prawns. Place the shells and heads in a pan and fry them, crushing the heads to extract the juice. Boil everything with a little water. Sauté the garlic and onion and add the drained green beans. Drain the broth from the boiled prawns with water, remove the heads and shells. Add the green beans with the fish stock and the concentrated liquid from the heads and shells, then add the peeled prawns and let boil for 2 more minutes. Garnish with parsley and serve.
notes: Pseudonym: Casa Saya

title: Chickpea cookies
preparation: In a bowl suitable for using a blender, place 1 jar of drained chickpeas, 2 eggs, 2 tsp of honey, and 1 sachet of Royal baking powder and blend well until a homogeneous dough is obtained. Add two cups of oats and the chocolate chips and mix with a fork. Place in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. Pre-heat the oven to 170 degrees. Bake for 15 minutes, let them cool and ... Enjoy.

title: Cold lentil salad with rice, apple, walnuts and ham
preparation: Dice the apple and place it in the juice of half a lemon. Cut the iberian ham into small pieces. Take the walnuts and chop them. Cook the rice for 15' and drain and rinse twice. Prepare the vinaigrette with extra virgin olive oil and mustard. Mix the lentils with the rice, walnuts, apple and ham. Place the whole salad in a round mold and turn it onto a plate for a better presentation. Add the vinaigrette.
notes: Pseudonym: Blamar

title: Pumpkin puree with chickpeas

ingredients.name: splash of extra virgin olive oil

preparation: In a pot, add ½ of water and cook all the vegetables. Once cooked, blend them in a blender to a puree texture. Make a sauté with the garlic and add it to the puree, then add the cooked chickpeas. Place in a bowl and top with the sliced hard-boiled egg. Serve.
notes: Pseudonym: Lalis

title: White bean cream with baby squid

ingredients.name: baby squid cut into small pieces

preparation: Clean and finely chop the leek. Sauté it in olive oil for about 5 minutes. Add the beans and a little water and salt, and let it cook for 15 minutes. Clean the baby squid thoroughly, cut them into small pieces and place them in a pan with olive oil and minced garlic, pour in the wine and let it cook for about 5 minutes. Blend the beans with the rest of the vegetables so it gains body and flavor. Serve in a dish with the baby squid arranged around it.
notes: Pseudonym: Thyme

title: DRY GREEN BEANS WITH ANCHOVIES AND ESCALIVADA

ingredients.name: red peppers (already roasted, ready to use)

preparation: Mix the green beans with the roasted peppers and the anchovies. Place the mint, oil, and salt in a blender. Emulsify well. Season the green beans 1 hour before serving.
notes: Enjoy your meal

title: Chickpea and Cod Burger
preparation: Mash the chickpeas and place them on parchment paper. Add the minced garlic and parsley and shape them. Crumble the cod with the egg and the bread, make meatballs, and fry them in hot oil. Serve the burgers and the cod meatballs.
notes: Pseudonym: Xavite

title: Chickpea salad
preparation: Boil the langoustines and peel them. In a bowl, place the drained cooked chickpeas, the tomato in pieces, the crumbled cheese, the langoustines, and the vinaigrette sauce. Serve.
notes: Nickname: Buella

title: Lentil omelet
