notes: You can stuff them with spinach and cheese, tuna and olives, mozzarella and tomato, vegetables (pumpkin, onion, carrot...), mushrooms and cheese, smoked salmon and avocado, etc. To adapt it to vegan diets, substitute the cheese and ham with vegetables, tofu, textured soy, "vegan cheese", etc. For hypertensive individuals, choose low-salt ham and cheese. Consult your dietitian-nutritionist or check the nutritional label of the cheese, as it may contain egg lysozyme and cooked ham.

title: Chickpeas with spinach
preparation: To start, in a small pot, bring half a liter of water to a boil and set aside. In another pot, large enough, add the 4 tbsp of EVOO and turn on the medium-low heat while you peel the garlic and the onion. When the EVOO is hot, add the minced garlic and wait 2 minutes until they brown slightly. Next, add the chopped onion and leave it all over medium heat for about 5 minutes or until you see that the onion starts to become transparent, making sure it doesn't burn. Season with salt and pepper. While the onion is browning, drain the spinach and rinse it. When the onion is almost transparent or to your liking, add the spinach to the pot and stir until it mixes with the garlic and the onion. Add the sweet paprika and the cumin and stir. Let it cook like this for about 5 minutes and take the opportunity to drain the chickpeas and clean them well, then you can add them to the pot. Once you have all the ingredients in the pot, add the half liter of hot water you prepared previously. Cook all the ingredients together for thirty minutes, stirring occasionally. If you notice that you are running out of water and you like your chickpeas soupy, add a little more, but always hot.

title: Red lentil dhal
preparation: Cut the vegetables into mirepoix (pieces neither too large nor too small). Sauté the onion, carrot, mushrooms, chopped tomato, ginger, and curry leaves in a pot with olive oil for about 10-15 minutes. Add the spices, salt, and pepper to taste and stir. Add the lentils and cover with water or vegetable broth until two fingers above the level. Cook over low heat for 25-35 minutes, until the lentils are tender and well cooked (if more liquid is needed during cooking, add a little more hot water or broth). After 25-30 minutes, it is ready to serve. It can be accompanied by basmati rice, chopped fresh coriander, or 1 tablespoon of natural yogurt.

title: Spinach and quinoa quiche
preparation: Mix the cooked quinoa, pepper, and eggs in a bowl and stir well. Press the mixture into the bottom and sides of a pastry mold covered with olive oil to prevent sticking. Bake the base at 180 °C for 20 minutes; let it cool. For the filling, heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the infused olive oil and scallions; sauté for 3 minutes before adding the spinach for another 3 minutes. In a bowl, mix the milk and the rest of the ingredients well. Pour the mixture onto the quinoa base and bake for another 40-45 minutes. Let it rest for 5 minutes; cut into 8 slices.
notes: Use ham/iberian ham or firm smoked tofu. Instead of spinach, you can use broccoli florets, pumpkin, or cabbage.

title: Green beans with romesco sauce and prawns
preparation: Place the tomatoes, onion, and garlic on a baking tray. Bake in the oven at 200 ºC for 45 minutes. Peel the roasted vegetables and blend them finely along with the nyora pulp, toasted almonds and hazelnuts, oil, vinegar, and a pinch of salt. Rinse the green beans with water and mix them in a saucepan with the romesco sauce. If necessary, add a little water. Let it cook for a few minutes. Peel the prawns but without removing their heads. Cook them in a pan with a drizzle of oil. Serve the dish with a base of green beans and the prawns on top. Sprinkle with chopped parsley.

title: Orange lentil couscous with marinated chicken and seasonal vegetables
preparation: The night before: cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and place it in a bowl with the oil, lemon juice, and mustard. Leave it in the refrigerator. Cut the onion, carrot, and zucchini into brunoise size. Cut the pumpkin into mirepoix size. Clean the mushrooms. Take the chicken out of the refrigerator and place it in the pan with all the marinade. Stir continuously until the chicken is cooked. Remove the chicken from the pan, leaving the juices. Add the onion and carrot to the pan. Let it cook over medium-low heat. Add the zucchini and the pumpkin. Once the vegetables are cooked, add the reserved chicken. Immediately after, add the couscous. Stir and add 200 ml of water and cover. Let it rest for 5 minutes and turn off the heat. Sauté the mushrooms in a separate pan. When they are done, add them to the pan. Plate.
notes: Vegan: you can substitute the chicken with tofu. Check the mustard label as it may contain other allergens.

title: Stuffed Pumpkin

ingredients.name: spices (herbs de Provence, basil, garlic, salt and pepper)

preparation: Wash the pumpkin and the rest of the vegetables. Cut the pumpkin longitudinally into 2 halves, hollow out the seeds and place in the oven at 180 ºC for 20 minutes, or until the pumpkin is cooked. Once warm, scoop out the flesh and set aside. Boil the basmati rice following the instructions and time on the package. Sauté the finely chopped vegetables (cabbage, turnip, carrot, and onion and/or leek) over low heat with the EVOO using a lid. When cooked, add the minced meat (or a plant-based protein in case of vegetarian options) until cooked through. Finally, add the pumpkin flesh that you removed earlier, the cooked basmati rice, and the spices, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Stuff the pumpkins with this mixture and if you wish, you can gratin them in the oven with cheese or almond powder, or you can omit the rice and add mashed potato on top and gratin it.
notes: Vegetarians: Instead of minced meat, add textured soy or another plant-based protein. Vegans: Instead of minced meat use plant protein such as textured soy, tofu, tempeh, seitan and instead of cheese gratin it with almond powder or do not add rice to the stuffing and gratin it with mashed potato.

title: Comforting Winter Soup

ingredients.name: red, yellow and/or green bell pepper

preparation: Cut all the vegetables into small pieces while the broth heats up. When the broth is boiling, add the vegetables to the pot. After 10 minutes, add the noodles. After 7 minutes have passed, add the cooked chickpeas and the whole eggs without shells. Stir well for 2 more minutes and the soup will be ready. When plating, add a drizzle of raw oil and if you wish to decorate, you can do so with grated parsley or any other spice you prefer.
notes: If you are vegan, you can replace the egg with dehydrated soy. If you have an egg allergy, you can replace them with chicken. If you have a gluten allergy, you can replace the noodles with gluten-free pasta. If you have high blood pressure, remember to prepare it without salt and if you buy pre-made broth, make sure it is also salt-free.

title: Spiral vegetable quiche
preparation: Prepare the dough: place the flour, water, and olive oil in a bowl and knead until you achieve an elastic dough. Roll out the dough with a rolling pin until you reach the desired size according to the mold. Place the dough in the mold and prick it in various areas with a fork. Beat the eggs with the rice cream, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and pour it over the dough. Clean the carrot, pumpkin, and eggplant and using a mandoline, slice them into thin strips; then, with patience, create layers forming a spiral by alternating one layer of each vegetable. Bake in the oven for approximately 40 min at 180 ºC.
notes: You can add pieces of parsley on top!

title: Moroccan-style Lentils
preparation: Peel and chop the onion, garlic, and ginger. Clean the carrots and tomatoes and dice them. Heat a little oil in a pan and sauté the onion along with the garlic, carrot, and tomatoes. When the onion is translucent, add the ginger. After about 20 minutes, incorporate the spices and the tomato paste and let them sauté for about five minutes. Finally, incorporate the lentils and stir until the flavors are well integrated.

title: Fake vegetable pizza
preparation: Preheat the oven to 220 ºC while you prepare the pizzas (1 pizza for 2 people: you must divide the ingredients between the 2 doughs). Roll out the pizza doughs on two oven-safe trays. Brush with tomato sauce. Cut the eggplant into strips. Place it in a microwave-safe bowl and let it cook for a first stage at maximum power for 4 minutes. Repeat the same procedure with the bell pepper (5 minutes in the microwave) and with the onion (5 minutes in the microwave). Place the vegetables over the doughs. Add the tuna, one and a half cans per dough (drain the oil). Slice the mozzarella and place it over the other ingredients. Add the olives. Sprinkle the grated cheese on top. To finish, add a pinch of oregano. Bake in the oven at 220 ºC for 15 minutes or until you see that the doughs are golden. Remove from the oven.
notes: Vegans: Instead of tuna, use textured soy. Take 100 g of raw textured soy and hydrate it. To hydrate it, take a bowl with 400 g of hot water, add the soy, and let it rest for 30 minutes. Once hydrated, add it to the pizza just as you would have added the tuna.

title: Curry Lentils

ingredients.name: spices to taste: curry, turmeric, cumin, black pepper

preparation: Wash and chop all the vegetables into very small pieces. In a large pan, sauté the onion and garlic with a little extra virgin olive oil, and once they are well browned, add the bell pepper. Next, add the mushrooms and the tomato and let it all cook together for a few minutes until well sautéed. Add the coconut milk and the spices and let it cook until it becomes a thick sauce. Add the cooked lentils and let it cook for 1 or 2 minutes. You can serve it accompanied by a garnish of rice or mashed potatoes. Serve hot.
notes: Dish suitable for vegans, vegetarians, celiacs, and lactose intolerant people

title: Mixed mushrooms with leek and prawns
preparation: Peel and slice the two leeks into thin rounds and sauté them with a drizzle of olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add the peeled prawns to the leeks and sauté everything together until cooked over high heat. Season with salt and pepper and set aside. Clean and slice the mushrooms. Finely mince the garlic cloves and sauté them in a second pan with olive oil. Add the mushrooms and the chopped parsley and let them cook until they have released all their water and are cooked. Mix the mushroom sauté with the leek and prawn sofrito and sauté everything together in a pan over high heat for 2-3 minutes to finish unifying the flavors. Season with salt again and it will be ready to plate.

title: Vegan Feijolada
preparation: Put the EVOO in a pan. Slice the garlic and sauté it until it turns slightly golden. Cut the carrot into irregular cubes and add it to the pan along with the garlic. Cook for 3 minutes. Remove the garlic and carrot without removing the oil, and sauté the seitan cut into large cubes until golden. Then, add the garlic, carrot, eggplant, and pumpkin (all cut into large cubes) back into the pan. Let it cook all together for about 10 minutes with the lid on. Once time is up, add the beans and the broth and cook for another 5 minutes. Immediately after, add the tofu cut into large cubes and turn off the heat. Add the pepper and salt, stir, and let it rest for 10 minutes. Once the time has passed, serve hot accompanied by some fresh bay leaves.
notes: Dish suitable for vegans.

title: Textured soy bolognese with butternut squash
preparation: Place the textured soy in a bowl and add the previously heated water. Let it rest for about 20 minutes so it hydrates. Afterward, drain it well and set aside for later. Peel and cut the onion, leek, carrots, and butternut squash into small cubes. Place the pan over heat with a little olive oil and when it is hot, add the vegetables with a bit of iodized salt. Let them cook over low heat until the vegetables are golden. Add the spices and the textured soy. Mix well and add the previously crushed tomato. Stir and let the whole mixture reduce for about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, cut the pumpkin in half, remove the seeds from the inside, peel it, and cut it into smaller pieces to be able to use a spiralizer (if you have one) or by hand in spaghetti shapes. Once the pumpkin is cut, sauté it for about 3-4 minutes in the pan with a little olive oil. Mix the bolognese sauce with the pumpkin and done!
notes: Special derivation: veganism, vegetarianism, and celiac disease.

title: Chickpea curry
preparation: In a pot heat the oil, add the garlic and ginger, and sauté for 30 seconds. Next, add the onion, cumin, turmeric, curry, and cayenne; sauté for 7 minutes until the onion is golden. Then add the pumpkin and cauliflower and sauté. Next, incorporate the coconut milk and the chickpeas and cover with water. Bring to a boil. Boil for about 25 minutes. Finally, add the spinach and when they are soft, it is ready. Serve with parsley on top.
notes: Vegetarian dish.

title: Vegetable rice
preparation: If the chanterelles are dehydrated, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes and then rinse them with cold water. Clean the artichokes and keep only the hearts, chop them, and sauté them along with the chanterelles. Set aside. Make a sofrito with the onion and the tomato. Incorporate the artichokes and the chanterelles. Add the vegetable broth and when it boils, add the rice and the salt. Let it cook and stir occasionally for between 15 and 18 minutes (depending on how you like the rice cooked). Let it rest for 5 minutes and serve.

title: Chickpea and Pumpkin Curry with Rice

ingredients.name: coconut milk (1 can) (not coconut plant milk)

preparation: Finely chop the onion, garlic, ginger, and dice the pumpkin into small pieces. Meanwhile, heat the EVOO, add the vegetables to the pan and sauté over low heat until the onion is tender. Next, bring 250 ml of water with a pinch of salt to a boil; once it boils, add the rice and cook for approximately 18 minutes or according to the package instructions. After this time, drain the cooking water and set it aside. Next, add the spices and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add the coconut milk, the chickpeas (previously rinsed), and the salt, then stir. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Once it starts to boil, lower the heat to minimum and cook for another 15 minutes. Let it rest for 5 minutes and serve accompanied by a bit of rice or pita-style bread.
notes: It can be prepared with any other vegetable (butternut squash, green beans...). If accompanied by a salad, it can be considered a complete single-course meal.

title: Chickpea curry with vegetables and brown rice
preparation: In a bowl, incorporate the brown rice and cover it with water to let it soak for 20 minutes. In a pot, bring water to heat. Next, wash and cut the broccoli. When the water reaches boiling point, add the broccoli and cook it for about 15 minutes. Peel and chop the onion and garlic and sauté them with 40 ml of olive oil. Wash, peel, and chop the tomato, pumpkin, and red bell pepper. Incorporate them into the pan with the onion and garlic. Cook everything over medium heat for 10 minutes. Immediately after, add the curry powder, paprika, ground nutmeg, and iodized salt. Stir well. Add the coconut milk and the cooked or canned chickpeas (previously rinsed with pressurized water). Stir well and let it cook for another 10 minutes. In a pot, bring 1 liter of water to heat and, when it starts to boil, add the brown rice. Cook it for between 30 and 40 minutes. After this time, pass it through cold water and let it finish cooling to room temperature. Finally, serve everything together on a plate.

title: Lentil and Pumpkin Lasagna
preparation:
Wash the vegetables and cut them into small cubes. In a large pan, add a good drizzle of olive oil, add all the vegetables and a pinch of salt, and let them cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally. After about 40-45 minutes, lower the heat.

When the vegetables are cooked, drain the lentils, and once they have lost all the water, add them to the pan. Add salt, nutmeg, oregano, and 3/4 parts of the jar of natural canned tomato, stir for 5-10 minutes, and remove from heat.

Fill a large tray with very hot water, place the pasta sheets in it (they should be covered) and let them soak for about 10-15 minutes. After this time, remove them from the water and leave them on paper towels, and with another paper, dry the surface.

Cover the bottom of a glass baking dish with tomato sauce, place two sheets of pasta at the base, then a bit of the filling, repeat one more time, and finish with a sheet of pasta.

Finally, make a light béchamel: add a good drizzle of olive oil to a saucepan and when hot, add a tablespoon of flour, let it cook for a few minutes, and gradually, without stopping to stir, add the milk or plant-based drink. Continue stirring, add nutmeg, black pepper, and salt, and when the béchamel begins to thicken, remove it from the heat.

Cover the surface of the lasagna, add the grated cheese on top, and place in a preheated oven at 180 ºC for about 15 minutes until the cheese is gratinated and golden. Serve half a lasagna per person and accompany it with a nice green sprout salad.
notes: Serve half a lasagna per person and accompany it with a nice green sprout salad.
